Research R-compat, decision D-compat (operator 2026-10-06). Today the skew guard keys only on __version__. A branch or source tree that adds kinds without a bump, every patch release, and unpinned MCP entries slip through. Add a ddflow.capabilities event: the first write that uses a capability records it, like git's repository format extensions. A writer then checks the capabilities a write needs against the ones it has. Examples: minting an id under a configured template it cannot render, writing a rule while rules are events, appending under a redaction profile it lacks. Only that write is refused (D-compat 2), with the version that provides the capability; everything else proceeds. Dedupe and definition digests are computed on normalized text (whitespace, case, and redaction markers mapped to one token), so clones on different redaction profiles reach the same match. The skew guard also compares FORMAT_LEVEL. Tests: an older capability set against a newer log, for each capability.

Separate sorted dumps exist at services/triggers.py:88/258 (no separators, so they disagree with canonical), flowstate.py:317/321, quota.py:266 and bugreport.py:456. Stored trigger definitions keep a legacy digest mode so existing digests still match.

Writers compare the header: same level -> normal; written by a newer level -> keep every part this version does not understand and refuse only a write that would downgrade or lose newer content (exit 3, 'upgrade ddflow to >= X'), per D-compat (2); hand-edited -> the D-doc-regions merge. rules_status and driver_drift stop calling every difference 'from an older version'. adopt --refresh-docs backs up before writing (B-upgrade.4 backups). Tests: an older writer meets a newer file in each artifact type.

Survey 2026-10-06: Seven 'is this file ours' schemes are in scope, including the ones outside the original globs: claudehooks._ours:91, legacy.HOOK_BEGIN/END:126/392 (legacy:222 re-scans adopt's BEGIN) and markdown.GENERATED:29 (enforce.py:1485), besides adopt BEGIN/END and MANAGED_MARK, enforce.HOOK_MARKER and export frame. Provide fsio.Managed(kind).owns/version/splice.

Research R-compat, decision D-compat (operator 2026-10-06). Today config --set and ddflow_configure validate the whole resulting file non-leniently, so an older ddflow cannot change any setting once a newer knob exists (R-upgrade-experiment). Change this: validate the keys being written plus every key this version knows; unknown keys and sections pass through byte-identical. Make checked list knobs whose value set grows (dedupe.kinds, agent.routers, trailer_waivers) tolerant: an unknown member is ignored with a note, never a brick. Add knob metadata renamed_from / default_changed_in / removed_in, applied at load and on write, with D-upgrade-config-changes confirmation for operator-set values. Add an optional config 'format = N' at the top and treat a newer format as D-compat (2). Make doctor's advice depend on install_info: 'merge main' only for a source tree, otherwise the upgrade command for the install method.

Survey 2026-10-06: Also: one running-version reader (core/version.running) and one source-tree test, replacing infra/log.py:96/110, install_info.py:47/184, export/registry.py:576 and export/write.py:337. One upgrade_advice(highest, install), replacing the 3 copies of 'Upgrade ddflow-mcp to >= X' in log.py:124 and upgrade.py:51/72.

Survey 2026-10-06: Also the reading side: fsio.read_json(path) -> dict | Unreadable, replacing four parsers that decide differently on invalid JSON (claudehooks._read, adopt.py:1205, launchers.py:118/148, harness.py:53).

A branch or source tree that adds kinds without a bump, every patch release, and unpinned MCP entries slip through. Add a ddflow.capabilities event: the first write that uses a capability records it, like git's repository format extensions. A writer then checks the capabilities a write needs against the ones it has. Examples: minting an id under a configured template it cannot render, writing a rule while rules are events, appending under a redaction profile it lacks. Only that write is refused (D-compat 2), with the version that provides the capability; everything else proceeds. The skew guard also compares FORMAT_LEVEL. Tests: an older capability set against a newer log, for each capability.

data.summary: Observed 2026-10-06, 16:50-22:45 UTC (.ddflow/local/flow/samples.jsonl): status showed 'parallel: 2 (auto: ceiling 8; limited by reviewer latency ratio)' while reviewer_latency_ratio was null in almost every sample (only 1.6 and 1.05 once), load_per_core was 0.05-0.07, and the deepseek vLLM server had 12 requests running, 0 waiting and 0.8% KV cache. Growth was blocked by gate_failure_ratio hovering at 1.2-1.6 (the low mark is 1.5). In a refactoring phase, failed review gates mean the reviewer found issues, not that capacity is short. (1) The 'limited by' reason should name the signal that actually held the limit in the latest decision, never a signal that is null now. (2) gate_failure_ratio should count only failures that indicate saturation (timeouts, unavailable reviewers, infrastructure errors), not review-finding failures, or it should be off by default. Regression test from these samples. Worked around by the operator's request: schedule.parallel = fixed, max_parallel_tasks = 4 in the local config.
data.title: Adaptive flow treats failed review gates as overload and blames a signal that is null; the limit stays at 2 with idle machine and reviewer

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-07, after measurement (34 fixes since 2026-10-06 12:00 UTC: median 62 min each; per fix about 2.1 full-suite unit_tests runs at 12 min, 2.9 rubber_duck and 2.9 critic rounds with about 65% failing, mostly on findings later refuted, and 2.2 ci runs). (1) A bug fix or small task runs only the selected tests in unit_tests (ddflow tests --item: tests for the changed files plus the regression test); the full suite runs once, in ci, on the final merge result, and a failure there still blocks the merge. (2) A change under about 150 changed lines gets ONE cross-family review whose prompt covers both rubber_duck and critic, and that outcome is recorded for both gates. Larger changes keep both reviews. At most 2 full rounds; after that, remaining findings are triaged, and the gate is passed-on-refutation (flagged, D-unify 5) or escalated to the operator. (3) A re-review always sends the item's full diff against its base, together with the previous findings and their triage, never only the newest commits.
data.title: Gate economy: targeted tests while iterating and the full suite once in ci; one combined cross-family review for small fixes with at most 2 full rounds; re-reviews see the whole item diff

data.body: Make D-gate-economy (1) the default workflow, not a convention. For fix tasks and small tasks (a size threshold knob), the unit_tests gate runs the tests selected by testselect: the tests for the changed files plus the declared regression test. The evidence lists which tests ran and why. The ci gate runs the full suite on the merge result before merge. Knobs: [gates] unit_tests_scope = selected|full per kind, default selected for fix and small tasks. A selection that cannot be computed falls back to the full suite and says so.
data.title: Targeted tests while iterating, the full suite once in ci (D-gate-economy 1)

data.body: For a diff under [review].combined_under_lines (default 150), ddflow review --gate rubber_duck,critic sends ONE request whose prompt covers both lenses and records the outcome for both gates, with the shared review id in evidence. Larger diffs keep both reviews, run in parallel. The round limit (max_rounds 2) also bounds delta rounds. After it, the gate is passed-on-refutation (flagged, D-unify 5) when every finding has a probe, or escalated to the operator.

data.body: Today a delta round often sees only the follow-up commit and reports 'fix absent'. A re-review sends the full item diff against its base (bug fixes are small), plus a compact list of the previous findings with their triage (confirmed and fixed, or refuted with the probe), and asks the reviewer to confirm each and look for new issues. Delta-only remains available, with --delta-only, for very large diffs.

data.body:
One loader per kind already exists or is planned on the overlay loader (B-uni-overlay); the bundle reader hands each subtree to that kind's loader as one more layer, so a bundle can carry anything a project can. manifest.roots declares which kinds/namespaces the bundle owns, so two bundles cannot both define the same enforced item (OPA roots); min_ddflow_version refuses a too-old ddflow with the upgrade remedy. Unknown keys in a bundle newer than the code follow the lenient rule (warn, skip) for defaults and fail-closed for policy.

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): the bundle layout adds decisions/ (decision records, decision packs and radar entries), and routing settings for subagents ride in config.toml and agents/ (which agent role serves which gate or task kind, separation of duties). mcp/ is NOT a separate directory: an MCP server is a companions.toml entry (name, launch line, what it buys, which gates it serves), which keeps one definition per tool.

Each kind registers with the overlay loader once (B-uni-overlay); this task proves each one resolves from an org bundle, is overridable by the project unless required by policy, reports provenance, and that executable parts stay inert until approved. Skills from an org bundle reuse the skills install/lock path (B-skills-install) rather than a second installer. Org-required companions appear in the brief's companion line with the source named.

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): two kinds were missing from the list and are now in scope: (1) architectural decisions and decision packs (owned by B-dec-presets; pinned 'always' decisions from B-dec-pinned, evidence requirements from B-dec-evidence, and policy-document sources from B-dec-policy-sources arrive through the same bundle; a decision the company enforces cannot be superseded locally); (2) subagent routing and separation of duties (B-sub-route, B-sub-sod) as org-set defaults, with 'allow' lists for which agents may satisfy which gates. The company's MCP servers are companions: each entry's launch line, install command and hooks are executable content, inert until a person approves its digest, then registered into each agent's config by the one mcpconfig.register writer.

Packs follow D-decision-management: python-library, python-service, web-frontend, go-service, container-infra, testing-baseline, security-baseline and upgrade-policy. They are loaded through the overlay loader, and a project can eject and edit them. `ddflow decision preset list|show|apply <pack>` asks the choice points (for example the test runner or the layering style), records the decisions as accepted by the operator, and tags them with pack@version. A newer pack version is offered as a diff, never applied silently (B-upgrade). Company packs arrive through P-org-config. A decision the company enforces cannot be superseded locally; a local waiver needs the company's policy to allow it.

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): company decision packs and enforced decisions travel in the org bundle's decisions/ directory (B-org-bundle); they are loaded through the same overlay loader, tagged with their source@rev, and shown by `ddflow decision status` with the source named.

Examples: floor review.min_other_family_reviewers=1; require gates.task_pipeline contains [critic, unit_tests]; pin enforce.commit_without_lease=block; allow companions=[roborev, codeguide-mcp]; allow reviewer models; require rules/security-baseline. A violating write from CLI, MCP, prompt or configure is refused (exit 3) naming the policy item, source and rev; a hand-edited file that violates is reported by doctor and, in enforce mode, claim/merge/complete refuse until fixed; audit mode only reports (brief + doctor). The four enforced kernel rules, human gates and D-reviewer-trust are re-expressed as shipped policy so the org layer extends one mechanism. A project-level policy file lets the operator lock a key locally the same way (generalising export disable --lock).

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): allow/require/pin items also cover: which companions and MCP servers may be proposed or registered (allow), which subagent roles must exist (require), which decisions are required and not supersedable locally (require), and which prompts or commands may not be overridden (pin).

Fixes bug Bf84a50bce3: MCP tools ddflow_rule_list (arguments json, limit) and ddflow_rule_remove (argument reason) accepted by 0.1.15 are rejected by 0.1.18 and later as unknown arguments (additionalProperties false): a breaking change with no alias, against D-compat 1. Found by the surface snapshots (tests/compat/surface.py) diffing 0.1.15 against 0.1.18. Restore the arguments (json and limit honoured, reason recorded or ignored as 0.1.15 did) and drop the declaration in tests/compat/test_surface.py. Found on B-uni-compat-tests.3-surface.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bf84a50bce3 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bf84a50bce3 --regression-test <test>` first).

Direction per D-compat (aliases until 1.0): do NOT restore the dead behaviour. Accept json and limit on ddflow_rule_list and reason on ddflow_rule_remove as deprecated no-op arguments (hidden from tools/list), answer with one deprecation note in the result, and remove their three entries from DECLARED in tests/compat/test_surface.py. The files overlap U2's B-upgrade.3-plan lease on ddflow/surfaces/tools/ — claim it as soon as that merges.

Stdlib only: Param(name, type, help, required, default, flag, choices, repeat) -> argparse arguments and JSON Schema 2020-12; call(repo, args, agent) -> Outcome; payload is the field tuple both surfaces print (33 of 51 CLI tuples already equal the MCP one); human renderer optional. data.claim: Today (main 478ae1e8): a research note is flat (core/records.py:756 ResearchNote: question, claim, mechanism, falsifier, probe, probe_output, verdict, flat sources, tags, item); one event research.recorded replaces the whole note; no edit, supersede or retire; probe is never re-run and a CONFIRMED verdict never goes stale; no link to code (no globs, no anchors), tests or decisions; the research gate (gates/defs.py:92, outcomes.py:365) accepts any non-empty free text and never looks for a linked record; brief and claim carry no research (brief.py injects lessons, decisions, memories); FTS indexes question, claim, probe and verdict only; duplicate detection is record-level TF-IDF (api/_dedupe.py) with no polarity, number or verdict logic, and a new REFUTED against an old CONFIRMED is accepted silently; 523 research rows exist. Of P-research's 16 tasks none depends on a P-unify component: B-rw-schema writes its own events though def-records reserves kind 'claim' (core/defs.py:38); B-rw-inject, B-rw-query and B-semantic-recall build their own injection, search and embedder; B-rw-stale and B-rw-sources build their own change and source checks; B-rw-revise duplicates def-records; B-rw-gate-link overlaps kind-pipeline. Landed and unused by research: ChangeDetector, run_shell, approval, upcasters, def-records, core/globs, OverlayLoader, GOVERNS test selection. Missing and unplanned: a typed link from a claim to code and tests, re-running a claim's check, a gate that makes implementation cite and match its claim, edit-time retrieval, claim-level duplicate and contradiction checks, and research-vs-research contradiction.
data.falsifier: A formula claim with known-answer vectors is implemented in code carrying '# ddflow: implements C-x@1'; changing the code or revising the claim to @2 surfaces 'outdated' or 'suspect' at the next gate, the vectors run and fail a wrong implementation, editing that file shows the claim in context, and a new REFUTED claim against an old CONFIRMED one is flagged; none of this requires a new search engine, queue or injector.
data.mechanism: Prior art: OpenFastTrace (spec items with revision; source tags [impl->dsn~x~1]; a bumped revision makes tags 'outdated coverage'), StrictDoc (@relation markers resolved to a symbol), Doorstop (links carry the target fingerprint; changed target = suspect link until reviewed), Swimm (auto re-pin of trivial change vs fail on substantive change), Reqstool/Tiger (build fails on missing implementation or passing test), DO-178C/ISO 26262 bidirectional trace matrices and change-impact analysis; executable specs: known-answer test vectors (NIST CAVP, RFC appendices), property-based and oracle and metamorphic tests, doctests, design by contract; claim-level verification: FActScore (atomic claims), ALCE and AIS (does the stored passage entail the claim), Chain-of-Verification, CRITIC (tool-checked), GRADE evidence grading; retrieval: hybrid BM25 + embeddings with reciprocal-rank fusion and rerank (Contextual Retrieval), repo maps, path-keyed edit-time injection; maintenance: Graphiti/Zep validity windows with invalidate-not-delete, Mem0, normalised subject/attribute/value/unit claims for exact contradiction detection, NLI for the rest.

data.question: How should ddflow's research system serve every context, including the writing and review of code that implements a formula, algorithm, constant or protocol, be correctable, verify duplicates and contradictions per claim, and reuse the shared components?

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-08 (answers to three questions) and design from R-research-system. (1) A research record holds atomic CLAIMS (kinds formula, algorithm, constant, protocol, behaviour, fact), stored as def-records of kind 'claim' with an upcaster from research.recorded; each claim has a revision, a structured subject/attribute/value/unit/conditions where it applies, sources with quoted passage, locator, content hash and retrieval date, an evidence grade, a validity window, and links to code anchors, tests and decisions. (2) Code references a claim with a plain comment tag in any language, pinned to a revision: '# ddflow: implements C-xxxx@N' (the code is the claim) or '# ddflow: uses C-xxxx@N' (it relies on it), resolved to the next function or class, with an optional commit trailer 'Implements: C-xxxx@N'. A claim revised past N makes the tag 'outdated'; a changed tagged symbol is classified trivial (comment, whitespace, rename: re-pinned) or substantive (re-verify); a removed tag or symbol makes the claim an orphan. (3) A claim's executable checks live in the repository's tests (named test ids; known-answer vectors, property, oracle, metamorphic and doctest checks stay in git); a bare shell-command check proposed by an agent is inert until the operator approves its digest; checks run through the shared command runner and an unrunnable check is 'unavailable', never passed. (4) Enforcement is warn by default and block per claim: uncited implementations and failed or unrunnable checks are shown at the gate, in brief and in review prompts; a claim set to block fails the gate. (5) Relevant claims reach every context through the one context pack: brief and claim, implement and review gate prompts, edit time (a hook keyed on the file being edited: anchored claims first, fuzzy hits after), claim time (neighbours for the duplicate and contradiction check) and MCP; exact anchors always outrank fuzzy hits. (6) Duplicates and contradictions are checked per claim: structured same-subject-and-attribute with a different value after unit normalisation is an exact contradiction; a new REFUTED against a live CONFIRMED, polarity and number conflicts are flagged and block CONFIRMED until resolved; nothing is deleted: revise bumps the revision, supersede sets validity, REFUTED flags every anchored code site as a suspected bug. (7) Every part reuses a P-unify component: def-records, upcasters, search-core, context-pack, change detector, command runner, approval, overlay loader, record surface, kind-pipeline predicates, guidance engine.
data.title: Research as claims anchored to code: revision-pinned comment tags, checks that live in the repo's tests, warn by default and block per claim, built on the shared components

data.title: Write the decision document for claim-anchored research from D-research-system and settle the remaining knobs

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces the design of B-rw-schema (do not build its own event kind): claims are def-records of kind 'claim' (core/defs.py already reserves it), written through the one definition-record fold. Claim fields: id C-xxxx and rev; kind formula|algorithm|constant|protocol|behaviour|fact; statement (one atomic sentence); structured {subject, attribute, value, unit, conditions} (required for constant and formula); sources [{url|path|sha, quote, locator, content_hash, retrieved}]; grade A-D; verdict CONFIRMED|REFUTED|THEORETICAL; validity {valid_from, valid_until, superseded_by}; anchors; checks; links to tasks, decisions and tests. A research record stays the container (question, mechanism, falsifier, probe). The 523 existing notes fold as one claim each through an upcaster, with no loss; research.recorded keeps replaying byte-identically. The research gate's pass requires a claim or record linked to THIS item (shared predicate from B-uni-kind-pipeline), or a skip or unavailable with a reason. Redaction applies to claim text and quoted passages (log profile).
data.title: Claims as def-records: kind 'claim' with revision, structured fields, source passages, grade, validity, anchors and checks; an upcaster from research.recorded; the research gate links records to items

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. One language-neutral scanner finds the tag in any comment syntax (#, //, /* */, --, ;, <!-- -->). Symbol resolution: stdlib ast for Python (function/class/method with a normalised AST hash that ignores comments, whitespace and local renames); other languages resolve to the next non-blank line/block (brace or indent) with a text hash; an optional tree-sitter adapter may arrive later as an extra, never required. The anchor index lives in the local store and is refreshed by ChangeDetector (changed files only). Drift states per anchor: current; outdated (claim revision above the tag's N); suspect (tagged symbol changed substantively since its last check; trivial changes are re-pinned and noted); orphan (tag without a live claim, or claim anchor whose symbol vanished). The commit trailer 'Implements: C-xxxx@N' is read by the existing trailer check. Anchor events are append-only (anchor.linked, anchor.checked). Tests: every state, each comment syntax, rename-only change stays trivial.
data.title: Code anchors: the '# ddflow: implements|uses C-xxxx@N' tag, symbol resolution, the Implements trailer, and an anchor index kept current by the change detector

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. A claim's check names existing test ids (selected for runs through the same GOVERNS test-selection mechanism, so a change to an anchored file selects the claim's tests) with their kind: vector (known-answer pairs, e.g. RFC/NIST test vectors kept in the test files), property, oracle (a slow reference implementation), metamorphic, doctest. A bare shell command is allowed only after the operator approves its digest (B-uni-approval; changed command = asked again). Execution goes through B-uni-cmdrunner (timeout, slot, output cap, redaction); outcomes ok/warn/fail/unknown/unavailable using verify's tri-state discipline (services/verify.py), recorded as claim.checked with the tree fingerprint; unknown or unavailable is never ok. `ddflow research check <claim>` and MCP twin. A failing check on a REFUTED/changed claim files a bug with the failing vector as its regression test.
data.title: Executable checks for claims: named repo tests (known-answer vectors, property, oracle, metamorphic, doctest), approved commands, run through the shared command runner with unavailable-not-passed

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. A gate predicate (B-uni-kind-pipeline's requires_evidence/applies_when) evaluates, for the item's diff: (1) every anchored claim touched: drift state and checks (run selected checks; a failing or unrunnable check is a finding); (2) 'unattributed algorithm': a new function the claim extraction heuristics classify as implementing a formula/algorithm/protocol with no tag (heuristic, warn only; reviewers confirm), plus any claim of kind formula/algorithm/constant/protocol with no anchor ('uncovered claim' report); (3) tags pointing at outdated, superseded or REFUTED claims. Findings carry file:line and the claim id@rev. Enforcement per D-research-system (4): warn by default; a claim marked block fails the gate (enforcement field on the claim); org policy may pin or floor it later. The implement, rubber_duck, critic and standards prompts receive the anchored claims (via B-rw-context) and are told to verify the code against them and cite the claim id. Evidence recorded with the claim fingerprints so a later revision makes it stale.
data.title: Conformance at the gates: when a diff touches an anchored symbol or adds an implementation of a formula/algorithm/constant/protocol, the item must cite its claim and the claim's checks must pass; warn by default, block per claim

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces the design of B-rw-inject and B-rw-query's retrieval (they must not build their own injector, search or embedder). Claims are a SearchSource in the one engine (statement, mechanism, structured fields, quoted passage, tags indexed), fused BM25 + trigram (+ embeddings when the [rag] extra is present), and a ContextPack builder with per-context budgets: brief ~2k tokens (claims first, record collapsed), claim time (top neighbours for dedupe), review ~3k (anchored claims + vectors), edit time ~1.5k. Edit time: the PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write (through the one hook table, B-uni-hooks; harnesses without such a hook fall back to the claim/brief injection and the MCP tool) injects the claims anchored to the file being edited, with their grade, vectors and a one-line citation; exact anchored claims are always included, fuzzy hits only fill the remaining budget; claims about third-party tools carry staleness labels. MCP: tool `ddflow_research_for(path|symbol|text)` and resource `ddflow://claim/<id>`. Each pack fenced as data with provenance. Fixes B204's gap in this area: a task whose globs have anchored claims cannot complete without the pack having been offered (recorded).
data.title: Research in every context: the one context pack and search source serve brief, claim, gate prompts, edit time (hook keyed on the file), claim time and MCP, with exact anchors ahead of fuzzy hits

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Plugs into B-coh-contradiction's engine rather than building another: for a new/revised claim, retrieve neighbours (same anchors, same subject, search-core), then (a) duplicate: equal structured subject+attribute+value or text similarity above the floor: offer same_as/extends, not a second claim; (b) exact contradiction: same subject+attribute, same conditions, different value after unit normalisation (a small stdlib unit table: SI prefixes, time, size; pint stays an optional extra, never required); (c) verdict conflict: a new REFUTED against a live CONFIRMED (or the reverse) for the same statement; (d) polarity/number flips by the shared deterministic detector, an optional different-family judge for flagged pairs only. A flagged pair writes claim.conflict_flagged, blocks the new claim from CONFIRMED until resolved, appears in brief and doctor, and routes to the operator when a decision or rule is involved (B-rw-vs-decision). Conflicts explained by different conditions or versions are resolved by recording the condition, not by picking a winner. Tests: each rule, units, no false conflict across conditions.
data.title: Claim-level duplicate and contradiction checks: structured same-subject/attribute conflicts after unit normalisation, polarity and number conflicts, new REFUTED vs live CONFIRMED, as a claim-kind plug-in of the shared coherence engine

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces B-rw-revise's own events: uses the def-record revise/supersede/retire/merge paths (B-uni-def-records, B-uni-record-surface), with a mandatory reason, who/model family, and the source or probe that justifies the change. Revise = same claim, rev+1; supersede = the world or source changed (valid_until + superseded_by, Graphiti-style invalidate-not-delete); merge records same_as. On revise/supersede/retire: list every anchor pinned to the old revision (they become 'outdated'), open one re-verification task per anchor group or block items touching them; the reviewer clears the pin with `ddflow research pin <claim> --code <anchor>` (Doorstop suspect-link clearing). A claim that becomes REFUTED (by probe, failing vector or a verifier) files a bug per anchored code site naming the claim; the refuting vector is the natural regression test. Evidence of every correction stays in the log.
data.title: Correct claims without deleting: revise (revision bump), supersede (validity window), retire and merge on the definition-record path; every anchor pinned to the old revision becomes suspect; a REFUTED claim flags its code sites as suspected bugs

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. `ddflow research trace [--path|--claim|--kind|--phase] [--json]` and MCP twin: a matrix claim -> anchors -> checks -> last result, with orphan and uncovered counts; doctor notes with remedies (tag missing, outdated anchors, checks not run in N days, unverifiable claims). Built on the record surface and the shared report renderer. Exports as a section of RESEARCH.md (the generated research view) grouped by topic with provenance.
data.title: Trace report and doctor notes: both directions (claims without implementation or check; code tags to refuted, superseded or unknown claims), by phase, path and kind

data.body: D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Throwaway project scenario with no repository-specific names: claim C1 (a hash or checksum formula with RFC-style vectors) -> implementation tagged '# ddflow: implements C1@1' -> the gate runs the vectors and passes; a wrong implementation fails; editing the file shows C1 in the injected context; the claim is revised to @2 -> the tag is outdated and a re-verification task appears; a new claim stating a different value for the same subject/attribute is flagged; a new REFUTED against the live CONFIRMED is flagged and blocks CONFIRMED; the source hash changes -> the claim goes stale and its probe is re-run. README section 'Research', help topic and driver notes updated.
data.title: Acceptance: a formula claim with known-answer vectors is implemented with a tag; a code change and a claim revision each surface at the gate; edit-time injection; a contradicting REFUTED is flagged; an old CONFIRMED probe is re-run on source change

Old notes fold as one claim. Replay test.

research edit|supersede|retire|merge <id> --reason; events research.edited (explicit field set), research.superseded, research.retired; a superseded or contradicted claim is invalidated with an end time, never deleted (bi-temporal, as Zep); show prints the revision history. A claim turns stale when review_by passed, a source's content hash changed, a version_bound dependency changed, or a file in its globs changed since it was verified; a default scheduled job files re-verify tasks; brief and recall label stale claims and do not inject them as current.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Use ChangeDetector (changed files and anchors), the local store and the trigger engine (B-uni-triggers) instead of a private detector; a claim is stale when review_by passes, a source content hash changes, a version_bound dependency changes, or an ANCHORED or globbed file changes substantively; staleness re-runs the claim's checks (B-rw-checks) before it asks a person.

A source that cannot be checked makes its claim unverifiable, not verified. Source-quality heuristics in the gathering prompt (prefer primary and authoritative sources over SEO content, the Anthropic finding). Network checks are optional and recorded unavailable offline.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Use the shared fetch/process helpers: one HTTP fetch with timeout, size cap, ETag and redaction (the same helper central configuration and documentation fetching use, B-org-sources), and infra.git for sha/path checks. Store quote, locator, content hash and retrieval date per source; a passage that no longer contains the quote marks the claim suspect.

ddflow research verify <id>: a pack of claims and sources for a different-family reviewer that writes its own verification questions and answers them without seeing the draft (CoVe), and a separate refute-this pass; per-claim outcome verified/disputed/unverifiable/unavailable recorded; CONFIRMED with any disputed claim never passes silently.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Generalise services/verify.py's ok/warn/fail/unknown tri-state and pack/judge to claims: verification per ATOMIC claim (FActScore), the verifier receives the stored passage and decides if it entails the statement (ALCE/AIS), a different model family from the author, plus an adversarial refute pass; the claim's executable checks (B-rw-checks) are run first and weigh more than any model opinion; a disputed CONFIRMED is downgraded or escalated.

A passed research gate must name a research id whose item is this item (or a skip with a reason, or unavailable); the evidence free text alone no longer passes it. Regression test: passed with no linked record is refused.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Use B-uni-kind-pipeline's requires_evidence(link) predicate: the research gate passes only with a claim or record linked to this item; and, for items whose diff has anchored claims, B-rw-conformance supplies the rest.

Stages: scope and question, recall first (B204), plan with effort scaled to complexity (one agent and few calls for a fact, 2-4 subagents for a comparison, more for an open question, per Anthropic), parallel gathering, source grading, synthesis, claim extraction, independent verification, adversarial review, probes and tests, verdict, record, link into the project. Each stage is a template the project can override; add/remove/reorder stages in config; doctor lints the workflow; changes to it are events so a past research shows the workflow it followed.

Unconfigured or unreachable -> BM25 exactly as today, and `doctor` says which is active. Measure recall quality on this repo's own corpus (a small set of queries whose right answer is known) before and after — adopt only if it wins. Needs B194 (it adds session summaries to the same index).

progress.detect findings for A supersedes B supersedes A, a record whose verdict or status flips more than N times, a lesson and a task that keep re-filing each other, a research item re-proposing itself beyond the B-research-items depth cap; [loops] thresholds; brief and doctor show them; on_detect block stops the cycle and asks.

Operator 2026-09-28: 'Could tasks be research tasks which could generate new phases and tasks by themselves?' Today items are phase|task with one task_pipeline for all; research is a gate and a separate record (ddflow research), and agents file follow-ups by hand (today's R-records -> B189-B193 and this phase). (a) per-tag pipelines ([gates.pipelines] research = ['research', 'probe', 'proposal', 'file']) so a research-tagged task never needs implement/merge; (b) its completion carries a research record (question, probe, verdict) and a proposal: tasks and phases with titles, globs, needs, priorities; (c) 'file' gate: proposed TASKS under existing phases are added automatically, linked back (source: research id); proposed PHASES and anything outward-facing wait on a human approval gate (reuse the B82 human gate); (d) a research item may propose further research items, with a depth/budget cap so it cannot recurse unbounded; (e) recall shows the chain research -> items. stash@{1}: On worktree-bridge-cse_015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK: B-rules-schema-wip; if anything differs, mark the review unavailable (not passed), restore only what ddflow itself can prove it changed (never reset anything else), file a note naming the tool, and refuse to record the gate until the operator or lane confirms. data.body:
Reported by U4 on 2026-10-08 (the bug summary lost its code snippets to shell substitution; this is the full text).

With gates.unit_tests_scope = 'selected' (the default, D-gate-economy 1) the unit_tests gate selects tests only when the item's ci gate has PASSED on the clean commit its tree holds now. Otherwise (ci missing, skipped, failed, run over uncommitted edits or on another commit, a larger task, a selection that cannot be made) it runs the whole suite.

`ddflow tests --item <id>` prints a fixed line, "The unit_tests gate still runs the whole suite" (ddflow/api/operations.py:385 and ddflow/surfaces/commands/operations.py:282), whether or not selection applies. Lanes whose tree changed after ci (follow-up commits, a merge of main) silently get 12-minute full runs again and cannot tell why.

Fix: `ddflow tests --item <id>` states which mode the gate would use right now and why (ci commit versus HEAD, the missing condition) and prints the selected list when selection applies; `ddflow gate status <id>` says the same before the gate runs. Regression: one test per fall-back reason.

data.claim: Grok is not supported as an agent today: it appears only as a model family (agent.families grok -> xai) and a reviewer preset (xAI endpoint, grok-4); there is no Grok adopt target, hook, instruction-file or test. Of Grok's surfaces exactly one is a drivable agent: the official Grok Build CLI (`grok`; AGENTS.md from the root down plus .grok/rules/ and CLAUDE.md/.cursor/rules for compatibility; MCP in [mcp_servers.<name>] of [REDACTED:path] or .grok/config.toml via `grok mcp add`; JSON hooks in [REDACTED:path] and .grok/hooks with PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop; skills and .grok/agents subagents; `grok -p` headless with --output-format json|streaming-json, --always-approve, `grok agent stdio` ACP; XAI_API_KEY or a subscription; no documented session-id variable), with a community near-twin superagent-ai/grok-cli ([REDACTED:path], MCP via `grok mcp add`, hooks unconfirmed; the two share [REDACTED:path]). Grok inside Copilot, Cursor, Cline, Kilo, opencode, Windsurf is a model, covered by the host agent's row and the xAI family rule. Grok chat/web/mobile/@grok on X and the xAI API are not agents ddflow can drive; no official xAI GitHub bot exists. Bots: ddflow can use a stdio MCP server only where the agent runs code in a VM we control (Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Copilot cloud agent via copilot-setup-steps.yml and COPILOT_MCP_-prefixed secrets, OpenHands, Amp, Droid); Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud agents and Codex cloud are instructions-only or remote-MCP-only until probed; review bots (CodeRabbit, Qodo) and Dependabot/Renovate are event sources; Sweep is deprecated. Nothing in the repo exercises a real agent or bot: P-harness-adapters (0/11) plans descriptors and fixture-based conformance only. Open facts to probe: Grok Build hook payload and session id and MCP approval step, Codex cloud custom MCP, Cursor cloud custom stdio MCP, Devin stdio inside its VM, Copilot AGENTS.md support, exit codes of grok/amp/droid.
data.falsifier: A throwaway repo is adopted for Grok Build; a scripted `grok -p` run calls ddflow_brief and claims, edits and completes a trivial task, the event log shows it under a distinct identity, a replayed recorded hook payload fixture passes conformance offline, and the same harness reports 'unavailable' (not pass) for an agent without a key.
data.mechanism: Three test layers: (1) deterministic MCP layer with no LLM (the MCP inspector CLI and the official conformance runner against ddflow's stdio server at pinned protocol versions); (2) offline conformance from live-recorded payload fixtures per agent (replay catches schema drift cheaply); (3) live smoke runs of each headless agent (claude -p, codex exec, gemini -p, grok -p, amp -x, droid exec, openhands --headless) with a fixed tiny task, asserting on ddflow's event log and not on prose, with turn caps, timeouts, one retry, majority-of-3 and 'unavailable' on missing key, CLI or rate limit; bots (Copilot cloud agent, @claude, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud) via a sandbox repo with scheduled smoke issues, advisory only. Prior art for adapters: Harbor and Terminal-Bench install-and-invoke agent adapters.
data.probe: Code grep (grok appears only in agent/config_sections/agent.py families and services/review.py xai preset), board census of P-harness-adapters and P-agent-hygiene, web survey of Grok Build, grok-cli, xAI API and 13 bots/cloud agents (confidence per fact tagged V/S/? in the report).

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Ask the operator, record D-agent-compat and write the doc. Draft defaults to put to them. TIERS: (1) Supported-live: stdio MCP + instructions + hooks + headless, tested live every release: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Amp, Factory Droid, OpenHands, Copilot CLI, Kilo, opencode, Qwen Code. (2) Supported-by-fixtures: IDE/GUI agents that cannot run headless: Cursor IDE, Cline, Roo, Devin Desktop (ex-Windsurf), Continue, Antigravity, Aider (conformance fixtures + manual checklist). (3) Cloud bots, advisory: Copilot cloud agent, @claude/Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin cloud, Cursor cloud agents (sandbox repo, scheduled, results advisory). (4) Event sources and reviewers: Dependabot, Renovate, CodeRabbit, Qodo (recorded as bot authors, never claim). Out of scope: Sweep (deprecated), Grok chat/web/X. 'Supported' means: adopt works idempotently; the MCP server registers and its tools are callable; session start and prompt capture work or fall back honestly; identity is distinct; a claim/edit/complete round trip leaves the event log consistent; gaps are listed in the compatibility report. BUDGET: live runs use cheap models, a turn cap and a spend cap per run (default 1 USD), keys only from the environment or the git-ignored local config, never committed; cadence weekly and before a release, plus on demand. SANDBOX: a dedicated GitHub repository the operator owns for bot smoke issues. Also decide whether ddflow may install an agent CLI itself for tests (default: never, only detect).

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). B-hx-research covers the 14 agents verified in 2026-09; this task adds Grok Build, superagent-ai/grok-cli, and the bots in R-agent-compat (Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Gemini CLI Action, Devin, OpenHands, Cursor cloud agents, Amp, Factory Droid, CodeRabbit/Qodo, Dependabot/Renovate) with the nine facts per agent (instructions, MCP registration and approval step, hooks, commands, skills/subagents, headless flags and exit codes, identity variables, where it runs, auth and cost) and the confidence of each (verified from a primary page, from a run, or unknown). Probe the open facts empirically with a live run where a key exists, otherwise record them unknown: Grok Build hook payload and session id and MCP approval step, Codex cloud custom MCP, Cursor cloud custom stdio MCP, Devin stdio inside its VM, Copilot AGENTS.md support, exit codes of grok, amp and droid. data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Descriptor for Grok Build: AGENTS.md (root-down) and .grok/rules/ for instructions; MCP in [mcp_servers.ddflow] of .grok/config.toml (project) via the one mcpconfig.register writer, with `grok mcp add` as the documented alternative; hooks as JSON files in .grok/hooks/ for UserPromptSubmit (prompt capture), Stop (the stop protocol), PreToolUse (edit-time research context, B-rw-context) and SessionStart/PreCompact only if the probe confirms them, else the first-call fallback of B-hy-first-call; the project-hook trust step `/hooks-trust` is told to the operator by adopt; identity from the hook payload's session id if present, else worktree-derived identity; skills/subagents under .grok/agents/. `ddflow doctor` runs `grok inspect` when the CLI exists and reports registered MCP/hooks/rules. The community superagent-ai/grok-cli shares [REDACTED:path] told apart by config.toml versus user-settings.json; instructions-only plus stdio MCP, no hooks assumed. Update the xai reviewer preset to a current model (grok-4.7 per the docs page) and keep the xAI family rule. Idempotent adopt, uninstall and upgrade-migration tests with recorded fixtures.
data.title: Grok Build support: harness descriptor, adopt targets, hook normaliser and writer, identity, doctor check with `grok inspect`; the community grok-cli recognised and told apart; xAI reviewer preset updated

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Descriptor fields: kind, integration mode and the facts that drive it. Identity: bot authors such as copilot/*, dependabot[bot], renovate[bot], coderabbitai[bot], claude and the Actions runner are recognised, recorded as bot authors, and event-source and review bots are never offered a claim. Generated, previewed and never silently written setup material per bot: Copilot cloud agent (copilot-setup-steps.yml that installs ddflow, the MCP JSON for repo settings with the required tools allowlist and COPILOT_MCP_-prefixed secrets, .github/copilot-instructions.md pointing at AGENTS.md), Claude Code Action workflow (mcp config, --allowedTools including the ddflow tools, the known permission-denied trap), Gemini CLI Action mcpServers input, Jules and Devin and Codex cloud instructions-only (AGENTS.md) with the remote MCP endpoint noted where they accept one. Cloud agents that accept only remote servers require the HTTP transport: depends on B-mcp-http-transport. Honest output when a mode is unsupported: 'instructions-only, MCP unavailable' rather than a broken config.

One process per assertion with the inspector CLI (initialize and server/discover, tools/list ordering and schemas, a read-only tool call, an error call, version negotiation) and the conformance scenarios for protocol 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28; JSON on stdout and exit codes as assertions. data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). `ddflow harness record <agent>` runs (or attaches to) a real session and stores each hook payload, the MCP request/response pairs and the files adopt wrote, with the agent's version and the date, passed through the log redaction profile; fixtures are committed per agent and version. B-hx-conformance replays them: normaliser output golden, hook command round trip, idempotent adopt, uninstall restores. A fixture older than N months or for a different major version is flagged in the compatibility report. Grok Build is the first agent recorded.
data.title: Live-recorded payload fixtures per agent and a recorder: capture real hook and MCP payloads from a live run, redact them, replay them offline in conformance

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Per-agent adapter as data in the descriptor ([test]: detect command, headless command template, env keys, turn cap flag, expected exit codes) for claude -p, codex exec, gemini -p, grok -p (--output-format json), amp -x, droid exec, openhands --headless, copilot, kilo and opencode run. Scenario: throwaway repo -> `ddflow adopt` for that agent -> prompt 'call ddflow_brief, claim the one task, add a file, run the gates you can, complete it' (cheap model, turn cap, spend cap per D-agent-compat) -> assertions only on ddflow: the MCP tool was called (event log), the claim exists under a distinct identity, the item completed or was released honestly, no stray lease, the shard committed. Controls: timeouts, one retry, N=3 with majority, seed/temperature where exposed. Outcomes pass/fail/unavailable (missing CLI, key, rate limit, network) -- unavailable is never pass. Runs through B-uni-cmdrunner (slots, output cap, redaction); results as events (agent.smoke) for the report. Never installs an agent CLI; keys only from the environment or the git-ignored local config.
data.title: Live smoke harness: for each headless-capable agent, install-or-detect, run a fixed tiny ddflow task in a throwaway repo, assert on the event log, with turn caps, timeouts, one retry, majority-of-3 and unavailable-not-pass

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Scenario over the smoke harness: agent A claims T1, agent B claims T2 (disjoint globs) and then tries T1 (refused); a bot author (a simulated dependabot branch) is never offered a claim; the reviewer gate accepts agent B's review of A's change only if B's model family differs; the stop protocol releases both honestly when one is killed. Pairs chosen from the live-supported tier; skipped as unavailable when fewer than two agents can run.
data.title: Two agents on one repository: two different agents (for example Claude Code and Grok Build, or Codex) work concurrently, identities stay distinct, leases never collide, and the other agent satisfies the cross-family review

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). For each cloud bot in tier 3 (Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud agents): generated setup files applied to the operator's sandbox repository (only with their approval), a smoke issue 'call ddflow_status and report', a scheduled workflow polls for the bot's PR or comment, and assertions are on what ddflow can see: PR author, the branch name pattern, ddflow's pr sync (`[flow].integration = pr`), the item parked IN REVIEW, the claim released. Results are advisory (agent.smoke events marked advisory), a bot with no key or no account is 'unavailable'. Cost and cadence per D-agent-compat. Review bots (CodeRabbit, Qodo) are checked as event sources: their review comments reach ddflow's review gates through the PR, with no MCP call by ddflow.
data.title: Bot-mode tests: a sandbox repository with a smoke issue per cloud bot, scheduled and advisory; workflow files; results recorded

data.body: R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). `ddflow harness report [--json]` and MCP twin: per agent and bot its tier, each capability's state (verified live on version X on date, fixture only, instructions only, unavailable, failing), the last smoke result and trend, fixture age, and open issues. Exported as COMPAT.md through the export registry (a doc type once P-docs-generic lands). Doctor notes: an agent whose tested version is older than the installed one, a failing capability, a missing key for a tier-1 agent. A failure is filed as a bug against ddflow with the failing payload, or, when the cause is the vendor's, as an upstream report draft through B-upstream-surfaces (sanitised, consent first). The release script prints the report and refuses a release when a tier-1 agent regressed from verified to failing.
data.title: Compatibility report and issue tracking: agent x capability x last live result x fixture age x version tested, exported as COMPAT.md, doctor notes for stale or failing agents, issues filed against ddflow or upstream

chunk_findings.detail: The plan says "invert B-dt-library's dependency on B-export-security-md", but the row records the action as `removes B-export-security-md`, and no row adds the inverted edge (B-export-security-md's new-need column lists only B-dt-sources; nothing gains a dependency on B-dt-library). The row's own reason ("SECURITY.md is an export doc type built on B-dt-sources, so the library consumes it, not the reverse") contradicts its action: "the library consumes it" means B-dt-library depends on the export/sources, which is precisely the edge the action deletes. Effect: after this queue update neither B-export-security-md nor B-dt-library depends on the other (both only depend on B-dt-sources), so the SECURITY.md export and the doc-type library are unordered and the library can be built before the SECURITY.md export it is supposed to consume. Either the inversion was not performed, or the edge was deleted without the plan's replacement edge being recorded.

data.body:
Follow-up to B-uni-cmdrunner (U1 report 2026-10-08): the runner is merged but three call sites still run or check commands on their own, which is exactly the drift D-unify wants gone (each re-decides timeout, missing-executable and redaction).
1. ddflow/api/operations.py:~425 -- "is the command installed" via shutil.which(words[0]): replace with cmdrunner.executable_missing (it handles VAR=x prefixes, builtins, shlex errors and the run's own PATH). Also operations.py:508 requires-check (shutil.which on property requirements) -- decide if it should use the same helper.
2. ddflow/services/onboard_tests.py:141 -- P.run_shell(command, merge_stderr=True): run through CommandRunner. The command there is detected and then accepted by the operator, not declared in config, so give Declared a source for an operator-accepted detected command (the accept step is the declaration) rather than loosening the TypeError on bare strings.
3. ddflow/services/review.py:~719 and ~1326 -- the command reviewer spawns with P.popen (streams, long-running, killed as a group). Give CommandRunner a streaming/background entry (or a documented exemption listed in surfaces/exemptions.py with the reason) so timeout, process-group kill, Slots admission and redaction come from one place; keep only the pre-check shared if a stream cannot fit and say why.
Pin behaviour first (probe before/after as B-uni-cmdrunner did), add a guard test that fails on a new direct P.run_shell/P.popen/shutil.which(words[0]) outside cmdrunner and the listed exemptions, and lower the matching baselines.
data.title: Remaining command call sites use CommandRunner: the installed-check in operations, onboarding test run, command reviewer streaming; a guard against new direct runs

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-09 (verbatim, session s20261008T141217-1597717): "Then first complete and merge P-upgrade after P-Unify and then pause so we can commit, upgrade, test and push and restart the agents with the new mcp version hoping the upgrade process will be smooth. Within the upgrade phase please do simulate a dry upgrade of this project in case of upgrade of ddflow to guarantee that the upgrade will go smooth"
Goal: before the operator upgrades THIS project, prove on a throwaway copy that the upgrade from the version now installed (and running as MCP) to the version on main is smooth, and make the proof repeatable as a script and a release check.
Method (nothing touches the live repository, its .ddflow, the installed ddflow or the running MCP server):
1. Copy: `git clone --local` this repository into a scratch directory (real history, real event log shards, real config, real hooks and adopted files), at the commit the installed version was built from, so it looks exactly like the project does today. Record the installed version, FORMAT_LEVEL and the log's stamps/capabilities.
2. Build: build the wheel of main (or run the source tree) in a scratch venv; never `uv tool install` over the live one.
3. Read-only pass with the NEW code on the old copy: `ddflow status`, `board`, `doctor`, `brief`, `show` on every item, `history`, `replay`/`rebuild` -- record the derived state digest. The new code must read the old log without refusing, and the older-writer/skew behaviour must be the designed one (D-compat).
4. `ddflow upgrade --plan` on the copy: list every pending change, repair, migration and stale reference; fail the dry run on any `unknown`, `conflict` or `needs confirmation` that the operator would hit. Save the plan as the upgrade preview for the operator.
5. `ddflow upgrade --apply --backup snapshot` on the copy; then assert: derived state digest unchanged except the intended `upgrade.applied` event; every managed file stamped; hand-edited files kept (`.local-edits`); `ddflow doctor` clean; the second apply is a no-op; `--restore` returns the copy byte-identical (git diff empty, shards equal).
6. Old reader/writer check: run the OLD ddflow (the installed one) against the upgraded copy and confirm it reads, refuses writes only where designed (exit 3 with the remedy), and loses nothing -- this is what happens to agents still on the old MCP during the restart.
7. MCP restart check: start the new MCP server (stdio) on the copy, run initialize + tools/list + a read tool + ddflow_brief; confirm tools/list under budget, and `[mcp].output_schemas` off.
8. Agent check: with two simulated agent identities on the copy run claim -> edit -> gates -> complete of a trivial task end to end with the new version, and release honestly.
9. Concurrent-shard check: shards written by the old version by two agents merge (merge=union) and fold identically under the new code.
Output: `scripts/ci/upgrade-dry-run` (idempotent, prints a PASS/FAIL table, exit 0/1/2, 2 = could not run e.g. no git/venv/network), a report file for the operator (docs/ddflow/UPGRADE-DRYRUN.md, generated, committed only when asked), a test that runs it against a small fixture project in CI, and a release-gate hook so a release is refused if the dry run on the previous release fails. A failure is filed as a bug before anything else proceeds.

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Make ddflow have a feature to periodically check for newer versions of ddflow, to propose to the operator upgrade of itself, to have self-upgrade cli command and capabilities which do migration and upgrades (in case of running docker it shall introduce check for upgrade and migration on container or mcp start and implement it while in container if the container version has been upgraded and database and other storage and config artifacts needs migration) need. The user should be capable to check, ask, request ddflow upgrade and orchestrate and monitor it'. D-self-upgrade (5). At `ddflow mcp` start and at container entrypoint: compare the running version with the project stamp and with each store it uses (event log readability, index schema, .ddflow/local config and caches, backups dir, instruction files, hooks, MCP launch entry); newer runtime -> run the release check (if enabled), rebuild derived stores, apply the categories [upgrade].on_start allows (check|safe|off, default safe: derived-store rebuilds and non-destructive, backed-up categories only), leave consent-needing items pending; report in the first brief/first tool reply what was migrated and what awaits the operator; NEVER refuse to start for a pending migration; bounded time, then serve and continue the plan as pending; older runtime than the project -> skew guard (D-upgrade-skew-guard). Works with read-only mounts (reports instead of writing) and with the project volume owned by another uid. The image documents the behaviour and the env switches (DDFLOW_UPGRADE_ON_START). A stale RUNNING server is detected the other way round: a server whose version is older than the stamp says 'restart me' in its replies. FAILING FIRST: an old-version fixture project + new runtime -> start migrates the safe categories, records upgrade.applied, first brief lists it; consent items stay pending; a read-only store -> served, reported, nothing written; on_start=off/check -> nothing applied; a failing migration step does not prevent serving; an old runtime refuses writes per the skew guard; a container smoke test if docker is available, else recorded unavailable (never passed unrun).

GENERALITY: shipped defaults in the package for every project; works on upgrade and on fresh ddflow init; tests in a throwaway project with NO network (fake release index, fake installer, injected clock); no reference to this repository's paths, hosts, agents or models; docs ship in README and ddflow/templates; works for every agent integration and for the CLI, MCP and container surfaces; everything configurable via config, ddflow config and ddflow_configure; tools/list byte budget stays green. Builds on the accepted upgrade decisions (ddflow decision show D-upgrade-event-kinds, -auto-check, -backups, -config-changes, -manifest-lint, -skew-guard) and D-self-upgrade.

Phase B-upgrade.

Operator decision 2026-10-09 (D-upgrade-on-mcp-connect): when the operator restarts the agent and it connects to the new MCP version, the server must detect the version difference against the project stamp by itself and START the upgrade flow -- an upgrade proposal (the read-only plan) presented to the operator in the handshake/first brief, and the apply run only after the operator's explicit permission (MCP elicitation where the client supports it, else the instructions tell the agent to ask the operator and to call the apply tool with the operator's confirmation). Never apply without consent; never fail to start; an old/new server skew says restart once. Builds on B-upgrade.6-notice ([upgrade].auto = check|safe).

data.body:
R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Ask the operator, record D-agent-compat and write the doc. Draft defaults to put to them. TIERS: (1) Supported-live: stdio MCP + instructions + hooks + headless, tested live every release: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Amp, Factory Droid, OpenHands, Copilot CLI, Kilo, opencode, Qwen Code. (2) Supported-by-fixtures: IDE/GUI agents that cannot run headless: Cursor IDE, Cline, Roo, Devin Desktop (ex-Windsurf), Continue, Antigravity, Aider (conformance fixtures + manual checklist). (3) Cloud bots, advisory: Copilot cloud agent, @claude/Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin cloud, Cursor cloud agents (sandbox repo, scheduled, results advisory). (4) Event sources and reviewers: Dependabot, Renovate, CodeRabbit, Qodo (recorded as bot authors, never claim). Out of scope: Sweep (deprecated), Grok chat/web/X. 'Supported' means: adopt works idempotently; the MCP server registers and its tools are callable; session start and prompt capture work or fall back honestly; identity is distinct; a claim/edit/complete round trip leaves the event log consistent; gaps are listed in the compatibility report. BUDGET: live runs use cheap models, a turn cap and a spend cap per run (default 1 USD), keys only from the environment or the git-ignored local config, never committed; cadence weekly and before a release, plus on demand. SANDBOX: a dedicated GitHub repository the operator owns for bot smoke issues. Also decide whether ddflow may install an agent CLI itself for tests (default: never, only detect).

ANSWERED by the operator 2026-10-09 -- see D-agent-compat (accepted): the draft tiers, 3 USD per run, weekly + before release, env/local-config credentials with install into a scratch dir allowed (consent per agent), no sandbox repo yet. This task is now only: write docs/ddflow/decisions/agent-compat.md from D-agent-compat (and the 'supported' definition above), and complete it. Do not ask the operator again.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). For each cloud bot in tier 3 (Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud agents): generated setup files applied to the operator's sandbox repository (only with their approval), a smoke issue 'call ddflow_status and report', a scheduled workflow polls for the bot's PR or comment, and assertions are on what ddflow can see: PR author, the branch name pattern, ddflow's pr sync (`[flow].integration = pr`), the item parked IN REVIEW, the claim released. Results are advisory (agent.smoke events marked advisory), a bot with no key or no account is 'unavailable'. Cost and cadence per D-agent-compat. Review bots (CodeRabbit, Qodo) are checked as event sources: their review comments reach ddflow's review gates through the PR, with no MCP call by ddflow.

DEFERRED 2026-10-09 (D-agent-compat): the operator has no sandbox repository yet. Build the generated workflow/setup files and the test harness so they run as 'unavailable: no sandbox repo configured', but apply nothing and run nothing live until the operator names a repo. This task completes with that state; B-ac-acceptance no longer waits for a live bot run.

data.claim: P-unify does not meet its -10% line target. Counted as R-unify did (all lines of every .py file under ddflow/, newline count): main e4342e62 had 73,400 lines in 176 modules; HEAD (caebb49a, before this task) has 104,929 lines in 393 modules: +31,529 lines, +43.0%. Non-blank lines: 64,479 -> 91,358 (+41.7%). Tests: 75,515 -> 119,528 lines (330 -> 559 files). By package (lines, before -> after): services 34,447->47,736; surfaces 11,591->16,242; core 5,866->10,477; api 13,598->18,088; infra 4,879->7,393; config_sections 0->2,534 (config.py 2,013->966 after its split, so config as a whole +1,487). Net ddflow/ lines added by first-parent merges since e4342e62, by phase: P-unify +16,879 (the shared interfaces, compat contract, record surface, guidance, tests-first migration), B-upgrade +3,418, Unphased +2,484, P-schedule +1,533, B-adaptive-flow +1,205, B-hot-files +1,084 (splits add module headers), bugs +930, P-harness-adapters +685, P-id-schemes +608, other mined backlog +546, gate-economy +451. About 13.8k net lines are features that did not exist at the baseline (upgrade, schedule, adaptive flow, harness adapters, id schemes, export, reporting); about 16.9k are P-unify's own, which landed the interfaces and migrated call sites in slices but has so far removed little duplicate code in absolute terms, and the largest removal was config.py (-1,047 before its sections moved out). Ratchets did go down (git_argv 26->0, hashlib 23->0, os_replace 1->0, write_text 40->10, subprocess_calls 42->13, tempfile 12->6, deferred_imports 620->534, complexity_d_or_worse 112->100, duplicate clusters 6->4) but none of subprocess_calls, write_text, tempfile reached zero.
data.falsifier: Refuted if the same count at HEAD is above 66,060 (73,400 x 0.9). It is 104,929.
data.mechanism: Line count is a size measure, not a cost measure: the shared interfaces were built before most call sites moved, and 2,100 commits of new features landed in the same period. The -10% target would hold only if the removals outweighed the roughly 14k net lines of new features, which they did not.

chunk_findings.detail: The new paragraph asserts a property of *every* optional extra: "Everything else is an optional extra, each imported in exactly one adapter module with a standard-library fallback". The table directly beneath it contradicts that for two of the four rows, whose "The one adapter" cell reads "not landed yet (declared in `pyproject.toml`)" — i.e. `ddflow[watch]` and `ddflow[mcp-sdk]` have no adapter module at all, and therefore no module that imports watchfiles or mcp, and no module carrying the advertised fallback. A reader following the acceptance goal of this change ("shared-interface map, each concern to its one module"; "every claim is accurate") is sent looking for a watch/mcp adapter module that the same table says does not exist, and the guarantee "imported in exactly one adapter module with a standard-library fallback" is false for exactly those two extras. This is the kind of claim the change was supposed to verify (the "one adapter" cell is doing load-bearing work — it is the justification for the surrounding invariant); it should either be scoped ("each extra that has landed is imported in exactly one adapter module…") or the two not-landed rows should be moved out of the table.

chunk_findings.detail:
The added sentence asserts the dependency policy as a property of *all* four extras — each is "an optional extra with a standard-library fallback", and "a feature whose extra is absent is reported `unavailable`, never passed" — and it names `ddflow[watch]` (watchfiles) and `ddflow[mcp-sdk]` (the MCP SDK) among them. The earlier review of this same item found (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:238-243, extras table) that exactly those two rows read "not landed yet (declared in `pyproject.toml`)" — i.e. there is no adapter module importing watchfiles or the MCP SDK, so the extra has no fallback path to select and no "extra absent → `unavailable`" branch to report. That finding is untriaged and nothing in the visible part of the diff answers it; the README change now propagates the same claim into the user-facing dependency policy, where it is an unconditional promise to the reader (a `pip install ddflow[watch]`/`ddflow[mcp-sdk]` installs a package nothing imports, and the "reported `unavailable`, never passed" behaviour cannot be observed because the feature/extra pairing is not wired). Re-reporting because the fix or probe the triage asked for is not present: either the two rows must lose the "not landed yet" cell (adapters landed, and then the claim is testable), or the README sentence and the ARCHITECTURE paragraph must be conditioned on the extras that actually have an adapter.

The other guidance items are not implicated: this is a docs-only change, so [D-phase-order-after-unify] (docs first) is respected, [D-push-after-acceptance] is untouched, and [D-rules-format] does not apply.

chunk_findings.detail: The same paragraph promises two mutually exclusive behaviours for one condition. It says that when an extra is missing the feature "is recorded `unavailable`, never silently downgraded", but the Fallback column of the table right beneath promises a working degraded implementation for every extra: `ddflow[search]` → difflib, `ddflow[rag]` → "BM25 only", `ddflow[watch]` → polling, `ddflow[mcp-sdk]` → "the stdlib stdio engine". chunk_findings.detail: The added sentence advertises `ddflow[watch]` (watchfiles) and `ddflow[mcp-sdk]` (the MCP SDK) as shipped optional extras "with a standard-library fallback". The extras table added by this very change in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` still fills those two rows' "The one adapter" cell with "not landed yet (declared in `pyproject.toml`)" and the paragraph above it now concedes "two extras are declared but not yet used". Nothing in this diff lands those adapters, so the README's demonstration is concrete: a user reading `README.md:15` and running `pip install 'ddflow[mcp-sdk]'` gets the SDK installed while no module in the tree imports `mcp`, i.e. the extra buys nothing and the advertised stdlib fallback/"reported `unavailable`" behaviour has no code path behind it. The triage left this untriaged, so the previous finding stands.

chunk_findings.detail: The new paragraph promises "Everything else is an optional extra. Each is to be imported in exactly one adapter module … with a standard-library fallback" and "Where the extra is absent the fallback below runs", but two of the four rows it introduces describe a fallback for a feature that does not exist: `ddflow[watch]` → "polling" and `ddflow[mcp-sdk]` → "the stdlib stdio engine", while both rows' adapter cells read "not landed yet (declared in `pyproject.toml`)". Operator 2026-10-09 (relayed by the coordinator): DO THE CLEANUP BEFORE THE PAUSE -- migrate the remaining call sites onto the shared interfaces and delete the old code. Constraints: no feature loss (golden snapshots and the full suite stay green, pinned before and after as every P-unify slice did); the compat aliases/deprecations that D-compat keeps until 1.0 stay; the work adds no new feature.

Why: P-unify finished with ddflow/ at 104,929 lines (393 modules), +43% against the 73,400 recorded in R-unify, against a -10% target (research R-unify-acceptance, REFUTED). The interfaces exist; call sites were migrated slice by slice; the old code was not all deleted.

The plan and its measured inventory are research R-unify-cleanup-plan. Realistic target (not -10%): ddflow/ about 102,700 lines (commit to <= 103,300; -2%), tests about 118,500 (-1,000); ratchets: subprocess_calls 13->4, write_text 10->0, tempfile 6->0, deferred_imports 534->90, surfaces-through-api 34->6, subprocess-home 7->1, fsio-home 7->1, complexity_d_or_worse 100->85 (F-grade 5->2), duplicate_code_clusters 4->0, unreferenced_functions 5->2. -10% of the original (66,060 lines) would need -38,869 lines (-37%) which only removing features could give; B-uc-acceptance says so plainly with the measurement.

Structure: 18 slices with disjoint file globs (by package or ratchet). Wave 1, ready at once: B-uc-guard-split (0.5 d, unblocks the three import-linter lanes), the three api slices, B-uc-core-views, the five services slices, B-uc-deps-comments. After the guard split: B-uc-infra-proc-fsio, B-uc-mcp, B-uc-surf-registry. After B-uc-surf-registry: the four B-uc-surf-* family slices. data.how: Before filing a phase, expand the globs against the tree and run core.globs.overlap pairwise on tasks that can run together; replace dir-position wildcards with explicit directories (as was done for P-unify-cleanup).
data.rule: Write task globs as literal paths or literal-directory patterns; never put * in a directory position
data.summary: overlap() is conservative: a * in a directory position makes a task look like it overlaps everything, serialising parallel lanes. match() is not the problem.
data.title: ddflow's glob overlap check is conservative about *: a * in a directory position overlaps almost everything
data.why: Spot-checked 2026-10-10 on core.globs: match('a/*.py','a/b/c.py') is False, so a single * does NOT cross a slash when matching a path. But overlap() -- the check the scheduler and the lease system use -- treats a * as able to span a slash: overlap('a/*/x.toml','a/y.toml') and overlap('a/*.py','a/b/c.py') are both True. A task glob like tests/guard_baselines/*/ddflow.api.lifecycle.*.toml therefore looked as if it overlapped every baseline file, and only one of 20 cleanup tasks was offered while five lanes waited about 20 minutes each and stopped.
