data.falsifier: A fetched page's current text contradicts the summary above, or a tool listed as lacking a capability documents it.
data.mechanism: What others have that ddflow lacks (mechanism): (1) Plan decomposition from a spec/PRD plus plan review before code: Task Master, Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec, Backlog.md; ddflow has no plan lint or plan-review step, only hand-filed tasks. (2) Atomic ready+claim in one call (Beads `ready --claim`): ddflow has next then claim, two calls with a race the lease already refuses, so this is cosmetic. (3) Memory decay / summarisation of closed work (Beads): ddflow has brief budgets and BL-knowledge compaction tasks. (4) Dependency waves shown up front (Kiro): ddflow has B-dag-waves-fanout open. (5) Speculative combined-tree testing and bisecting a failed batch (Zuul, bors, GitHub queue, Mergify): ddflow has B-batch-integration open, with no bisect-on-failure stated. (6) Affected-target test selection from a dependency graph (Nx, Bazel; ML in Launchable): ddflow selects by name and governs only. (7) Per-task token and cost attribution plus hard budgets (Langfuse, OpenHands max_budget_per_task, Claude Code --max-budget-usd and OTel): ddflow has quota percent windows planned (B-quota-*), no per-task or per-lane spend. (8) Stuck/loop detection with automatic stop (OpenHands): ddflow has B-am-loops planned. (9) A live board/TUI/web view (Backlog.md, Vibe Kanban, Claude Squad, Conductor): ddflow renders markdown and text only. (10) Issue intake and PR/check-run feedback (Emdash, Copilot agent, Linear agents): ddflow has external sync, pr_sync and a one-way tracker sink planned, no check-run publishing. (11) Sandboxed execution (OpenHands, Inspect, Copilot firewall): ddflow runs gate commands from repository config unsandboxed. (12) Hooks that block task creation/completion (agent teams TaskCreated/TaskCompleted): ddflow gates are stronger. Where ddflow is ahead: append-only content-addressed log with Lamport order and per-agent shards (merge without conflict, replay), expiry leases that report rather than steal, unavailable-not-passed gate semantics, enforced cross-family review and failing-first regression tests, glob-based admission with named alternatives, decisions/lessons/research as governed records with dedupe and provenance fencing, one declaration for CLI and MCP with a parity test, upgrade model with skew guard. None of the fetched tools had an equivalent of any of these as an enforced rule; Beads and Backlog.md are closest on storage in git but have no gates. The bors-ng and Vibe Kanban/Crystal status facts show that thin worktree-manager UIs are being sunset or absorbed by harness vendors and merge queues by GitHub, which is the evidence for 'do not build a UI or a merge-queue service'.
data.question: What do comparable AI-agent workflow tools, work-queue and merge-queue systems do that ddflow lacks, and where is ddflow ahead?

data.body: Operator request 2026-10-10 for a gap analysis of ddflow against similar tools and its own history. Evidence: R-gaps-evidence (CONFIRMED), R-gaps-survey (THEORETICAL). Every task waits for B-gap-decide, where the operator picks, orders or drops them. Only gaps not already on the roadmap are filed here; overlaps are cross-referenced in the task bodies.
data.title: Gaps found by the 2026-10 survey: log scale, lane ledger, plan lint, metrics, affected tests, fold properties, spend, DR, trust

data.body:
Operator request 2026-10-10 (verbatim): "Make a research for this ddflow tool and similar tools or workflows and your honest opinion having in mind the roadmap and your research what other features this workflow and queue tool might need to have or would be great to have, or is missing, and could you create a phase and tasks to implement the gaps?"

Evidence: research records R-gaps-evidence (CONFIRMED, measured on this repo's log) and R-gaps-survey (THEORETICAL, 21 pages fetched, the rest summarised).

ASK THE OPERATOR which of the tasks in P-gaps to build, in what order, and whether to build them at all; nothing in P-gaps starts before this task is answered. Recommended order and defaults (accept, reorder, or drop each):
1. B-gap-log-scale (MUST) -- the log is 46% lease.renewed events and `ddflow status` takes 5.4 s at 35 MB after 13 active days (~1 GB/year at this rate). Default: yes, first, measure then coalesce renewals and move gate evidence out of line.
2. B-gap-lanes (MUST) -- lane ledger and restart briefs replacing hand-written coordinator briefs; ledger + advisor only, no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon). Default: yes.
3. B-gap-plan-lint (MUST) -- mechanical plan check at task/phase add (literal globs, cycles, disjointness, acceptance present) and an optional plan-review step. Default: yes, lint now, plan-review as a flag.
4. B-gap-metrics (GREAT) -- one log-derived metrics service behind `ddflow metrics`, `ddflow forecast`, `ddflow retro <id>`; B-rm-changes ETA hint, B-af-headroom and B-sub-metrics should consume it instead of each writing their own replay. Default: yes after 1-3.
5. B-gap-affected-tests (GREAT) -- import-graph reverse closure for `ddflow tests`, fast subset at the unit gate, full suite at batch integration. Default: yes.
6. B-gap-fold-properties (GREAT) -- seeded model-based and property tests of fold, shard merge order, leases. Default: yes, no new dependency.
7. B-gap-spend (GREAT) -- per-lane/per-item token and spend ledger from harness transcripts plus per-item budgets. Default: yes, but only after B-am-ingest and B-quota-meters land; tokens not dollars on subscription plans.
8. B-gap-log-backup (GREAT, small) -- doctor notes for unpushed event shards and a verify/restore drill. Default: yes.
9. B-gap-command-trust (GREAT, research first) -- trust-on-change for gate commands that arrive via a branch. Default: research only; build when ddflow runs on others' PRs or CI.
10. B-gap-checks-publish (GREAT, late) -- publish gate outcomes as GitHub commit statuses/check-runs so branch protection can require them. Default: defer until a second human or CI uses the repo.
Questions: (a) Is the single operator model still true for the next quarter? If yes, drop 9 and 10. (b) Dollar budgets or token/turn budgets for B-gap-spend? (c) May B-rm-changes, B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics be re-pointed at B-gap-metrics (they are open and unclaimed)? (d) Accept the DO-NOT-BUILD list in the research record R-gaps-survey (web UI/TUI beyond `lanes --watch`, a process-spawning daemon, a merge-queue service, ML test selection, bidirectional Jira/Linear sync, RBAC, LLM-based decomposition inside ddflow, a template marketplace, hosted dashboard)? Record answers as decisions (ddflow decision add --globs) and update the tasks.
Expected size: one question round; the answer file is docs/ddflow/decisions/gap-priorities.md. Acceptance: each of the ten above carries an explicit build / defer / drop and an order; decisions recorded; open tasks updated or removed.
data.title: Operator decisions: which gaps from the 2026-10 survey to build and in what order (recommended list and defaults in the body)

data.body:
WHAT: keep the event log and the CLI fast as it grows. (1) Measure first (research record): per-kind bytes and counts, time of fold / index rebuild / status / next at 1x, 4x, 16x this log, where the 5.4 s of `ddflow status` goes (parse, fold, index, render). (2) Coalesce lease renewals: lease.renewed is 24,413 of 53,163 events (46%); log one only when the expiry would otherwise move by more than [lease].renew_log_min_s (or keep per-machine heartbeats in .ddflow/local via infra.LocalStore and fold only the last committed renewal), without changing what an observer on another clone computes as expiry. (3) Evidence out of line: gate.failed/passed carry 52% of bytes; store large evidence/tails as content-addressed blobs under .ddflow/blobs/ referenced by hash (event id stays a content address; doctor verifies the blob; tamper-evidence unchanged). (4) A checkpoint: a verified folded-state snapshot at a lamport mark so a read replays only the tail (B-log-snapshot-knobs already exists for the read snapshot; reuse it, do not add a second). (5) Shard rotation/archive is OUT of scope unless the measurement shows it is needed.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence: 35 MB and 53k events in 13 active days (~2.7 MB per active day, ~1 GB per year at this intensity); status 5.4 s, next 2.2 s with six lanes polling. T-performance-scale only measures, and is scheduled after all feature work; the operator feels this today. Temporal's lesson (R-gaps-survey): history replay is only viable with bounded history per execution, i.e. checkpoints.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: infra.EventLog and its read snapshot, infra.LocalStore (D-unify), the upcaster/version mechanism (D-upgrade-event-kinds) for any new event shape or blob reference, doctor for the new notes, config_sections/log.py for knobs. Any change to what is written needs an upcaster and the skew guard (D-upgrade-skew-guard); old logs must still fold identically.
HOW TO TEST: replay-equivalence: fold of the old log == fold of the coalesced/blob log for status, next, board, lease expiry, on this repository's real log copied into a tmp dir; a size/time ratchet test on a generated 10x log (cap runtime, no sleeps); blob tamper detected by doctor; two-clone merge test with coalesced renewals; failing-first for each.
SIZE: large (3-5 days of lane time, ~600-900 lines plus tests). Hot files: ddflow/infra/log.py, ddflow/services/leases.py -- expect to wait for B-hy-commit-events.
ACCEPTANCE: measured before/after table in a research record; lease.renewed share under 10% of events on the generated workload; `ddflow status` under 2 s on this log; byte-identical fold output on this log; old ddflow refuses or reads the new log per the skew guard; README/ARCHITECTURE updated.
data.title: Log scale: measure, coalesce lease renewals, move gate evidence out of line, checkpoint the fold (status 5.4 s at 35 MB)

data.body:
WHAT: a lane ledger and advisor: `ddflow lanes` (CLI + MCP ddflow_lanes, one declaration) shows each agent lane -- name, harness, model, current item, last heartbeat, state (working, waiting-on-glob naming the blocking lane, waiting-on-dep, idle-with-ready-work, stopped: context exhausted / quota / crash / done, stale) and how long; `--watch` is a plain-text refresh built on ddflow wait, no new dependency. `ddflow lanes brief <lane>` renders the restart/lane brief (objective, assigned phase/tags, last handoff and see-also pointers when B-am-handoff/B-am-restart-brief exist, open lease and worktree, what the lane was told not to do) so the coordinator stops hand-writing briefs; `ddflow lanes advise` lists concrete moves: lanes idle while ready work exists but is blocked by named globs (name the holder), a lane that stopped on context exhaustion with an unfinished item (print the exact spawn line from the harness descriptor), more lanes than the adaptive limit. It NEVER spawns or kills a process and starts no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon, D-trigger-actions-create-items); it prints the line the operator or a Routine runs.
WHY: this session's coordinator briefs were written by hand per lane; lanes stopped on context exhaustion and were noticed late; memory M801fd9dc2b records 'do not restart a lane that stops idle'; waiting lanes polled (962 gate.out_of_order, 24k lease heartbeats are the log's trace of lanes). Claude Code agent teams (R-gaps-survey) have idle/failed teammate notifications and a panel but no resume and a 'task status can lag' limitation; Claude Squad / Conductor / Emdash are UIs over the same idea and are being sunset or absorbed (Vibe Kanban, Crystal). The state is already in ddflow's log: it is a projection, not new storage.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: fold over existing session.*, lease.*, item.*, worktree.* events (add at most one lane.declared event for intent, via the registry in core/events.py with an upcaster); schedule.plan for 'what could this lane take'; P-harness-adapters descriptors for spawn lines (until they land, read-only ledger and brief only); B-af-headroom for the idle/ready numbers; fenced provenance for any text from a lane (B-lean-and-trusted).
HOW TO TEST: fixtures from a recorded multi-lane log (golden table output); property test: ledger state is a pure function of the log; a lane with no heartbeat for lease.ttl is stale, not working; advise names the correct blocker for a glob stall built from two overlapping tasks; no subprocess is spawned (monkeypatch proc to fail); CLI/MCP parity test passes.
SIZE: medium-large (~700 lines + tests). Touches the shared registration files, so it is first in the chain with B-gap-plan-lint, B-gap-metrics, B-gap-spend.
ACCEPTANCE: on this repository's current log `ddflow lanes` lists the real lanes with correct states; `lanes brief` output is accepted by an agent as its whole first prompt in a dry run; README section and help topic; no daemon, no spawn.
data.title: Lane ledger and advisor: ddflow lanes (state, brief, advise, watch) instead of hand-written coordinator briefs; no daemon, no spawn

data.body:
WHAT: mechanical plan checking, not LLM decomposition. `ddflow plan check <file|->` takes a proposed set of phases/tasks (TOML or JSON: id, title, needs, globs, body, acceptance) and reports, before anything is filed: (1) a `*` in a directory position or a glob that matches more than N files (L-glob-overlap-is-conservative); (2) cycles and dependencies on unknown ids; (3) tasks that can run together (no dependency path between them) whose globs overlap, with the exact pair and the glob that collides, and the waves the plan would give (B-dag-waves-fanout's schedule.waves when present); (4) tasks missing acceptance, test plan or size; a task whose globs span more than K top-level directories (candidate for split); (5) duplicates against the existing queue through the add-time similar check. `ddflow plan apply` files a checked plan with one command and one transaction. The same check runs as a warning at `task add` and `phase add` so hand-filed tasks get it too. Optional flag `plan review` records a plan-review round with the existing cross-family reviewers (kind 'plan'), prompt template overridable, findings go through review triage like any review. Glob suggestion: given a title/body, list literal globs from past completed tasks whose merged files co-changed with the same words (read-only advice from worktree.merged records).
WHY: the glob-overlap stalls this session came from wildcard globs filed by hand; the coordinator hand-writes dozens of tasks per phase. Task Master, Spec Kit (analyze), OpenSpec (validate) and Backlog.md (spec-review and plan-review checkpoints) all gate on plan quality before code; ddflow has gates for code and none for the plan. Decomposition itself stays with the agent: it is a prompt-quality problem, and the harness models are better placed.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core.graph and core.schedule for cycles, waves and overlap (the same overlap test claim uses), services/similar for duplicates, Command declaration + api for CLI/MCP parity, services/review for the plan-review round, services/importer parsers for TOML/JSON plan input.
HOW TO TEST: table of bad plans each failing exactly one check (failing-first); a plan that passes check also passes real claim overlap decisions (cross-check against core.schedule on random plans); apply is atomic (kill mid-way, nothing half-filed); warning at task add does not change exit code.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests). Needs B-gap-lanes first only for the shared registration files.
ACCEPTANCE: the 11 tasks filed for P-gaps pass `plan check` with zero findings; a wildcard-directory glob in a throwaway plan is reported with the colliding pair; README and driver doc say 'run plan check before filing a phase'.
data.title: Plan check before filing: ddflow plan check/apply (literal globs, cycles, disjoint parallel tasks, acceptance present), warning at task add, optional plan-review round

data.body:
WHAT: one log-derived metrics service and three views. `ddflow metrics [--phase P] [--since D]`: cycle time per item (started->completed), time per gate, review rounds per item, gate failure/skip/unavailable rates by gate and by reviewer, queue wait (ready->claimed), lease wait on glob conflicts, rework (completed items later hit by a bug), lane utilisation (working vs idle-with-ready). `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`: critical-path ETA and a P50/P90 range for a phase from measured per-kind cycle times and the dependency graph (simple bootstrap over observed durations; says 'not enough data' under a minimum sample; marked an estimate). `ddflow retro <id>`: the timeline of one item (claim, first gate, each review round, waits, merge) with the biggest gap named -- the answer to 'why was this task slow'. A skip audit: `gate skip` rate per gate with reasons, skips never followed by a later pass, skips by agent.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence from this log: median item 1.04 h, p90 2.8 h, max 31.8 h (n=667); rubber_duck and critic fail 860/849 times against 639/618 passes (every findings round is a failed event), so review rounds dominate wall time but nobody has the number per item; docs gate skipped 149 times against 25 passes (a gate the process routes around, B-docs-stage is the fix, the audit would have shown it earlier); 508 bugs against 850 completions. Three open tasks each plan their own replay: B-rm-changes (throughput ETA hint), B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics. Without a shared service that is three half-metrics. Langfuse/Inspect (R-gaps-survey) show the value of per-run traces and scores; ddflow's log already is the trace.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: the fold and the existing replay helpers in views/ and core/flowsignals.py; Command + Param declarations; core.graph critical_path; knowledge of clock.now (B-arch-clock-now) so tests are deterministic.
HOW TO TEST: golden output on a frozen mini-log fixture; forecast on a synthetic log with known durations lands inside the stated range in a seeded 1000-run test; retro names the injected slow gap; sparse data returns exit 2 'not enough data', never a number.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines + tests). Re-pointing B-rm-changes / B-af-headroom / B-sub-metrics is a decision for B-gap-decide (c), not part of this task.
ACCEPTANCE: the three commands work on CLI and MCP on this log; the figures above are reproduced within rounding; README + help topic; B-gap-decide (c) answered.
data.title: One log-derived metrics service: ddflow metrics, forecast (critical-path ETA range) and retro <id> (why was it slow), plus a gate-skip audit

data.body:
WHAT: a usage ledger per lane and per item: tokens in/out/cache and, where the agent exposes it, cost estimate, recorded as usage.recorded events from harness transcripts (via the B-am-ingest reader) and statusline/OTel snapshots (via B-quota-meters readers); `ddflow usage [--by lane|item|phase|model]`; an optional per-item budget ([budget].max_tokens / max_usd on a task) that turns into a gate-status warning at 80% and a claim-time refusal when exceeded, and a 'cost per merged item' figure for B-gap-metrics. Unreadable usage is UNAVAILABLE, never zero.
WHY: 857.9 agent-hours (status) with six lanes and cross-family review rounds and no number for what a phase cost; B-quota-* meters the vendor window (percent) per agent, not per task. Claude Code reports cost locally from token counts at list price (/usage, --max-budget-usd, OTel), agent teams cost ~7x tokens in plan mode (R-gaps-survey, costs doc); OpenHands has max_budget_per_task; Langfuse tracks cost per trace. Subscription plans have no dollars: tokens and turns are the honest unit.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: B-am-ingest turn store (token fields), B-quota-meters reader registry, B-quota-pause for enforcement (do not build a second pause path), events registry with upcaster, redaction (no prompt text in usage events).
HOW TO TEST: fixture transcripts per harness with known token sums; unreadable file gives UNAVAILABLE; budget refusal is failing-first; no secret/prompt text in the event.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines). Needs B-am-ingest and B-quota-meters; do not start before they land. Evidence is thin for harnesses other than Claude Code (transcript token fields unverified): the first step is a probe record per harness.
ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow usage --by phase` on a throwaway multi-agent project matches the harness's own totals within 5% for the harnesses probed; others report UNAVAILABLE with the reason.
data.title: Usage ledger per lane and item from harness transcripts, ddflow usage, optional per-item token/spend budget (UNAVAILABLE not zero)

data.body:
WHAT: seeded, dependency-free model-based tests of the kernel. (1) Generate random valid event streams (claims, renewals, gates, completions, abandons, removals, upcasted old shapes) over N shards; assert: fold is deterministic; merging shards in any order gives the same State (the sort key is (lamport, agent, id)); fold(prefix) then incremental apply equals fold(whole); replay of the same log twice is identical; every upcaster round-trips on stored sample events from every schema version. (2) A lease state-machine model (acquire/renew/expire/reclaim/resolve/release) checked against the real fold on random interleavings, including clock skew within bounds and a decreasing shard. (3) An invariant list asserted after every random step: no two live leases on overlapping globs, no completed item with an unsatisfied gate, no passed gate without evidence, unavailable never counted as passed. (4) A fuzz corpus for the JSONL reader: truncated last line, glued lines, unknown kind, huge field, NUL, non-UTF-8, duplicate id -- must be reported by doctor, never crash fold.
WHY: the log is the single source of truth, so a fold bug is a project-wide bug and the lessons show repeated lease/identity bugs (B0cb404c94e heartbeat revives a lapsed lease, B190/B205 identity clock, D-resolve-fresh-window). Existing coverage is example-based; B-res-chaos-tests kills processes, B-par-equivalence-tests compares parallel to serial; neither tests the fold algebra itself. Temporal's guarantee is deterministic replay; ddflow claims the same and should test it as a property.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core.events/core.model fold entry points, tests/helpers.py (B-uc-tests-helpers), the existing schema-version fixtures. No hypothesis dependency: seeded random.Random with the seed printed on failure, so a failure replays.
HOW TO TEST: this is the test; prove it can fail by mutating the fold (swap sort key, drop an upcaster) in a mutation probe and recording the failing run.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines of tests, no production code unless it finds a bug; each bug found goes through the bug workflow).
ACCEPTANCE: runs in under 60 s under -n 16; seed reproduces; mutation probe fails the suite; any real bug filed with its own regression test.
data.title: Model-based and property tests of the fold, shard merge order, upcasters and the lease state machine, plus a JSONL reader fuzz corpus

data.body:
WHAT: disaster recovery for the log, small. (1) doctor notes: event shards committed but unpushed for more than [log].unpushed_warn_h, uncommitted shards (B-hy-commit-events covers committing), no remote configured, a shard with a lamport regression or a content-address mismatch (tamper-evidence already detects; make it a named note with the repair). (2) `ddflow doctor --restore-drill` clones the repository to a temp directory, runs replay and status there and compares decisions, lessons, research, open items with the live fold; exit 1 on a difference. (3) Document the offline backup recipe (git bundle of the log directory plus the blobs of B-gap-log-scale) in README; no new command.
WHY: the whole project memory is one directory of JSONL; a push is gated on the operator's say-so ('no push unless asked'), so the only off-machine copy is as old as the last push. Upgrade backups exist (services/backups.py) but cover upgrade snapshots, not log DR. The claim 'delete everything but the log and replay rebuilds it' is documented and tested in pieces, never drilled end to end.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/doctor checks, infra/git helpers, ddflow replay, B-hy-commit-events (needs to land first).
HOW TO TEST: a temp repo with an unpushed shard triggers the note; a corrupted event id triggers the mismatch note; the drill passes on a clean repo and fails when a shard is deleted before the clone.
SIZE: small (~250 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: doctor and drill on this repository report real state; README recipe verified by running it.
data.title: Log disaster recovery: doctor notes for unpushed or unverifiable shards and a restore drill

data.body:
WHAT: make `ddflow tests` (services/testselect.py: today it selects by name and governs only) a real affected-test selector: add the reverse import closure over the package (changed module -> every module that imports it, transitively, -> the tests that import any of them), a conservative fallback to the full suite when a changed file is not Python/unknown or the closure exceeds a size, and a --why column. Use it in the unit_tests gate as an optional first stage ([gates].unit_tests.fast = affected) so an agent gets a failing signal in seconds, while the full suite still runs once at batch integration (B-batch-integration) and in CI parity (D-ci-parity). The fast stage records which tests it chose and the full run is never skipped silently: a gate satisfied by the subset records partial, not passed.
WHY: the full suite is ~11k tests, 24 min serial / ~48 s at -n 48 (memory run-tests-in-parallel) and the MCP unit_tests gate times out; flaky failures appear under load. Nx affected (git diff -> project graph -> reverse closure) and Bazel/Launchable (R-gaps-survey) do exactly this; ML selection is not needed, a conservative graph is enough and explainable.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/testselect.py, ast-based import scan already used by the layering guard (tests/test_layering), gates defs, B-gate-when-globs.
HOW TO TEST: a fixture package: change a leaf module and assert the exact selected tests; change a file the graph cannot map and assert full-suite fallback; selecting a subset yields gate outcome partial; a missed dependency (dynamic import) test documents the fallback; compare against a full run on 20 historical commits from this repo: every test that failed in the full run is in the selection (recall 100% or the fallback fired).
SIZE: medium (~400 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: recall check above passes; median selected set under 15% of the suite on this repo's last 100 merges; README and driver text say the subset is a first stage only.
data.title: Affected-test selection: reverse import closure for ddflow tests, fast first stage at the unit gate (partial, never passed), full suite stays at integration

WHAT: RESEARCH FIRST (verify before building -- unverified hypothesis). Gate commands, hooks and companions come from committed config (.ddflow/gates.toml, config.toml). If a branch or a cloned repository changes a gate command, `ddflow gate run` on a machine that merges or checks it out executes it with the operator's rights; there is no approval-by-digest for a changed command (D-reviewer-trust covers reviewers, B-sub-trust covers agent files, B-org-trust covers org sources, none covers gate commands; grep for approv/trust in services/gates/defs.py and api/gates.py found nothing relevant). Step 1: a research record that reproduces or refutes it (a tmp clone whose gates.toml runs `touch marker`; does `gate run`, `merge`, `ci run` or a hook execute it unprompted?). Step 2 only if confirmed: record a digest of each gate/hook command at operator approval (events), refuse to run a command whose digest differs, show the diff, allow `--trust` by the operator only (never by an agent, same rule as reviewers), and extend the same to prompt-injected task text that edits config (task bodies are already fenced as data).
WHY: Copilot cloud agent runs behind a firewall and OpenHands/Inspect run code in sandboxes (R-gaps-survey); ddflow runs unsandboxed commands from repository text. Irrelevant for a solo operator on their own repo, relevant the day ddflow runs in CI on contributors' PRs or an agent is pointed at a foreign repository.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: the approval-by-digest pattern of B-sub-trust and D-reviewer-trust, configwrite's operator-only paths, events registry.
HOW TO TEST: failing-first reproduction in step 1; step 2: changed command refused, unchanged runs, agent cannot trust, digest survives upgrade.
SIZE: small for the research, medium if built.
ACCEPTANCE: research record with a verdict; if CONFIRMED, the refusal behaviour above and a doc note in the security model.

Operator request 2026-10-10 (verbatim): "Make a research for this ddflow tool and similar tools or workflows and your honest opinion having in mind the roadmap and your research what other features this workflow and queue tool might need to have or would be great to have, or is missing, and could you create a phase and tasks to implement the gaps?"

Evidence: research records R-gaps-evidence (CONFIRMED, measured on this repo's log) and R-gaps-survey (THEORETICAL, 21 pages fetched, the rest summarised).

ASK THE OPERATOR which of the tasks in P-gaps to build, in what order, and whether to build them at all; nothing in P-gaps starts before this task is answered. Recommended order and defaults (accept, reorder, or drop each):
1. B-gap-log-scale (MUST) -- the log is 46% lease.renewed events and `ddflow status` takes 5.4 s at 35 MB after 13 active days (~1 GB/year at this rate). Default: yes, first, measure then coalesce renewals and move gate evidence out of line.
2. B-gap-lanes (MUST) -- lane ledger and restart briefs replacing hand-written coordinator briefs; ledger + advisor only, no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon). Default: yes.
3. B-gap-plan-lint (MUST) -- mechanical plan check at task/phase add (literal globs, cycles, disjointness, acceptance present) and an optional plan-review step. Default: yes, lint now, plan-review as a flag.
4. B-gap-metrics (GREAT) -- one log-derived metrics service behind `ddflow metrics`, `ddflow forecast`, `ddflow retro <id>`; B-rm-changes ETA hint, B-af-headroom and B-sub-metrics should consume it instead of each writing their own replay. Default: yes after 1-3.
5. B-gap-affected-tests (GREAT) -- import-graph reverse closure for `ddflow tests`, fast subset at the unit gate, full suite at batch integration. Default: yes.
6. B-gap-fold-properties (GREAT) -- seeded model-based and property tests of fold, shard merge order, leases. Default: yes, no new dependency.
7. B-gap-spend (GREAT) -- per-lane/per-item token and spend ledger from harness transcripts plus per-item budgets. Default: yes, but only after B-am-ingest and B-quota-meters land; tokens not dollars on subscription plans.
8. B-gap-log-backup (GREAT, small) -- doctor notes for unpushed event shards and a verify/restore drill. Default: yes.
9. B-gap-command-trust (GREAT, research first) -- trust-on-change for gate commands that arrive via a branch. Default: research only; build when ddflow runs on others' PRs or CI.
10. B-gap-checks-publish (GREAT, late) -- publish gate outcomes as GitHub commit statuses/check-runs so branch protection can require them. Default: defer until a second human or CI uses the repo.
Questions: (a) Is the single operator model still true for the next quarter? If yes, drop 9 and 10. (b) Dollar budgets or token/turn budgets for B-gap-spend? (c) May B-rm-changes, B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics be re-pointed at B-gap-metrics (they are open and unclaimed)? (d) Accept the DO-NOT-BUILD list in the research record R-gaps-survey (web UI/TUI beyond `lanes --watch`, a process-spawning daemon, a merge-queue service, ML test selection, bidirectional Jira/Linear sync, RBAC, LLM-based decomposition inside ddflow, a template marketplace, hosted dashboard)? Record answers as decisions (ddflow decision add --globs) and update the tasks.
Expected size: one question round; the answer file is docs/ddflow/decisions/gap-priorities.md. Acceptance: each of the ten above carries an explicit build / defer / drop and an order; decisions recorded; open tasks updated or removed.

ANSWERED 2026-10-10 by the operator: see D-gap-defaults (accepted). Do not ask again.

From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02; 126 jobs measured): a roborev job takes a median 299 s and p90 963 s, plus queue wait; an agent running 'roborev review --wait' holds its item's lease and file globs throughout (mcp.py was held 40-65 min per task). Design: 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async' enqueues the job (roborev review <sha> without --wait), records the gate PENDING with the roborev job id, and returns at once; 'ddflow gate collect <id> standards' reads the job's STATUS (never the exit code: 'roborev review --wait -q' exits 1 for findings OR any failure) and records passed / failed(with findings) / unavailable (errored, canceled, timed out, no review stored). Merge and complete refuse while the gate is pending ('pending is not passed'). Leases renew while the item has pending jobs. Acceptance: pending is recorded with the job id and returns in < 5 s; a canceled, errored, timed-out or no-review job collects as unavailable, never passed; merge and complete refuse while pending; a regression test fails against the synchronous gate; CLI and MCP parity test. Reference: roborev wait --job N, roborev show --job N (a review stored after a wrapper timeout is still retrievable).

Absorbed 2026-10-10 from B-roborev-wait-by-job (same design, the driver-text half): the implement driver and every per-agent delta say: run 'roborev review <sha>' WITHOUT --wait (or 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async'), then wait by job id ('roborev wait --job N') with ddflow heartbeats at least every 10 min; read the result with 'roborev show --job N' even after a timeout (job 943 ran 27 min and its review was still retrievable); never trust the exit code of 'roborev review --wait -q' (1 = findings OR any failure), read the job status; review only the new tip (range jobs run 2.7x longer than single commits) unless a merge interaction is the point; do not hold file globs longer than the code edit needs. Acceptance: driver and every per-agent delta say so; the help-consistency test passes and every command named exists. WHAT: one log-derived metrics service and three views. `ddflow metrics [--phase P] [--since D]`: cycle time per item (started->completed), time per gate, review rounds per item, gate failure/skip/unavailable rates by gate and by reviewer, queue wait (ready->claimed), lease wait on glob conflicts, rework (completed items later hit by a bug), lane utilisation (working vs idle-with-ready). `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`: critical-path ETA and a P50/P90 range for a phase from measured per-kind cycle times and the dependency graph (simple bootstrap over observed durations; says 'not enough data' under a minimum sample; marked an estimate). `ddflow retro <id>`: the timeline of one item (claim, first gate, each review round, waits, merge) with the biggest gap named -- the answer to 'why was this task slow'. WHAT: mechanical plan checking, not LLM decomposition. `ddflow plan check <file|->` takes a proposed set of phases/tasks (TOML or JSON: id, title, needs, globs, body, acceptance) and reports, before anything is filed: (1) a `*` in a directory position or a glob that matches more than N files (L-glob-overlap-is-conservative); (2) cycles and dependencies on unknown ids; (3) tasks that can run together (no dependency path between them) whose globs overlap, with the exact pair and the glob that collides, and the waves the plan would give (B-dag-waves-fanout's schedule.waves when present); (4) tasks missing acceptance, test plan or size; a task whose globs span more than K top-level directories (candidate for split); (5) duplicates against the existing queue through the add-time similar check. `ddflow plan apply` files a checked plan with one command and one transaction. The same check runs as a warning at `task add` and `phase add` so hand-filed tasks get it too. Optional flag `plan review` records a plan-review round with the existing cross-family reviewers (kind 'plan'), prompt template overridable, findings go through review triage like any review. Glob suggestion: given a title/body, list literal globs from past completed tasks whose merged files co-changed with the same words (read-only advice from worktree.merged records).
WHY: the glob-overlap stalls this session came from wildcard globs filed by hand; the coordinator hand-writes dozens of tasks per phase. Task Master, Spec Kit (analyze), OpenSpec (validate) and Backlog.md (spec-review and plan-review checkpoints) all gate on plan quality before code; ddflow has gates for code and none for the plan. Decomposition itself stays with the agent: it is a prompt-quality problem, and the harness models are better placed.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core.graph and core.schedule for cycles, waves and overlap (the same overlap test claim uses), services/similar for duplicates, Command declaration + api for CLI/MCP parity, services/review for the plan-review round, services/importer parsers for TOML/JSON plan input.
HOW TO TEST: table of bad plans each failing exactly one check (failing-first); a plan that passes check also passes real claim overlap decisions (cross-check against core.schedule on random plans); apply is atomic (kill mid-way, nothing half-filed); warning at task add does not change exit code.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests). Needs B-gap-lanes first only for the shared registration files.
ACCEPTANCE: the 11 tasks filed for P-gaps pass `plan check` with zero findings; a wildcard-directory glob in a throwaway plan is reported with the colliding pair; README and driver doc say 'run plan check before filing a phase'.

Acceptance: a test where recall/search ordering differs with the extra installed vs not; one doctor line per extra. If the operator decides the rerank is not wanted, record that decision and delete core/fuzzy.py and the parameter instead.
(c) Duplicate bodies the cleanup plan named: api/rules.RuleDedupAnswer becomes the api/_dedupe.Answer (RELATIONS-based problem); services/guidance/deffields._iso becomes core.clock.iso_at; surfaces/context._csv calls csv_list. Acceptance: the three definitions are gone, tests unchanged.
(d) Dead code: services/export/query.sorted_by (kept alive only by a docstring mention; fix the docstring and tighten the unreferenced_functions counter to ignore docstring and comment mentions), Command.tool_listing (surfaces/registry.py), slots.Slot.try_hold, FlowSignals.as_signals - delete each with its test, or move it into the one test that uses it.
(e) The 15 remaining private `def _git` copies in tests/ use tests/helpers.git (B-uc-tests-helpers: 91 to 15, target 0).
data.title: Unify leftovers named and left by P-unify and the cleanup: token arithmetic onto core.budget, rapidfuzz rerank and extras doctor lines, duplicate helpers, dead code, tests/_git copies

data.body:
Measured remaining duplication surfaces after the cleanup, ranked, for the next unification pass (nothing here is done; each should be re-measured before it is claimed): (a) 45 hand-written cmd_* handlers still in surfaces/commands/ (of 135 declared commands; 4 tools are still HAND_WRITTEN in surfaces/tools: ddflow_external_sync, ddflow_identify, ddflow_list, ddflow_onboard) -> each family either converts to call+render or is declared a deliberate exception. (b) shell/tool lookup: shutil.which at 18 sites in 9 files (forge, paths, launchers, cmdrunner, operations, companions, adopt, roborev, enforce) with no single resolver. (c) tomllib read directly at 16 sites in 16 files although infra/tomlcfg.py is the declared overlay reader. (d) HTTP: urllib/urlopen in 3 modules (upstream_dedupe, review, install_info; U2 adds release check) with their own timeouts and error mapping, no infra/http.py. (e) sqlite3 imported in 3 modules (infra/store, services/similar, services/enforce) -- two outside infra, the layering says disk belongs to infra. (f) god modules: services/importer.py 3219, enforce.py 2461, api/review.py 1756, services/review.py 1629, flow.py 1587, api/setup.py 1550, adopt.py 1465; complexity D-or-worse is at 58 (guard baselines) and the largest files cluster there. Pick (b)-(e) as ratcheted counters first: they are cheap and the guard framework already exists.

Audit 2026-10-10: this task stays MEASURE-ONLY. The code change of (a) (declare or except the hand-written leaves, move the stderr refusal prints into cliexec, ratchet them) is B-arch-hand-written-leaves; the named leftovers (token arithmetic, rapidfuzz rerank and extras doctor lines, duplicate helpers, dead code, tests/_git copies) are B-arch-unify-leftovers. Do not implement them here.

Two enforcement mechanisms disagree about the layer model. tests/test_layering.py ALLOWED says services and views are PEERS and core may import config (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md follows it). .importlinter contract `layers` says surfaces > api > views > services > infra > config > core, so it flags 9 imports as violations and hides them in tests/guard_baselines/importlinter-layers.toml: 7 core -> config (core.flow, flowparams, flowsignals, globspec, ids, progress, schedule) and 2 services -> views (services.enforce and services.sessions import views.markdown). Plus 9 surfaces -> infra entries (surfaces.context 4, surfaces.mcp 4, surfaces.tools._common -> services.adopt 1) in importlinter-surfaces-through-api/. Decide ONE model: either move config below core in the contract and make views a peer (the allowlist's 9 layer entries vanish), or drive the 9 imports to zero (hand core its knobs; have enforce/sessions receive a renderer). Then make the other check derive from or be dropped in favour of the single one. Evidence: grep of both files; guards pass 558 today because each encodes a different allowlist.

ANSWERED 2026-10-10 by the operator: see D-layer-model-strict (accepted). Do not ask again.

SCOPE 2026-10-10 (reorganisation audit): per D-layer-model-strict this task drives to zero everything the single strict model leaves: (a) the 7 core -> config entries (hand each of core.flow, flowparams, flowsignals, globspec, ids, progress, schedule its knobs as arguments), (b) the 2 services -> views entries (services.enforce and services.sessions receive a renderer), (c) surfaces.tools._common -> services.adopt (move AGENT_TARGETS behind an api function). The 8 surfaces.mcp and surfaces.context entries belong to B-arch-mcp-policy and are NOT done here (it does not touch mcp.py or context.py). Acceptance: tests/guard_baselines/importlinter-layers.toml and importlinter-surfaces-through-api/ddflow.surfaces.tools._common.toml are deleted; lint-imports passes with the strict ranking; tests/test_layering.py derives from .importlinter or is deleted; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states one model and that fsio-home keeps two permanent home entries (fcntl and tempfile, because fsio.scratch_dir and temp_text own tempfile; the cleanup plan's 7 -> 1 is 7 -> 2 by design) and subprocess-home one. enforce.py and core/schedule.py are hot files: claim late.

Three detectors, all enqueue only (never index inline except as below): (a) stat scan of the scope (size, mtime_ns, inode vs files table) throttled to once per scan_interval_s, run at brief, next, claim, search and MCP tool calls; (b) git hooks installed by setup/hooks (opt-in like other hooks) enqueue the paths a commit/merge/checkout changed (git diff --name-only); (c) in the MCP server, a daemon thread: watchfiles if importable (optional, no hard dependency), else polling with exponential backoff when idle; it survives exceptions (logged, restarted with backoff) and never blocks the request loop. A search reads the index as is: when the queue holds paths in its scope the reply says 'index N files behind', and a queried file under small_file_bytes is indexed inline first. [docsearch].watch = auto|poll|off. Tests: each detector with a temp repo, the thread dies and is restarted, a request is not delayed past budget while a large batch drains.

Audit 2026-10-10: also add the [watch] doctor line (D-unify 2: watchfiles installed or not, never silent) and change the pyproject.toml `watch` extra comment from "declared, no module imports it yet (no task)" to name this task.

[docsearch].semantic = off|companion; the companion contract: stdin JSON lines of texts -> stdout vectors (any local model: ollama, llama.cpp, sentence-transformers wrapper), with a timeout. Vectors in docs.db (float32 blobs); cosine in pure Python over the BM25/trigram candidate set, or sqlite-vec if loadable. A model change invalidates all vectors (model id recorded). Embedding runs inside the queue worker's budget. Listed in `ddflow companions` with what it buys and what it would run; never installed without asking. Hybrid fusion weight configurable. Tests with a fake embedder: only changed chunks re-embedded, model change rebuilds, absent companion -> lexical results plus an explicit 'semantic unavailable' note.

Operator 2026-10-10 ('do what you recommend' on the order review): do NOT define a second embedding contract. Reuse the shared embedder (ddflow/services/embed.py, the [rag] section: command/model_dir/timeout_s, strict vector contract, unavailable-not-guessed). [docsearch].semantic = off|on only switches whether docs search asks the shared embedder; vectors per chunk are stored with the model id as designed. The module is docsearch/semantic.py (an adapter), not a new embed.py.

Audit 2026-10-10: state whether the sqlite-vec half of [rag] gets an adapter here (only worth it above N chunks) or the operator removes the unused extra; the shared embedder imports model2vec only. Update the pyproject.toml comment of the rag extra to name this task.

Operator 2026-09-29, from a fact-check of 'works with remote agents': today the MCP server is stdio only (surfaces/mcp.py), so a remote agent needs its own clone and shares state through git. Add `ddflow mcp --http HOST:PORT` implementing MCP streamable HTTP over the same TOOLS registry (no second implementation). Security first: bind [REDACTED:ipv4] by default; refuse a non-loopback bind without a bearer token (token from an env var or a machine-local file, never config); per-connection identity (a remote client must declare it, as ddflow_identify does); one repo per server. The sequential-request assumption behind the unlocked parse cache (infra/log.py _PARSE_CACHE) must hold or be guarded — serialize tool calls per server. Tests: a real HTTP round-trip of initialize/tools/list/tools/call; refusal without a token on 0.0.0.0; two clients get distinct identities.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Needed by B-ac-bot-model: cloud agents that accept only remote MCP servers (Devin, Cursor cloud agents, Copilot with OAuth-less remote servers) need this transport; coordinate its tests with B-ac-mcp-tests.

Audit 2026-10-10: decide and record whether the streamable-HTTP transport is stdlib or uses the optional [mcp-sdk] extra (D-unify 2: official SDK only for the HTTP transport); if stdlib, ask the operator to remove the unused mcp-sdk extra and update its pyproject.toml comment. Add the [mcp-sdk] doctor line either way (see B-arch-unify-leftovers (b)).

Query pipeline: normalise (code-aware split from core/textsim), BM25 over chunks_fts, trigram matches over chunks_tri for misspellings ('confgure' finds 'configure'), reciprocal-rank fusion, boosts for heading-path and document-title hits, optional textsim cosine rerank of the top 50, dedupe adjacent chunks of one section. Modes: ranked (default), --fuzzy-off, --exact, --regex (reusing search.check_regex safety). Filters: --path glob, --type, --section, --limit. `ddflow search` gains source `doc` (on by default) and recall shows top doc hits labelled DOC within its budget. Precision measured on a labelled query set from this repository's docs (recorded as research), with a regression test on that set.

Audit 2026-10-10: name the search source `docs` (plural, like records, sessions, prompts, rules, skills, agents, schedules in ddflow search --source), not `doc`; recall labels the hits DOC.

Operator request 2026-10-10 (verbatim): "Make a research for this ddflow tool and similar tools or workflows and your honest opinion having in mind the roadmap and your research what other features this workflow and queue tool might need to have or would be great to have, or is missing, and could you create a phase and tasks to implement the gaps?"

Evidence: research records R-gaps-evidence (CONFIRMED, measured on this repo's log) and R-gaps-survey (THEORETICAL, 21 pages fetched, the rest summarised).

ASK THE OPERATOR which of the tasks in P-gaps to build, in what order, and whether to build them at all; nothing in P-gaps starts before this task is answered. Recommended order and defaults (accept, reorder, or drop each):
1. B-gap-log-scale (MUST) -- the log is 46% lease.renewed events and `ddflow status` takes 5.4 s at 35 MB after 13 active days (~1 GB/year at this rate). Default: yes, first, measure then coalesce renewals and move gate evidence out of line.
2. B-gap-lanes (MUST) -- lane ledger and restart briefs replacing hand-written coordinator briefs; ledger + advisor only, no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon). Default: yes.
3. B-gap-plan-lint (MUST) -- mechanical plan check at task/phase add (literal globs, cycles, disjointness, acceptance present) and an optional plan-review step. Default: yes, lint now, plan-review as a flag.
4. B-gap-metrics (GREAT) -- one log-derived metrics service behind `ddflow metrics`, `ddflow forecast`, `ddflow retro <id>`; B-rm-changes ETA hint, B-af-headroom and B-sub-metrics should consume it instead of each writing their own replay. Default: yes after 1-3.
5. B-gap-affected-tests (GREAT) -- import-graph reverse closure for `ddflow tests`, fast subset at the unit gate, full suite at batch integration. Default: yes.
6. B-gap-fold-properties (GREAT) -- seeded model-based and property tests of fold, shard merge order, leases. Default: yes, no new dependency.
7. B-gap-spend (GREAT) -- per-lane/per-item token and spend ledger from harness transcripts plus per-item budgets. Default: yes, but only after B-am-ingest and B-quota-meters land; tokens not dollars on subscription plans.
8. B-gap-log-backup (GREAT, small) -- doctor notes for unpushed event shards and a verify/restore drill. Default: yes.
9. B-gap-command-trust (GREAT, research first) -- trust-on-change for gate commands that arrive via a branch. Default: research only; build when ddflow runs on others' PRs or CI.
10. B-gap-checks-publish (GREAT, late) -- publish gate outcomes as GitHub commit statuses/check-runs so branch protection can require them. Default: defer until a second human or CI uses the repo.
Questions: (a) Is the single operator model still true for the next quarter? If yes, drop 9 and 10. (b) Dollar budgets or token/turn budgets for B-gap-spend? (c) May B-rm-changes, B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics be re-pointed at B-gap-metrics (they are open and unclaimed)? (d) Accept the DO-NOT-BUILD list in the research record R-gaps-survey (web UI/TUI beyond `lanes --watch`, a process-spawning daemon, a merge-queue service, ML test selection, bidirectional Jira/Linear sync, RBAC, LLM-based decomposition inside ddflow, a template marketplace, hosted dashboard)? Record answers as decisions (ddflow decision add --globs) and update the tasks.
Expected size: one question round; the answer file is docs/ddflow/decisions/gap-priorities.md. Acceptance: each of the ten above carries an explicit build / defer / drop and an order; decisions recorded; open tasks updated or removed.

ANSWERED 2026-10-10 by the operator: see D-gap-defaults (accepted). Do not ask again.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the operator ACCEPTED the defaults as D-gap-defaults (2026-10-10). Record them in docs/ddflow/decisions/gap-priorities.md (build: log-scale, lanes, plan-lint, metrics, affected-tests, fold-properties, spend, log-backup; defer: command-trust research only, checks-publish; budgets in tokens and turns; do-not-build list accepted; B-rm-changes, B-af-headroom and B-sub-metrics re-pointed at B-gap-metrics, done) and complete this task. Acceptance: that file exists and names D-gap-defaults. (D-gap-defaults names the file as governed, and it did not exist.)

Header records since=; a Changed section lists phases and tasks added, completed, blocked or reprioritised since (Keep a Changelog style); decisions and research that govern each phase by glob overlap; an ETA hint from the median completion throughput, labelled an estimate and off if D-roadmap says so.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the ETA hint calls B-gap-metrics `forecast` (critical-path P50/P90 for the phase) instead of a private median-throughput replay; keep the label 'estimate' and the D-roadmap off switch; when forecast says 'not enough data' (exit 2) print NO ETA, never a number. The Changed section (added / completed / blocked / reprioritised), the `since=` header and the decision and research links by glob overlap stay as written above.

Productise the research probe: for each hour of the last N (default 48) fold the events up to that instant with core.model.fold, run core.schedule.plan, and report live leases, offered ready, cap-held, conflict-blocked, deps-ready candidates and the greedy independent set, plus the top overlapping glob pairs and the files they name. Read-only, bounded (cap the number of folds, and say when it sampled), --json and a plain table, so any project can see what parallelism its own DAG would allow and which files hold it back; the output also tells the operator whether raising max_parallel_max would help ('independent work exceeds the ceiling in 91% of hours').
FAILING FIRST (tests/test_headroom.py): a scripted log with two items sharing a glob -> the pair is counted and the independent set is 1; disjoint globs -> 2; empty log -> exit 2 'nothing to measure'; the hour grid uses the injected clock.
README/doctor/MCP/config: README section; ddflow_status gets no new text; MCP exposure through the existing ddflow_status/history path only if the byte budget allows, else CLI only and stated.

GENERALITY (operator: general feature of ddflow, decision D-adaptive-flow, research R-task-time): shipped defaults in the package; works on upgrade (a config with no new keys, and one with the old explicit max_parallel_tasks = 4 / worktree.max_parallel = 4) and on fresh `ddflow init` with no config change; tests in a throwaway project (no companions, no network, no host signals assumed: use the injected clock and signal source); no reference to this repository's hosts, models, core counts or agent names in code, messages or shipped docs; docs ship in ddflow/templates; works for every agent integration (CLI, MCP, and the agents' command files). Knobs are settable via config (.ddflow/config.toml and the git-ignored .ddflow/local layer), `ddflow config --set`, and MCP ddflow_configure; `config --explain`, README and the help topic list each; tools/list byte budget stays green; use ddflow's own fold/plan, never a reimplementation. Machine-specific values (a measured core count, a calibrated threshold) go to the local layer, never the committed config. Hot-file note: touching config.py / mcp.py / cli.py / lifecycle.py serializes other work; claim late and merge fast.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the hourly fold-and-plan sampler (fold up to instant t, core.schedule.plan, bucket live / offered / cap-held / conflict-blocked / deps-ready, capped number of folds, says when it sampled) is a helper in services/metrics.py built by B-gap-metrics; this task is the `ddflow parallel headroom` view over that helper plus the top glob pairs, the independent-set computation and the max_parallel_max advice. It adds no second replay. The failing-first tests and the GENERALITY block above are unchanged.

Keyed by agent and definition digest so a prompt change shows its effect: gate pass rate, findings confirmed vs refuted, rework rounds, latency (flowsignals), quota cost. ddflow agent stats, and a line per agent in status.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: built as a group-by view over B-gap-metrics (key = agent name + definition digest; B-gap-metrics exposes the dimension). Its own additions stay: findings confirmed vs refuted per agent (review triage) and cost per agent read from B-gap-spend `ddflow usage --by model|lane` (UNAVAILABLE stays UNAVAILABLE, never 0).

WHAT: one log-derived metrics service and three views. `ddflow metrics [--phase P] [--since D]`: cycle time per item (started->completed), time per gate, review rounds per item, gate failure/skip/unavailable rates by gate and by reviewer, queue wait (ready->claimed), lease wait on glob conflicts, rework (completed items later hit by a bug), lane utilisation (working vs idle-with-ready). `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`: critical-path ETA and a P50/P90 range for a phase from measured per-kind cycle times and the dependency graph (simple bootstrap over observed durations; says 'not enough data' under a minimum sample; marked an estimate). `ddflow retro <id>`: the timeline of one item (claim, first gate, each review round, waits, merge) with the biggest gap named -- the answer to 'why was this task slow'. A skip audit: `gate skip` rate per gate with reasons, skips never followed by a later pass, skips by agent.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence from this log: median item 1.04 h, p90 2.8 h, max 31.8 h (n=667); rubber_duck and critic fail 860/849 times against 639/618 passes (every findings round is a failed event), so review rounds dominate wall time but nobody has the number per item; docs gate skipped 149 times against 25 passes (a gate the process routes around, B-docs-stage is the fix, the audit would have shown it earlier); 508 bugs against 850 completions. Three open tasks each plan their own replay: B-rm-changes (throughput ETA hint), B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics. Without a shared service that is three half-metrics. Langfuse/Inspect (R-gaps-survey) show the value of per-run traces and scores; ddflow's log already is the trace.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: the fold and the existing replay helpers in views/ and core/flowsignals.py; Command + Param declarations; core.graph critical_path; knowledge of clock.now (B-arch-clock-now) so tests are deterministic.
HOW TO TEST: golden output on a frozen mini-log fixture; forecast on a synthetic log with known durations lands inside the stated range in a seeded 1000-run test; retro names the injected slow gap; sparse data returns exit 2 'not enough data', never a number.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines + tests). Re-pointing B-rm-changes / B-af-headroom / B-sub-metrics is a decision for B-gap-decide (c), not part of this task.
ACCEPTANCE: the three commands work on CLI and MCP on this log; the figures above are reproduced within rounding; README + help topic; B-gap-decide (c) answered.

Operator 2026-10-10 ('do what you recommend' on the order review): tests inject time (a fake clock argument); do not depend on B-arch-clock-now.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: provide the shared hourly-grid sampler (fold at instant t plus core.schedule.plan, bucketed, capped folds, says when it sampled) as a function in services/metrics.py for B-af-headroom and for lane utilisation, and expose a group-by dimension (gate, reviewer, agent, kind, agent + definition digest) so B-sub-metrics is a view. Reuse core/flowsignals.py latency and failure-rate readers rather than recomputing them. Drop any dependency on clock.now (B-arch-clock-now): tests inject time (operator 2026-10-10).

Read-only, redacted import of a harness transcript into a LOCAL-ONLY searchable turn store, plus a committed transcript POINTER event. The foundation for search/timeline/diff/dump.

WHY (measured): no code reads a transcript except services/compaction.py digest(), which takes only the last turns, drops tool traffic and skips isMeta entries (so it also treats an isCompactSummary entry as operator text). The harness deletes sub-agent transcripts after 30 days; 1.1 GB sits in [REDACTED:path] and none of it is searchable by ddflow.

DESIGN: services/transcripts.py reads a transcript through the descriptor's [transcripts] format (task B-am-harness-probe), yields normalised turns (session, agent/sub-agent id, seq, role: operator|agent|tool_call|tool_result|compact_summary, ts, text, tool name, result digest via core/digest.content_digest). Every text field passes redactor('log') (core/redact.py profiles; invalid pattern raises, as sessions.redact does) and <private> spans are stripped BEFORE anything is stored; tool results keep the digest + first N bytes (config), never the whole output. Storage: infra/localstore.LocalStore (git-ignored .ddflow/local), keyed by (harness, session, seq), idempotent (re-import appends only new turns by offset+hash; a truncated or rewritten source is detected, not silently merged). The committed side is one new event kind session.transcript {harness, path, size, sha256, turns, first_ts, last_ts, agent_id, parent_session} written through core/events.py + core/model.py handler + core/redact.py field list + core/upcasters stamp (first writer in the same change; strict fold). Triggered by hook events (stop/session_end/post_compact), by `ddflow session ingest <path|--session id|--all>`, and by a tick (services/ticks.py) so transcripts are imported before the harness deletes them.

SAFETY: stored text is DATA: it is only ever shown inside the provenance fence (core/provenance.py, trust=agent|imported) - enforced where it is displayed (see the search-source and restart-brief tasks), asserted here by a test that a turn containing 'ignore previous instructions' is stored byte-for-byte but flagged. Failures are reasons, never raises (hook rule).

PIN/TEST: fixtures: real-shape claude jsonl (user/assistant/tool_use/tool_result/isCompactSummary/isSidechain), property: import twice = same store; secret in a tool result never reaches the store (planted AKIA/ghp_/PEM); partial last line; 100 MB transcript streams under a memory bound. EXPECTED SIZE: ~450 lines + tests ~300.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: each normalised turn also carries model and usage {input, output, cache_read, cache_write, message_id, request_id} when the transcript format exposes them (claude: message.usage; dedupe key (message_id, request_id)); a field the format does not expose is null, never 0. This is the ONE transcript token reader: B-gap-spend (which says it reads 'B-am-ingest turn store (token fields)') and B-quota-meters (b)(c) call it. Test: a fixture transcript with known sums; a transcript with no usage gives null. `<private>...</private>` spans are removed by ONE function in core/redact.py next to the Redactor profiles; B-am-capture records, B-am-handoff text and B-am-retention use it and do not re-implement it. Storage: a local sqlite (.ddflow/local/transcripts.db, FTS5, WAL, single writer) built like ddflow/infra/docindex.py (B-ds-index); LocalStore holds only ingest offsets, retention state and the queue (it is a document/queue primitive, not a row store). The index code is ddflow/services/searchcore/indexed.py (search_table), not infra/store/indexed.py.

D-quotas (3), R-usage-quota. Readers: (a) Claude Code vendor windows: [REDACTED:path] cachedUsageUtilization (0-100, fetchedAtMs; stale after stale_after_s or once resets_at passed), a statusline snapshot file written by 'ddflow quota snapshot' (statusline stdin rate_limits.{five_hour,seven_day}.{used_percentage,resets_at}), and stream-json rate_limit_event (utilization 0-1, resetsAt epoch) -- normalise units; (b) Claude transcript tokens ([REDACTED:path] incl. subagents/, dedupe on (message.id, requestId)); (c) kilo.db session/message tokens; (d) session counts from the ddflow log. Samples to [REDACTED:path] Each reading carries source, observed_at, stale flag; a failed reader returns UNAVAILABLE.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (b)(c) token counts read from transcripts use the same parser and (message.id, requestId) dedupe as services/transcripts.py of B-am-ingest once it exists; until then keep the local reader behind one function with that dedupe so B-gap-spend can swap it. No second jsonl parser.

WHAT: a usage ledger per lane and per item: tokens in/out/cache and, where the agent exposes it, cost estimate, recorded as usage.recorded events from harness transcripts (via the B-am-ingest reader) and statusline/OTel snapshots (via B-quota-meters readers); `ddflow usage [--by lane|item|phase|model]`; an optional per-item budget ([budget].max_tokens / max_usd on a task) that turns into a gate-status warning at 80% and a claim-time refusal when exceeded, and a 'cost per merged item' figure for B-gap-metrics. Unreadable usage is UNAVAILABLE, never zero.
WHY: 857.9 agent-hours (status) with six lanes and cross-family review rounds and no number for what a phase cost; B-quota-* meters the vendor window (percent) per agent, not per task. Claude Code reports cost locally from token counts at list price (/usage, --max-budget-usd, OTel), agent teams cost ~7x tokens in plan mode (R-gaps-survey, costs doc); OpenHands has max_budget_per_task; Langfuse tracks cost per trace. Subscription plans have no dollars: tokens and turns are the honest unit.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: B-am-ingest turn store (token fields), B-quota-meters reader registry, B-quota-pause for enforcement (do not build a second pause path), events registry with upcaster, redaction (no prompt text in usage events).
HOW TO TEST: fixture transcripts per harness with known token sums; unreadable file gives UNAVAILABLE; budget refusal is failing-first; no secret/prompt text in the event.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines). Needs B-am-ingest and B-quota-meters; do not start before they land. Evidence is thin for harnesses other than Claude Code (transcript token fields unverified): the first step is a probe record per harness.
ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow usage --by phase` on a throwaway multi-agent project matches the harness's own totals within 5% for the harnesses probed; others report UNAVAILABLE with the reason.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: token usage comes ONLY from the single transcript reader of B-am-ingest (it now carries model and usage); the claim-time budget refusal goes through the quota pause path of B-quota-pause and B-af-claim-limit's refusal shape (exit 3 with remedy); the gate-status warning and the usage.recorded event kind are why the globs above gained api/lifecycle, services/gates and core/events.py.

WHAT: a lane ledger and advisor: `ddflow lanes` (CLI + MCP ddflow_lanes, one declaration) shows each agent lane -- name, harness, model, current item, last heartbeat, state (working, waiting-on-glob naming the blocking lane, waiting-on-dep, idle-with-ready-work, stopped: context exhausted / quota / crash / done, stale) and how long; `--watch` is a plain-text refresh built on ddflow wait, no new dependency. `ddflow lanes brief <lane>` renders the restart/lane brief (objective, assigned phase/tags, last handoff and see-also pointers when B-am-handoff/B-am-restart-brief exist, open lease and worktree, what the lane was told not to do) so the coordinator stops hand-writing briefs; `ddflow lanes advise` lists concrete moves: lanes idle while ready work exists but is blocked by named globs (name the holder), a lane that stopped on context exhaustion with an unfinished item (print the exact spawn line from the harness descriptor), more lanes than the adaptive limit. It NEVER spawns or kills a process and starts no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon, D-trigger-actions-create-items); it prints the line the operator or a Routine runs.

WHAT: seeded, dependency-free model-based tests of the kernel. (1) Generate random valid event streams (claims, renewals, gates, completions, abandons, removals, upcasted old shapes) over N shards; assert: fold is deterministic; merging shards in any order gives the same State (the sort key is (lamport, agent, id)); fold(prefix) then incremental apply equals fold(whole); replay of the same log twice is identical; every upcaster round-trips on stored sample events from every schema version. (2) A lease state-machine model (acquire/renew/expire/reclaim/resolve/release) checked against the real fold on random interleavings, including clock skew within bounds and a decreasing shard. (3) An invariant list asserted after every random step: no two live leases on overlapping globs, no completed item with an unsatisfied gate, no passed gate without evidence, unavailable never counted as passed. (4) A fuzz corpus for the JSONL reader: truncated last line, glued lines, unknown kind, huge field, NUL, non-UTF-8, duplicate id -- must be reported by doctor, never crash fold.
WHY: the log is the single source of truth, so a fold bug is a project-wide bug and the lessons show repeated lease/identity bugs (B0cb404c94e heartbeat revives a lapsed lease, B190/B205 identity clock, D-resolve-fresh-window). Existing coverage is example-based; B-res-chaos-tests kills processes, B-par-equivalence-tests compares parallel to serial; neither tests the fold algebra itself. Temporal's guarantee is deterministic replay; ddflow claims the same and should test it as a property.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core.events/core.model fold entry points, tests/helpers.py (B-uc-tests-helpers), the existing schema-version fixtures. No hypothesis dependency: seeded random.Random with the seed printed on failure, so a failure replays.
HOW TO TEST: this is the test; prove it can fail by mutating the fold (swap sort key, drop an upcaster) in a mutation probe and recording the failing run.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines of tests, no production code unless it finds a bug; each bug found goes through the bug workflow).
ACCEPTANCE: runs in under 60 s under -n 16; seed reproduces; mutation probe fails the suite; any real bug filed with its own regression test.

UserPromptSubmit already records prompts; classify by configurable patterns ([research].trigger_patterns: research, investigate, compare, find out, deep dive) and inject a short instruction to follow the research workflow and open a research item; a shipped /research slash command and MCP prompt do the same explicitly. The classification is recorded so a miss can be corrected.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: register the prompt handler in the one hook table (B-uni-hooks); no separate installer.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces B-rw-revise's own events: uses the def-record revise/supersede/retire/merge paths (B-uni-def-records, B-uni-record-surface), with a mandatory reason, who/model family, and the source or probe that justifies the change. Revise = same claim, rev+1; supersede = the world or source changed (valid_until + superseded_by, Graphiti-style invalidate-not-delete); merge records same_as. On revise/supersede/retire: list every anchor pinned to the old revision (they become 'outdated'), open one re-verification task per anchor group or block items touching them; the reviewer clears the pin with `ddflow research pin <claim> --code <anchor>` (Doorstop suspect-link clearing). A claim that becomes REFUTED (by probe, failing vector or a verifier) files a bug per anchored code site naming the claim; the refuting vector is the natural regression test. Evidence of every correction stays in the log.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: also covers the requirements of B-rw-revise (superseded in design by this task): `research show` prints the revision history (revisions, valid_until, superseded_by, the reason and who); the silent same-id overwrite stays a bug (fix-B14d796e03b), not a feature.

Filed by the 2026-10-10 reorganisation audit: small requirements that P-unify and the P-unify-cleanup plan promised, the lanes left, and no open task owned. Each is independent; each states its acceptance. Re-measure before claiming.
(a) Token arithmetic: ddflow/views/markdown.py `_approx_tokens` (len // 4, line 451) and the `budget * 4` sites (about lines 1096-1101) move onto core.budget (approx_tokens, chars_for, Budget); delete markdown._approx_tokens and its use at api/lifecycle/brief.py:214. Acceptance: no `// 4` or `* 4` token arithmetic outside core/budget.py; brief goldens and tests/test_context_pack.py unchanged. (B-uni-context-pack.1-budget promised this and .2-pack did not do it.)
(b) The optional rapidfuzz rerank D-unify 2 promised is reachable: pass rerank_by_likeness from the search and recall path (store.search has the parameter, core/rank.py `rerank` is reachable only from tests), difflib fallback; and `ddflow doctor` prints one line per optional extra ([search] rapidfuzz, [watch], [mcp-sdk], [rag] already) - installed or not, never silent, like services/embed.doctor_notes. Acceptance: a test where recall/search ordering differs with the extra installed vs not; one doctor line per extra. If the operator decides the rerank is not wanted, record that decision and delete core/fuzzy.py and the parameter instead.
(c) Duplicate bodies the cleanup plan named: api/rules.RuleDedupAnswer becomes the api/_dedupe.Answer (RELATIONS-based problem); services/guidance/deffields._iso becomes core.clock.iso_at; surfaces/context._csv calls csv_list. Acceptance: the three definitions are gone, tests unchanged.
(d) Dead code: services/export/query.sorted_by (kept alive only by a docstring mention; fix the docstring and tighten the unreferenced_functions counter to ignore docstring and comment mentions), Command.tool_listing (surfaces/registry.py), slots.Slot.try_hold, FlowSignals.as_signals - delete each with its test, or move it into the one test that uses it.
(e) The 15 remaining private `def _git` copies in tests/ use tests/helpers.git (B-uc-tests-helpers: 91 to 15, target 0).

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (f) the last duplicate_code_cluster (cleanup target 0, now 1): the merge output field list ('id, sha, independence, forced, coverage_gaps, note, woke, bugs_closed') repeated in surfaces/declared/lifecycle.py and lifecycle_cli.py; one definition. (g) EventLog with an empty agent either resolves through services.identity or refuses (infra/log.py falls to default_agent_id today; services/enforce.py passes '' for two reads). (h) fsio-home 2 vs target 1 is by design (fcntl and tempfile); recorded in B-arch-layer-contracts' docs sentence, nothing to do here.

A new export document, SECURITY.md (root by default; .github/ or docs/ if that is where one already lives). Managed block between <!-- ddflow:security:start --> and <!-- ddflow:security:end -->: (1) Supported Versions table from the version history: current release line supported; older lines marked deprecated or unsupported by a [security].supported_lines knob, a version carrying an open security bug or an unfixed dependency advisory marked 'vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>'; (2) Known issues: open and fixed bugs tagged security and findings of the security pass, with ids and the fixing version, never exploit detail for an unfixed one without the operator's say-so (a [security].disclose knob, default ids and severity only); (3) a reporting section is seeded ONCE with a clearly marked TODO for the operator (contact, private vulnerability reporting link, response time): ddflow never invents a contact. Text outside the markers is never touched; a file with no markers gets the block appended after the operator confirms. Refresh triggers: version cut, security pass completion, dependency upgrade merge, document maintenance (export refresh). Dry-run diff first; drift is reported by doctor like other exported documents.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: B-dt-library (SECURITY doc type) needs this task and renders from its DATA (supported lines, deprecated versions, known issues from security-tagged bugs and the security pass). Build that collection as a plain function returning data, separate from the managed-block writer, so the doc type reuses it and no second collection is written; the managed block stays this task's own output.

Re-filed by the 2026-10-10 reorganisation audit: part of B-uni-record-surface (done) was never delivered. api/records.py declares the RULE RecordKind but nothing generates the real `ddflow rule` group from it (api/records.py says it is wired to nothing until a family moves onto it; its named wire-in site, B-rules-cli, was removed on 2026-10-10 as 'already delivered', which covered the commands but not this). The original B-uni-record-surface asked that rules (and the knowledge kinds) move onto it and onto def-records, removing about 500 lines; the def-record half is done (B-uni-rules-import).

WHAT: wire api.records.RULE into the real CLI and tool table: `ddflow rule add|edit|list|show|remove|search|sync` and the rules MCP tool are generated from the descriptor, keeping the group word, every flag and every output byte (goldens, tests/test_rules_cli.py, tests/test_rules_surface.py, the tools/list budget). Delete the parallel code: RuleDedupAnswer and _cross_kind in api/rules.py, the hand-written handlers in surfaces/declared/rules.py, rules_manifest where the def view supersedes it. Then either declare lessons, bugs, items and research as RecordKinds, or record a decision that they stay hand-written, naming the duplicated blocks (api/decisions.py:90 vs api/items.py:507; api/knowledge/bugs.py:68 vs research.py:76); decisions are B-dec-manage's, research B-rw-query's, lessons and bugs B199's, so only items and viewers have no owner. Also add the two small things the original rule CLI body asked for and the registry pilot lacks: `rule list --state` (if rules have a state) and an incremental `rule tag add|remove` (today `rule edit --tags` replaces the whole list).
ACCEPTANCE: ddflow/ shrinks by the measured amount (about 500 lines was the estimate), all rule tests unchanged, one MCP tool for rules, the three duplicated definitions gone.
data.title: Move rules (and decide the knowledge kinds) onto the RecordKind surface: generate ddflow rule and its MCP tool from api.records.RULE and delete the parallel code
