data.body:
R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). B-hx-research covers the 14 agents verified in 2026-09; this task adds Grok Build, superagent-ai/grok-cli, and the bots in R-agent-compat (Copilot cloud agent, Claude Code Action, Codex cloud, Jules, Gemini CLI Action, Devin, OpenHands, Cursor cloud agents, Amp, Factory Droid, CodeRabbit/Qodo, Dependabot/Renovate) with the nine facts per agent (instructions, MCP registration and approval step, hooks, commands, skills/subagents, headless flags and exit codes, identity variables, where it runs, auth and cost) and the confidence of each (verified from a primary page, from a run, or unknown). Probe the open facts empirically with a live run where a key exists, otherwise record them unknown: Grok Build hook payload and session id and MCP approval step, Codex cloud custom MCP, Cursor cloud custom stdio MCP, Devin stdio inside its VM, Copilot AGENTS.md support, exit codes of grok, amp and droid. The matrix is data (the descriptor files of B-hx-descriptor), rendered into docs; a test fails when a descriptor lacks a fact's confidence.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: descriptors live in ddflow/harnesses/*.toml (the glob ddflow/templates/harnesses/ never existed). Start from R-hx-grok and the existing R-hx-* records (B-hx-research is done): upgrade THEORETICAL facts only by a measured run, do not re-research what a record holds. Add a tenth fact per agent: transcripts (path template, format, compaction-summary marker, subagent events), filled in the [transcripts] descriptor section defined by B-am-harness-probe, else recorded unknown.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Descriptor for Grok Build: AGENTS.md (root-down) and .grok/rules/ for instructions; MCP in [mcp_servers.ddflow] of .grok/config.toml (project) via the one mcpconfig.register writer, with `grok mcp add` as the documented alternative; hooks as JSON files in .grok/hooks/ for UserPromptSubmit (prompt capture), Stop (the stop protocol), PreToolUse (edit-time research context, B-rw-context) and SessionStart/PreCompact only if the probe confirms them, else the first-call fallback of B-hy-first-call; the project-hook trust step `/hooks-trust` is told to the operator by adopt; identity from the hook payload's session id if present, else worktree-derived identity; skills/subagents under .grok/agents/. `ddflow doctor` runs `grok inspect` when the CLI exists and reports registered MCP/hooks/rules. The community superagent-ai/grok-cli shares [REDACTED:path] told apart by config.toml versus user-settings.json; instructions-only plus stdio MCP, no hooks assumed. Update the xai reviewer preset to a current model (grok-4.7 per the docs page) and keep the xAI family rule. Idempotent adopt, uninstall and upgrade-migration tests with recorded fixtures.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: descriptors are ddflow/harnesses/*.toml. Fill the descriptor's [skills], [subagents] and [commands] tables only; B-skills-sync and B-sub-sync write the files.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Descriptor fields: kind, integration mode and the facts that drive it. Identity: bot authors such as copilot/*, dependabot[bot], renovate[bot], coderabbitai[bot], claude and the Actions runner are recognised, recorded as bot authors, and event-source and review bots are never offered a claim. Generated, previewed and never silently written setup material per bot: Copilot cloud agent (copilot-setup-steps.yml that installs ddflow, the MCP JSON for repo settings with the required tools allowlist and COPILOT_MCP_-prefixed secrets, .github/copilot-instructions.md pointing at AGENTS.md), Claude Code Action workflow (mcp config, --allowedTools including the ddflow tools, the known permission-denied trap), Gemini CLI Action mcpServers input, Jules and Devin and Codex cloud instructions-only (AGENTS.md) with the remote MCP endpoint noted where they accept one. Cloud agents that accept only remote servers require the HTTP transport: depends on B-mcp-http-transport. Honest output when a mode is unsupported: 'instructions-only, MCP unavailable' rather than a broken config.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: descriptors are ddflow/harnesses/*.toml and the schema validator is services/harnessreg.py (the kind/integration fields change what it accepts); bot-author identity recognition touches infra/harness_identity.py or services/identity.py.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Per-agent adapter as data in the descriptor ([test]: detect command, headless command template, env keys, turn cap flag, expected exit codes) for claude -p, codex exec, gemini -p, grok -p (--output-format json), amp -x, droid exec, openhands --headless, copilot, kilo and opencode run. Scenario: throwaway repo -> `ddflow adopt` for that agent -> prompt 'call ddflow_brief, claim the one task, add a file, run the gates you can, complete it' (cheap model, turn cap, spend cap per D-agent-compat) -> assertions only on ddflow: the MCP tool was called (event log), the claim exists under a distinct identity, the item completed or was released honestly, no stray lease, the shard committed. Controls: timeouts, one retry, N=3 with majority, seed/temperature where exposed. Outcomes pass/fail/unavailable (missing CLI, key, rate limit, network) -- unavailable is never pass. Runs through B-uni-cmdrunner (slots, output cap, redaction); results as events (agent.smoke) for the report. Never installs an agent CLI; keys only from the environment or the git-ignored local config.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (1) descriptors are ddflow/harnesses/*.toml; the [test] section changes the validator (services/harnessreg.py), and the agent.smoke event kind needs registering (core/events.py, model, upcasters). (2) CORRECTION of 'never installs an agent CLI': per D-agent-compat (accepted) a missing agent CLI is `unavailable` unless the operator consented for that agent; with consent install into a scratch dir only, never globally; keys only from the environment or git-ignored local config. (3) Also assert what D-agent-compat's 'supported' requires: a session.started exists with the harness name, and a session.prompt was captured or the descriptor's ladder level says 'no native prompt hook, first-call fallback' and the report shows that level; a gap is listed in the compat report, never failed silently. (4) B-hx-guide mentions the [test] section and the tier criteria (B-ac-smoke); that text is delivered HERE by extending docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md, it is not an edge of B-hx-guide (which would break wave order).

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). `ddflow harness record <agent>` runs (or attaches to) a real session and stores each hook payload, the MCP request/response pairs and the files adopt wrote, with the agent's version and the date, passed through the log redaction profile; fixtures are committed per agent and version. B-hx-conformance replays them: normaliser output golden, hook command round trip, idempotent adopt, uninstall restores. A fixture older than N months or for a different major version is flagged in the compatibility report. Grok Build is the first agent recorded.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: ONE fixture directory: B-hx-conformance replays tests/fixtures/harness/<id>/<event>.json, so the recorder writes there, not tests/fixtures/harnesses/. For tier-2 agents that cannot run headless (Cursor IDE, Cline, Devin Desktop, Continue, Antigravity, Aider; D-agent-compat) ship docs/ddflow/agents/checklist/<agent>.md (adopt, MCP approval step, prompt capture, a claim/complete round trip, with version and date); `harness report` shows 'fixture only, checklist dated D' and flags a checklist older than N months. The recorder is `ddflow harness record` in the group B-hx-cli creates.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). `ddflow harness report [--json]` and MCP twin: per agent and bot its tier, each capability's state (verified live on version X on date, fixture only, instructions only, unavailable, failing), the last smoke result and trend, fixture age, and open issues. Exported as COMPAT.md through the export registry (a doc type once P-docs-generic lands). Doctor notes: an agent whose tested version is older than the installed one, a failing capability, a missing key for a tier-1 agent. A failure is filed as a bug against ddflow with the failing payload, or, when the cause is the vendor's, as an upstream report draft through B-upstream-surfaces (sanitised, consent first). The release script prints the report and refuses a release when a tier-1 agent regressed from verified to failing.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: `ddflow harness report` lives in the harness command group and ddflow/api/harness.py that B-hx-cli creates (edge added). The release refusal is in scripts/release.sh. The vendor-cause path files an upstream report draft through B-upstream-surfaces (sanitised, consent first); that old task is held behind the core/docs wave, so until it exists the draft is a plain text file under .ddflow/local and the task says so (no edge, to keep the wave order). MCP: a verb on an existing tool unless the tools/list budget test passes.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). End to end on a throwaway repository with no repository-specific names: adopt for Grok Build (fixtures) -> offline conformance passes -> a live `grok -p` smoke run when XAI_API_KEY and the CLI exist, otherwise reported unavailable -> the report lists the agent as verified or unavailable with the reason -> a second agent runs alongside it. README section 'Supported agents and bots' with the tiers and what 'supported' means, a help topic, and a delta note per agent including Grok Build.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the 'Supported agents and bots' README section extends the table B-hx-guide generates from the descriptors (adding the tier column); it is not a second hand-written list.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). One process per assertion with the inspector CLI (initialize and server/discover, tools/list ordering and schemas, a read-only tool call, an error call, version negotiation) and the conformance scenarios for protocol 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28; JSON on stdout and exit codes as assertions. Node/npx are optional tooling: missing means 'unavailable', never passed; the job runs in ci when present and in the release script. No cost, no credentials.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: when B-mcp-http-transport has landed, add the streamable-HTTP transport to the inspector and conformance runs (loopback only).

Rename/alias windsurf to devin-desktop (.devin/rules, .devin/hooks.json, global MCP), add roo (.roo/mcp.json, .roo/rules, .roo/commands) and amp (amp.mcpServers, .amp/plugins, AGENTS.md), fix opencode's plural dirs (plugins, commands, agents) and Kilo's .kilo-only dirs; delta docs updated.

R-agent-compat (2026-10-08). Add Grok Build (.grok/config.toml, .grok/hooks, .grok/rules, .grok/agents) as an adopt target through B-ac-grok, not by hand.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: also add descriptors for factory-droid (tier 1) and continue (tier 2) from R-agent-compat (D-agent-compat tiers); every fact NOT VERIFIED until B-ac-matrix measures it. Tier 1 needs instructions, MCP registration, hooks if any and the [test] headless command (B-ac-smoke runs `droid exec`).

Create the [memory_history] config section with the operator's answers from B-am-decide, so every later task reads knobs instead of inventing them.

WHY (measured): nothing configurable exists for this: [session] has log_prompts, redact_patterns, redact_extra, brief_max_tokens, compaction_digest_chars (config_sections/session.py:20-70) and [loops] has the queue detectors; there is no knob for what is captured, how much, how long, or whether history is shared across agents.

KNOBS (names provisional until the decision): capture (prompts|briefs|transcripts), committed_max_bytes_per_record, local_max_bytes, local_max_days, tool_result_bytes, share_across_agents, semantic (off|auto), handoff_max_bytes, restart_share (fraction of brief budget). Each with a doc, choices in KNOB_CHOICES and the strictest/most-private value in KNOB_STRICTEST (KNOB_OUTWARD where the value widens who sees data), plain bare keys (D-plain-keys), README knob count updated, `ddflow config --explain` golden updated and shown as the only diff.
INTERFACE (reuse): @declare/knob in config_sections/_docs.py; re-export from ddflow/config.py. PIN/TEST: tests/test_am_config.py: defaults, invalid value refused with the choices, strictest listed, docs present. EXPECTED SIZE: ~80 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: this task OWNS the [memory_history] section (B-am-retention reads its knobs and adds none). Knobs also: loop_reminders (off|warn|block, default warn, block honoured through [loops].on_detect) and strip_private (default on; it widens nothing, so it needs no KNOB_OUTWARD entry, a lower-privacy value would). Separate caps for brief/report (8 KB) and handoff (6 KB) records, per D-agent-memory-defaults.

Retention, size caps, privacy and the doctor/tick that enforce them for everything the memory phase stores.

WHY (measured): the committed log is 35 MB across 53056 events with no pruning; session events are only ~190 KB today, but briefs, reports and handoffs per lane run add up, and a local transcript store would reach hundreds of MB (1.1 GB of harness transcripts already). The harness deletes sub-agent transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays=30. Redaction today = the 'log' profile on prompts/notes; session.redact_patterns defaults cover keys/bearer/PEM only.

DESIGN: [memory_history] section (config_sections, declared knobs with choices/strictest and README counts): capture (prompts|briefs|transcripts), committed_max_bytes_per_record, local_max_bytes, local_max_days, tool_result_bytes, share_across_agents, semantic, loop_reminders. A tick (services/ticks.py, registered, budgeted, local state) imports new transcript data and prunes the local store oldest-first; pruning never deletes handoffs or pointers and writes a session.transcript_pruned event with counts. <private>...</private> spans stripped before storage. `ddflow doctor` lines: store size vs cap, last ingest age, hooks missing (PreCompact/SubagentStop/prompt capture 'not installed' as measured), embedder state. Privacy: local store files 0600 in git-ignored .ddflow/local; `ddflow session forget <id>` removes a session's local turns and records a tombstone (the committed pointer stays, as ddflow memory forget keeps records with a reason). Export uses the 'export' or 'upstream' profile, never raw.

PIN/TEST: cap enforcement with seeded sizes, prune order, tombstone, 0600 mode, doctor goldens, knob docs/count tests. EXPECTED SIZE: ~300 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: reads the knobs defined by B-am-config and adds none (ignore its own DESIGN sentence that creates the [memory_history] section); its code stays tick, prune, forget and the doctor lines. `<private>` stripping is the one function B-am-ingest defines in core/redact.py.

A structured handoff summary, logged as an event, written at lane stop and at PreCompact, enriched from the harness's own compaction summary, and checked by a round-trip test.

WHY (measured): the only compaction record is services/compaction.py: a 2000-char (cfg.session.compaction_digest_chars) tail of the last operator/agent turns BEFORE compaction, a free-text session.note; its docstring says 'no hook receives the summary', but the harness writes the real summary into the transcript as an isCompactSummary entry (verified), which SessionStart(source=compact) can read from transcript_path. Lane end: session.ended carries a one-line free-text summary (U6: 335 bytes) if the lane remembers to call it. Neither is structured, neither is checked, neither says what FAILED. Anthropic's compaction guidance (preserve architectural decisions, unresolved bugs, implementation details; drop redundant tool output) and Factory's probe study (structured, anchored summaries beat free text: 3.70 vs 3.44/3.35; all methods weak on artifact trail 2.19-2.45/5) say the file/command trail needs deterministic help.

SCHEMA (new event kind session.handoff, versioned via core/upcasters, redacted via core/redact, size-capped): goal; state (done/in-progress/blocked); items_held[] (from the fold: leases); decisions[] (ids); open_items[]; files_touched[] (from git diff of the worktree + event globs, NOT model memory); failed_attempts[] {what, why it failed, evidence ref}; commands_failed[] {argv redacted via redact_argv, exit, output digest} (from gate runs and ingested tool results); next_step; pointers {session, transcript, turns range}; produced_by: deterministic|agent|harness-summary. The deterministic skeleton is computed from the log + worktree with no LLM; narrative fields (goal, failed_attempts, next_step) come from the agent via `ddflow session handoff --goal ... --next ...` (CLI+MCP, registry-declared) or from the ingested isCompactSummary text (stored verbatim, labelled harness-summary, size-capped). Triggers: pre_compact (skeleton), SessionStart source=compact (attach the harness summary), lane stop/session end (skeleton + agent fields), a tick for crashed sessions (B-res-session-lifecycle marks them interrupted).

ROUND-TRIP CHECK: `ddflow session handoff --verify <id>`: (a) mechanical: every item id/decision id/file path named exists, every held lease is mentioned, the failed-command digests resolve in the transcript store; (b) probe questions generated from the log ('which items did you hold?', 'which gate failed last and why?', 'what is the next step?') answered from the summary text ALONE by a rule-based extractor; an optional reviewer-model answerer (other model family, recorded 'unavailable' when it cannot run - never passed) scores it. Verdict stored on the event. This is the Factory probe idea at ddflow scale; keep the question set small and deterministic.

PIN/TEST: golden handoff for a seeded two-item session; summary missing a held item fails verify; secret planted in a failed command is redacted; compaction.py record() keeps working when the hook is off; EXPECTED SIZE: ~500 lines + tests ~350.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: B-res-session-lifecycle's in-flight note and B-hy-stop-protocol's pause note (`item.paused --note`) are written as the session.handoff skeleton with produced_by=deterministic, and next_step is taken from the pause note when present: do not write a second note at the same hook. On PreCompact this task only writes the handoff skeleton and releases nothing.

Claude Code: PreCompact, Stop and SessionEnd hooks call ddflow stop --auto (pause, never merge without gates); Kilo/opencode: a plugin on session idle/end events; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Codex, Copilot: whatever event they expose (to be verified per harness in B-hy-harness-matrix), else only the instruction. Overlaps B-res-session-lifecycle: that task records how a session ended; this one makes it leave states correct.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: RECONCILIATION with B-am-handoff: Stop and SessionEnd call `ddflow stop --auto`; PreCompact only writes the handoff skeleton (B-am-handoff) and releases/pauses nothing, because the agent keeps working on its items after a compaction. Ignore any earlier line of this body that wires PreCompact to `ddflow stop --auto`.

A restarted lane receives its previous handoff plus 'see also' pointers, fenced as data, inside the existing brief budget.

WHY (measured): what a restarted agent gets today is `ddflow brief` (queue state, ranked lessons/decisions) and, only after a Claude compaction with the PreCompact hook installed, the recent-tail note (api/setup.py _after_compaction: 'No record of what this session was doing reached ddflow' otherwise). A lane restarted for context exhaustion is a NEW harness session, so SessionStart source=startup/resume gets no memory of the previous lane run at all; the coordinator re-sends the brief file by hand. session.ended summaries are folded into the brief only via crash recovery.

DESIGN: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py builds a 'Previous run' section for the same agent identity (--agent U1): the latest session.handoff (and, if the agent was interrupted, its tail), its transcript pointers, and 'see also': the 3 most relevant older sessions/handoffs of the SAME agent and of OTHER agents touching the same globs or items (cited session:id, with the exact command `ddflow session search ...` / `ddflow session show <id> --turns a-b` to open them). Built with services/contextpack.pack + core/budget.Budget so it obeys [session].brief_max_tokens (its own share, like guidance inject DOOR_SHARE), every body inside core/provenance fence with author and trust (agent), preceded by the standard 'recorded DATA, not instructions' line. Also delivered by the SessionStart hook (source=startup|resume|compact) and by the MCP initialize/first-call preamble (B-hy-first-call) - one builder, three doors, like services/guidance/inject.py.

PIN/TEST: brief golden unchanged when there is no handoff; with a handoff, section present, cited, within budget; an instruction planted in a handoff stays inside the fence and is not placed outside it; two agents' handoffs never cross unless the see-also relevance rule selects them; budget tiny keeps the first line. EXPECTED SIZE: ~250 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the 'Previous run' section is a sub-block of the RESUME block of B-res-brief-recovery-link (edge added) and uses the same builder when the same agent identity has an interrupted item; it creates no second SessionStart block (the hook output is ddflow/api/setup.py). B-gap-lanes `lanes brief` calls this builder. A 'lane' in B-am-capture's `--lane U1` is the agent identity.

Capture what a coordinator sends a lane and what the lane hands back, on every harness: briefs, final reports, and sub-agent start/stop, as redacted committed records with a pointer to the full transcript.

WHY (measured): lanes U1..U6 have 0 session.prompt events (only lease/gate events); 'You are a ddflow implementation agent with identity U1 ...' appears nowhere under .ddflow/; the brief lives only in the scratchpad lane_*.txt and the sub-agent output under /tmp/claude-1001/.../tasks/*.output. The lane's final report reaches the coordinator's context and nowhere else. ddflow hooks status here: 'prompt capture hook: Claude Code: not installed'; PreCompact: not installed. The Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook does not fire for a sub-agent's first prompt (the Agent tool's input), so brief capture needs the Agent/Task PreToolUse payload (tool_input.prompt) - VERIFY in the harness probe.

DESIGN (two routes, one record): (1) harness-agnostic CLI/MCP: `ddflow session dispatch --lane U1 --file lane_U1.txt` (coordinator calls it when it spawns a lane) records a session.prompt with auto=false, source='dispatch:U1', redacted, size-capped (committed cap from D-agent-memory), plus the brief's sha; `ddflow session report --lane U1 --text/--file` records the lane's report as a session.note source='report:U1'. Declared once in the command registry (ddflow/surfaces/declared) so CLI and MCP match. (2) Claude hooks: pre_tool filtered to the Agent/Task tool and subagent_start/subagent_stop replace _on_nothing for those events only (ddflow/api/setup.py), recording the same two records with agent_type/agent_id and, on stop, last_assistant_message and the sub-agent transcript pointer (session.transcript from B-am-ingest). ddflow hooks install --claude installs the new hooks idempotently (ddflow/services/claudehooks.py) and hooks status/doctor report each one by name.

BOUNDARIES: stop/session_end handling belongs to B-res-session-lifecycle and B-hy-stop-hooks (they own those events and share claudehooks.py/sessions.py; the scheduler serialises, do not duplicate their session.ended work, call into it). A hook never blocks or fails (exit 0, reasons to stderr).

PIN/TEST: hooks run goldens for existing events byte-identical; new fixtures for PreToolUse(Agent) and SubagentStop payloads; dispatch twice with the same brief is one record; a brief containing a planted secret is redacted; oversized brief is cut with an explicit '[cut N bytes; full in transcript]' marker; MCP tool list golden gains exactly session_dispatch/session_report. EXPECTED SIZE: ~350 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: claudehooks.py is being turned into ddflow/services/hookwriters/ by B-hx-hook-writers: edit whichever exists. MCP side of session_dispatch and session_report: a verb or kind on an existing tool unless the tools/list budget test passes with a new tool (tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py CORE_BUDGET).

Behaviour-level loop/repeat detection and reminders: the same failing command, the same claim refused repeatedly, the same lesson violated, the same review finding re-raised - and a reminder to the agent, with a pointer to where it happened before.

WHY (measured): core/progress.py has 7 finding kinds - dependency_cycle, duplicate_work, gate_flapping, no_progress, reopened, repeat_claims, repeated_failure - all about the QUEUE and gate outputs (repeated_failure needs the same gate and output digest 3x). `ddflow loops` on this repo prints only gate_flapping and duplicate_work warnings (11 gate_flapping, 4 duplicate_work). Nothing looks at an agent's commands, repeated refused claims/merges (exit 3), a lesson re-violated after being recorded, or a subagent repeating a dead end found earlier. OpenHands' StuckDetector (docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/agent-stuck-detector) uses concrete thresholds: same action+observation 4x, same action+error 3x, monologue 3 messages, ping-pong 6 cycles. Reminders reach agents today through guidance inject at brief/claim/review gates (services/guidance/inject.py), but selection is by file globs/gate/tags, never by 'you already tried this'.

DESIGN: new detectors in core/progress.py (pure, over the log + the B-am-ingest store): repeated_command (same normalised argv signature via core/redact.redact_argv + same result digest, N=3), repeated_refusal (same item+same refusal reason from events, N=3), lesson_recurrence (a lesson's pattern/verify matches again after being recorded: reuse `lesson verify` machinery), reraised_finding (same review finding text digest across rounds), pingpong (two signatures alternating, N=6). Knobs in [loops] (config_sections/loops.py) with choices declared (KNOB_CHOICES / KNOB_STRICTEST), warn by default, on_detect=block honoured. Reminder: a 'Seen before' block built by guidance inject (one more door, same Budget/fence): 'You ran <argv> 3 times with the same result (digest ..); last time it was resolved by <note/commit> in session X; open it with ddflow session show X --turns a-b'. Surface: ddflow loops, doctor, brief, claim (existing) plus ticks for sessions with no ingest hook. The reminder is advice, fenced, never an instruction to bypass a gate.

PIN/TEST: seeded streams for each detector (below-threshold silent, at-threshold fires once, a pass or different digest resets); no false positive on legitimate polling (wait/heartbeat allowlist); existing ddflow loops output byte-identical on the current log; reminder obeys budget. EXPECTED SIZE: ~350 lines + tests ~300.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: whichever of this task and B-rs-guard lands second reuses the signature helper (core/loopsig.py) of the first. The reminder text cites `ddflow session show X`, and adds `--turns a-b` only once B-am-session-cli has landed.

WHAT. Guards: a per-item step cap and char budget (default modest, config), a repeat detector (same normalized text or the same ruled_out target N times in a row -> the add reply says 'you have already recorded this' and, at 2N, suggests `ddflow block` / asking the operator), a global off switch `reasoning.enabled = false` that makes add a quiet no-op returning exit 2 and removes the advice from brief and mcp_instructions.
WHY. Extra tool calls cost tokens and latency; OpenHands' stuck detector (repeated actions 4+, errors 3+, monologue 3+) shows the loop is real; the off switch lets a project that finds no value turn it off.
REUSE. config_sections/ (pattern: config_sections/session.py), core/budget.py, core/textsim.py or services/guidance/similarity.py for near-duplicate text, `ddflow loops` (see how it detects) -- add the reasoning repeat as another signal there rather than a new mechanism.
TEST. Pin the thresholds with fixtures; off switch leaves no events and no brief text.
SIZE ~120 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: add reasoning_repeat as a detector in core/progress.py through the same signature helper B-am-loops uses (core/loopsig.py); the [reasoning] config section is created by B-rs-model (see there), this task adds only the service.

WHAT. The step record: event `reasoning.step` {id, item, gate, kind in question|hypothesis|evidence|ruled_out|decision, text (redacted via core/redact, capped), revises (step id), branch (name), cites (R-/B-/D- ids), agent, ts}, its fold into State, an upcaster entry, and a def-record style digest for promotion. Steps are immutable; a revision is a NEW step pointing at the old; the folded view marks the old one 'revised'. Branches are a name on a step, a branch point is a step id; validated (unlike the external server): revises/branch-from must exist on the same item, kind must be known, text must be non-empty, and a ruled_out step must name what it rules out (its revises/branch target or a hypothesis id).
WHY (gap). The recurring failure R-reasoning-sequential cites: an agent converges on a plausible-wrong cause and never records what it ruled out. Today that lives in free text in a gate --evidence or a session note, unstructured and unsearchable by kind.
REUSE. core/events.py + core/handlers/ (pattern: handlers/sessions.py _h_session_note), core/upcasters.py, core/defs.py, core/redact.py, infra/localstore.py per decision B-rs-decide.2.
TEST. Pin: fold of a revision marks the target; unknown revises refused; redaction applied before write; replay of the event log reproduces the folded state; the upcaster round-trips a v1 event. Regression-style: a ruled_out step with no target is refused.
SIZE. ~250 lines + ~200 lines tests.
ACCEPTANCE. Append hypothesis H1, ruled_out H1 with evidence, a decision citing R-x; rebuild the index from the log; the state shows H1 as ruled out with its evidence.
DOCS. docs/ddflow/REASONING.md section 'record' is written by B-rs-docs; here only docstrings.
COMPANION TRANSITION. None yet.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (1) STORAGE: B-rs-decide Q2 recommended steps in the LOCAL store, uncommitted, promoted as a digest at `gate record`; this body builds a committed `reasoning.step` event folded into State. Do not build until B-rs-decide's answer fixes which; the pin test and the 'rebuild the index from the log' acceptance are written after it. (2) This task creates config_sections/reasoning.py (enabled, max_steps_per_item, max_chars_per_item, reviewer_digest, gate_advice) so B-rs-cmd's 'budget left' and B-rs-gates' switch have a home. (3) Use the redaction profile and the `<private>` function of core/redact.py; do not copy the capture store of P-agent-memory. `cites` accepts claim ids C-xxxx once B-rw-claims exists.

WHAT. `ddflow think add|show|search` and MCP `ddflow_think` (names per B-rs-decide.3), declared once in the command registry with CLI+MCP parity and cliexec, following ddflow/surfaces/declared/memory.py. `add` appends a step and RETURNS the item's current reasoning state (open hypotheses, ruled-out, branches, step count, budget left); `show ITEM` prints it; `--json` for MCP.
WHY (gap). The external tool returns only counters, so the agent gets nothing back for the tool call. Parity matters because ddflow's rule is that every verb is both CLI and MCP.
REUSE. surfaces/registry.py Command/Param, surfaces/declared/*.py, surfaces/commands/, surfaces/parsers/, surfaces/tools/__init__.py, api/ layer.
TEST. The existing registry parity tests pick the new command up; add a cliexec test for add -> show; MCP tools/list contains ddflow_think with the registry description; refuse unknown item/gate with exit 3.
SIZE ~150 lines + tests.
ACCEPTANCE. In a scratch repo: `ddflow think add B1 --kind hypothesis --text ...` then the same through MCP gives the same state.
DOCS. --help text and the MCP description say what a step is and that it is NOT a substitute for the research record.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: MCP side (ddflow_think): an action on an existing tool unless the tools/list budget test passes with a new tool.

WHAT. (a) `gate status` for research and bug_hunt shows the item's reasoning digest (hypotheses still open, ruled_out list) and a one-line advisory when none is recorded; (b) promotion: `gate record <item> bug_hunt|research` folds the digest into the committed gate evidence / links it to a research record's claim, mechanism, falsifier and probe fields (a step of kind hypothesis feeds the claim, evidence the probe output, ruled_out the falsifier history) -- it does NOT create a second research artifact; (c) rubber_duck/critic review prompts may include the digest as fenced, untrusted DATA under the context Budget, behind a config switch default per B-rs-decide.5.
WHY. A cross-family reviewer auditing the reasoning is the one capability the external server cannot offer (its history is invisible outside its process).
REUSE. services/gates/evidence.py, services/gates/kinds.py, services/review.py prompt building, services/contextpack.py + core/budget.py, services/guidance for fencing, core/redact.
TEST. Pin: with no steps, gate status and review prompts are unchanged; digest is fenced and capped; promotion twice is idempotent; a reviewer prompt never contains un-redacted text.
SIZE ~200 lines + tests. ACCEPTANCE: bug_hunt on a fixture item with two ruled-out hypotheses shows both in gate status and in the recorded evidence.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: wording: a hypothesis step feeds the research record's mechanism; ruled_out feeds the falsifier history; evidence feeds probe_output; once B-rw-claims exists a decision step may cite a claim id C-xxxx@N. No edge on P-research (that would put P-reasoning behind it). The switch and caps come from the [reasoning] section created by B-rs-model.

WHAT. A measurement of the claimed value on real ddflow work, so the feature is kept only if it earns its place. Fixed set of >=12 tasks drawn from past closed bugs (those with a known root cause and a regression test) and research items; run each with arms: (A) no reasoning tool, (B) native `ddflow think`, (C) external `sequential`, across at least two models (one with native extended thinking, one without). Metrics: root cause correct (checked against the known fix), number of discarded hypotheses recorded, tool calls, input+output tokens, wall time, reviewer verdict. N is small; report effect sizes and say plainly when the difference is within noise. Output: a research record (verdict CONFIRMED/REFUTED on the claim 'the native log improves root-cause accuracy or review findings per token'), and a recommendation to the operator: keep / keep optional / remove.
WHY. There is no published benchmark for sequentialthinking itself (only the think tool's tau-bench numbers: airline 0.370 -> 0.404, 0.584 with a prompt; retail 0.783 -> 0.812 vs 0.770 for extended thinking; SWE-bench +1.6%), and Anthropic now prefers extended thinking. Our claim must be our own measurement.
REUSE. existing live_test/bisect tooling, `ddflow research`, git history of fixed bugs for ground truth.
SIZE: mostly agent time; harness script ~150 lines. DOCS: results in the research record.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: run the arms through the headless adapter of B-ac-smoke (ddflow/services/agent_smoke.py) and CommandRunner; no second runner (same for B-skills-adherence-eval and B-sub-eval).

WHAT. A SearchSource (name 'reasoning', kinds hypothesis/ruled_out/decision/...) registered with services/searchcore so `ddflow recall`, `think search` and brief find past steps, including ruled-out hypotheses ('we already ruled this out on B-x'). Reasoning rows are ranked below lessons/decisions by default and capped.
WHY. A second scratchpad nobody can search is the main objection to the external server; the whole value of a ruled-out list is that the NEXT agent sees it.
REUSE. services/searchcore/hit.py SearchSource/FuncSource/register, services/search.py (how existing sources register), core/rank.py. Mirror R-U3-search-sources: adding the source must not change existing rows' scores or order.
TEST. Pin: with no reasoning rows every existing recall output is byte-identical; a ruled_out step is found by a query on its text; redacted text is not searchable by its secret.
SIZE ~100 lines + tests. ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow recall "<cause already ruled out>"` returns the step with its item and gate.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: a new SearchSource must not crowd out lessons or decisions in recall's one-per-source round robin; a golden shows the existing recall output is unchanged.

A 'transcripts' SearchSource so `ddflow search`, `ddflow recall` and the MCP search/recall tools find old context of the same or other pipelines, with agent/session/time filters, citations and a token budget.

WHY (measured): `ddflow search --source sessions|prompts` indexes only session notes/summaries and operator prompts (services/search.py:314-318 over _session_docs; research R700403e095 and B194 show even session.ended summaries were once missing). `ddflow search "lane" --source prompts --owner U6` -> 'searched 0 records': lane context is simply absent. recall --sources lists decisions,lessons,memories,research,bugs,items,prompts - no transcripts, no handoffs, no briefs/reports. Ranking is BM25 (searchcore/rank.py); services/embed.rerank reorders candidates only at query time and only when [rag].command or [rag].model_dir is configured, with the BM25 order kept and SAID (embed.py:194); there are no stored vectors.

DESIGN (no second searcher): register FuncSource('transcripts', kinds turn|handoff|brief|report) in searchcore (hit.py register/gather) over the B-am-ingest local store (FTS5 via infra/store/indexed.py search_table patterns), plus session.handoff/dispatch/report records from the log. Filters reuse the existing flags: --owner (agent), --since, --phase, --state, new --session and --role (operator|agent|tool_result|handoff). Ranking: BM25 + recency decay + same-agent boost; semantic rerank through embed.rerank when available (BM25 order and an explicit note when not); fold near-duplicate hits with textsim as contextpack does. Hits are Candidates (contextpack.candidate) with cite 'transcripts:<session>#<seq>' and fenced via core/provenance; recall gains --sources history and the pack's one-per-source round robin so history cannot crowd out lessons/decisions. Progressive disclosure like claude-mem (search -> timeline -> get, ~10x token saving by filtering before fetching): the search hit is an index line (id, role, ts, 160-char snippet); `session show --turns` opens detail.

PIN/TEST: goldens for existing search/recall unchanged; seeded two-agent store: agent filter, since filter, cross-agent hit labelled with its author, budget respected, regex path still guarded (regexsafe), no embed => note says BM25; ranking determinism (ties by id). EXPECTED SIZE: ~300 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: same golden rule as B-rs-search: existing recall output unchanged. The index helper is ddflow/services/searchcore/indexed.py (search_table), not infra/store/indexed.py. Transcripts are reranked at query time through services/embed.py; stored vectors for them only if [memory_history].semantic enables it (B-semantic-recall does not embed transcripts).

Operator 2026-09-29, from a fact-check: the pitch says 'fast search and RAG', but recall and brief are lexical (SQLite FTS5 bm25, infra/store.py); there are no embeddings. Add an OPTIONAL embedding index, derived and rebuildable like index.db and never committed: an [recall] embeddings config naming an OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint (local vLLM/ollama or a configured provider, key via api_key_env only), vectors stored in SQLite next to the FTS tables (no new runtime dependency — brute-force cosine is fine at 100k), hybrid ranking (BM25 + cosine, reciprocal-rank fusion), and brief/recall using it when configured. MERGE with the shared Embedder of B-uni-context-pack (one embedder interface, the [rag] extra, unavailable without it): do not add infra/embed.py. data.claim: Yes: no removed or split item was lost wholesale, but about 9 requirements had no owner and about 20 open task bodies still described building what already shipped or what another task owns; all are now owned or rescoped.

data.body:
WHAT: make `ddflow tests` (services/testselect.py: today it selects by name and governs only) a real affected-test selector: add the reverse import closure over the package (changed module -> every module that imports it, transitively, -> the tests that import any of them), a conservative fallback to the full suite when a changed file is not Python/unknown or the closure exceeds a size, and a --why column. Use it in the unit_tests gate as an optional first stage ([gates].unit_tests.fast = affected) so an agent gets a failing signal in seconds, while the full suite still runs once at batch integration (B-batch-integration) and in CI parity (D-ci-parity). The fast stage records which tests it chose and the full run is never skipped silently: a gate satisfied by the subset records partial, not passed.
WHY: the full suite is ~11k tests, 24 min serial / ~48 s at -n 48 (memory run-tests-in-parallel) and the MCP unit_tests gate times out; flaky failures appear under load. Nx affected (git diff -> project graph -> reverse closure) and Bazel/Launchable (R-gaps-survey) do exactly this; ML selection is not needed, a conservative graph is enough and explainable.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/testselect.py, ast-based import scan already used by the layering guard (tests/test_layering), gates defs, B-gate-when-globs.
HOW TO TEST: a fixture package: change a leaf module and assert the exact selected tests; change a file the graph cannot map and assert full-suite fallback; selecting a subset yields gate outcome partial; a missed dependency (dynamic import) test documents the fallback; compare against a full run on 20 historical commits from this repo: every test that failed in the full run is in the selection (recall 100% or the fallback fired).
SIZE: medium (~400 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: recall check above passes; median selected set under 15% of the suite on this repo's last 100 merges; README and driver text say the subset is a first stage only.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: SCOPE CORRECTION, supersedes the WHAT above where they differ: `ddflow tests --item` and the unit_tests gate ALREADY select by reverse import closure with a reason per test (ddflow/services/testselect.py, B16, MAX_HOPS=2 chosen because an unbounded closure reached 42 of 87 test files; D-gate-economy 1; `[gates].unit_tests_scope` selected|full). Do not rebuild it and do not add ddflow/services/importgraph.py unless you can justify it against testselect._import_reach. This task adds ONLY: (1) a measured recall check of the selection against the full suite on 20 historical commits of this repository (every test that failed in the full run is in the selection, or a fallback fired) with a median-selected-size figure; (2) a conservative full-suite fallback when a changed file is non-Python/unmapped or the selection exceeds a size cap (extend the existing 'no test reaches the change' fallback); (3) the README/driver sentence that the subset is a first stage only. Do NOT introduce a 'partial' gate outcome for a selected run: D-gate-economy (accepted) lets a selected unit_tests gate stand because the ci gate runs the full suite on the merged tree; supersede that decision first if the operator wants the change. B-gate-when-globs is kept as a prerequisite only because the operator's order lists it; this task does not use it.

Operator 2026-10-10: keep D-gate-economy. No 'partial' gate outcome: the rescoped task builds only the import-graph closure for test selection; a gate stays passed or failed.

ASK THE OPERATOR (plain text, then stop) before any other P-reasoning task starts. Evidence: R-reasoning-sequential (the external server returns no thought text, persists nothing, validates nothing; Anthropic's think-tool post since 2025-12-15 recommends native extended thinking over a dedicated think tool in most cases). Each question carries my recommended default; record the answers with `ddflow decision add --globs ...` and update the other tasks' bodies.
1. SCOPE. Default: build a THIN reasoning log whose point is the auditable record of what was RULED OUT, attached to an item and a gate; not a clone of sequentialthinking, not a thinking aid. Alternatives: (a) do not build; only fix the docs (B-rs-companion-honest only); (b) smallest build: add a repeatable `--ruled-out` field to `bug found`, `research add` and `gate record bug_hunt/research` and nothing else; (c) the default.
2. STORAGE. Default: steps live in the LOCAL store (infra/localstore, uncommitted, per worktree) and are PROMOTED into the committed log only as a digest at gate-record time (hypotheses kept, ruled_out list, decision) -- keeps the committed log small and avoids committing raw chain-of-thought. Alternatives: all steps committed as redacted events (full audit, log growth); local only (no audit).
3. TOOL SHAPE. Default: one command `ddflow think` / MCP `ddflow_think` with kinds question|hypothesis|evidence|ruled_out|decision, optional --revises STEP, --branch NAME, --item, --gate, --cites R-id/B-id; it RETURNS the item's current state (open hypotheses, ruled-out list, branches), unlike the original which returns counters. Also `think show|search`. Alternative: reuse `session note` with a --kind flag.
4. GATES. Default: advisory only: bug_hunt/research gate status SHOWS the ruled-out list and warns when none is recorded; no gate is refused for lack of one (a mandatory ritual would produce filler). Alternative: configurable `reasoning.require_ruled_out` on bug_hunt, default off.
5. REVIEWERS. Default: a cross-family reviewer for rubber_duck/critic gets the item's reasoning digest as fenced DATA, capped by the context Budget, off by default until B-rs-eval shows it helps. 
6. COMPANION. Default: keep `sequential` listed but not default-recommended now (default=false, and the text says plainly what it does and does not do); mark superseded only if B-rs-eval is positive; never auto-uninstall.
7. EVALUATION. Default: run B-rs-eval before the optional parts (reviewer feed, gate nudge) are enabled by default.
8. RELATION TO P-agent-memory. Default: steps are item/gate-scoped reasoning; P-agent-memory owns session/transcript capture and handoff. Share its capture store and redaction profile if it defines one first; otherwise this phase defines the step event and P-agent-memory reads it.

ANSWERED 2026-10-10 (storage, question 2): the operator chose ALL reasoning steps COMMITTED AS EVENTS (not the recommended local store plus promoted digest). Consequences to carry into B-rs-model: reasoning.step is a committed event kind with a first writer and upcaster entry; every step passes the 'log' redaction profile and <private> stripping, with hard caps per step and per item (the budget knob) so the committed log cannot balloon (the log grows ~2.7 MB/day already); no separate local step store; gate evidence cites step ids instead of a digest; search indexes the events. Record this as a decision (D-reasoning-steps-committed) when writing the decision doc; the other B-rs-decide questions remain open.

WHAT. The step record: event `reasoning.step` {id, item, gate, kind in question|hypothesis|evidence|ruled_out|decision, text (redacted via core/redact, capped), revises (step id), branch (name), cites (R-/B-/D- ids), agent, ts}, its fold into State, an upcaster entry, and a def-record style digest for promotion. Steps are immutable; a revision is a NEW step pointing at the old; the folded view marks the old one 'revised'. Branches are a name on a step, a branch point is a step id; validated (unlike the external server): revises/branch-from must exist on the same item, kind must be known, text must be non-empty, and a ruled_out step must name what it rules out (its revises/branch target or a hypothesis id).
WHY (gap). The recurring failure R-reasoning-sequential cites: an agent converges on a plausible-wrong cause and never records what it ruled out. Today that lives in free text in a gate --evidence or a session note, unstructured and unsearchable by kind.
REUSE. core/events.py + core/handlers/ (pattern: handlers/sessions.py _h_session_note), core/upcasters.py, core/defs.py, core/redact.py, infra/localstore.py per decision B-rs-decide.2.
TEST. Pin: fold of a revision marks the target; unknown revises refused; redaction applied before write; replay of the event log reproduces the folded state; the upcaster round-trips a v1 event. Regression-style: a ruled_out step with no target is refused.
SIZE. ~250 lines + ~200 lines tests.
ACCEPTANCE. Append hypothesis H1, ruled_out H1 with evidence, a decision citing R-x; rebuild the index from the log; the state shows H1 as ruled out with its evidence.
DOCS. docs/ddflow/REASONING.md section 'record' is written by B-rs-docs; here only docstrings.
COMPANION TRANSITION. None yet.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (1) STORAGE: B-rs-decide Q2 recommended steps in the LOCAL store, uncommitted, promoted as a digest at `gate record`; this body builds a committed `reasoning.step` event folded into State. Do not build until B-rs-decide's answer fixes which; the pin test and the 'rebuild the index from the log' acceptance are written after it. (2) This task creates config_sections/reasoning.py (enabled, max_steps_per_item, max_chars_per_item, reviewer_digest, gate_advice) so B-rs-cmd's 'budget left' and B-rs-gates' switch have a home. (3) Use the redaction profile and the `<private>` function of core/redact.py; do not copy the capture store of P-agent-memory. `cites` accepts claim ids C-xxxx once B-rw-claims exists.

Operator 2026-10-10: steps are committed events (see B-rs-decide). Redact with the 'log' profile, strip <private>, cap per step and per item, register the event kind with its first writer and the upcaster table; do not build a local step store.

data.body:
Operator question 2026-10-11 ("are the decisions, and the questions you ask me recorded ... so the user can review them ... and with multiple developers each with multiple agents in their own clones the data is shared and conflicts minimised?"). Measured answer: decisions ARE events (decision.recorded, merged by id, 'merge never replace') and reach agents through their globs, but (1) the QUESTION and its options are never recorded -- only the coordinator's paraphrase of the answer inside the decision text; the operator's reply in a question dialog (AskUserQuestion) is not captured because no hook records it; (2) a decision is linked to the work it affects only by globs and by decision ids typed into task bodies -- there is no structural decision<->task/phase link, so `ddflow show <task>` does not list the decisions behind it; (3) two clones can independently choose the same human-written decision id; the fold merges fields instead of flagging a conflict.
Build: (a) capture operator Q&A: a PostToolUse (and harness equivalent) hook for the question tool that records question, options offered, chosen answer and free-text notes verbatim (redacted, committed, small) as a session event linked to the session and any item named; (b) `ddflow decision add --from-qa <id>` and a `decided_by_answer` link so each decision cites the Q&A that produced it, and `ddflow show <task|phase>` and `ddflow brief` list the decisions that govern it by explicit link as well as by glob; (c) a conflict rule for same-id decisions from different shards: identical content merges silently, different content records a conflict that `doctor` and `ddflow decision list` show until superseded explicitly (never silently merged); decision ids minted with a short content/author suffix by default so independent clones cannot collide; (d) a two-clone scenario test (two clones, two agents each, same decision id, tasks edited on both sides, merge) that proves the merged log folds identically on both and conflicts are surfaced. Reuse: session events, def-records/upcasters, the record surface, B-am-capture hooks and B-dec-* tasks (dedupe with B-dec-manage and B-am-capture: this task extends them, it is not a parallel store).
data.title: Record operator questions and answers, link decisions to the work they govern, and surface same-id conflicts across clones

data.summary: BROKEN (silent data loss, multi-clone): two clones that each record a decision, lesson or research note under the SAME id (decision add --id D-x, lesson add --id L-x, research add --id R-x) merge cleanly in git and then fold last-writer-wins by (lamport, agent): the loser's content disappears from decision show/list/applicable/brief and lesson search, `ddflow doctor` stays clean and exits 0, and nothing is CONTESTED (B191 contests only item.added and claims). The decision handler also merges FIELDS (empty field keeps the previous value), so the surviving D-m is bob's decision text with alice's Context and Consequences: a record neither author wrote. Contradictory decisions are the ones that GOVERN code, so an agent is told the wrong rule with no warning. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s2b.py (same-id decision/lesson/research, transcript /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s2b.transcript.txt) and /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s3b.py (field mix). Observed: both clones print identical state with only one version; history shows two DECISION events. Severity: high. Failing-first regression test must assert: after two clones add the same decision id with different content and merge, (1) decision show prints a CONTESTED block listing both definitions with agents, (2) doctor exits 1 with a PROBLEM naming the id, (3) decision applicable and brief withhold or flag it, (4) no field of one definition appears on the other; same for lesson and research ids; identical re-adds (same digest) are not a contest; `ddflow resolve <id> --keep <event-id|agent>` settles it. Reuse core/handlers/items.py contest logic and P-unify def records (core/defs.py).

data.summary: BROKEN (wrong shared state, multi-clone): an identity that two clones share is trusted as one agent. `--agent X`, `ddflow_identify` names, DDFLOW_AGENT and a committed [agent].id are used verbatim (no per-clone suffix; only the DERIVED id has one, B190). Two users who both run an agent called U1 (or opus-lead) write the same shard .ddflow/events/U1.jsonl; git merge=union concatenates them (18 lines, lamport 6..14 twice), both claim T1 and both rc=0, and the fold sees ONE holder: no CONTESTED, `status` shows T1 in flight by U1, `doctor` exits 0 (only a NOTE that the Lamport clock decreases). Two worktrees do the same work and nothing says so. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s4.py (transcript /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s4.transcript.txt, section 4a); the operator's own convention `--agent opus-lead` on every write is exactly this. Severity: high. Failing-first regression test: two clones, same --agent name, both claim one item offline, pull each other: assert the item is CONTESTED (or the second claim is refused/flagged because the claim event carries a clone id), `doctor` exits 1 with a PROBLEM (not a NOTE) when one shard has two Lamport runs, and the note says how to give each clone its own id. Interface: log.py default_agent_id/clone suffix, leases claim event data, core/handlers/leases.py contest keyed by (holder, clone).
