data.summary: DEGRADED (claim contest is invisible where agents look): after two offline clones claim one task (B191 contested), only `show` and `doctor` (exit 1) say so. `status` shows "In flight: T1 - U2" in BOTH clones, so alice's own claim vanishes from her view; `next` just omits T1; `brief` and `heartbeat` ("no lease held") say nothing. `merge T1` SUCCEEDED for the claim that lost (rc 0, "merged T1 into main") while contested. After `resolve --keep U1` and a pull, bob's doctor is Healthy, `show` says U1 holds it, and bob's own branch ddflow/T1 with a unmerged commit is reported by `cleanup` as "LEAVE ALONE - held by U1" (it is his own branch). Nobody tells bob his claim was released. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s1.py (transcript /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s1.transcript.txt); the opt-in [flow].claims=remote path works (/tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s1b.py). Severity: medium. Regression test: contested item appears in status and brief with the resolve command; merge/complete refuse a contested claim (exit 3); after resolve, the loser's brief/next names the branch and says its claim was released.
data.title: A contested claim is not shown by status/next/brief, merge is not refused, and the losing clone is never told

data.summary: DEGRADED (stranded work): bob removes T2 while alice (another clone) holds a live lease and has a commit on ddflow/T2. After the pull alice's `heartbeat T2` says "renewed T2" on a removed item, `merge T2` says "no such item (it was removed)", `cleanup` says LEAVE ALONE (live lease), `recover` says nothing to recover, `status` and `doctor` are silent, so her finished branch is unreachable by any ddflow command and nobody is told. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s2d.py section 2h. Severity: medium. Test: removing an item with a live lease from another clone leaves a doctor PROBLEM on the pulled log naming the holder and branch; heartbeat refuses a removed item; cleanup/recover list the branch with the exact git command to keep or delete it.
data.title: Item removed in one clone while another clone holds its lease: the lease and branch are stranded silently

data.summary: DEGRADED (contradictory governing text): alice records D-sql (storage MUST be sqlite) and bob D-pg (MUST be postgres, sqlite forbidden), same globs, offline. After the merge `decision applicable T1` and `brief` list BOTH under "Binding unless the operator says otherwise", `doctor` is clean. Concurrent supersession of one decision by two different decisions leaves both replacements live with no warning. Order-independent supersession is correct (D-e edited by alice while bob superseded it folds the same in both clones). Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s2d.py section 3 and 3b; overlaps P-coherence (contradiction check on add, which cannot see a decision that has not arrived yet). Severity: medium. Test: after a merge that brings two live decisions with overlapping globs authored by different clones since the last common ancestor, doctor reports a decision-overlap NOTE/PROBLEM and brief marks them "unreconciled".
data.title: Concurrent decisions with overlapping globs are both presented as binding; no reconcile prompt after a merge

data.summary: DEGRADED (anyone can disturb another user's live state): (a) `ddflow release T2` run by agent U2 released the LIVE lease of U9 held in another clone: rc 0, "released T2", no --force, and U9's next `heartbeat` says "no lease held" (leases.release() lets any agent release any lease; right for an operator clearing a crashed agent, wrong for a live holder on another machine). (b) `gate run T1 unit_tests` by bob, who has no worktree for T1, wrote gate.unavailable and flipped alice's recorded unit_tests pass to [?] for every clone (last event wins, no ownership check). Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s4b.py and /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s9.py. Severity: medium. Test: release/gate record/gate run on an item whose live lease is held by another agent is refused (exit 3) unless --force with a reason, and the override is recorded and shown to the holder in brief.
data.title: A non-holder can release another user's live lease and overwrite its gate outcomes without --force

data.summary: DEGRADED (wall-clock leases across machines): lease expiry compares the claim's own `at` (the claimant's clock) with the observer's clock. With alice's clock 2 h behind, bob sees "lease U1 (-5401s left)", `next` and `status` print INTERRUPTED, `claim` says EXPIRED and, with --force, takes it; `recover` says "worktree is gone; nothing to salvage. ddflow release T1 to clear the claim" - advice to drop a LIVE claim (the worktree is "gone" only because it exists in the other clone). With alice 2 h ahead bob sees a lease of 8999 s. Lamport order is unaffected (good); only leases, cadence and any age rule use wall time. Also every lease from another clone reads as "worktree gone" in recover/cleanup. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s7.py (sitecustomize time offset). Severity: medium. Test: an event whose `ts`/`at` is more than skew_tolerance from the observer's clock at pull time produces a doctor NOTE naming the author; expiry of a lease owned by another clone is judged from heartbeat evidence seen locally (receipt time), and recover/cleanup say "worktree is in another clone" instead of "gone".
data.title: Lease expiry trusts the claimant's wall clock; a skewed clock makes a live claim look expired and recover advises releasing it

data.summary: DEGRADED (self-lockout): the derived agent id is host-dir-<clone-id> and the clone-id lives in git-ignored .ddflow/local/clone-id. After `rm -r .ddflow/local` (or git clean -xfd, a re-image, a fresh checkout of the same working copy) alice is a new agent: `heartbeat T1` = "no lease held", `claim T1` = "held by [REDACTED:hostname]-alice-fce1e0 for another 1799s", status shows her own work held by a stranger, and a second shard appears. Only wait or `release` (by anyone) clears it. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s11e.py. Severity: medium. Test: with .ddflow/local removed, the clone id is re-derived from something committed or recoverable (git config local key, or the shard whose last event is this tree's) or doctor names the old id and offers `ddflow identify --adopt <old id>`.
data.title: Deleting git-ignored .ddflow/local changes the agent identity and locks the user out of their own lease

data.summary: DEGRADED (frequent merge conflicts in generated tracked files, and a conflicted config blinds ddflow): docs/ddflow/QUEUE.md, LESSONS.md, LESSONS-SUMMARY.md (`ddflow render`) are tracked; two clones that each render and commit conflict on all three on every pull (CONFLICT content), doctor says only "mid-merge". Regenerating (`checkout --theirs docs/ddflow; ddflow render`) resolves it but nothing says so. A concurrent `config --set` of one key in .ddflow/config.toml conflicts too, and while the markers are in the file EVERY command (status, show, gate status, history) dies with "TOMLDecodeError: Invalid statement (at line 41, column 1)" - no hint of the merge. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s6i.py and /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s8.py. Severity: medium-high (daily). Test: doctor on a mid-merge tree with conflicted generated views prints the exact regenerate command; a config with conflict markers yields exit 3 with "resolve the merge conflict in .ddflow/config.toml" and read commands still work from the last good layer; adopt writes a .gitattributes policy for generated views.
data.title: Tracked generated views conflict on every concurrent render; a conflicted config.toml makes every command fail with a raw TOMLDecodeError

data.summary: DEGRADED (version skew writes managed files): clone B runs v0.2.0 (also v0.1.18) while the project was upgraded by 0.2.1. Log writes are refused cleanly and reads work (exit 3, "upgrade ddflow-mcp to >= 0.2.1"), but `ddflow adopt` by the OLDER version exits 0 and rewrites the newer managed files: docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md loses its begin/end header and the paragraphs 0.2.1 added, and AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md get a SECOND managed block with the old markers appended (45 added lines; two blocks), so every later instruction refresh by either version flip-flops. Released versions cannot be fixed; the current guard (B-uni-compat-contract) refuses this only against newer files. A second skew cost: any patch difference (0.2.0 vs 0.2.1, same FORMAT_LEVEL 1) refuses ALL writes of every older clone, a lockstep upgrade the team has no way to schedule or even see. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s5.py v0.2.0 and v0.1.18 (transcripts s5_v0.2.0/v0.1.18.transcript.txt). Severity: medium. Test: doctor/sync-check reports two managed blocks in one file and an instruction file whose stamp is older than the log's highest stamp; the log records a team minimum version that adopt/upgrade --apply of an older ddflow can see (new releases only).
data.title: An older ddflow's adopt downgrades newer managed files and duplicates the managed block; any patch skew locks the older clones out of writes

data.summary: DEGRADED (silent event loss after history rewrite): events live in git history only. After `git push -f` of an older main (or a revert of the events commit) and the other user's `reset --hard origin/main`, alice's claim of T1 is gone from her tree: `show` says open, `heartbeat` "no lease held", `doctor` Healthy, `cleanup` calls her worktree "orphan, fully merged - safe to remove", and the only trace is her reflog. A deleted shard file is equally silent. Torn lines, conflict markers and hand-edited events ARE detected (doctor PROBLEM), duplicates and CRLF are tolerated: so only the missing-event class is blind. Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s6.py (6c, 6d) and /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s6e.py/s6g.py. Severity: medium. Test: a local high-water mark per shard (.ddflow/local, count and last event id) lets doctor say "shard X lost N events since you last saw it; they may still be in git reflog/origin: git show <sha>"; never auto-repair.
data.title: Events removed by force-push, revert or reset vanish silently: no shard high-water mark, doctor stays healthy

data.summary: DEGRADED (fresh clone is not equivalent to the adopter's clone): a clone gets no git hooks (not tracked) and `doctor` says Healthy; only `hooks status` (exit 2) reveals pre-commit and commit-msg are NOT installed. Tracked .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json carry the adopter's absolute interpreter and PYTHONPATH (with --launch python/source installs; hooks fall back to a PATH ddflow, .mcp.json does not), so they differ per machine and flip-flop on every adopt/upgrade by another user. The pre-commit lease check does work across users once installed (bob's commit on alice's leased src/a.py printed the STOP message, from the shared log). Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s11.py. Severity: low-medium. Test: doctor on a clone with the managed git hooks missing prints a NOTE with `ddflow hooks install`; adopt writes machine-independent launch commands by default or the generated entries are marked machine-local and git-ignored.
data.title: A fresh clone has no hooks and doctor is Healthy; tracked .mcp.json and settings hooks hold one machine's absolute paths

data.summary: DEGRADED (a pass means different things per user): [gate.unit_tests].command is set in each user's git-ignored .ddflow/local/config.toml. Alice's pass with command "python -c 'print(1)'" shows as [x] unit_tests for bob (and for `complete`), with no word that the command is local to her; the gate.passed evidence has the command and tail, but gate status, brief and complete do not say it differs from the committed/shared command. The evidence output_log points at .ddflow/runs/... which is git-ignored, so other users get a dangling path. The reviewer-family rule is evaluated from recorded model names, so it holds across users (PASS). Repro: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu/s9.py. Severity: low-medium. Test: gate.passed stores the layer (committed|local|env) and digest of the command; gate status shows "passed with a local-only command" and complete under a project that sets gates.shared_command_required refuses it.
data.title: Gate passes made with a user-local command look the same as passes with the project's command

data.claim: Textual merging of shards is safe in every tested git flow, but cross-clone meaning is protected only for item ids and claims; same-id knowledge records, shared agent names, clocks, version skew, generated files and history rewrites are silently wrong or noisy
data.falsifier: Any two-clone run in which same-id decisions, a shared agent name or a force-push is detected by doctor with a PROBLEM and a named remedy
data.mechanism: Events are per-writer shards merged by git (merge=union), ordered by (lamport, agent, id); B191 folds a second definition or an overlapping claim of one id into CONTESTED. Everything else is last-writer-wins on (lamport, agent) or wall-clock based, so correctness across clones depends on (a) distinct agent ids, (b) every record kind having a contest rule, (c) the reader noticing foreign events, (d) all clones running compatible ddflow.
data.probe: python <scratchpad>/mu/s*.py with real git, bare origin, private HOME, ddflow main 0.2.1, v0.2.0, v0.1.18 trees (git archive)
data.probe_output: Harness: harness.py/common.py in the mu directory; scripts s1 s1b s2b s2c s2d s3b s4 s4b s5(v0.2.0,v0.1.18) s6 s6e s6g s6i s7 s8 s9 s10 s11 s11e s12 (200 and 2000 events per shard). Observed (PASS=safe, D=degraded, B=broken): claim same task offline -> D (doctor rc1 CONTESTED; status/next silent; merge not refused); remote claims ref -> PASS (second claim rc3, offline remote refuses); same id task/phase -> PASS contested; same id decision/lesson/research -> B silent last-writer-wins, doctor clean, decision fields mixed across authors; same agent name on two clones -> B double claim, one shard with lamport 6..14 twice, doctor NOTE only; non-holder release -> D; removed item with live lease -> D; contradictory decisions -> D; older ddflow v0.2.0/v0.1.18 -> writes refused rc3 with a clear message, reads work, but its adopt rewrites newer managed files and duplicates the AGENTS.md block -> D; squash/rebase/merge of shards -> PASS; force-push/revert/reset loses events silently -> D; torn line, conflict markers, edited event -> PASS (doctor PROBLEM), CRLF and duplicate lines tolerated; shard deleted -> D silent; concurrent render of tracked views -> conflict on 3 files every time; conflicted config.toml -> every command dies with TOMLDecodeError; clock 2h behind -> live lease shown expired, recover advises release; local config differs -> pass looks identical; fresh clone has no hooks and doctor Healthy; rm .ddflow/local -> own lease locked out; scale 1.5MB 6000 events status 1.0s, 14.8MB 60000 events status 7.3s on a loaded host. 13 bugs filed (B230e852e10, B36aa4c8ee5, B2809f4213b, B71dedb76d2, B0dcccd8594, B90b43dd2d8, B5a6651cd8e, B839f599cb5, B6b8d1f7a0f, B63635ddc6a, Ba24a8d32ee, Bec9a971c5d, B924bdc92d7).
data.question: What does ddflow do when several users with their own clones, versions and agents work and merge periodically, and what breaks?

data.claim: Systems that stay correct across clones share four mechanisms ddflow lacks in part: collision-free or namespaced ids, a detected-and-surfaced conflict state for every record kind, a stored schema/version floor that older tools respect, and server-or-ref-backed arbitration only for exclusive claims
data.falsifier: A comparable system that merges concurrent same-id edits silently and is still considered safe
data.mechanism: git-bug and ddflow both use immutable ops ordered by Lamport clocks; Beads adds hash ids and a version guard; jj makes conflict a stored state; Gerrit keeps identity in the change; locks (git-lfs, merge queues, remote claim refs) need one arbiter
data.probe: none possible: documentation survey
data.probe_output: Fetched and summarised by a small model (summarised, not read in full): git-bug data model (operations as immutable blobs in a DAG, Lamport clocks, deterministic order by clock then pack id, no conflicts) https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/doc/design/data-model.md ; Gerrit Change-Id (an id in the commit footer that survives rebase, amend, cherry-pick; matched on id+repo+branch) https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/user-changeid.html ; Jujutsu first-class conflicts (conflict stored in the commit, resolved lazily, same-change auto-resolves) https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/technical/conflicts/ ; git-lfs locks (server-side lock registry, locks verified per owner, force unlock exists) https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/docs/man/git-lfs-locks.adoc ; Beads (hash-based ids to avoid merge collisions, atomic --claim in one transaction, schema-version guard stops older binaries corrupting a migrated db, Dolt cell-level merge) https://github.com/steveyegge/beads ; Claude Code agent teams (shared task list, claiming uses file locking, tasks pending/in progress/completed with dependencies, one team per session, task status can lag) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams ; protobuf rules (never reuse tag numbers, reserve removed fields, preserve unknown fields, no required fields) https://protobuf.dev/best-practices/dos-donts/ ; Tolerant Reader https://martinfowler.com/bliki/TolerantReader.html ; GitHub merge queue (temporary branch = base + queued PRs, required checks, failing PR dropped and queue rebuilt) https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue ; Zuul speculative gating (each change tested on top of those ahead) https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html ; OPA bundles (signed bundle, revision field, failed activation keeps the previous bundle) https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-bundles ; CRDTs (op-based need causal delivery and no duplication; tombstones; LWW vs OR-set) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict-free_replicated_data_type ; Taskwarrior sync (server replicas via TaskChampion; warns against file-sync tools, page does not describe conflict handling) https://taskwarrior.org/docs/sync/ ; Backlog.md (markdown tasks in the repo, checkActiveBranches to read task state across branches, no conflict rules documented) https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md. Not verified: Fossil tickets and clock skew (the page fetched did not cover them), Perforce exclusive checkout, Amp threads, Dolt conflict tables (redirected, not fetched).
data.question: How do comparable git-native and offline-sync systems handle many writers, identity, version skew and locks, and what can ddflow adopt without a server?

data.body:
Operator request 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "Do a research of what this tool does or is expected to do (future task for implementing) and what issues and problems could happen if multiple users work on the same project and have their own local git clone of it use local ddflow tools some potentially with different versions and do decisions in parallel and work and merge the code periodically (no matter what branching flow approach it is selected by the developers to work with) - how ddflow would behave and support such multi user work, what issues could or might happen, how could we prevent or mitigate them and respectively what features we need to develop in ddflow to make it more rebust for multi user multi agent multi version use?"
Evidence: R-multiuser-experiments (CONFIRMED, 12 scenario families run on real git with three ddflow versions; scripts in the research coordinator's scratchpad mu/ directory, copied into tests/ by B-mu-harness) and R-multiuser-survey (THEORETICAL). Bugs filed from it: B230e852e10 and B36aa4c8ee5 (BROKEN, their fix tasks run unheld), B2809f4213b, B71dedb76d2, B0dcccd8594, B90b43dd2d8, B5a6651cd8e, B839f599cb5, B6b8d1f7a0f, B63635ddc6a, Ba24a8d32ee, Bec9a971c5d, B924bdc92d7 (DEGRADED, fixed by the tasks below). Existing multi-user work reused, not repeated: B190/B205 (clone-unique derived ids), B191 (contested ids and claims), B192 ([flow].claims=remote), B193 (docs/ddflow/MULTI-USER.md), B-hy-commit-events and B189 (committing the shards), B-gap-log-backup, B-gap-log-scale, B-org-* (central config), B-coh-* (contradictions), B-res-* (resume). No server, no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon): everything is git-native. Held behind the P-gaps core and the docs wave like the other old work (D-old-work-behind-core-docs); the two BROKEN bug fixes are not held. MUST = needed for several users each with several agents; GREAT = worth building; the SKIP list is in B-mu-decide.
data.title: Several users, several clones, several agents, several ddflow versions: detect, prevent and explain cross-clone problems (git-native, no server)
Operator decisions for multi-user work: claim arbitration, same-id policy, version skew, config source, what to commit, privacy, lease semantics, supported branching flows (defaults in the body)

data.body:
PRIORITY: MUST (first; everything else waits for it). WHAT: ask the operator the multi-user design choices, with recommended defaults, and record them as decisions in docs/ddflow/decisions/multiuser.md (one decision per question, --globs on the code it governs). Write the options, my recommendation and the evidence for each, then WAIT for the operator.
QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS:
1 Claim arbitration across clones. Options: (a) optimistic: allow, detect at merge (today, B191); (b) [flow].claims=remote, a CAS ref refs/ddflow/claims/<id> (B192, built, tested: second claim exits 3, offline remote refuses); (c) a dedicated claims branch; (d) 'git push as the lock'. DEFAULT: (a) for solo or one-machine; (b) is the recommended team default and ddflow doctor/onboard offers it when a second author appears in the log; (c)(d) rejected: they need a push per claim and a branch ddflow cannot repair. Note forks (PR flow) cannot push refs to upstream: claims stay optimistic there.
2 Same-id policy. DEFAULT: every record kind follows B191: a second DIFFERENT definition under one id is CONTESTED and settled by `ddflow resolve`, never merged field-by-field; an identical re-add is not a contest; ids minted by ddflow are content/clone-derived (D-id-schemes-final) so human-chosen ids are the only source.
3 Id minting. DEFAULT: human-chosen ids stay allowed; `task add` without an id mints hash ids; teams may choose [ids] templates with a user or clone token (P-id-schemes).
4 Version skew between users. Options: refuse writes of the older clone (today), tolerate read-only, warn. DEFAULT: keep refuse-write/allow-read for FORMAT_LEVEL or event-kind differences, but make a PATCH difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL a warning (no refusal) from the first release that ships this task, and record a team minimum version in the log.
5 Shared config / policy source of truth. DEFAULT: committed .ddflow/config.toml is team policy; .ddflow/local is per user and may only tighten or set machine facts (paths, endpoints, worker counts); org bundles (P-org-config) sit below the project; gate pass evidence records which layer supplied the command.
6 Commit vs local. DEFAULT: committed: events, config, gates, rules, docs/ddflow managed drivers; generated views (QUEUE.md, LESSONS*.md) NOT committed by default in a team project (git-ignored, `ddflow render` on demand, CI renders), or committed with a merge=ours style strategy chosen in B-mu-generated-files; local: clone-id, index, runs, hooks.
7 Privacy of host names and paths in the shared log. DEFAULT: derived agent ids use a user-chosen handle instead of the host name once a project has more than one author; evidence tails pass the redactor; absolute paths never enter events (already true).
8 Lease semantics across machines. DEFAULT: a lease is evidence of intent, not a lock: expiry for another clone's lease is judged from heartbeat events seen locally; release/gate writes on a live lease of another agent need --force with a reason; no stealing (D-reclaim report).
9 Branching flows supported and tested. DEFAULT: trunk-based and PR-with-merge-commit, rebase-merge and squash-merge are tested in the harness (squash/rebase/merge of shards already PASS); gitflow and release lines with `port` are tested after B-mu-harness; long-lived branches work with `ddflow sync-check` run after every pull.
10 What is SKIPPED on purpose: a central lock or claim server, a daemon, vector clocks or a CRDT library, per-user signing keys inside the log (later, with B-org-trust), automatic resolution of contests, Perforce-style exclusive checkout of source files.
11 Roll-out order. DEFAULT: B-mu-harness, B-mu-identity, B-mu-conflicts, B-mu-sync-check, B-mu-generated-files, B-mu-lease-guards, B-mu-version-policy, then the GREAT tasks.

data.summary:

PRIORITY: MUST (first; everything else waits for it). WHAT: ask the operator the multi-user design choices, with recommended defaults, and record them as decisions in docs/ddflow/decisions/multiuser.md (one decision per question, --globs on the code it governs). Write the options, my recommendation and the evidence for each, then WAIT for the operator.
QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS:
1 Claim arbitration across clones. Options: (a) optimistic: allow, detect at merge (today, B191); (b) [flow].claims=remote, a CAS ref refs/ddflow/claims/<id> (B192, built, tested: second claim exits 3, offline remote refuses); (c) a dedicated claims branch; (d) 'git push as the lock'. DEFAULT: (a) for solo or one-machine; (b) is the recommended team default and ddflow doctor/onboard offers it when a second author appears in the log; (c)(d) rejected: they need a push per claim and a branch ddflow cannot repair. Note forks (PR flow) cannot push refs to upstream: claims stay optimistic there.
2 Same-id policy. DEFAULT: every record kind follows B191: a second DIFFERENT definition under one id is CONTESTED and settled by `ddflow resolve`, never merged field-by-field; an identical re-add is not a contest; ids minted by ddflow are content/clone-derived (D-id-schemes-final) so human-chosen ids are the only source.
3 Id minting. DEFAULT: human-chosen ids stay allowed; `task add` without an id mints hash ids; teams may choose [ids] templates with a user or clone token (P-id-schemes).
4 Version skew between users. Options: refuse writes of the older clone (today), tolerate read-only, warn. DEFAULT: keep refuse-write/allow-read for FORMAT_LEVEL or event-kind differences, but make a PATCH difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL a warning (no refusal) from the first release that ships this task, and record a team minimum version in the log.
5 Shared config / policy source of truth. DEFAULT: committed .ddflow/config.toml is team policy; .ddflow/local is per user and may only tighten or set machine facts (paths, endpoints, worker counts); org bundles (P-org-config) sit below the project; gate pass evidence records which layer supplied the command.
6 Commit vs local. DEFAULT: committed: events, config, gates, rules, docs/ddflow managed drivers; generated views (QUEUE.md, LESSONS*.md) NOT committed by default in a team project (git-ignored, `ddflow render` on demand, CI renders), or committed with a merge=ours style strategy chosen in B-mu-generated-files; local: clone-id, index, runs, hooks.
7 Privacy of host names and paths in the shared log. DEFAULT: derived agent ids use a user-chosen handle instead of the host name once a project has more than one author; evidence tails pass the redactor; absolute paths never enter events (already true).
8 Lease semantics across machines. DEFAULT: a lease is evidence of intent, not a lock: expiry for another clone's lease is judged from heartbeat events seen locally; release/gate writes on a live lease of another agent need --force with a reason; no stealing (D-reclaim report).
9 Branching flows supported and tested. DEFAULT: trunk-based and PR-with-merge-commit, rebase-merge and squash-merge are tested in the harness (squash/rebase/merge of shards already PASS); gitflow and release lines with `port` are tested after B-mu-harness; long-lived branches work with `ddflow sync-check` run after every pull.
10 What is SKIPPED on purpose: a central lock or claim server, a daemon, vector clocks or a CRDT library, per-user signing keys inside the log (later, with B-org-trust), automatic resolution of contests, Perforce-style exclusive checkout of source files.
11 Roll-out order. DEFAULT: B-mu-harness, B-mu-identity, B-mu-conflicts, B-mu-sync-check, B-mu-generated-files, B-mu-lease-guards, B-mu-version-policy, then the GREAT tasks.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: decisions API (decision add --globs), B-gap-decide pattern. HOW TO TEST: the decision file exists, every question answered or explicitly deferred, tests/test_decisions_live.py-style check passes. SIZE: small. ACCEPTANCE: each downstream task cites its decision id.

NOTE 2026-10-11 (bug fixes ahead of this task): the 11 DEGRADED multi-user bug fixes (fix-<bug id>) were built on proposed decision D-mu-bugfix-defaults, not on your answers; revisit it first: 1 claims optimistic + contested surfaced, 8 lease guard scoped to another CLONE, receipt-time expiry, 4 patch skew warns, 5 local command labelled not refused, 6 only conflict handling not the tracked-vs-ignored choice.

data.alternatives: Wait for B-mu-decide before fixing (leaves 11 known degraded behaviours open); build the whole P-multiuser feature set (sync-check, harness, team minimum version, privacy) now (much larger, not asked).
data.consequences: If B-mu-decide answers differently, the affected fix is reworked; the bug-fix tasks and held P-multiuser tasks name which default they use. Operator-visible trade-offs: lease guard scoped to another clone (not another agent name), receipt-time lease expiry delays a dead lease by up to one TTL after first sight, patch-skew relaxation loosens a guard, doctor NOTE (not PROBLEM) for missing hooks.

data.decision: Working defaults the 11 multi-user bug-fix tasks (fix-B2809f4213b, fix-B71dedb76d2, fix-B0dcccd8594, fix-B90b43dd2d8, fix-B5a6651cd8e, fix-B839f599cb5, fix-B6b8d1f7a0f, fix-B63635ddc6a, fix-Ba24a8d32ee, fix-Bec9a971c5d, fix-B924bdc92d7) are built on, taken from the recommended defaults of B-mu-decide: (1) claim arbitration stays OPTIMISTIC; a contested claim is surfaced in status/next/brief and refused by merge/complete; nothing is auto-resolved (B-mu-decide 1). (2) A lease is evidence of intent, not a lock: release and gate run/record/skip on a LIVE lease of another CLONE need --force with a reason and the override is recorded; agents of the same clone, the holder, expired leases and leases without a recorded clone are unchanged (8). (3) Liveness of another clone's lease is judged from renewals as first seen by this clone (receipt time in .ddflow/local), never from the claimant's wall clock; the fold stays pure (8). (4) Decisions record which live overlapping decisions their author saw (additive `saw` on decision.recorded); two overlapping decisions neither names the other are UNRECONCILED in doctor/brief (2, 8). (5) Version skew: a patch-only difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL and no capability gap warns instead of refusing writes; FORMAT_LEVEL, minor and capability gaps still refuse (4). (6) Committed config is team policy: a conflict-marked config is named (exit 3), a local command gate pass is LABELLED in evidence and status (command_layer, command_digest), refusing it is a later opt-in (5). (7) Generated views are regenerated on conflict; whether they stay tracked is B-mu-decide 6 and is not decided here (6). (8) Event loss by history rewrite is made visible by a local per-shard high-water mark and a doctor PROBLEM, never auto-repaired (10). (9) A fresh clone's missing git hooks and machine-absolute launch paths are doctor NOTES (PROBLEM only under [enforce] block). (10) No central server, no daemon (10); every event-payload addition is additive and every local file is a LocalStore document.
data.title: Design defaults used for the multi-user bug fixes

Design default (B-mu-decide 4): keep refuse-write for FORMAT_LEVEL or unknown-capability differences; a PATCH difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL and no capability gap becomes a WARNING from the first release that ships this task; no team minimum event here.
FAILING-FIRST REGRESSION TESTS (they must fail on current main): tests/test_adopt_duplicate_block.py - synthesize what the old adopt leaves (a stamped block plus a legacy-marker block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; a driver doc without its begin/end header): (1) `doctor` exits 1 with a PROBLEM 'AGENTS.md holds 2 managed blocks' naming the file, and a NOTE when an instruction file's stamp is older than the log's highest stamp; (2) `ddflow adopt --refresh-docs` collapses to exactly ONE current block, keeps text outside the markers byte-identical and is idempotent; (3) a single healthy block produces neither line. tests/test_patch_skew_policy.py - using the stamp fixtures of the existing skew tests: a log stamped by a higher PATCH of the same version line with the same FORMAT_LEVEL and no capability the running version lacks lets the older code WRITE with a one-time warning and the event carries the existing `older_ddflow` mark; a higher FORMAT_LEVEL, a higher MINOR, or a capability gap still raises SkewRefused (exit 3); `[upgrade].skew = "refuse"` set explicitly in config keeps today's strict behaviour only if the operator chooses (default per B-mu-decide 4 is the patch warning - state the final knob spelling in the test); reads are unaffected.

Never rewrites old events.

data.summary: Two lanes (U1 on fix-B230e852e10 and fix-B0dcccd8594, 2026-10-11) reported that `ddflow wait --item <id> --globs <paths>` returned READY immediately although the globs were held by another agent's live lease (U4 on records.py/health.py; U5 on health.py). The lanes then waited about 25 minutes for nothing or were told a claim was possible when `update --globs` / commit was refused. Expected: wait on an item (or on globs) returns only when the item can actually be claimed or widened, i.e. no live lease of another agent overlaps those globs (use the same overlap check as claim / update --globs). Repro: agent A claims item X with globs [f.py]; agent B runs `ddflow wait --item Y --globs f.py --timeout 5` where Y declares f.py -> must NOT report READY while A's lease is live. Regression test (tests/test_wait_globs_held.py): fails on current main (READY immediately), passes when the lease overlap is honoured and READY appears after A releases.
data.title: ddflow wait --item/--globs reports READY while another agent's live lease holds those globs

data.claim:
VS Code (docs read 2026-10-11): a SESSION is the unit of work with an agent: workspace + code changes + one or more chats (sessions.md, manage-sessions). A session has a main chat plus optional PEER chats that the USER prompts independently; each chat has its own history, title and agent/model, all share the session's workspace and worktree; a new chat starts BLANK and does not inherit other chats' history. Context moves only explicitly: FORK (branch a chat, inherits history, keeps prompt cache), side chat (privately inherits the source chat), /compact and automatic compaction (summary), HANDOFF (carries conversation history and context when the harness/environment/agent changes; custom-agent frontmatter handoffs[] = label, agent, prompt, send, model), delegation (remote: send_remote_message / get_remote_session / list_agent_hosts), and persistent sources (instructions, memory). Local subagents get NO parent history and are stateless (no follow-ups); settings chat.subagents.* (nesting depth max 5). Memory tool scopes: user /memories (first 200 lines loaded), repo /memories/repo (workspace-local, NOT shared), session /memories/session; all stored locally; team guidance is to move stable facts into source-controlled docs or instructions. Session history is a local SQLite DB synced to GitHub unless chat.sessionSync.enabled=false; search via /chronicle:search (keyword, file path, PR/issue ref). Export: command 'Chat: Export Chat...' (JSON). VS Code discovers local sessions created by Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, Claude Code and Codex. Agent Host owns sessions (AHP JSON-RPC, clients subscribe to session/chat URIs). Proposed extension API chatSessionsProvider. Hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStart/Stop, Stop; files .github/hooks/*.json, [REDACTED:path]; Claude-format .claude/settings.json read when chat.useClaudeHooks (matchers ignored). Files: .github/agents/*.agent.md (also .claude/agents), .github/prompts/*.prompt.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md (applyTo), AGENTS.md (chat.useAgentsMdFile), CLAUDE.md (chat.useClaudeMdFile). Claude Code (docs read): session = JSONL transcript [REDACTED:path]<project>/<session-id>.jsonl (entry format internal, changes between versions); subagent transcripts .../<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl (30-day cleanup); --resume/--continue/--fork-session//branch; hooks get session_id, transcript_path, agent_id, agent_type; SessionStart source startup|resume|clear|compact|fork, additionalContext (10k chars); agent teams (experimental): lead + teammates, shared task list + JSON mailbox files under [REDACTED:path] and [REDACTED:path], no session resume of in-process teammates, one team per session; cross-session messaging (v2.1.224+): ListAgents/SendMessage over a per-session unix socket, plain text only, a message is never consent and cannot change config or approve prompts, inbound controls accept/hold/refuse; agent view (claude agents --json: sessionId, state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, waitingFor, name, cwd); subagent persistent memory dirs .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/ (project scope shareable via git); Claude Code Projects (public beta, Pro/Max, not Team/Enterprise): one coordinator conversation starting a cloud-session THREAD per task; every thread gets project instructions (16,000 chars), project memory (MEMORY.md index + files) and repo CLAUDE.md, but not the coordinator's history; threads report back. claude.ai Projects (support article): knowledge base uploads + custom instructions + RAG on paid plans + sharing (can view/can edit) + chats inside the project.
ddflow today (measured by reading tasks and code in this repo 2026-10-11): ddflow session has start/prompt/note/adopt-orphans/end/list/show; session.started folds only the model; there is NO parent/child link, role or goal on a session; lanes U1..U6 have only lease events; brief + restart brief + PreCompact digest exist; P-agent-memory (B-am-*) already plans capture, handoff, restart-brief, search, session-cli, ingest of Claude transcripts, loops, retention; B-gap-lanes plans a lane ledger; adopt for vscode/copilot today writes only .vscode/mcp.json, .github/mcp.json, AGENTS.md and delta docs (verified by running adopt in a scratch repo): no .github/agents, .github/prompts, .github/hooks, .github/instructions.

Evidence: R-session-context (THEORETICAL: vendor docs read through a summarising fetch) and R-session-context-adopt (CONFIRMED: adopt for vscode/copilot writes no .github/agents, prompts, hooks, instructions).

data.body:
A short practical guide: how to use sessions, sub-sessions, hand-offs and project knowledge together with ddflow TODAY, plus the ddflow-to-VS Code / Claude Code / Claude Projects concept map.

CONTENT (docs/ddflow/session-context.md, a help topic `ddflow help session-context`, the driver note): (1) the concept map: VS Code session / main chat / peer chat / fork / handoff / agent-host; Claude Code session / --resume / --fork-session / subagent / agent team / cross-session message / agent view; Claude Projects coordinator + threads + project instructions + project memory; each next to its ddflow counterpart (session, lane, claim+worktree, session.handoff, brief, decision/rule/memory, lanes). (2) recipes that need no new code: one VS Code session per ddflow item (worktree isolation) and one peer chat per lane role (reviewer, tester) - chats share the worktree so give each its own ddflow agent id (ddflow --agent) and never two chats editing the same globs; do not rely on a chat inheriting another's history - run `ddflow brief --agent <id>` first; use VS Code custom agents with `handoffs:` for plan -> implement -> review; use Claude Code subagents with `memory: project` (.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/) for reviewer lessons and let ddflow memory import them; Claude Projects for non-repo knowledge (contracts, tickets), ddflow decisions/rules for repo knowledge; claude --resume <id> after a lane stops; claude agents / lanes to see who is waiting. (3) what NOT to do: do not put approvals or secrets in a cross-session message; remote-session MCP tools are coordinator tooling, not a ddflow channel; VS Code repository memory is local-only so facts that matter go to ddflow memory/decisions (committed). (4) every claim carries the verified date and the research record; unverified items say so.
Also mark in docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/{vscode,claude-code}.md. No code. Docs gates: docscheck/docsync pass.

PIN/TEST: docs lint/links; help topic registered (services/help.py golden gains exactly one topic). EXPECTED SIZE: ~200 lines of docs.
data.title: Guide: using sessions, sub-sessions, hand-offs and project knowledge with VS Code, Claude Code and Claude Projects today, and the concept map to ddflow

data.body:
Ask the operator, then record a decision D-session-context in docs/ddflow/decisions/session-context.md. Nothing else in P-session-context is built before the answers (research R-session-context, R-session-context-adopt; request verbatim in the phase body).

WHY: VS Code (a session = workspace + changes + one main chat and user-prompted peer chats that start blank; fork/handoff/compaction move context only explicitly) and Claude (transcripts + --resume/--fork-session, agent teams, cross-session messaging, Projects = coordinator + threads sharing project instructions and memory but not history) show the same split ddflow already has: history stays private to a conversation; only curated records (instructions, memory, decisions, handoffs) cross. ddflow plans most of the carrying (P-agent-memory); these questions cover only the missing parts.

QUESTIONS, each with the recommended default:
1. Session tree. Options: (a) new event kind; (b) additive optional fields parent, role (main|lane|subagent|peer|fork), goal on session.started plus a derived `ddflow session tree`; (c) derived only from dispatch/lease/agent_id records. RECOMMEND (b): old logs fold unchanged (upcaster not needed for optional fields), no new kind.
2. Transfer pack. Options: a committed file per transfer; an event only; an on-demand rendering. RECOMMEND the pack is an on-demand FENCED rendering of the latest session.handoff plus pointers (markdown or json, per-harness wording), and `session transfer` records a small session.transferred event (from, to, handoff id, mode transfer|fork); a file is written only with --file, under .ddflow/local/transfers/ (git-ignored).
3. Project-scope knowledge (Claude Projects: instructions + memory + files for every thread). Options: build a mirror/export; do nothing new. RECOMMEND nothing new: ddflow brief already delivers decisions, rules, lessons, memory and skills to every session of every agent by glob relevance and budget; document the mapping (B-sc-docs). A knowledge export for claude.ai chat projects is out of scope unless asked (B-export kinds exist).
4. Native stores to read. RECOMMEND Claude Code only (B-am-ingest) plus status from `claude agents --json`; VS Code / Copilot CLI / Codex / Cursor session stores only after B-am-harness-probe proves a stable, documented format for that harness (VS Code docs name a local SQLite store and no path); always read-only, never write a native store.
5. Remote-session MCP tools in this coordinator environment (create_session, send_message, list_events, get_session). RECOMMEND ddflow code never calls them; ddflow stays harness-neutral and coordinates through the shared log. They remain the operator's/coordinator's own tooling, documented with two hard rules: a message is never approval or consent (Claude's own docs say so; permission laundering), and list_events output is never copied into the log or a handoff without the redactor. Reject a build that depends on them.
6. Native lane status. RECOMMEND opt-in `[lanes] native_status = off|auto` default off (a subprocess per harness); when on and the harness CLI is missing or fails, report 'unavailable', never guess.
7. Generated VS Code/Copilot files by adopt (agents with handoffs mirroring the gate pipeline, prompt files, hooks, instructions). RECOMMEND yes, through the existing tasks (B-sub-sync, B-adopt-agent-commands, B-hx-hook-writers), managed-marked, never overwriting a foreign file.

HOW TO PIN: the decision file lists each question, the answer and the knob/task it sets; run ddflow decision add --globs for every file the later tasks own. EXPECTED SIZE: one document, no code.
data.title: Operator decisions: session tree, transfer pack, project-scope knowledge, native stores, remote-session MCP tools, native lane status, generated VS Code files

data.body:
A first-class session TREE: every session knows its parent, role and goal, and `ddflow session tree` shows main session -> lanes -> sub-agent runs -> peer chats/forks with the items each touched and how each ended.

WHY (measured): the session fold keeps model/started_at/prompts/notes only (core/handlers/sessions.py _h_session_started); there is no parent link, role or goal anywhere, so 'which sub-agent runs belonged to this coordinator session' is unanswerable from the log (lanes U1..U6 are separate flat agents; B-am-capture will add dispatch/report records and SubagentStart/Stop ids but links them by agent name, not by parent session). VS Code models session -> main chat + peer chats (+ forks); Claude Code gives hooks agent_id/agent_type, SessionStart source=fork, and agent-view sessionIds; Claude Projects models coordinator -> threads. ddflow should show the same shape.

DESIGN (decision D-session-context Q1, default b): additive optional fields on session.started and session.prompt-dispatch records: parent (session id), role (main|lane|subagent|peer|fork), goal (short text, redacted, capped), harness_session (the native id when the descriptor exposes it, from B-hx-identity). No new event kind and no upcaster for old events (absent = main). `ddflow session start --parent <id> --role lane --goal ...` (CLI+MCP from one declaration), set automatically by the B-am-capture dispatch/SubagentStart paths when the parent is known. A pure fold service services/session_tree.py builds the tree: node = session, edges = parent, annotations = items touched (leases/gates in the session's span), outcome (session.ended summary or handoff state), state (open/ended/interrupted). `ddflow session tree [--root id] [--open] [--json]` plus `session show` gains the parent and children lines. Cycles and a missing parent are shown, not crashed on ('parent unknown').

NOT in scope: the lane liveness table (B-gap-lanes; the tree is history, the ledger is now), transcripts (B-am-ingest), the handoff body (B-am-handoff).

PIN/TEST: a seeded log with coordinator -> 2 lanes -> sub-agent runs gives a golden tree; old log with no new fields renders every session as a root; a parent id that does not exist is labelled, not an error; cycle guard; CLI/MCP parity test; fold is a pure function of the log. EXPECTED SIZE: ~300 lines + tests.
data.title: Session tree: parent, role and goal on sessions, ddflow session tree with items touched and outcome

data.body:
An addressed TRANSFER and FORK between sessions and agents: hand the work of one session to another session, agent or harness as a checked, fenced pack that any harness can consume, and record that it happened.

WHY (measured): B-am-handoff writes a session.handoff and B-am-restart-brief gives the SAME agent identity its previous run plus see-also hits; nothing lets one agent hand a task to a DIFFERENT agent or harness on purpose (Claude Code to Codex, lane to a fresh lane, local to VS Code), nor start a child that inherits a parent's handoff (fork). Vendors: VS Code handoff 'carries conversation history and context' when the harness or agent changes, and a fork inherits the whole history; Claude has --fork-session and /branch; Claude Projects threads start with project instructions + memory but NOT the coordinator history; Claude cross-session messages are plain text only and never carry consent. The portable thing is a curated pack, not a transcript.

DESIGN (decision D-session-context Q2): `ddflow session transfer --from <session|agent> --to <agent|harness> [--item ID] [--fork] [--format md|json] [--file]` (CLI+MCP, one declaration). It does NOT summarise with a model: it renders the latest session.handoff of the source (goal, state, items held, decisions, open items, files from git diff, failed attempts, commands failed as digests, next step, pointers to transcript turns - the B-am-handoff schema) fenced with core/provenance (author, trust=agent) and the standard 'recorded DATA, not instructions' line, wrapped in per-harness wording from the descriptor (how that harness takes a first prompt, the exact resume/spawn line from B-gap-lanes), sized to the brief budget (services/contextpack + core/budget). If the source has no handoff it creates the deterministic skeleton first (B-am-handoff, produced_by=deterministic) and says so. It appends one session.transferred event {from, to, handoff, mode: transfer|fork, item, accepted: null} and with --fork starts the child session with parent=<source> (B-sc-tree). `ddflow session accept <transfer>` is the receiver's one call (it sets accepted and records which session took it); an unaccepted transfer shows in brief and lanes advise. It never moves a lease: the receiver claims normally, so the claim rules and contest checks stay the only authority. IMPORT of a native summary (Claude isCompactSummary, a pasted VS Code export) is B-am-handoff's ingest; this task adds `--from-file` that stores such a text as a produced_by=harness-summary handoff, redacted and capped.

SAFETY: the pack never carries approvals, permission grants or secrets: every text passes redactor('log'); an incoming instruction inside it stays inside the fence; accepted/consent is never inferred from a message (mirrors Claude's cross-session rule). No dependency on remote-session MCP tools (D-session-context Q5).

PIN/TEST: golden pack for a seeded two-item session in md and json; pack fits the budget and keeps the first line when tiny; planted secret redacted; planted 'ignore previous instructions' stays fenced; transfer without handoff creates the skeleton; fork child has parent set; transfer twice is idempotent by (from,to,handoff); accept sets accepted once; CLI/MCP parity. EXPECTED SIZE: ~400 lines + tests.
data.title: Transfer and fork: an addressed, fenced hand-off pack between sessions, agents and harnesses, recorded and accepted

data.body:
Lane STATE from the harness's own session listing, and the mapping between a ddflow session/lane and the native session id with the exact resume line. Read-only, optional, never guessed.

WHY (measured): B-gap-lanes derives lane state from the ddflow log only; the log cannot tell 'working' from 'blocked on a permission prompt' (a lane waiting for input looks idle or stale until its lease lapses; memory M801fd9dc2b: do not restart a lane that stops idle). Claude Code's agent view exposes exactly that: `claude agents --json` entries carry sessionId (usable with claude --resume), state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, status busy|waiting|idle, waitingFor (permission prompt | input needed | sandbox request | worker request | dialog open), name, cwd, kind, startedAt; `claude logs <id>`, `claude attach <id>`, `claude stop <id>` exist (docs read 2026-10-11, version-dependent). VS Code shows a similar status in its sessions list and badge, but its docs name no machine-readable store or path: not built on.

DESIGN (decision D-session-context Q4/Q6): services/nativesessions.py with one adapter per harness descriptor key [native_sessions] (command, json fields, resume_line template, verified date, record); only claude is filled from a live probe, every other harness is 'unavailable' until B-am-harness-probe proves it. `[lanes] native_status = off|auto` (default off; strictest = off). When on, `ddflow lanes` (B-gap-lanes) joins a lane to a native session by cwd + start time + the session id the SessionStart hook recorded (B-sc-tree harness_session), shows the native state next to the log state, and says 'native: unavailable (reason)' when the CLI is missing, times out (hard timeout, one subprocess, no daemon) or the payload shape changed. `ddflow session show` and `lanes brief` print the resume line (claude --resume <sessionId>). A native 'blocked/waitingFor' becomes a lane advise line ('lane U3 is waiting for a permission prompt: attach it, do not restart') - ddflow never answers the prompt, never sends keys, never stops a session.

NOT in scope: reading transcripts (B-am-ingest), spawning (B-gap-lanes prints the line, nothing runs it), the remote-session MCP tools.

PIN/TEST: recorded `claude agents --json` fixtures (tests/fixtures/harness/claude/agents.json, B-hx-conformance layout) incl. an unknown future field and a missing field; join golden; CLI absent/timeout/garbage gives 'unavailable' never a state; off mode spawns nothing (monkeypatch proc to fail); no subprocess output reaches the log unredacted. EXPECTED SIZE: ~300 lines + tests.
data.title: Native lane state and resume line: claude agents --json joined to the lane ledger, read-only, optional, never guessed

data.body:
Add a [transcripts] section to the harness descriptors and the missing canonical lifecycle events, verified per harness; no behaviour yet.

WHY (measured): ddflow/services/harnessreg.py CANONICAL_EVENTS has 7 events (session_start, prompt, pre_tool, post_tool, pre_compact, stop, session_end) and ddflow/api/setup.py _on_nothing is the handler for pre_tool/post_tool/stop/session_end. Claude Code also has SubagentStart/SubagentStop (payload adds agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message) and PostCompact (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Sub-agent transcripts sit at [REDACTED:path]<project>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl (541 on this machine) and are deleted after cleanupPeriodDays (30). The compaction summary is written to the session transcript as a user entry with isCompactSummary:true (verified on this machine, text starts 'This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context ... Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent:'). Nothing in ddflow reads either. A PostCompact compact_summary field is claimed only by third-party issues: PROBE IT LIVE (a hook that dumps stdin) and record the result; do not assume.

INTERFACE (reuse): harness TOML descriptors (ddflow/harnesses/*.toml + services/harnessreg.py validation) get [transcripts] with: path template (session and sub-agent), format (jsonl-claude, other, none), summary_marker (isCompactSummary), retention_days, verified date + record. Add canonical events post_compact, subagent_start, subagent_stop (claude: PostCompact, SubagentStart, SubagentStop). claude is filled from the live probe; every other harness is nv (not verified) unless a probe proves it - never guessed. One research record per harness probed, like R-hx-claude.

PIN/TEST: tests/test_am_harness_transcripts.py: descriptor schema accepts/rejects, golden for claude, an nv harness yields 'unknown' not a path, CANONICAL_EVENTS unchanged order for existing events (hooks run goldens byte-identical). EXPECTED SIZE: ~150 lines + one probe note.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: store the dumped payloads under tests/fixtures/harness/claude/<event>.json (the B-hx-conformance layout) so B-ac-fixtures can re-record them later.

Session-context extension 2026-10-11 (R-session-context, phase P-session-context): the same probe step also records, per harness, whether the harness has (a) a documented machine-readable listing of its sessions with a native session id, state and name (Claude Code: `claude agents --json`, fields sessionId/state/waitingFor/name/cwd, docs read 2026-10-11; VS Code: docs name a local SQLite session store and /chronicle:search but NO path or schema, and say VS Code discovers sessions made by Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, Claude Code and Codex) and (b) a resume command (claude --resume <id>, --fork-session). Record each as a [native_sessions] descriptor field marked nv (not verified) unless a live probe proves it; do not read or write VS Code, Copilot CLI, Codex or Cursor stores until a probe shows a stable documented format. B-sc-native-status consumes these fields; this task adds no behaviour.

Reuse the skills sync engine: managed marker, never overwrite a foreign file, drift detection; a field a harness cannot express (Cursor has no tool allowlist, Codex has sandbox_mode not tools) is reported as lossy per harness, never silently dropped.

Session-context extension 2026-10-11 (R-session-context-adopt, phase P-session-context): for the VS Code/Copilot target (.github/agents/*.agent.md, also read from .claude/agents) the writer must know the harness-only frontmatter fields instead of dropping them as lossy: `handoffs` (label, agent, prompt, send, model - suggested workflow buttons, e.g. Plan -> Implement -> Review, which ddflow can derive from the gate pipeline), `agents` (allowed subagents, `*` for all), `user-invocable`, `disable-model-invocation`, `model` as an ordered list, `tools` with MCP `<server>/*` names. Measured: ddflow adopt writes no .github/agents today. Local subagents in VS Code get no parent history and are stateless (docs), so a generated reviewer agent's prompt must be self-contained (goal, constraints, expected result) - ddflow supplies the brief command, not history. Verify each field against the live custom-agents page at implementation time.

AGENT_COMMANDS has one entry: claude -> .claude/commands/implement.md. Several other supported agents also read slash commands from a project directory (Cursor's .cursor/commands/ is one; research which others do, from primary docs). Add an entry per agent whose directory is verified, with the DDFLOW:MANAGED mark, keeping an operator's own file of the same name exactly as _write_command already does. Also research which clients surface MCP prompts as slash commands: where they do, the file may be unnecessary — say so in that agent's delta doc.

data.claim:
ddflow already has the engine for strict and unstrict guidance, but no goal concept and no proposal store; the attached document (Architectural Orchestration of Goals, Defeasible Principles, and Invariants) is wrong about most names and about where the gaps are. Verified on main 2026-10-11.

data.question: What does ddflow already have for goals, principles, strict and unstrict rules and periodic feature discovery, and which claims of the attached agentic-workflows document are true of this repository?

data.claim:
Goals, principles and proposals need no parallel store: goals and proposals are two new definition-record kinds on the existing def.* model and record surface; a principle is a guidance record (rule or decision) whose override mode is deviate (an agent-recorded reason, item-scoped, counted) instead of waive (operator-approved, 90 days); strict rules stay enforcement=block with waive or none. Periodic discovery is a schedule job that files ONE research item whose output is at most K proposals, with backpressure (open-proposal cap), dedupe against the board and against rejected proposals, and an operator-only adopt/defer/reject that records the reason. THEORETICAL: this is a design, not measured; thresholds are initial hypotheses to calibrate in the evaluation task.

SURVEY (VERIFIED = page fetched and read; the fetch returns a model summary, so quotes are approximate):
- Hard vs soft is almost always 'context vs enforcement': Claude Code says CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced, and 'to block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook' (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, VERIFIED); Kiro steering is soft and hooks can gate (kiro.dev/docs/steering, /hooks, VERIFIED); Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot and OpenHands rules differ in WHEN text is loaded (always, globs, agent-chosen, manual), not whether it is obeyed (cursor.com/docs/context/rules; docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories; docs.github.com custom instructions; docs.openhands.dev microagents-overview; all VERIFIED).
- Graduated severity ladders exist in policy tools: Gatekeeper enforcementAction dryrun, warn, deny (open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper violations, VERIFIED); Kyverno Audit vs Enforce, with pre-existing resources grandfathered (kyverno.io validate docs, VERIFIED); Conftest deny, violation, warn (conftest.dev, VERIFIED thin); RFC 2119 MUST absolute, SHOULD 'valid reasons to ignore... implications understood and carefully weighed', MAY optional (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119, VERIFIED).
- Principles vs requirements: Spec Kit constitution (principles that stay constant) separate from specs; deviations go in a 'Complexity Tracking' section with justification (github.com/github/spec-kit spec-driven.md, VERIFIED, one page; amendment process not verified). OpenSpec records changes as ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED deltas (github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec, VERIFIED README).
- Exceptions: Kyverno PolicyException is a separate object, disabled by default; no expiry or approver field seen. ArchUnit FreezingArchRule stores existing violations so only NEW ones fail (archunit.org userguide, VERIFIED): the pattern for adopting a hard rule on legacy code. No verified tool combines reason + expiry + approver in one record; ddflow's waiver already does, which is beyond verified prior art.
- Goals: Linear initiatives have status and health, but health comes from a human-written update, not computed (linear.app/docs/initiatives, VERIFIED); GitHub milestones compute percent of closed issues (docs.github.com milestones, VERIFIED thin); SonarQube quality gates are numeric conditions on new code, 'Clean as You Code' (docs.sonarsource.com quality gates, VERIFIED); fitness functions are executable goals (thoughtworks.com fitness-function-driven-development, VERIFIED). Jira goals and OKR key-result design NOT verified.
- Proposal generation and noise control: Jules Suggested Tasks scans periodically, shows cards the user starts or dismisses, dismissal is used as feedback, daily task caps (jules.google/docs/suggested-tasks, /usage-limits, VERIFIED); Dependabot open-pull-requests-limit default 5, ignore rules, grouping, cooldown, security updates exempt (docs.github.com dependabot options reference, VERIFIED); Renovate prConcurrentLimit, prHourlyLimit, ignoreDeps, dependency dashboard approval (docs.renovatebot.com configuration-options, VERIFIED); Linear Triage: Accept, Decline with reason, Mark duplicate, Snooze (linear.app/docs/triage, VERIFIED); Devin Knowledge suggestions are edited or rejected by a human before saving (docs.devin.ai knowledge, VERIFIED). Claude Code /loop expires recurring tasks after 7 days and a bare loop 'does not start new initiatives outside that scope' (code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks, VERIFIED).
- ADR/MADR: status proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded by ADR-N, plus a 'Confirmation' section saying how compliance is verified (github.com/adr/madr template, VERIFIED).
NOT COVERED or not verifiable: Factory, LangGraph/AutoGen planner-executor, Jira goals, OKR design, CodeScene hotspots, import-linter contract types, Devin scheduled sessions, Copilot proactive tasks, defeasible-logic literature (used only as a pattern: default holds unless a recorded defeater), AI-product-owner tools (search snippets only).

DESIGN FACTS used: precedence org floor (override none) > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle (warn, deviate) > preference (advisory); goals never constrain, they steer ranking and discovery. Soft rules fail by silence, so a principle's finding must be answered (comply or deviate with a reason) before complete, and repeated deviations trigger a review of the principle (existing revisit-trigger mechanism). Proposal flood is controlled by an open cap (Dependabot default 5), a per-run cap, backpressure when the cap is reached, a rejected-ideas memory (Linear decline, Dependabot ignore) and a circuit breaker on zero-accept runs (B-sched-run).
data.falsifier: Falsified if, after at least 3 discovery runs and 20 completed items under principles (task B-goal-eval): proposal acceptance stays under 10 percent (ideas are noise), or rejected ideas are re-proposed, or principle deviation rate is above 30 percent or the answered-finding rate is below 90 percent (soft rules are either wrong or ignored), or goal progress cannot be computed from the DAG for the first real goals.
data.mechanism: A principle differs from a rule only in how a finding is cleared (deviate by an agent with a reason, versus waive by a person with an expiry), so the existing waiver and review-trigger machinery carries it; a goal is a measurable target whose progress is computed from the DAG, metrics and approved checks (unavailable never counts as progress); a proposal is a record outside the queue until a person adopts it, so the scheduler and next never see unadopted ideas.

data.question: How should goals, defeasible principles, strict rules and periodic feature proposals be modelled in ddflow, reusing the guidance, waiver, record, schedule and research engines, given what comparable tools do?

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim, also recorded as a session prompt): "Separately, Is there a way for a workflow management engine to follow project goals (have the concept of goals) and automatically research periodically what next features might be needed and suggest that, while separately follow common principles for the project which are some sort of a weak rule, which defines what we prefer to do unless there is a better reason, and then we have a set of strict or unstrict as defined rules, which have to be followed? ... propose features or fill-up gaps, investigate if for those features we could use the already existing internals and rules + decisions + architectural decisions engines implemented or planned to be implemented and add a phase + tasks for us to do them."

Evidence: R-goals-existing-map (CONFIRMED: what exists and what the attached document got wrong) and R-goals-principles-proposals-design (THEORETICAL: survey of Kiro, Spec Kit, Claude Code, Cursor, Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Dependabot, Renovate, Jules, Linear, SonarQube, ArchUnit, MADR, RFC 2119, and the design).

DESIGN IN ONE PARAGRAPH (nothing here is a parallel store):
- RULES (strict or unstrict) are the guidance engine's rule and decision records: enforcement block | warn | advisory, checks, waivers, review_by. Already built in services/guidance; P-decisions finishes and wires them. This phase adds nothing to what a rule IS.
- PRINCIPLES are NOT a new kind. A principle is a guidance record (a decision or a rule) whose OVERRIDE MODE is deviate: follow it unless you record a reason. A rule is override=waive (a person approves, scoped, at most 90 days, D-decision-management) or none (an org floor). RFC 2119 vocabulary: MUST = block + waive|none, SHOULD = warn + deviate, MAY = advisory. A finding against a SHOULD must be answered (comply or deviate with a reason) before the item completes; repeated deviations flag the principle for review. That feedback loop is what keeps a soft rule from silently vanishing or silently becoming hard.
- GOALS are a new definition-record kind (def.* events, record surface, search, history, upcasters come free): a title, an owner, a status, linked phases/tasks/decisions, and key results with a measurable source (dag progress, a ddflow metric, an approved check command, or a dated manual attestation that goes stale). Progress is computed, never typed. A goal never overrides a rule; it steers what the brief shows, what discovery proposes and what the roadmap displays.
- PROPOSALS (periodic feature discovery) are a second new def-record kind that lives OUTSIDE the queue until a person adopts it, so next/claim never see an unreviewed idea. A shipped, opt-in schedule job files ONE research item per run whose output is at most K proposals, each citing a goal, evidence, a principle check, a size estimate and a dedupe result against the board AND against rejected proposals. Adopt/defer/reject (with reason) are person-only. Caps, backpressure, a circuit breaker and a rejected-ideas memory prevent idea spam.
- PRECEDENCE: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; the nearest scope wins within a tier; goals never constrain.

Order: decide -> {deviation, cites, goal model} -> {progress, proposal model} -> {inject, discover} -> report -> acceptance -> eval. Held behind the P-gaps core, the docs wave and P-decisions (D-old-work-behind-core-docs): it builds on the decision engine tasks B-dec-model, B-dec-waivers, B-dec-monitor, B-dec-review, on B-research-items and the schedule tasks, and on B-gap-metrics.

Extends (does not duplicate): B-dec-model, B-dec-waivers, B-dec-review, B-rules-onto-record-surface, B-rm-template, B-research-items, B-sched-defaults, B-sched-escalation, B-gap-metrics, B-org-kinds, B-org-policy (each got a marked paragraph on 2026-10-11).
data.title: Goals, principles and proposals on the guidance engine: defeasible principles with recorded deviations, measurable goals injected into the brief, and periodic feature discovery that proposes and never queues

data.body:
Ask the operator, record the decision, write docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md. Ask them one at a time with the recommended default; record each answer verbatim (ddflow session prompt) and as a decision (ddflow decision add --globs ...). Do not start any other B-goal-* or B-prop-* task before this is answered.

QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS (evidence: R-goals-existing-map, R-goals-principles-proposals-design):
1. Is a principle a new kind or a field? DEFAULT: a field, not a kind. Add one field to the guidance record, override = none | waive | deviate (how a finding is cleared), orthogonal to enforcement (how hard a finding is). Principle = enforcement warn + override deviate; rule = block + waive; org floor = block + none; preference = advisory. Vocabulary shown to people: MUST / SHOULD / MAY (RFC 2119) next to the enforcement word. Rejected: a separate principle store (a second engine to keep in step), and enforcement alone (a warn finding needs no answer, so a soft rule fails by silence).
2. Who may deviate from a principle, and does it expire? DEFAULT: the authoring agent records a deviation, item-scoped, reason required (evidence optional), no approval, no expiry (it dies with the item), always visible in brief, completion summary and the operator's decision list. Only block rules need a person's waiver (up to 90 days, approved by digest, unchanged). A deviation from a principle on a CHECK-LESS record (judged by a reviewer) is accepted the same way.
3. Must a principle finding be answered before complete? DEFAULT: yes for SHOULD with a mechanical check or a reviewer finding that cites the id; complete refuses (exit 3) listing the unanswered ones; an answer is comply (fixed) or deviate (reason). MAY findings never refuse. Gate OUTCOME stays passed (a principle is not a blocker); the ledger carries the answer.
4. Precedence order. DEFAULT: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; nearest scope (gate, then globs, then category, then always) wins within a tier, then priority, then newest; unreconciled conflicts are a doctor note and a B-coh item, never a silent pick. Goals never override a rule or a principle. Extends D-rules-hierarchy (workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults); it does not replace it.
5. Goal record shape. DEFAULT: def-record kind goal; fields title, body, status (proposed | active | achieved | dropped), owner, target_date, parent (at most 2 levels), links (phases, tasks, decisions, research), key_results[] each {id, text, source = dag | metric | check | manual, ref, baseline, target, direction}. Progress is computed: dag = done share of the linked phases' tasks (tasks weighted equally; a removed or abandoned task leaves the count); metric = a named ddflow metric (B-gap-metrics); check = a command through the shared runner, operator-config or approved by digest only; manual = an operator attestation with a date that goes STALE after [goals].manual_stale_days (default 30) and is then reported unavailable, never green. Overall goal progress = the minimum-of-trajectory view is NOT used; show each KR and their mean, marked an estimate.
6. What does the brief show of goals? DEFAULT: at most 3 lines (active goals by priority: title, mean KR progress, weakest KR, days to target, stale flag), plus at claim the item's goal chain (task -> phase -> goal) labelled Direction, not a constraint; orphan work (completed items under no goal) counted in the roadmap and doctor, never a gate.
7. Proposal storage and triage states. DEFAULT: def-record kind proposal outside the queue (status proposed | adopted | deferred (snooze_until) | rejected | expired | superseded); adopt creates a task through services/items.add_task (dup check included) in a phase the operator names and links back; adopt/defer/reject are person-only (CLI; no MCP verb, like ddflow approve); reject REQUIRES a reason and is remembered: a new proposal whose fingerprint or similarity matches a rejected one is not filed unless it carries new evidence the operator can see. Rejected: proposal as a task state (every scheduler, board and next path would need to learn it), and proposal as a research record (no adopt/reject lifecycle).
8. Discovery cadence and budget. DEFAULT: OFF until the operator turns it on (job feature_discovery shipped disabled); then weekly by the calendar, or every 2 completed phases, whichever the operator picks; per run at most 3 new proposals; at most 7 open (proposed, undecided) at any time, and the job does not run while the cap is reached (backpressure); at most 20 000 reviewed tokens per run when B-gap-spend can measure it (UNAVAILABLE, not zero, when it cannot, and then the run cap is the turn cap); circuit breaker after 3 consecutive runs with zero adopted proposals (job pauses and says so in brief); stale undecided proposals expire after 60 days. The job files ONE research item (kind research) through the normal claim, so any lane may take it and quotas apply.
9. What may discovery read? DEFAULT: the repository, the ddflow log, its own research records, dependency advisories through the configured companions; the web ONLY if the operator enabled [discovery].web (default false); the log redaction profile is applied to every proposal body; no file contents above 40 lines are quoted. Org policy may force web off.
10. Scope. DEFAULT: goals and principles may come from an org bundle (P-org-config) as read-only team goals/principles; a project may add its own and cannot deviate from an org floor; proposals and deviations are always local to the project log; personal (local-only) goals are allowed under .ddflow/local and never reach the brief of other users.
11. Evaluation gate for turning discovery on by default. DEFAULT: never on by default; recommend turning on after B-goal-eval reports >= 3 runs with acceptance in 20-70 percent.

ACCEPTANCE: the answers are recorded as a decision with the reasons; the doc lists every question with the answer; the dependent tasks' bodies are amended if an answer differs from the default (ddflow update). Tests: none (docs only); gates: research, rules, docs.
SIZE: small. DOCS: docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md.
data.title: Operator decisions for goals, principles and proposals: principle as a field, deviation semantics, precedence, goal record shape, proposal states, discovery cadence and budget, scope
