data.body:
WHAT: make a principle real. (1) The override field (none | waive | deviate) on the guidance record and its fold/file format/definition fields, with MUST/SHOULD/MAY shown beside the enforcement word in every door (brief, claim, gate status, review prompt) by guidance/inject.py (_line tags). (2) A deviation: ddflow decision deviate <id> --item <item> --reason "..." [--evidence ...] and its twin on the MCP decision tool; stored as a waiver record in mode deviation (B-dec-waivers); item-scoped, no approval, no expiry, reason required. (3) The completion check: ddflow complete refuses (exit 3, naming each) while a finding against a record with override=deviate is neither fixed nor deviated; a finding is a failing mechanical check result (checks.gate_verdict warnings) or a reviewer finding that cites the id (B-goal-cites). A SHOULD that has neither check nor citation is never a finding; a MAY never refuses. (4) precedence.py: the one function that orders applicable records (org floor > rule > decision > principle > preference; scope; priority) and reports an unreconciled conflict instead of picking silently; inject.rank_key calls it. (5) A deviation is shown to the operator: brief line 'deviations since your last look', decision list column, completion summary.
WHY (evidence, R-goals-existing-map): decisions already default to warn, but a warn finding requires no answer (checks.Verdict.warnings never changes the outcome), and a waiver needs a person and expires within 90 days (D-decision-management) - right for a rule, too heavy for a preference, so people will skip it and a soft rule fails by silence. RFC 2119 SHOULD is exactly 'valid reasons to ignore, carefully weighed'; Spec Kit records deviations as justified entries (Complexity Tracking); no verified tool combines reason + expiry + approver, ddflow's waiver already does for the strict case.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{record,deffields,inject,checks,waivers}.py, B-dec-model (override field lands in the decision v2 events and its upcaster; this task wires behaviour), B-dec-waivers (storage), B-dec-monitor (the decisions gate), services/completion.py (the existing refusal list), core.provenance for fencing. No new event kind unless B-dec-waivers did not carry the mode (then register it with its first writer).
HOW TO TEST (failing first): a SHOULD with a failing check: complete refuses; after deviate it passes and the summary lists the deviation; a MUST with the same check blocks the gate and deviate does NOT clear it (only waive does); deviate on a MUST refused with the reason; a MAY never refuses; precedence table test (every pair of tiers, scope tie-break, priority tie-break) and an unreconciled pair reported; fold/replay of an old log with no override field gives block->waive, warn/advisory->deviate; tool parity test; budget: pinned MUST text never trimmed (existing test unchanged).
SIZE: large (~600 lines + tests); the completion refusal and inject tags are the risk.

WHAT: compute goal progress and the goal gap, never store it. (1) A registry of key-result evaluators (same shape as guidance/checks.py: register(kind, fn), a result is value | unavailable with a reason, an evaluator that cannot run is UNAVAILABLE and never counts as progress): dag (done share of the tasks under the linked phases/tasks, from the folded state and core.graph; removed and abandoned tasks excluded; also the number open, blocked and ready), metric (a named metric from B-gap-metrics: open bugs, review rounds per item, cycle time, gate skip rate, plus a provider hook so other services register more), check (an approved command through services/cmdrunner: exit code or a numeric last line, timeouts, unavailable on error), manual (value + attestation date; stale after [goals].manual_stale_days). (2) ddflow goal status [id] [--json]: per goal each KR with baseline, current, target, progress percent, trend since the last reading (readings are cached in .ddflow/local, derived and disposable), staleness, and an estimate flag; overall = mean of KR progress, marked an estimate. (3) The GOAL GAP signal, advisory and bounded: an active goal that has an unmet KR and no open, ready or in-flight linked task; a KR whose trajectory misses target_date by the throughput estimate (B-gap-metrics forecast; says not enough data under the minimum sample); a manual KR gone stale; linked phases all done while a KR is unmet (the plan was complete but the goal is not). The signal is a list of reasons per goal, shown by goal status, doctor and (B-goal-inject) the brief; it files nothing and blocks nothing.
WHY: Linear's initiative health is a human-written update (verified), a GitHub milestone is closed/total, Sonar is a numeric threshold on new code, a fitness function is an executable goal: the measurable ones are all counts or thresholds. ddflow already knows the DAG and the log (R-gaps-evidence: 667 items, cycle-time distribution), so progress is a projection. Unmeasurable or hand-typed progress is the known failure (goal gaming, stale green).
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core/graph.py and core/schedule.py (closure, readiness), core/progress.py aggregation, B-gap-metrics service and forecast, services/cmdrunner.py + approval.py, core/clock.py (tests inject time), services/guidance/checks.py as the pattern (do not subclass it: a KR is not a guidance check).
HOW TO TEST: fixture DAG with 3 phases of known done counts: dag KR equals hand-computed value; removing a task changes the denominator; an unavailable metric yields unavailable not 0; a check KR with a failing command is unavailable with the reason; a stale manual KR is reported stale and excluded from the mean; gap reasons each fire on a purpose-built fixture and none fires on a healthy one; fake clock; status identical on CLI and MCP.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: on this repository with one real goal (for example 'P-unify accepted and pushed') ddflow goal status gives the same percent as ddflow board for the linked phase.

WHAT: the proposal record and its triage. Def kind proposal (core/defs.py) and a RecordKind PROPOSAL (api/records.py) so ddflow proposal list|show|add|edit|search and ONE MCP tool ddflow_proposal exist from the descriptor, plus the triage verbs as ops: adopt, defer, reject, snooze. Fields: title, body (problem, evidence, acceptance, globs, size in S/M/L, estimated tokens), goal (a goal id; may be empty only for proposals tagged maintenance), evidence (research ids/claim ids, metric readings, advisory ids, file:line), principles_checked (ids + comply|deviate|n/a), fingerprint (normalised title + globs digest), source (job id + run key or agent), status (proposed | adopted | deferred | rejected | expired | superseded), decided_by, decision_reason, snooze_until, adopted_as (a task id). Rules: (1) a proposal is NOT a queue item: next, claim, board and status never see it (they read items); (2) adopt <id> --phase P creates a task through services/items.add_task (the one way a task is created, add-time duplicate check included), copies globs and body, links both ways, and records adopted_as; the operator may edit the body first; (3) adopt, defer, reject are PERSON-ONLY: the CLI verbs exist, the MCP tool offers add/edit/list/show/search only and the exemption is a field in surfaces/exemptions.py with that reason (same precedent as ddflow approve); an agent may add a proposal; (4) reject requires --reason; a rejected proposal stays in the log and is checked at every add: a new proposal whose fingerprint matches or whose similarity (services/similar) is at least [proposals].reject_floor to a rejected or deferred-not-due one is refused with the old id and reason, unless the new one cites evidence the old did not (the evidence list is diffed); (5) defer needs snooze_until; the proposal reappears in the list on that date; (6) undecided proposals expire after [proposals].expire_days (default 60) to status expired (kept); (7) an MCP resource ddflow://proposals (open proposals, newest first, bounded) next to ddflow://research, which stays the research log; (8) every proposal body goes through the log redaction profile and is fenced as data wherever shown.
WHY: R-goals-existing-map: nothing like it exists (ddflow://research renders findings with verdicts, not proposals; the paper's ddflow_feature_propose / ddflow_proposal_triage / task adopt do not exist). Jules suggested tasks, Dependabot, Renovate and Linear Triage all keep suggestions OUT of the work queue until a person accepts, offer decline-with-reason, snooze and duplicate, and remember ignores; idea spam is the failure they all cap. B-research-items files tasks directly from a verdict, which is right for the operator's own research and wrong for unattended discovery.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/records.py + surfaces/records.py (one tool per kind; check tools/list budget test), core/defs.py + upcasters, services/items.add_task, services/similar.py and api/_dedupe.py (closed-match semantics of B-coh-readd-closed, reversed here: a rejected match is NOT re-added), services/approval.py not needed, surfaces/exemptions.py, surfaces/mcp.py RESOURCES.
HOW TO TEST (failing first): adopt creates exactly one task and links it, a second adopt refused; next/board unchanged by 50 open proposals; reject without reason refused; re-proposing a rejected idea is refused naming the rejection; the same idea with new evidence is filed and linked as supersedes; snooze hides until the fake-clock date; expiry; MCP tool has no adopt verb (parity exemption test); replay identical.
SIZE: medium-large (~600 lines + tests). Shares core/defs.py and api/records.py with B-goal-model (serialised by needs).
ACCEPTANCE: scenario in B-goal-acceptance.
DOCS: README 'Proposals', help topic goals.

WHAT: periodic discovery of next features that proposes and never queues. (1) A shipped, DISABLED-by-default schedule job feature_discovery (a schedule definition, templates/schedules/feature-discovery.toml, due by calendar days or by completed phases, overridable like every shipped job; D-sched-no-daemon: due state is computed on commands, a trigger such as cron or /loop is pluggable). (2) When due it files ONE research item (kind research, B-research-items pipeline) through the normal queue and claim - never an agent run of its own (D-trigger-actions-create-items) - with a rendered prompt (templates/prompts/commands/discover.md, overridable). The prompt: read the active goals' gap reasons (B-goal-progress), the open and done board, decisions and principles, advisories, hotspots from the log (files with many bug fixes), the lessons and research already recorded, then propose at most K proposals, each with goal, evidence, acceptance, globs, size, and a principle check. (3) Budgets and brakes, all knobs under [discovery]: max_new_per_run (3), max_open (7: the job does NOT run, and says so in brief, while this many proposals await a decision - backpressure), run token cap when B-gap-spend can measure (else a turn cap; unavailable is reported, never zero), circuit breaker (3 consecutive runs with no adopted proposal pauses the job: B-sched-run), per-run wall time, web off by default. (4) Filtering BEFORE the operator sees anything (proposals/dedupe.py): drop or merge a candidate similar to an open task, a done task, an open or rejected or deferred proposal, a decision (it was decided), or a lesson; a candidate that violates a MUST rule is dropped, one that conflicts with a SHOULD is kept with the conflict shown; a candidate with no goal link and not tagged maintenance is dropped; a candidate with no evidence is dropped. The counts of dropped candidates per reason are recorded in the run, so tuning is data. (5) The run output is written with proposal add; the run is complete when the research item's verdict (what was scanned, what was dropped and why) is recorded; the brief carries one line 'N proposals await a decision' while any are open.
WHY: Jules (suggested tasks: periodic scan, cards, dismissal feedback, daily caps), Dependabot (open-pull-requests-limit 5, ignore, grouping, cooldown), Renovate (prConcurrentLimit, dashboard approval, ignoreDeps) and Linear Triage (decline with reason, duplicate, snooze) all verify that unattended discovery is only usable with an open cap, a decline memory, dedupe and an approval step; the LLM idea-spam failure is unbounded generation. ddflow already has the due engine (cadence.py; architecture_review is a count pass today with no template, B-architecture-pass), job templates (B-sched-defaults), caps and expiry for job-created items (B-sched-escalation), the run record with a circuit breaker (B-sched-run) and research items that file results (B-research-items). The paper's 'ddflow_cadence claims a research worker and emits proposal_created to ddflow://research' does not exist; the real flow is due job -> research item -> proposals.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/schedule.py and cadence.py (job definition, run key, missed policy skip), B-sched-run (render, run record, budget caps, circuit breaker, dedupe key), B-sched-escalation (open caps and expiry; proposals counted under their own cap), B-research-items (kind research item whose verdict files results; proposal mode below), services/similar.py, B-goal-progress gap reasons, B-gap-spend, services/contextpack.py for the evidence the prompt carries, core.redact.
HOW TO TEST: fake clock + stub researcher: a due job files exactly one research item; max_open reached: no item, brief says why; 5 candidates, 3 filed, 2 dropped with reasons recorded; a candidate equal to a rejected proposal is dropped; a candidate violating a MUST is dropped and the count says so; three runs with no adoption pause the job; disabled by default (a fresh project files nothing); no agent process is spawned (monkeypatch proc to fail); web off means no network access.
SIZE: large (~700 lines + templates + tests). Hot shared files templates/schedules/** and prompts/commands/**: wait for B-sched-defaults.
ACCEPTANCE: scenario in B-goal-acceptance; B-goal-eval measures acceptance on real runs.
DOCS: README 'Proposals'; help topic goals; driver notes (the agent that takes the discovery item: what it may read, how many it may file, how to cite evidence).

WHAT: the feedback loop and the numbers. (1) services/guidance/adherence.py: per guidance record over a window: applicable items completed, findings (mechanical + cited), answered by compliance, answered by deviation, unanswered at completion (should be 0), waivers, deviation rate = deviations / applicable items, and for proposals: proposed, adopted, deferred, rejected, expired, acceptance rate = adopted / decided, time to decision, adopted-then-completed and adopted-then-bug rate (rework), rejected-then-reproposed count (must be 0). Goals: KR progress delta per week, goals with a gap reason, stale KRs. (2) Register them as providers in B-gap-metrics (ddflow metrics --group-by guidance|goal) and add ddflow goal report [--window 30d] [--json] on CLI and MCP (one more action of the goal tool, not a new tool). (3) Register the revisit trigger repeated-deviation with guidance/review.register_trigger: a live record with override=deviate whose deviation rate over the last [goals].review_window_items (default 10) applicable items is at least [goals].deviation_review_rate (default 0.3), or at least 3 deviations by 2 different agents, becomes DUE for review: ddflow decision review (B-dec-review) offers reaffirm (the principle stands; the deviations were legitimate), change (narrow its globs, rewrite it, or demote it to MAY) or promote (make it MUST with a check); it never changes itself. A principle with zero applicable items in 90 days is reported unused (candidate to retire). (4) The proposal acceptance trigger: 3 consecutive runs under 10 percent acceptance pause the job and file a needs_operator note (B-sched-escalation) to tune the prompt or retire it.
WHY: soft rules die by silence (Windsurf documents auto-captured memories as the weak, unversioned tier; Claude Code docs say conflicting CLAUDE.md instructions are resolved arbitrarily and ship an audit command) and generators die by noise. The loop (deviations feed a review, rejections feed the generator) is the part no surveyed tool offers; it needs numbers to be tunable and to be falsifiable (B-goal-eval).
INTERFACE TO REUSE: B-gap-metrics (providers, group-by, forecast, minimum sample says 'not enough data', exit 2 not a number), B-goal-cites (counts), B-goal-deviation (records), B-prop-model (statuses), B-dec-review (review record and reminder budget), B-sched-run/escalation (pause, needs_operator).

data.body:
Acceptance for P-goals, end to end on a throwaway repository with a fake clock and a stub researcher (no network, no real model):
1. A MUST rule with a mechanical check (a forbidden import) blocks the decisions gate; deviate is refused; only an approved waiver clears it for at most 90 days and it resurfaces on the day after expiry.
2. A SHOULD principle with a check: a diff that violates it makes complete refuse listing it; ddflow decision deviate --item ... --reason ... lets the item complete; the completion summary and the brief show the deviation; a MAY never refuses.
3. A reviewer finding citing [id] is stored with cites; a cited id that was not sent is flagged.
4. Five deviations by two agents in ten items make the principle due for review (ddflow decision review); reaffirm moves review_by, change files a superseding PROPOSED decision for the operator; nothing changes by itself.
5. A goal with three key results (dag, metric, manual): progress equals the hand-computed value; the manual KR goes stale on the fake clock and drops out of the mean; the goal gap lists 'no open work toward an unmet KR'; the brief shows the goal in at most 3 lines and drops it first under a tiny budget while a pinned MUST stays whole; the claim of a task under the linked phase prints the goal chain as direction.
6. Discovery (enabled for the test): the due job files one research item; the stub files 5 candidates; 3 become proposals, 2 are dropped (one equal to a rejected proposal, one violating a MUST); the cap of open proposals stops the next run and the brief says why; adopt creates one task, reject records its reason, and re-proposing the rejected idea is refused naming the rejection; three runs with no adoption pause the job. next/board never listed a proposal.
7. An org bundle carrying a floor principle (override none) cannot be deviated from by the project; project-level goals/principles layer on top; proposals and deviations stay local.
8. CLI and MCP bodies are identical for goal, proposal, deviate and report; the tools/list budget test passes; README, help topic goals and the implement-phase driver (both copies) updated.

data.title: Acceptance for goals, principles and proposals: a strict rule blocks, a principle is deviated from with a reason, goals show in the brief, discovery proposes within caps and never re-proposes a rejection; README, help topic, driver notes

data.body:
Evaluation: does the feature earn its place? Turn it on for this project (operator opt-in) after B-goal-acceptance, collect real data, and record a verdict.
MEASURE (from ddflow goal report, B-goal-report; thresholds are INITIAL HYPOTHESES to calibrate, and the verdict may change them with a reason):
- Proposals: at least 3 discovery runs. Healthy acceptance (adopted / decided) 20-70 percent. Under 10 percent over 3 runs: the generator is noise (change the prompt or turn it off). Over 80 percent: the cap or the filter is too tight, or ideas are too safe. Median time to decision under 14 days or the operator is not reading them (lower the cap). Rejected-then-reproposed must be 0. Adopted tasks completed without a later bug in at least 70 percent of cases (a measure of quality, not only of interest).
- Principles: at least 20 completed items under SHOULD records. Unanswered at completion is 0 (the refusal works). Deviation rate per principle between 2 and 25 percent: above 30 means the principle is wrong or too broad (change or demote), 0 over 30 applicable items with findings present means a check that never fires or a principle nobody meets (look at it, maybe retire), no findings and no applicable items means unused. Count how many deviations the operator later judged illegitimate.
- Goals: the first real goals have computable progress (no hand-typed value); at least one goal gap reason led to an item that moved a KR; the brief goal lines were read (operator says so) and cost under 3 lines.
- Cost: tokens per discovery run (B-gap-spend or the turn cap), added brief tokens, added seconds on claim/complete, support burden (needs_operator notes created).
DECISION RULE: keep (as is), tune (names the knobs and values), or remove (discovery and/or principle semantics off, records kept). The verdict is a recorded decision citing the numbers, a research record with CONFIRMED figures, and the shipped defaults updated if they change. Falsifier (R-goals-principles-proposals-design): acceptance under 10 percent, a re-proposed rejection, deviation above 30 percent, or answered-findings below 90 percent.
DELIVERABLES: services/goals/eval.py (a function that evaluates the thresholds from the report and prints keep|tune|remove with the failing thresholds), a shipped monthly review job goals_eval (disabled until discovery is enabled), docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-evaluation.md (the verdict, written after the data exists), tests with a synthetic report for each branch.
SIZE: small code; the calendar time is the cost (weeks). It can only complete once the data exists: if it does not, record the gate unavailable with the reason, never passed.

WHAT: the goal record. Register def kind goal in core/defs.py (DEF_KINDS) and declare a RecordKind GOAL in api/records.py so ddflow goal list|show|add|edit|remove|search|revise and ONE MCP tool ddflow_goal exist from the descriptor (D-unify 4; tools/list budget: this is one of the ~8 remaining tools, tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py). Fields: title, body, status (proposed | active | achieved | dropped), owner, target_date, parent (a goal id, depth at most 2), links (phase, task, decision, research ids), key_results (a list of tables {id, text, source = dag|metric|check|manual, ref, baseline, target, direction up|down|reach}). DOCS NOTE: the README tool-table row comes from python -m ddflow.surfaces.tool_table in this task; the prose is written by B-goal-acceptance.

CONFIG (added by the filer): this task also declares the three config sections the phase needs, so no later task edits ddflow/config.py: [goals] (manual_stale_days = 30, review_window_items = 10, deviation_review_rate = 0.3, max_depth = 2), [proposals] (reject_floor, expire_days = 60, max_open = 7) and [discovery] (enabled = false, every_days / every_phases, max_new_per_run = 3, web = false, token_cap, turn_cap, breaker_runs = 3). Each is a knob() with doc and, for enums, the strictest fallback (D-enum-fallback-strict). Later tasks edit only their own section file.

Extend Decision with: category (from the configured list); owner (a person, team or CODEOWNERS entry); enforcement (advisory | warn | block); review_by (a date); revisit_on (trigger names such as dependency-major, repeated-violation, contradicting-research, org-change); links to research, tasks, bugs and other decisions; and checks (a list of typed check specs, B-dec-checks). Statuses gain deprecated, retired and rejected; live means accepted. Every change is recorded through B-uni-def-records (recorded, updated, retired, superseded), and an upcaster (B-uni-compat-events) maps existing decision.recorded events with no loss. Tests: fold and replay of old and new events, and status transitions with who may make them.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals (operator request on goals, principles and rules; R-goals-principles-proposals-design): add ONE field to the decision v2 record and to GuidanceRecord/deffields: override = none | waive | deviate (how a finding is cleared; enforcement stays how hard it is). Upcaster default: enforcement block -> waive, warn or advisory -> deviate. A principle is a decision (or rule) with override=deviate; MUST/SHOULD/MAY (RFC 2119) is only the label shown next to the enforcement word. Declare it here, while the decision events are being versioned, so P-goals does not need a second upcaster; the behaviour (deviation records, the completion refusal, precedence) is B-goal-deviation. Do not add a separate principle kind.

A waiver is a record linked to the decision and check, with scope globs, a reason, an expiry (maximum from D-decision-management) and approval through B-uni-approval. A waived finding passes the gate with 'waived' visible in gate status, brief and the completion summary. An expired waiver makes the finding live again and notifies in brief and doctor. `ddflow decision waive|waivers|unwaive` on CLI and MCP. A proposal to change the decision instead is a proposed superseding decision for the operator, never automatic.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the waiver record carries a mode, approved (as above: person, scope globs, expiry at most 90 days) or deviation (recorded by the authoring agent for a record whose override is deviate: item-scoped, reason required, evidence optional, no approval, no expiry). One storage and one display path, so brief, gate status and the completion summary list both. A deviation can NOT clear a finding on a record with override waive or none (refused with the reason). The CLI verb for a deviation (ddflow decision deviate) and the completion refusal are B-goal-deviation; this task only makes the record able to hold the mode.

`ddflow decision status` lists, per category: live decisions, those with checks, compliance (pass/fail/unavailable/waived), stale ones (review_by passed), triggered revisits and open waivers. Doctor and brief carry budgeted reminders. A periodic 'decision review' job files one task per due decision. `decision review <id> --reaffirm|--change` records the outcome. Contradicting research is routed to the operator through B-rw-vs-decision.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the revisit triggers named above gain repeated-deviation (a record with override=deviate whose deviation rate over its last N applicable items, or deviations by 2 different agents, passes a configured rate). The trigger is registered by B-goal-report through guidance/review.register_trigger; the review record and its outcomes (reaffirm, change, plus promote to MUST or demote to MAY) are this task's. The per-category compliance report adds deviation and unanswered counts. Never automatic.

Re-filed by the 2026-10-10 reorganisation audit: part of B-uni-record-surface (done) was never delivered. api/records.py declares the RULE RecordKind but nothing generates the real `ddflow rule` group from it (api/records.py says it is wired to nothing until a family moves onto it; its named wire-in site, B-rules-cli, was removed on 2026-10-10 as 'already delivered', which covered the commands but not this). The original B-uni-record-surface asked that rules (and the knowledge kinds) move onto it and onto def-records, removing about 500 lines; the def-record half is done (B-uni-rules-import).

WHAT: wire api.records.RULE into the real CLI and tool table: `ddflow rule add|edit|list|show|remove|search|sync` and the rules MCP tool are generated from the descriptor, keeping the group word, every flag and every output byte (goldens, tests/test_rules_cli.py, tests/test_rules_surface.py, the tools/list budget). Delete the parallel code: RuleDedupAnswer and _cross_kind in api/rules.py, the hand-written handlers in surfaces/declared/rules.py, rules_manifest where the def view supersedes it. Then either declare lessons, bugs, items and research as RecordKinds, or record a decision that they stay hand-written, naming the duplicated blocks (api/decisions.py:90 vs api/items.py:507; api/knowledge/bugs.py:68 vs research.py:76); decisions are B-dec-manage's, research B-rw-query's, lessons and bugs B199's, so only items and viewers have no owner. Also add the two small things the original rule CLI body asked for and the registry pilot lacks: `rule list --state` (if rules have a state) and an incremental `rule tag add|remove` (today `rule edit --tags` replaces the whole list).
ACCEPTANCE: ddflow/ shrinks by the measured amount (about 500 lines was the estimate), all rule tests unchanged, one MCP tool for rules, the three duplicated definitions gone.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: api/records.py RULE declares only title, content, tags, scope, priority and globs, so ddflow rule add cannot set enforcement, override, status, owner, review_by, checks, links, categories or gates, although services/guidance/deffields.py stores them and the file format reads them (verified: ddflow rule add --help). When rules move onto the generated surface, add those fields to the descriptor (enforcement, override, status, owner, review_by, categories, gates, links as flags; checks as a file or TOML table argument) so a strict rule (MUST: block) and an unstrict one (SHOULD/MAY) can be created from the CLI and MCP, with the same dedupe and the same limits. Acceptance gains: ddflow rule add --enforcement block --override waive produces a rule that resolve/inject ranks as pinned when always-scope.

The template is the skeleton: Vision/Goals/Notes are plain user sections, Now/Next/Later/Graph/Changed are regions. This repo's ROADMAP is adopted with B-tpl-adopt and its hand-written parts kept.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: when goal records exist (B-goal-model), the template also carries a generated Goals region (ddflow-managed, named, hash-stamped like the others) listing active goals, their key results and computed progress, marked an estimate; the user's own Vision/Goals/Notes prose stays untouched and is never overwritten. The region is produced by B-goal-inject; this task only has to leave room for it (a named region slot) and keep the golden tests passing with and without goals.

Operator 2026-09-28: 'Could tasks be research tasks which could generate new phases and tasks by themselves?' Today items are phase|task with one task_pipeline for all; research is a gate and a separate record (ddflow research), and agents file follow-ups by hand (today's R-records -> B189-B193 and this phase). (a) per-tag pipelines ([gates.pipelines] research = ['research', 'probe', 'proposal', 'file']) so a research-tagged task never needs implement/merge; (b) its completion carries a research record (question, probe, verdict) and a proposal: tasks and phases with titles, globs, needs, priorities; (c) 'file' gate: proposed TASKS under existing phases are added automatically, linked back (source: research id); proposed PHASES and anything outward-facing wait on a human approval gate (reuse the B82 human gate); (d) a research item may propose further research items, with a depth/budget cap so it cannot recurse unbounded; (e) recall shows the chain research -> items. Test: completing a research item with a proposal of 2 tasks + 1 phase files the tasks, parks the phase for approval.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Verdict-bearing research items file tasks; the proposed tasks cite the claims (id@rev) that justify them; the item's research record is the claim container (B-rw-claims).

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: create the item with kind=<doc|research|job|bug> so it runs [gates].kind_pipelines.<kind> (config_sections/_kinds.py, services/gates/kinds.py); do not introduce a second pipeline selector. Item.kind is only "phase" | "task" in core/records.py today, so the first of the tasks that needs a non-task kind widens it (check whether another of B-dt-workflow, B-research-items, B-sched-run, B-bugs-as-items already did before adding it a second time).

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: a research item may end in PROPOSALS instead of tasks. Item (c) above files proposed tasks straight into the queue, which is right for the operator's own research and wrong for unattended discovery. Add a proposal mode to the file gate: when the item carries the discovery tag (set by the feature_discovery job, B-prop-discover), proposed tasks are written as proposal records (B-prop-model) and nothing is added to the queue until a person adopts one. The depth/budget cap in (d) also counts proposals. Same verdict-plus-proposal shape, one more destination.

Each default is a schedule definition (TOML) plus a jinja prompt; a project overrides either by file in .ddflow/schedules/ or .ddflow/prompts/commands/. All start in report-only mode with fix opt-in; dependency, security and architecture jobs always need operator approval before merge. Folds in B-security-pass, B-architecture-pass, B-dependency-upgrades and B-dupes-sweep as default jobs (their own tasks keep the gate/command pieces). ddflow schedule init lets the operator pick the set at onboarding. The pre-commit/CI-health job runs the ci command on main and escalates to the operator with the findings when it cannot fix them.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the shipped list does NOT include feature discovery; it is owned by B-prop-discover (a disabled-by-default job feature_discovery and a monthly goals_eval job, B-goal-eval) because it needs the proposal record and the goal engine. This task only has to guarantee that a project or a later task can add a shipped job template without editing the services (templates/schedules/<id>.toml is enough) and that the architecture_review count pass (a cadence name with no template today) maps to the template this task ships.

Failure modes from the research: noisy reports, stale PR pile-ups, a green run that hides a failed task, silent no-fire. A job that cannot finish a fix files a needs_operator item with what it tried and what it needs; the brief lists them first; approvals are recorded events.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the cap on open job-created items and the stale-item expiry also cover proposals, counted under their own cap ([proposals].max_open) so that unreviewed ideas can neither flood the queue nor hide behind it; 'N proposals await a decision' is a brief line like the needs_operator notices, and the dashboard of what jobs created lists proposals filed by the discovery job with their status (proposed, adopted, rejected).

WHAT: one log-derived metrics service and three views. `ddflow metrics [--phase P] [--since D]`: cycle time per item (started->completed), time per gate, review rounds per item, gate failure/skip/unavailable rates by gate and by reviewer, queue wait (ready->claimed), lease wait on glob conflicts, rework (completed items later hit by a bug), lane utilisation (working vs idle-with-ready). `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`: critical-path ETA and a P50/P90 range for a phase from measured per-kind cycle times and the dependency graph (simple bootstrap over observed durations; says 'not enough data' under a minimum sample; marked an estimate). `ddflow retro <id>`: the timeline of one item (claim, first gate, each review round, waits, merge) with the biggest gap named -- the answer to 'why was this task slow'. A skip audit: `gate skip` rate per gate with reasons, skips never followed by a later pass, skips by agent.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence from this log: median item 1.04 h, p90 2.8 h, max 31.8 h (n=667); rubber_duck and critic fail 860/849 times against 639/618 passes (every findings round is a failed event), so review rounds dominate wall time but nobody has the number per item; docs gate skipped 149 times against 25 passes (a gate the process routes around, B-docs-stage is the fix, the audit would have shown it earlier); 508 bugs against 850 completions. Three open tasks each plan their own replay: B-rm-changes (throughput ETA hint), B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics. Without a shared service that is three half-metrics. Langfuse/Inspect (R-gaps-survey) show the value of per-run traces and scores; ddflow's log already is the trace.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: the fold and the existing replay helpers in views/ and core/flowsignals.py; Command + Param declarations; core.graph critical_path; knowledge of clock.now (B-arch-clock-now) so tests are deterministic.
HOW TO TEST: golden output on a frozen mini-log fixture; forecast on a synthetic log with known durations lands inside the stated range in a seeded 1000-run test; retro names the injected slow gap; sparse data returns exit 2 'not enough data', never a number.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines + tests). Re-pointing B-rm-changes / B-af-headroom / B-sub-metrics is a decision for B-gap-decide (c), not part of this task.
ACCEPTANCE: the three commands work on CLI and MCP on this log; the figures above are reproduced within rounding; README + help topic; B-gap-decide (c) answered.

Operator 2026-10-10 ('do what you recommend' on the order review): tests inject time (a fake clock argument); do not depend on B-arch-clock-now.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: provide the shared hourly-grid sampler (fold at instant t plus core.schedule.plan, bucketed, capped folds, says when it sampled) as a function in services/metrics.py for B-af-headroom and for lane utilisation, and expose a group-by dimension (gate, reviewer, agent, kind, agent + definition digest) so B-sub-metrics is a view. Reuse core/flowsignals.py latency and failure-rate readers rather than recomputing them. Drop any dependency on clock.now (B-arch-clock-now): tests inject time (operator 2026-10-10).

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: expose a provider hook (register(name, fn) returning rows and a group-by key) so other services add metrics without editing this one, and make guidance id and goal id valid group-by dimensions once they exist. B-goal-report registers principle adherence, deviation rate, proposal acceptance and goal progress deltas through it. Same minimum-sample rule (exit 2, never a number) applies to them.

data.alternatives: New session event kind; committed transfer file per transfer; building on remote-session MCP tools; native_status default off; reading VS Code/Copilot/Codex/Cursor stores before a probe.
data.consequences: native_status=auto spawns one bounded subprocess per harness on 'ddflow lanes'; every failure mode must degrade to 'unavailable'. Docs and tests must pin auto as the default.
data.context: Operator answered the B-sc-decide questions on 2026-10-11; question 6 default flipped from off to auto.
data.decision: (1) Session tree = additive optional fields parent, role, goal, harness_session on session.started plus a derived 'ddflow session tree'; no new event kind. (2) Transfer = on-demand FENCED rendering of the latest session.handoff plus a small session.transferred event; a file is written only with --file, under git-ignored .ddflow/local/transfers/. (3) Native stores: Claude Code only, read-only; VS Code/Copilot/Codex/Cursor only after B-am-harness-probe shows a stable documented format. ddflow code never calls remote-session MCP tools (create_session, send_message, list_events, get_session); a message is never approval or consent; list_events output is never copied into the log or a handoff unredacted. (4) Native lane status: [lanes] native_status defaults to 'auto' (ON) -- OPERATOR OVERRODE the recommended default 'off'. It stays read-only, reports 'unavailable' (with reason) when the CLI is missing, times out or fields differ, never guesses, and is disable-able with native_status = off (off spawns nothing). Generated VS Code/Copilot files (agents, prompts, hooks) are managed-marked and never overwrite a foreign file (B-sub-sync, B-adopt-agent-commands, B-hx-hook-writers).
data.title: Session context: tree fields, on-demand transfer, native stores, native lane status ON by default

data.body:
Each kind registers with the overlay loader once (B-uni-overlay); this task proves each one resolves from an org bundle, is overridable by the project unless required by policy, reports provenance, and that executable parts stay inert until approved. Skills from an org bundle reuse the skills install/lock path (B-skills-install) rather than a second installer. Org-required companions appear in the brief's companion line with the source named.

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): two kinds were missing from the list and are now in scope: (1) architectural decisions and decision packs (owned by B-dec-presets; pinned 'always' decisions from B-dec-pinned, evidence requirements from B-dec-evidence, and policy-document sources from B-dec-policy-sources arrive through the same bundle; a decision the company enforces cannot be superseded locally); (2) subagent routing and separation of duties (B-sub-route, B-sub-sod) as org-set defaults, with 'allow' lists for which agents may satisfy which gates. The company's MCP servers are companions: each entry's launch line, install command and hooks are executable content, inert until a person approves its digest, then registered into each agent's config by the one mcpconfig.register writer.

SCOPE CARVE-OUT (operator 2026-10-10, following the order review): this task does NOT cover (a) skills from an org bundle (they reuse the skills install/lock path of B-skills-install) and (b) subagent roles, routing and separation-of-duties defaults with the 'allow' lists (B-sub-route, B-sub-sod). Both depend on tasks that run later (P-skills, P-subagents, rounds ~22-23) and would have pushed all of waves 3 and 4 back. They are moved to B-org-kinds-skills-subagents in P-subagents, which runs after those tasks. Every other kind in the list above is wired here as described.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: principles (decisions or rules with override=deviate), the override field itself, and goals are syncable kinds: an org bundle may carry team principles and team goals (read-only in the project, labelled with the source and revision in brief and doctor; a project adds its own on top). Proposals, deviations and discovery runs are never synced (local project log); the [discovery] knobs may be pinned or capped by policy (for example web = false). Personal goals under .ddflow/local never reach another user's brief.

Examples: floor review.min_other_family_reviewers=1; require gates.task_pipeline contains [critic, unit_tests]; pin enforce.commit_without_lease=block; allow companions=[roborev, codeguide-mcp]; allow reviewer models; require rules/security-baseline. A violating write from CLI, MCP, prompt or configure is refused (exit 3) naming the policy item, source and rev; a hand-edited file that violates is reported by doctor and, in enforce mode, claim/merge/complete refuse until fixed; audit mode only reports (brief + doctor). The four enforced kernel rules, human gates and D-reviewer-trust are re-expressed as shipped policy so the org layer extends one mechanism. A project-level policy file lets the operator lock a key locally the same way (generalising export disable --lock).

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): allow/require/pin items also cover: which companions and MCP servers may be proposed or registered (allow), which subagent roles must exist (require), which decisions are required and not supersedable locally (require), and which prompts or commands may not be overridden (pin).

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: a floor is a guidance record with enforcement block and override none; the project cannot waive or deviate from it, and the precedence function (B-goal-deviation) ranks it above project rules. 'Require' items may name principles (a company principle must exist and cannot be demoted to MAY locally); 'pin' covers [discovery].web and [proposals].max_open. Audit mode reports a local demotion instead of refusing it.

Ask the operator, then record a decision D-session-context in docs/ddflow/decisions/session-context.md. Nothing else in P-session-context is built before the answers (research R-session-context, R-session-context-adopt; request verbatim in the phase body).

WHY: VS Code (a session = workspace + changes + one main chat and user-prompted peer chats that start blank; fork/handoff/compaction move context only explicitly) and Claude (transcripts + --resume/--fork-session, agent teams, cross-session messaging, Projects = coordinator + threads sharing project instructions and memory but not history) show the same split ddflow already has: history stays private to a conversation; only curated records (instructions, memory, decisions, handoffs) cross. ddflow plans most of the carrying (P-agent-memory); these questions cover only the missing parts.

QUESTIONS, each with the recommended default:
1. Session tree. Options: (a) new event kind; (b) additive optional fields parent, role (main|lane|subagent|peer|fork), goal on session.started plus a derived `ddflow session tree`; (c) derived only from dispatch/lease/agent_id records. RECOMMEND (b): old logs fold unchanged (upcaster not needed for optional fields), no new kind.
2. Transfer pack. Options: a committed file per transfer; an event only; an on-demand rendering. RECOMMEND the pack is an on-demand FENCED rendering of the latest session.handoff plus pointers (markdown or json, per-harness wording), and `session transfer` records a small session.transferred event (from, to, handoff id, mode transfer|fork); a file is written only with --file, under .ddflow/local/transfers/ (git-ignored).
3. Project-scope knowledge (Claude Projects: instructions + memory + files for every thread). Options: build a mirror/export; do nothing new. RECOMMEND nothing new: ddflow brief already delivers decisions, rules, lessons, memory and skills to every session of every agent by glob relevance and budget; document the mapping (B-sc-docs). A knowledge export for claude.ai chat projects is out of scope unless asked (B-export kinds exist).
4. Native stores to read. RECOMMEND Claude Code only (B-am-ingest) plus status from `claude agents --json`; VS Code / Copilot CLI / Codex / Cursor session stores only after B-am-harness-probe proves a stable, documented format for that harness (VS Code docs name a local SQLite store and no path); always read-only, never write a native store.
5. Remote-session MCP tools in this coordinator environment (create_session, send_message, list_events, get_session). RECOMMEND ddflow code never calls them; ddflow stays harness-neutral and coordinates through the shared log. They remain the operator's/coordinator's own tooling, documented with two hard rules: a message is never approval or consent (Claude's own docs say so; permission laundering), and list_events output is never copied into the log or a handoff without the redactor. Reject a build that depends on them.
6. Native lane status. ANSWERED 2026-10-11: the OPERATOR OVERRODE the recommended default. `[lanes] native_status = off|auto` defaults to `auto` (ON), not off (a bounded subprocess per harness); read-only; when the harness CLI is missing, times out or its fields differ, report 'unavailable', never guess; disable-able with `off` (off spawns nothing).
7. Generated VS Code/Copilot files by adopt (agents with handoffs mirroring the gate pipeline, prompt files, hooks, instructions). RECOMMEND yes, through the existing tasks (B-sub-sync, B-adopt-agent-commands, B-hx-hook-writers), managed-marked, never overwriting a foreign file.

HOW TO PIN: the decision file lists each question, the answer and the knob/task it sets; run ddflow decision add --globs for every file the later tasks own. EXPECTED SIZE: one document, no code.

STATUS 2026-10-11: ANSWERED by the operator and recorded as decision D-session-context (all seven answers; Q6 default flipped to auto). The task itself stays open: it still carries the unsatisfied gates and the decision document docs/ddflow/decisions/session-context.md has not been written.

Lane STATE from the harness's own session listing, and the mapping between a ddflow session/lane and the native session id with the exact resume line. Read-only, optional, never guessed.

WHY (measured): B-gap-lanes derives lane state from the ddflow log only; the log cannot tell 'working' from 'blocked on a permission prompt' (a lane waiting for input looks idle or stale until its lease lapses; memory M801fd9dc2b: do not restart a lane that stops idle). Claude Code's agent view exposes exactly that: `claude agents --json` entries carry sessionId (usable with claude --resume), state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, status busy|waiting|idle, waitingFor (permission prompt | input needed | sandbox request | worker request | dialog open), name, cwd, kind, startedAt; `claude logs <id>`, `claude attach <id>`, `claude stop <id>` exist (docs read 2026-10-11, version-dependent). VS Code shows a similar status in its sessions list and badge, but its docs name no machine-readable store or path: not built on.

DESIGN (decision D-session-context Q4/Q6): services/nativesessions.py with one adapter per harness descriptor key [native_sessions] (command, json fields, resume_line template, verified date, record); only claude is filled from a live probe, every other harness is 'unavailable' until B-am-harness-probe proves it. `[lanes] native_status = off|auto` (default `auto` = ON, OPERATOR decision 2026-10-11 overriding the recommended off; `off` disables it and spawns nothing; strictness profiles may force off). When auto, `ddflow lanes` (B-gap-lanes) joins a lane to a native session by cwd + start time + the session id the SessionStart hook recorded (B-sc-tree harness_session), shows the native state next to the log state, and says 'native: unavailable (reason)' when the CLI is missing, times out (hard timeout, one subprocess, no daemon) or the payload shape changed. `ddflow session show` and `lanes brief` print the resume line (claude --resume <sessionId>). A native 'blocked/waitingFor' becomes a lane advise line ('lane U3 is waiting for a permission prompt: attach it, do not restart') - ddflow never answers the prompt, never sends keys, never stops a session.

NOT in scope: reading transcripts (B-am-ingest), spawning (B-gap-lanes prints the line, nothing runs it), the remote-session MCP tools.

PIN/TEST: recorded `claude agents --json` fixtures (tests/fixtures/harness/claude/agents.json, B-hx-conformance layout) incl. an unknown future field and a missing field; join golden; CLI absent/timeout/garbage gives 'unavailable' never a state; the default config resolves to auto (pin test); off mode spawns nothing (monkeypatch proc to fail); auto with the CLI absent degrades to 'unavailable' without error; no subprocess output reaches the log unredacted. EXPECTED SIZE: ~300 lines + tests.

data.text: make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project - mcp and cli interfaces, add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert, rag export interfaces and functionalities, so the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify, split, evidence is logged, sessions are automatically informed for changes, they retrieve brief on session start, and can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do

Please investigate for the option of the rules, and principles to manage the pipeline workflow or define how the pipeline workflow should work, to allow with such definitions, particular projects to have different or extended pipeline workflow, modified by the agent to match the principle or rule requirements?

data.summary: A REQUIRED gate is silently dropped for an item whose declared globs miss its [gate.X] applies_when: completion.verdict excludes not_applicable gates from the required check and status() counts them settled. The globs are agent-editable (ddflow update <id> --globs replaces them, no approval), and applies_when is judged on declared globs, not the diff. Repro (throwaway repo): [gate.unit_tests] applies_when=["src/**"]; task globs docs/x.md -> gate status prints "[-] unit_tests -- not applicable"; completion treats it as settled. Expected: a gates.required gate is never made not-applicable by declared globs alone (judge on the diff, record the evidence, or keep it owed). Found during the pipeline-requirements investigation 2026-10-11; the fix is owned by B-gate-when-globs (extended); its regression test must fail against current code.

data.claim: Today a project can shape its pipeline only through config: [gates].task_pipeline/phase_pipeline/promotion_pipeline/kind_pipelines (whole ordered lists per kind), [gate.<id>] definitions (command|prompt, reviewer, requires_evidence, applies_when on the item's DECLARED globs, needs_branch; required lives in [gates].required), and ddflow workflow pipeline|gate|drop (CLI and MCP, validated, dry-run; 'ask the operator' only in tool text). Nothing per glob/category/tag/rule: no rule, decision or principle influences the pipeline (guidance Scope.gates only selects which text is injected at a gate prompt). pipeline_for(item,cfg) is a pure function of (cfg, item.kind, promote_to); not_applicable is derived at read time from declared globs, not recorded. The four invariants are NOT a floor: unavailable-never-passed is structural (runner/outcomes), but require_outcome, agent.reviewer_family_must_differ, lessons.require_regression_test, gates.required and allow_skip_with_reason are plain knobs any writer (an agent over CLI or ddflow_configure) can flip with no approval; only gate.<id>.human and agent-written command reviewers are guarded (configwrite). Bug B-na-required-gate: a required gate becomes not-applicable by agent-editable declared globs.
data.falsifier: Refuted if a config write of gates.require_outcome=false were refused for an agent, or if a required gate stayed owed when applies_when misses.
data.mechanism: pipeline_for is the single selector (kind -> list); applies_when narrows per item from declared globs; completion.verdict reads status() so a not-applicable required gate is settled; invariants are knobs in config_sections/gates.py, agent.py, lessons.py with no policy tier until B-org-agent-guard.

(2) ddflow config gates.require_outcome false / agent.reviewer_family_must_differ false / lessons.require_regression_test false / gates.allow_skip_with_reason false / gates.required [] all accepted and written ([file]). data.claim: Pipeline requirements need no new store: ONE optional field `pipeline` on the existing guidance record (rule or decision, def.* events, record surface) names an effect on the effective pipeline of every item the record's Scope covers: require=[gate...] (additive, with optional after=), allow_na=[gate...] with a reason class, forbid_skip=[gate...], order=[[a,b]...], and kinds=[...] to restrict by item kind. Project-specific gates stay in [gate.<id>] (command gates are executable, so approved by digest, B-gap-command-trust). Strength reuses the P-goals pair enforcement x override: MUST (block, waive|none) = the gate cannot be dropped, skipped or made N/A; only a person's approved waiver (<=90 days, scoped) lifts it. SHOULD (warn, deviate) = the gate is added as recommended; an agent may record an item-scoped deviation with a reason, answered before complete. MAY = shown only. Resolution is a pure function effective_pipeline(cfg, item, records, diff_paths) -> gates each tagged with its source (base:kind, rule:id, principle:id, org:id) and N/A/deviations; resolved at claim and recorded as a pipeline.resolved event (digest of inputs), re-resolved at gate status/complete on the ACTUAL diff, additions only mid-flight. Agent changes are additive by default (add a gate to one item); any weakening (remove, demote, N/A of a MUST/required gate, change of a floor) is a proposal a person approves. Precedence = P-goals order (org floor > project MUST > accepted decision > principle > preference); additions collect (union), removals use the strictest-wins rule (a MUST require beats any allow_na), an order cycle is a doctor error that falls back to base order.
data.falsifier: Falsified if, after B-pipe-acceptance, a project cannot express 'ddflow/core/** needs mutation_tests' and 'docs-only skips unit_tests' with the field alone, or if agents' additive changes exceed [pipeline].max_added on more than 10 percent of items, or if resolve differs between claim and complete for an unchanged rule set, or if any weakening applies without a person.
data.mechanism: A requirement is a guidance record effect, so lifecycle, scope matching, waivers, deviations, search and RAG come from the record surface; the pipeline stays one selector (pipeline_for) extended with recorded per-item additions.

Survey, fetched and read 2026-10-11 (WebFetch returns a model summary, quotes approximate) VERIFIED: GitHub rulesets layer, most restrictive wins, bypass list, org-level rulesets (docs.github.com .../about-rulesets); the available-rules page lists 'require status checks' and NO dedicated require-workflows rule, and docs .../required-workflows is 404 (so the removal of required workflows is NOT verified). Gerrit submit requirements: applicableIf / submittableIf / overrideIf expressions, children inherit and override only if parent sets canOverrideInChildProjects, override replaces the whole requirement, remove by is:false (gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-submit-requirements.html). GitLab pipeline execution policies: inject_policy adds to the project pipeline, override_project_ci replaces it, [skip ci] cannot bypass by default, scope by project/group/compliance framework (docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/application_security/policies/pipeline_execution_policies.html). Conftest: deny/violation/warn rules in Rego over CI pipeline definitions (conftest.dev; exception semantics not on the page). Kyverno: mutate runs before validate, chained rules need ordering (kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/cluster-policy/mutate/; PolicyException not covered by the page). Jenkins shared libraries: global trusted vs folder untrusted, @version pinning, 'allow default version to be overridden' (jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/shared-libraries/). Airflow dynamic task mapping: tasks created at runtime, visible in Grid view, max_map_length 1024 cap, zero inputs -> SKIPPED (airflow docs). LangGraph conditional edges / Send / Command route at runtime (docs.langchain.com .../graph-api).
