Claude Code hooks: PreToolUse/TaskCompleted/ConfigChange exit 2 blocks, managed-policy hooks cannot be disabled by users, allowManagedHooksOnly (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Jira: workflows assigned to projects and work types by workflow schemes, active workflows cannot be renamed, copy-modify-activate (support.atlassian.com work-with-issue-workflows). INHERITED from R-goals-principles-proposals-design (fetched by the earlier author, not re-fetched here): Kiro steering/hooks, Gatekeeper enforcementAction dryrun/warn/deny, Kyverno Audit vs Enforce, RFC 2119, Spec Kit Complexity Tracking, ArchUnit FreezingArchRule. NOT VERIFIED (summarised from background): DMN hit policies (OMG PDF unreadable, Camunda page lacked the list), BPMN, Argo Workflows, Temporal, Linear workflows, GitHub required workflows.
COPY: Gerrit's applicable/submittable/override split and per-requirement inherit-with-explicit-override-permission (canOverrideInChildProjects = ddflow override none vs waive vs deviate); GitLab inject (additive) vs override (replace) as two distinct, named strategies with additive default; GitHub's most-restrictive-wins and evaluate/disabled states (a dry-run enforcement tier); Tekton skipped-with-reason listing and Airflow SKIPPED on empty; Jenkins version pinning of shared definitions; Claude Code managed hooks that users add to but cannot remove. AVOID: pipeline sprawl (Airflow needed a max_map_length cap; cap added gates per item), agents weakening their own gates (Jenkins trusted vs untrusted: the writer of the policy must not be the subject), undebuggable dynamic graphs (LangGraph/Airflow: freeze the resolved graph and show the source of each node), silent drift (a rule edit changing in-flight items: record pipeline.resolved with input digests), full-replace overrides (Gerrit/GitLab override_project_ci hide what was lost: diff against base).
data.question: How can rules and principles define a project's pipeline (extra gates, allowed skips, order), resolved per item and modified by agents within floors, reusing the guidance, waiver, config and workflow engines?

data.body:
A common policy shape is 'if you touch these paths, run this check' — an API change needs its contract validated, a schema change needs a migration, a change under a container's source needs that image rebuilt. Today such a gate is always on or skipped by hand on every item, which trains skipping. Decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (the diff against base, plus untracked), not only the declared globs, since globs can under-declare. A gate that does not apply is recorded with its own outcome and the evidence (which paths, which patterns) — never silently absent, per 'silence is not a pass'. Re-evaluate at complete: a later commit that brings the item into scope must bring the gate back. gate verify / mutations unchanged.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: `[gate.X] applies_when` already shipped in B-uni-kind-pipeline.2-when (services/gates/kinds.py:34-60) and decides on the DECLARED globs. What remains here is only: decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (diff against base plus untracked), re-evaluate at complete, record the evidence (which paths, which patterns). Keep the knob name applies_when; do not add a second `when_globs`. The 'always on or skipped by hand' sentence above describes the state before that.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): this task also OWNS bug B-na-required-gate (CONFIRMED by probe): a gate in [gates].required is never made not-applicable by declared globs alone, because globs are agent-editable (ddflow update --globs, no approval). Rule: not-applicable relief for a required gate needs the ACTUAL diff to miss the patterns (changed_paths, as readme_report already does), is recorded as evidence (paths, patterns) on the item, and is re-evaluated at complete; when the diff cannot be read the gate stays owed (unavailable, never N/A). Non-required gates may still be judged on declared globs when no diff exists yet. Regression test: the probe in the bug (applies_when src/**, task globs docs/x.md, diff touching src/) must fail against current code. The applicability inputs (declared globs, diff paths) become the same function B-pipe-resolve uses for pipeline requirements; do not build a second path matcher.

Examples: floor review.min_other_family_reviewers=1; require gates.task_pipeline contains [critic, unit_tests]; pin enforce.commit_without_lease=block; allow companions=[roborev, codeguide-mcp]; allow reviewer models; require rules/security-baseline. A violating write from CLI, MCP, prompt or configure is refused (exit 3) naming the policy item, source and rev; a hand-edited file that violates is reported by doctor and, in enforce mode, claim/merge/complete refuse until fixed; audit mode only reports (brief + doctor). The four enforced kernel rules, human gates and D-reviewer-trust are re-expressed as shipped policy so the org layer extends one mechanism. A project-level policy file lets the operator lock a key locally the same way (generalising export disable --lock).

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): allow/require/pin items also cover: which companions and MCP servers may be proposed or registered (allow), which subagent roles must exist (require), which decisions are required and not supersedable locally (require), and which prompts or commands may not be overridden (pin).

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: a floor is a guidance record with enforcement block and override none; the project cannot waive or deviate from it, and the precedence function (B-goal-deviation) ranks it above project rules. 'Require' items may name principles (a company principle must exist and cannot be demoted to MAY locally); 'pin' covers [discovery].web and [proposals].max_open. Audit mode reports a local demotion instead of refusing it.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): pipeline requirements are policy items too. A floor on the pipeline is a guidance record with a `pipeline` effect (B-pipe-model), enforcement block and override none, shipped in the bundle; 'require' items may name such a record so a project cannot delete or demote it, and the effective-pipeline resolver (B-pipe-resolve) reads it above project MUST records. The four invariants (gates.require_outcome, agent.reviewer_family_must_differ, lessons.require_regression_test, and unavailable-is-never-pass which is already structural) plus gates.required are shipped as pinned policy so they become a real floor (CONFIRMED today: each is a plain knob an agent can flip, R-pipeline-configurable-today). A policy 'pin' of a knob must not be satisfiable by dropping the gate from every pipeline (existing inert_requirements catches the config form; the resolver catches the per-item form).

Today only tool-description wording stops an agent from setting enforce.commit_without_lease=off or uninstalling hooks over MCP; the review-budget case writes a session note. Mark knobs with tier=policy in their metadata; an agent write becomes a pending config proposal (event) shown in brief and doctor until a person approves (B-uni-approval) or rejects; refuse mode refuses outright; allow keeps today's behaviour. Org policy can pin the mode.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): the policy-tier list is incomplete. CONFIRMED by probe: gates.require_outcome, agent.reviewer_family_must_differ, lessons.require_regression_test, gates.required and the pipeline writers (ddflow workflow pipeline|gate|drop, MCP ddflow_workflow_*) are all applied immediately for an agent; this task's list names gates.allow_skip_with_reason but not them. Add them to tier=policy, and route a workflow pipeline|gate|drop by an agent through the same pending-proposal path when it REMOVES a gate, lowers a gate's reviewer/evidence requirement, or edits [gates].required (an addition of a gate stays free: additive by default, B-pipe-agent). Agent identity alone is not the test (any agent can claim to be the operator over the CLI): the proposal is cleared only by the person-only approve verb.

Reminders: brief and claim list the applicable decisions by category within the context-pack budget (B-uni-context-pack). The rubber_duck, critic and standards prompts include the applicable decisions and their checks, so a cross-family reviewer verifies compliance and cites the decision id. A new 'decisions' task gate runs the checks of the applicable decisions on the item's diff; enforcement decides whether it fails or warns, and the gate is offered through B-uni-kind-pipeline. Pre-commit runs only fast checks on staged files and manifests. The periodic full sweep is a shipped schedule job (B-uni-triggers / B-sched-defaults) that files a drift report and bugs for new violations. Triggers: a dependency manifest changed, a decision accepted (one whole-tree check), a waiver expired.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): the 'decisions' task gate added here is the first pipeline effect of a guidance record. Do not hard-wire it per kind: implement it as the default `pipeline.require = ["decisions"]` effect of any decision or rule with a mechanical check, resolved by B-pipe-resolve, so a project can opt out for docs-only work by a recorded allow_na effect rather than by editing [gates]. Until B-pipe-resolve exists the gate is offered through B-uni-kind-pipeline as written.

WHAT: mechanical plan checking, not LLM decomposition. `ddflow plan check <file|->` takes a proposed set of phases/tasks (TOML or JSON: id, title, needs, globs, body, acceptance) and reports, before anything is filed: (1) a `*` in a directory position or a glob that matches more than N files (L-glob-overlap-is-conservative); (2) cycles and dependencies on unknown ids; (3) tasks that can run together (no dependency path between them) whose globs overlap, with the exact pair and the glob that collides, and the waves the plan would give (B-dag-waves-fanout's schedule.waves when present); (4) tasks missing acceptance, test plan or size; a task whose globs span more than K top-level directories (candidate for split); (5) duplicates against the existing queue through the add-time similar check. `ddflow plan apply` files a checked plan with one command and one transaction. The same check runs as a warning at `task add` and `phase add` so hand-filed tasks get it too. Optional flag `plan review` records a plan-review round with the existing cross-family reviewers (kind 'plan'), prompt template overridable, findings go through review triage like any review. Glob suggestion: given a title/body, list literal globs from past completed tasks whose merged files co-changed with the same words (read-only advice from worktree.merged records).
WHY: the glob-overlap stalls this session came from wildcard globs filed by hand; the coordinator hand-writes dozens of tasks per phase. Task Master, Spec Kit (analyze), OpenSpec (validate) and Backlog.md (spec-review and plan-review checkpoints) all gate on plan quality before code; ddflow has gates for code and none for the plan. Decomposition itself stays with the agent: it is a prompt-quality problem, and the harness models are better placed.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core.graph and core.schedule for cycles, waves and overlap (the same overlap test claim uses), services/similar for duplicates, Command declaration + api for CLI/MCP parity, services/review for the plan-review round, services/importer parsers for TOML/JSON plan input.
HOW TO TEST: table of bad plans each failing exactly one check (failing-first); a plan that passes check also passes real claim overlap decisions (cross-check against core.schedule on random plans); apply is atomic (kill mid-way, nothing half-filed); warning at task add does not change exit code.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests). Needs B-gap-lanes first only for the shared registration files.
ACCEPTANCE: the 11 tasks filed for P-gaps pass `plan check` with zero findings; a wildcard-directory glob in a throwaway plan is reported with the colliding pair; README and driver doc say 'run plan check before filing a phase'.

Traceability 2026-10-10 (reorg audit): this task OWNS the wave computation, because B-dag-waves-fanout was narrowed to reuse it (it now needs this task): build `core.schedule.waves(items)` as a pure function over any item set (the proposed plan here; B-dag-waves-fanout later feeds it the open queue for next/board), with the earliest wave of each item given needs + glob conflicts + caps, and a test on a fixture DAG that matches hand-computed levels including a glob conflict that serialises two otherwise-independent items (the acceptance B-dag-waves-fanout originally carried). Do not wait for B-dag-waves-fanout; it is not "when present", it is built here. B-dag-waves-fanout keeps only the next/board display and the mermaid DAG.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: open design points: ddflow/templates/prompts/review/ does not exist (review prompts are review_system.md and review_user.md): say where a plan-review round is recorded before an item exists, or defer that flag; the add-time warning also edits ddflow/api/items.py and the README/driver text (the acceptance names both). Call the existing core/graph.find_cycles and core/globs.overlap (and the add-time similar check); share the overlap report with B-par-auto-split.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): `plan check` also prints, per proposed task, the EFFECTIVE pipeline it would run (kind pipeline plus every pipeline requirement its declared globs/kind/tags match, each added gate tagged with its source record) by calling the pure resolver of B-pipe-resolve (no second implementation, no I/O); a requirement that adds a gate to a task whose globs are too wide to judge (a wildcard directory) is reported like the overlap findings. The flag is optional and absent until the resolver exists. `ddflow workflow preview` (B-pipe-preview) is the same function for one hypothetical item.

WHAT: one log-derived metrics service and three views. `ddflow metrics [--phase P] [--since D]`: cycle time per item (started->completed), time per gate, review rounds per item, gate failure/skip/unavailable rates by gate and by reviewer, queue wait (ready->claimed), lease wait on glob conflicts, rework (completed items later hit by a bug), lane utilisation (working vs idle-with-ready). `ddflow forecast [--phase P]`: critical-path ETA and a P50/P90 range for a phase from measured per-kind cycle times and the dependency graph (simple bootstrap over observed durations; says 'not enough data' under a minimum sample; marked an estimate). `ddflow retro <id>`: the timeline of one item (claim, first gate, each review round, waits, merge) with the biggest gap named -- the answer to 'why was this task slow'. A skip audit: `gate skip` rate per gate with reasons, skips never followed by a later pass, skips by agent.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence from this log: median item 1.04 h, p90 2.8 h, max 31.8 h (n=667); rubber_duck and critic fail 860/849 times against 639/618 passes (every findings round is a failed event), so review rounds dominate wall time but nobody has the number per item; docs gate skipped 149 times against 25 passes (a gate the process routes around, B-docs-stage is the fix, the audit would have shown it earlier); 508 bugs against 850 completions. Three open tasks each plan their own replay: B-rm-changes (throughput ETA hint), B-af-headroom, B-sub-metrics. Without a shared service that is three half-metrics. Langfuse/Inspect (R-gaps-survey) show the value of per-run traces and scores; ddflow's log already is the trace.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: the fold and the existing replay helpers in views/ and core/flowsignals.py; Command + Param declarations; core.graph critical_path; knowledge of clock.now (B-arch-clock-now) so tests are deterministic.
HOW TO TEST: golden output on a frozen mini-log fixture; forecast on a synthetic log with known durations lands inside the stated range in a seeded 1000-run test; retro names the injected slow gap; sparse data returns exit 2 'not enough data', never a number.
SIZE: medium (~600 lines + tests). Re-pointing B-rm-changes / B-af-headroom / B-sub-metrics is a decision for B-gap-decide (c), not part of this task.
ACCEPTANCE: the three commands work on CLI and MCP on this log; the figures above are reproduced within rounding; README + help topic; B-gap-decide (c) answered.

Operator 2026-10-10 ('do what you recommend' on the order review): tests inject time (a fake clock argument); do not depend on B-arch-clock-now.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: provide the shared hourly-grid sampler (fold at instant t plus core.schedule.plan, bucketed, capped folds, says when it sampled) as a function in services/metrics.py for B-af-headroom and for lane utilisation, and expose a group-by dimension (gate, reviewer, agent, kind, agent + definition digest) so B-sub-metrics is a view. Reuse core/flowsignals.py latency and failure-rate readers rather than recomputing them. Drop any dependency on clock.now (B-arch-clock-now): tests inject time (operator 2026-10-10).

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: expose a provider hook (register(name, fn) returning rows and a group-by key) so other services add metrics without editing this one, and make guidance id and goal id valid group-by dimensions once they exist. B-goal-report registers principle adherence, deviation rate, proposal acceptance and goal progress deltas through it. Same minimum-sample rule (exit 2, never a number) applies to them.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): register through the provider hook: pipeline requirement hit counts per record (items it added a gate to), added gates per item (the sprawl measure, against [pipeline].max_added), N/A and deviation rate per requirement and per agent, and requirements that never fired in N items. The gate-skip audit gains the 'skipped a gate a MUST requirement owed' row (must be zero). Same minimum-sample rule.

WHAT: make a principle real. (1) The override field (none | waive | deviate) on the guidance record and its fold/file format/definition fields, with MUST/SHOULD/MAY shown beside the enforcement word in every door (brief, claim, gate status, review prompt) by guidance/inject.py (_line tags). (2) A deviation: ddflow decision deviate <id> --item <item> --reason "..." [--evidence ...] and its twin on the MCP decision tool; stored as a waiver record in mode deviation (B-dec-waivers); item-scoped, no approval, no expiry, reason required. (3) The completion check: ddflow complete refuses (exit 3, naming each) while a finding against a record with override=deviate is neither fixed nor deviated; a finding is a failing mechanical check result (checks.gate_verdict warnings) or a reviewer finding that cites the id (B-goal-cites). A SHOULD that has neither check nor citation is never a finding; a MAY never refuses. (4) precedence.py: the one function that orders applicable records (org floor > rule > decision > principle > preference; scope; priority) and reports an unreconciled conflict instead of picking silently; inject.rank_key calls it. (5) A deviation is shown to the operator: brief line 'deviations since your last look', decision list column, completion summary.
WHY (evidence, R-goals-existing-map): decisions already default to warn, but a warn finding requires no answer (checks.Verdict.warnings never changes the outcome), and a waiver needs a person and expires within 90 days (D-decision-management) - right for a rule, too heavy for a preference, so people will skip it and a soft rule fails by silence. RFC 2119 SHOULD is exactly 'valid reasons to ignore, carefully weighed'; Spec Kit records deviations as justified entries (Complexity Tracking); no verified tool combines reason + expiry + approver, ddflow's waiver already does for the strict case.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{record,deffields,inject,checks,waivers}.py, B-dec-model (override field lands in the decision v2 events and its upcaster; this task wires behaviour), B-dec-waivers (storage), B-dec-monitor (the decisions gate), services/completion.py (the existing refusal list), core.provenance for fencing. No new event kind unless B-dec-waivers did not carry the mode (then register it with its first writer).
HOW TO TEST (failing first): a SHOULD with a failing check: complete refuses; after deviate it passes and the summary lists the deviation; a MUST with the same check blocks the gate and deviate does NOT clear it (only waive does); deviate on a MUST refused with the reason; a MAY never refuses; precedence table test (every pair of tiers, scope tie-break, priority tie-break) and an unreconciled pair reported; fold/replay of an old log with no override field gives block->waive, warn/advisory->deviate; tool parity test; budget: pinned MUST text never trimmed (existing test unchanged).
SIZE: large (~600 lines + tests); the completion refusal and inject tags are the risk.
ACCEPTANCE: scenario in B-goal-acceptance; README section 'Principles: follow unless you say why'; help topic.
DOCS: README, help topic goals, driver notes (agent: how to deviate; when a deviation is a sign the principle is wrong).

DOCS NOTE: README and help-topic text for this task is written by B-goal-acceptance (the single README editor, so parallel tasks keep disjoint globs); this task writes the driver/prompt text it owns and a docstring-level description.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): a deviation (and a person's waiver) also applies to a pipeline requirement: the finding is 'gate X owed by record R has no outcome'. Deviating from a SHOULD requirement records the item, the gate and the reason through the same deviation record and appears on the gate row ('deviated: reason, by agent'). The precedence function is the one B-pipe-resolve calls; its tiers are not duplicated. override=none or waive on a pipeline record means the gate cannot be deviated; only waive (person, <=90 days, scoped) lifts a MUST.

Ask the operator, record the decision, write docs/ddflow/decisions/pipeline-requirements.md. One question at a time with the recommended default; record each answer verbatim (ddflow session prompt) and as a decision (ddflow decision add --globs ...). Do not start another B-pipe-* task first. Evidence: R-pipeline-configurable-today (CONFIRMED), R-pipeline-requirements-design (THEORETICAL), bug B-na-required-gate.

QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS
1. Field or kind? DEFAULT: one optional `pipeline` field (a table) on the existing guidance record (rule or decision); no new kind, no new store, no new config file. Rejected: a pipeline-rule kind (a second engine beside the record surface), and growing [gates] with per-glob tables (invisible to search, brief and RAG, outside the waiver/deviation engine).
2. What may an effect say? DEFAULT: require=[gate...] (with optional after=), allow_na=[gate...] with a reason class, forbid_skip=[gate...], order=[[a,b]...], kinds=[...] (item kinds it covers), define={gate table} for a project-specific gate backed by a declared command (executable: approved by digest, inert until approved, B-gap-command-trust). Gate DEFINITIONS stay in [gate.*]; the record only names ids.
3. Strength. DEFAULT: reuse enforcement x override from B-goal-decide. MUST (block, waive|none): the gate cannot be dropped, skipped or made N/A; only a person's waiver (<=90 days, scoped to globs) lifts it. SHOULD (warn, deviate): the gate is added as recommended; an agent records an item-scoped deviation with a reason, answered before complete. MAY (advisory): listed in gate status, never refused. A deviation never lifts a MUST.
4. What does 'scope matches' read? DEFAULT: the existing Scope (globs, categories, gates) plus kinds and tags; globs are matched against the item's declared globs at claim and against the ACTUAL diff (changed_paths) at gate status and complete; a requirement that matches either one applies (additions can only grow); an allow_na needs the diff to MISS (declared globs alone never grant N/A: bug B-na-required-gate).
5. Resolution time. DEFAULT: at claim, recorded as a pipeline.resolved event (resolved gate list with the source of each, digest of rule and config inputs, engine version); re-resolved at gate status/complete: gates may be ADDED mid-flight (the agent is told which rule added it), never removed without a recorded N/A or waiver. A rule edit never silently changes an in-flight item.
6. Agent powers. DEFAULT: additive and free: add a gate to this item (reason required, event, shown in review and metrics, capped by [pipeline].max_added = 3 per item, then a note); N/A of a non-required gate not covered by a MUST: allowed with reason class and evidence; ANY weakening (remove a gate from a pipeline or kind, N/A or skip of a required/MUST gate, lower a reviewer/evidence requirement, edit [gates].required, demote a record's strength) becomes a pending proposal only a person clears (builds on B-org-agent-guard). Agent-authored requirement records start status proposed, additive effects only, active after the operator accepts (like decisions).
7. The four invariants. DEFAULT: shipped as an org-style floor that no project record can weaken: unavailable never passes (already structural), every pipeline gate carries an outcome (gates.require_outcome), a cross-family reviewer on authored tasks, a regression test for a bug. They become policy-tier knobs (B-org-agent-guard) and the resolver refuses a requirement whose effect would remove them.
8. Precedence. DEFAULT: the P-goals order (org floor > project MUST > accepted decision > principle > preference); additions COLLECT (union); removals use strictest-wins (any MUST require beats any allow_na); an order cycle is a doctor error and the base order stands. Not 'first match' (DMN first-hit hides rules).
9. Preview. DEFAULT: ddflow workflow preview (--kind, --globs, --tags) and workflow diff (this change vs current, over open items) on CLI and MCP; an enforcement tier 'evaluate' that resolves and reports but adds nothing (GitHub ruleset evaluate idea, Gatekeeper dryrun) for the first N days of a new requirement.
10. Versioning and skew. DEFAULT: unknown `pipeline` keys in a record are carried, not dropped; an engine that does not know the field refuses to complete an item that a block-level requirement covers (fail closed), warns for warn-level.
11. Sprawl brake. DEFAULT: [pipeline].max_added = 3, a requirement that adds a gate must name a gate with a command or an evidence contract (no pure-prose extra gates), requirements that fired on zero items in 60 days are listed for review (B-dec-review), and a rule count cap shared with [rules].
ACCEPTANCE: answers recorded as a decision citing the reasons; the doc lists each question with the answer; B-pipe-* bodies amended (ddflow update) where an answer differs. Tests: none (docs only); gates: research, rules, docs. SIZE: small. DOCS: docs/ddflow/decisions/pipeline-requirements.md.
data.title: Operator decisions for pipeline requirements: field not kind, effects, strength, resolution time, agent powers, invariants floor, precedence, preview, skew, sprawl brake

data.body:
WHAT: the `pipeline` field on GuidanceRecord (services/guidance/record.py, deffields.py FIELDS, fileformat) for rules and decisions: effects require, allow_na, forbid_skip, order, kinds, define (per B-pipe-decide), validated (gate ids exist or are defined, no self-contradiction, order acyclic), digested into the def.* content, rendered in the authored file, folded, upcast (absent field = no effect; no change to any existing digest). Lint: a require of a gate with neither command nor evidence contract is refused (B-pipe-decide 11). The `define` table is stored inert; a command is runnable only after a person approves its digest.
WHY: R-pipeline-configurable-today: no record can influence the pipeline; Scope.gates only selects injected text. A field (not a kind) gives lifecycle, search, history, waivers, deviations, RAG and the CLI/MCP record surface for free.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{record,deffields,fileformat,limits}.py, core/defs, B-dec-model (override field and upcaster land there), B-rules-onto-record-surface (the generated rule/decision commands carry the new field as one more Param, not a second command), services/approval for define digests.
TESTS (failing first): round trip file <-> fields <-> fold with and without the field; a log with no field replays byte-identical (golden); invalid effects are refused with the exact reason; cycle in order refused; digest unchanged for records without the field; unknown future effect key is carried not dropped.
RECORD-SURFACE CONFORMANCE (the contract audited 2026-10-11): add, edit (incl. clearing the field), delete/retire, merge and split of two requirement records, search (a requirement is found by gate id and by the globs it covers), context insert at claim and gate prompts (relevance-matched, fenced), RAG export, evidence logged (a def event with who/why), sessions notified when a requirement that covers a held lease changes (brief 'changed since your claim'), shown in brief at session start. Each is a test row; no pipeline-specific command, search or injection path.
SIZE: medium (~350 lines + tests). ACCEPTANCE: B-pipe-acceptance scenario 1. DOCS: docstrings; README written by B-goal-acceptance (single README editor); driver text for the agent: 'a requirement names a gate, not a fix'.

data.body:
WHAT: the pure resolver effective_pipeline(cfg, item, records, diff_paths) in services/gates/effective.py: base = kind_pipeline(cfg, kind); collect require effects of live records whose Scope/kinds/tags match (insertion by after=, else before merge, never after merge; order effects applied, a cycle falls back to base order and is a doctor error); allow_na only where no MUST require/forbid_skip and no [gates].required covers the gate AND the diff (not the declared globs) misses; every gate carries its SOURCE (base:<kind>, rule:<id>, principle:<id>, org:<id>). Precedence via the one function of B-goal-deviation; additions union, removals strictest-wins. pipeline_for(item, cfg) stays the single selector and returns the item's RECORDED resolution when one exists (so the 8+ callers, status, completion, verify, views, testselect, need no edits). New event pipeline.resolved at claim (gate list with sources, input digest of the matching record digests and the cfg gates digest, engine version); gate status and complete re-resolve against the diff: new additions are appended and the agent is told 'gate X added by rule R-..'; nothing is removed except through a recorded N/A or waiver. `ddflow gate status` and `ddflow workflow explain <item>` print 'X added by <record>', 'Y not applicable: <why> (<record>)'. Fail-closed: a block-level requirement whose record this engine cannot parse blocks complete and says so; the inputs digest makes drift visible (doctor note 'requirement R changed after <item> was resolved').
WHY: 'changes under ddflow/core require mutation_tests' and 'docs-only tasks skip unit_tests' cannot be expressed today except as whole-project config; not_applicable is derived at read time and unrecorded. Freezing the resolved graph is the lesson of Airflow/LangGraph dynamic graphs (undebuggable otherwise) and Gerrit's explicit applicability.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/gates/{kinds,defs,outcomes}.py, completion.verdict, B-gate-when-globs path evaluation (needs it; one matcher), services/guidance/resolve.py (Scope), core/globs.overlap, changed_paths, the events/fold registration pattern of an existing item-level event.
TESTS (failing first): table: rule scope x item x diff -> exact gate list with sources; mutation_tests added for ddflow/core/** and absent for docs; docs-only allow_na grants N/A only when the diff misses, and the probe of bug B-na-required-gate stays red; rule edited after claim -> in-flight item unchanged, drift note shown, later gate status adds only; a MUST cannot be removed by allow_na of another record; resolver purity (no I/O) and determinism (same inputs, same output, any record order); replay of an old log with no resolved event gives today's pipeline; event fold/replay/upcaster.
SIZE: large (~600 lines + tests). ACCEPTANCE: B-pipe-acceptance scenarios 2-4. Needs the completion.py edits to follow B-goal-deviation (same file).

data.body:
WHAT: the agent's powers over ONE item's pipeline, CLI and MCP from one declaration (ddflow pipeline add-gate|na|deviate|propose, tool ddflow_pipeline with action verbs). (1) add-gate <item> <gate> --reason: free, additive, event with reason and evidence, shown in gate status, review prompts and metrics, capped by [pipeline].max_added (default 3; above it a NOTE and the operator is told). (2) na <item> <gate> --class <reason class> --evidence: allowed only for a gate no MUST/forbid_skip/[gates].required covers and the diff misses; otherwise refused naming the record. It is the structured form of today's gate skip (same event family, a class field), not a second mechanism. (3) deviate: a SHOULD requirement's item-scoped deviation (B-goal-deviation's record). (4) propose: any weakening (remove a gate from a pipeline or kind, lower reviewer/evidence, edit [gates].required, demote or retire a requirement record) is filed as a pending config proposal (B-org-agent-guard path) and shown in brief and doctor until a person clears it with the person-only approve verb; the agent's own session never clears it. An agent may also author a requirement record: status proposed, additive effects only (require/order), active only after the operator accepts; an agent record that would remove a gate is refused. workflow pipeline|gate|drop by an agent route through the same guard.
WHY: the operator asked that agents can modify the pipeline to match principles and rules. Additive changes cost little and are what a principle usually asks for ('prefer a rubber_duck for security-touching changes'); weakening is exactly what an agent under time pressure would do to its own gates (CONFIRMED reachable today, R-pipeline-configurable-today).
INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/gates.py gate skip path, B-org-agent-guard proposals, services/approval (approve by digest), B-goal-deviation records, Command declaration (CLI/MCP parity), the deviation lines in brief and the completion summary.
TESTS (failing first): agent add-gate allowed, evented, capped; na of a required gate refused; na of a MUST-covered gate refused; propose creates a pending proposal and changes nothing until a person approves; MCP cannot clear a proposal (no tool); an agent-authored removing requirement refused; CLI/MCP body parity golden; tools/list budget test passes.
SIZE: medium-large (~500 lines + tests). ACCEPTANCE: B-pipe-acceptance scenarios 5-6. DOCS: driver notes: 'adding a gate is yours; removing one is a proposal'.
data.title: Agent-modified pipelines within floors: add a gate or mark N/A with reason and evidence; any weakening is a person-cleared proposal; agent-authored requirements start proposed

data.body:
WHAT: seeing a pipeline before it exists. `ddflow workflow preview [--kind K] [--globs G] [--tags T] [--item ID]` prints the effective pipeline of a hypothetical item (or an existing one) with each gate's source, via the pure resolver; `ddflow workflow diff [--record ID | --change <file>]` shows, over the open items and a few typical shapes (docs-only, core, tests-only), which items' pipelines would change if a requirement were added, edited or retired (no writes). An 'evaluate' tier: a new requirement can be set to evaluate, which resolves and reports 'would add X' in gate status for N days (default 14) without adding anything, then is promoted by the operator (GitHub rulesets evaluate idea). doctor notes: requirements that matched no item in 60 days; a requirement whose gate has no definition; order cycles; in-flight items resolved under an older rule digest. Metrics provider rows (B-gap-metrics): hits, added gates per item, N/A and deviation rates. MCP parity: ddflow_workflow gains preview and diff actions (no new top-level tool).
WHY: dynamic pipelines are undebuggable unless the operator can ask 'what would this change do' first (Airflow/LangGraph lesson); B-gap-plan-lint does the same for plans; silent drift is the risk the sprawl brake needs numbers for.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/gates/effective.py, services/plancheck.py (B-gap-plan-lint), services/metrics.py provider hook, api/reporting/health.py doctor notes, the existing workflow command group and its dry-run convention.
TESTS (failing first): preview == the real claim resolution for the same shape (cross-check on random shapes); diff names exactly the items whose gate list differs; evaluate tier adds nothing and promotes on command; doctor notes each; golden outputs; parity.
SIZE: medium (~450 lines + tests). ACCEPTANCE: B-pipe-acceptance scenario 7. DOCS: help topic text via B-goal-acceptance.

data.body: Acceptance for pipeline requirements on a throwaway repo with a fake clock and a stub reviewer (no network). 1. A MUST rule 'ddflow/core/** requires mutation_tests' (define = command gate, digest-approved) adds the gate to a task touching core, tagged 'added by r-core-mutation' in gate status, explain and brief; a docs-only task does not get it; complete refuses without its outcome; only an approved waiver lifts it. 2. 'docs-only tasks skip unit_tests' as allow_na: N/A is granted only when the DIFF misses src; the declared-globs trick of bug B-na-required-gate stays refused for a required gate. 3. A rule edited after claim leaves the in-flight item's resolved pipeline unchanged, the drift note shows, and a new addition appears with its source at the next gate status. 4. Org floor: a bundle carrying a pipeline requirement (override none) cannot be demoted, waived or deviated by the project; a project requirement layers on top; a conflicting allow_na loses (strictest wins). 5. A SHOULD principle ('prefer a rubber_duck for security-touching changes unless trivial'): complete refuses until the agent complies or records a deviation with a reason; the deviation shows on the gate row, in the completion summary and in metrics. 6. Agent powers: add-gate allowed and capped; N/A of a required gate refused; removal of a gate from the kind pipeline becomes a pending proposal that only the person-only approve clears; the four invariants cannot be switched off by an agent. 7. preview equals the real resolution; diff names the affected open items; the evaluate tier adds nothing; doctor notes fire. 8. Record-surface conformance for a pipeline requirement: add, edit, delete, merge, split, search, context insert, RAG export, evidence logged, sessions notified, brief at start, relevance-matched context. 9. CLI and MCP bodies identical for pipeline, workflow preview/diff; tools/list budget test passes; skew: an engine without the field fails closed on a MUST-covered item. README, help topic, implement-phase driver (both copies) updated (this task edits README after B-goal-acceptance). Integration gaps found are filed as bugs, not patched here. Files: tests/scenarios/test_pipeline_requirements.py plus docs. SIZE: medium.

How to manage skills and subagents and integrate those in our workflow is a separate development phase which will extend the features of the ddflow to allow it to use skills and agents and manage them into the project. Do not add those skills to this project, just read the content and think of generic ideas that worth to be implemented in our default pipeline, but do follow the principles of this project - nothing have to be hardcoded - everything should be possible to configure, change, remove, change order, constants, variables, pipelines, workflows should be configurable, changeable, written as config (if modified default behavior) and able to be shared, managed by the user, ddflow cli or the agents, including via mcp interface

data.body:
Fixes bug B-na-required-gate: A REQUIRED gate is silently dropped for an item whose declared globs miss its [gate.X] applies_when: completion.verdict excludes not_applicable gates from the required check and status() counts them settled. The globs are agent-editable (ddflow update <id> --globs replaces them, no approval), and applies_when is judged on declared globs, not the diff. Repro (throwaway repo): [gate.unit_tests] applies_when=["src/**"]; task globs docs/x.md -> gate status prints "[-] unit_tests -- not applicable"; completion treats it as settled. Expected: a gates.required gate is never made not-applicable by declared globs alone (judge on the diff, record the evidence, or keep it owed). Found during the pipeline-requirements investigation 2026-10-11; the fix is owned by B-gate-when-globs (extended); its regression test must fail against current code.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-na-required-gate --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-na-required-gate --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-na-required-gate: A REQUIRED gate is silently dropped for an item whose declared globs miss its [gate.X] ap...

data.body:
A common policy shape is 'if you touch these paths, run this check' — an API change needs its contract validated, a schema change needs a migration, a change under a container's source needs that image rebuilt. Today such a gate is always on or skipped by hand on every item, which trains skipping. Decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (the diff against base, plus untracked), not only the declared globs, since globs can under-declare. A gate that does not apply is recorded with its own outcome and the evidence (which paths, which patterns) — never silently absent, per 'silence is not a pass'. Re-evaluate at complete: a later commit that brings the item into scope must bring the gate back. gate verify / mutations unchanged.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: `[gate.X] applies_when` already shipped in B-uni-kind-pipeline.2-when (services/gates/kinds.py:34-60) and decides on the DECLARED globs. What remains here is only: decide on the change's ACTUAL paths (diff against base plus untracked), re-evaluate at complete, record the evidence (which paths, which patterns). Keep the knob name applies_when; do not add a second `when_globs`. The 'always on or skipped by hand' sentence above describes the state before that.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): this task also OWNS bug B-na-required-gate (CONFIRMED by probe): a gate in [gates].required is never made not-applicable by declared globs alone, because globs are agent-editable (ddflow update --globs, no approval). Rule: not-applicable relief for a required gate needs the ACTUAL diff to miss the patterns (changed_paths, as readme_report already does), is recorded as evidence (paths, patterns) on the item, and is re-evaluated at complete; when the diff cannot be read the gate stays owed (unavailable, never N/A). Non-required gates may still be judged on declared globs when no diff exists yet. Regression test: the probe in the bug (applies_when src/**, task globs docs/x.md, diff touching src/) must fail against current code. The applicability inputs (declared globs, diff paths) become the same function B-pipe-resolve uses for pipeline requirements; do not build a second path matcher.

Superseded in part 2026-10-11 (operator decision: fix B-na-required-gate before the pause): the required-gate part of the paragraph above (never N/A by declared globs alone; judge a [gates].required gate on the ACTUAL diff; record the evidence; re-judge at complete) is delivered by fix-B-na-required-gate and is NOT to be redone here. What remains for this task: extend the diff-based judgement to the non-required gates' reporting and evidence display, and share the applicability function with B-pipe-resolve. Reuse the diff-based helper that fix-B-na-required-gate adds in services/gates/kinds.py; do not write a second path matcher.

data.alternatives: Per-kind lifecycle, notification and export tasks (rejected: five or more copies, the pattern D-unify exists to stop); a daemon pushing notifications (rejected: D-sched-no-daemon, ddflow answers at the doors a harness already calls).
data.consequences: Shared mechanisms are built once (P-record-contract) and goals, proposals, rules and decisions consume them; per-kind search sources, resources, injectors and lifecycle code are not written. More verbs live inside the one tool per kind, so the tools/list budget is not spent per verb.
data.context: Operator request 2026-10-11 after P-goals was filed. Existing basis: D-unify 4 (one record surface), D-no-duplicates, D-compat, D-lean-and-trusted, D-decision-management, D-viewer-lists-consolidated. Audit found no mid-session change notification, no merge/split/history verbs on the record surface, no RAG export, and search/recall/resource registration hard-coded per kind.
data.decision:
The record-surface contract (operator request 2026-10-11, verbatim in the session log: every goal, principle and rule follows the project's principles: MCP and CLI interfaces; add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert and RAG export; the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify and split; evidence is logged; sessions are informed of changes automatically, get the brief at start, and can search, ask or automatically receive context related to what they do). Every record kind (rule, decision, principle = a guidance record with override=deviate, goal, proposal, waiver and deviation, and every later kind) meets these rows; a kind that cannot meet one lists an exemption with its reason in the conformance test, and exemptions only shrink.
RC1 One declaration, two faces: one RecordKind descriptor (api/records.py) generates the CLI group and ONE MCP tool per kind (verbs are actions, never a tool per verb; tools/list budget test), bodies identical (parity test). Operator-only verbs are declared fields (surfaces/exemptions.py): refused on MCP with an explained exit 3.
RC2 Verbs: list, show, add (add-time duplicate and contradiction check, D-no-duplicates), edit (field level, clearing allowed), remove (= retire with a reason: a tombstone, never a silent hard delete), revise (whole replace), search, and the lifecycle verbs history, supersede, merge (many into one), split (one into several), restore. Every mutating verb needs a reason. Merge, split and supersede link both records with provenance. An agent's weakening change (lower enforcement, retire, drop, accept) is flagged for the operator until acknowledged (D-decision-management 2).
RC3 Evidence: every change is a log event on the def.* envelope with who, when, reason, session, source prompt (via the session) and before/after digest; show and history [--diff] display it; replay reproduces it; text is redacted (D-unify 6) and shown fenced as data.
RC4 Retrieval derived from the descriptor, no per-kind code: ddflow search --kind, the kind's own search, ddflow recall (the budgeted ask), context-pack candidates cited by kind:id.
RC5 RAG export: chunks with stable ids, status, validity, provenance, redaction, trust fence and tombstones for retired, merged and split ids; ddflow export records; MCP resource ddflow://records/{kind}/{id}.
RC6 Sessions are informed: at start the brief (bounded, fenced, pinned never trimmed) and the SessionStart/first-call door; at claim the guidance and direction that apply to the item's files, gate and category; mid-session the change feed ('changed since you last looked', with the agent's own changes excluded) delivered through the prompt, pre-tool and post-tool hooks where the harness honours injection, otherwise as a notice on MCP replies, heartbeat and wait; relevance-matched context (scope match first, then text match to the task, thresholded, once per session unless the record changed).
RC7 Ask: ddflow recall (and recall --for item|path|text) for agents, ddflow search for people; both over the one engine.
RC8 Review: kinds that can go stale carry review_by or a staleness rule, surfaced in doctor and brief; revisit triggers and repeated-deviation triggers register with the one review facility; acts that need a person are declared operator-only.
RC9 Scope and privacy: org-sourced records are read-only locally, labelled with source and revision, and the project layers on top; proposals, deviations, waivers and discovery runs are local to the project log; local-only records never reach another user's brief, feed or export; every displayed text is redacted and fenced.
RC10 Format: new payload fields are additive and the upcaster is registered with the kind's first writer (D-compat); an older ddflow preserves what it does not understand.
RC11 Docs: a help topic per kind (or the shared 'records' topic), the README tool-table row generated, driver notes for agent-facing behaviour.
RC12 Conformance: one generated test over every declared kind asserts RC1 to RC11 (task B-rc-conformance).
Built by phase P-record-contract (B-rc-lifecycle, B-rc-changes, B-rc-participation, B-rc-context, B-rc-rag-export, B-rc-conformance) in the core wave after the P-unify checkpoint, with the P-goals, P-decisions, rules and other tasks extended to use it rather than build per-kind versions. Defaults chosen without the operator, to confirm: split = child def.recorded events with provenance.split_from plus a def.retired of the original carrying split_into (no new event kind); the mid-session feed delivers only BINDING changes (rule, decision, principle, goal status, waiver expiry, contested) and counts the rest; remove stays a tombstone and there is no hard purge except the redaction purge.
data.title: Record-surface contract: every record kind (rule, decision, principle, goal, proposal, waiver, deviation, later kinds) has CLI and MCP from one declaration, full lifecycle (edit, remove, merge, split, restore, history), logged evidence, search/ask/context/RAG export from the descriptor, and sessions informed at start, at claim and mid-session

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim, also recorded as a session prompt): "make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project - mcp and cli interfaces, add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert, rag export interfaces and functionalities, so the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify, split, evidence is logged, sessions are automatically informed for changes, they retrieve brief on session start, and can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do"

The contract is decision D-record-surface-contract (rows RC1 to RC12). This phase builds the SHARED mechanisms once, so goals (P-goals), rules (B-rules-onto-record-surface), decisions (P-decisions), proposals and every later record kind consume them instead of growing per-kind versions. Audit (2026-10-11, verified against the code and every task body): record verbs today are list/show/add/edit/remove/search/revise (api/records.py VERBS); merge, supersede and split exist only as API calls (api/defs.py def_merge, def_supersede) or for tasks, no surface offers them and no history or restore verb exists; ddflow search, recall and the MCP resources register each kind by hand (services/search.py KINDS and _DEF_KINDS, infra/store.py RECALL_SOURCES, surfaces/mcp.py RESOURCES), so a new kind is invisible to search/recall until someone edits those; there is no RAG export of records (ddflow export makes human documents); and nothing tells a running session that a rule, decision, principle or goal changed (hooks prompt, pre_tool, post_tool, stop and session_end are wired and handled by _on_nothing; the brief shows state once at start; research gets its own pre-tool injector only in B-rw-context).

Tasks, in order: B-rc-lifecycle (history, supersede, merge, split, restore on the record surface) -> B-rc-participation (search, recall, context-candidate and resource registration derived from the descriptor); B-rc-changes (the change feed, per-session cursor and its doors) -> B-rc-context (relevance-matched automatic context at prompt, tool and claim time); B-rc-rag-export; then B-rc-conformance (a generated test over every declared kind).

Placement (operator 2026-10-11): after the P-unify checkpoint, in the core wave, off the upgrade path; the phase waits for B-checkpoint-after-unify through its P-unify need and changes no existing wave's first round. No daemon (D-sched-no-daemon): ddflow answers at the doors a harness already calls.
data.title: Record-surface contract: one lifecycle, change feed, retrieval registration, relevance-matched context and RAG export for every record kind, built once for goals, principles, rules, decisions, proposals and later kinds

data.claim: ddflow has the gate engine (GateDef: applies_when, requires_evidence, evidence_fields, human, reviewer family, unavailable/partial exits), mutation-proven gates, cross-family reviewers, a mechanical docs check (identifiers and links only) and a planned document-type engine, but has no scenario-card record, no terminology dictionary, no persisted evergreen/point-in-time class, no last-reviewed cursor or deferred-claims count, no corpus-level docs checks, no per-gate review lens as data (api/review.py _LENSES is a two-entry code constant; review_system.md is one refute prompt per reviewer), no multi-reviewer panel with a synthesis record, and no per-tool allow/deny guard on the MCP surface (tiers choose what is advertised only).
data.falsifier: A task, decision, rule or code path that already stores a document class, a review stamp with a sha, a terminology entry, a scenario card, a per-gate review lens, a reviewer panel with synthesis or an MCP tool deny list refutes the matching gap.
data.mechanism: Read the five skill files; read ddflow/services/gates/defs.py, ddflow/api/review.py:1299, ddflow/services/review.py Reviewer fields, templates/prompts/review_system.md, config_sections/mcp.py, the docscheck core task body, and the bodies of the docs, search, roadmap, skills, subagents, review-budget, agent-compat, schedule and test-robustness phases' tasks; ddflow search for dictionary, terminology, evergreen, point-in-time, last-reviewed, tmux, panel, synthesis found no record.

data.question: Which ideas in five Claude skills (e2e-scenario-testing, maintaining-documentation, mcp-cli, roborev-design-review and -branch) are already in ddflow, planned, or missing, judged against the repo as it is on 2026-10-11?

data.claim: They are worth building as configuration and shipped templates on existing engines (document types, gate defs, schedule jobs, def-records, reviewer dispatch), each off or advisory by default so no existing project changes behaviour: the skills' own evidence is that agents rewrite historical records, verify a noun not a verb, and skip gates under pressure, which ddflow already answers with enforced rules for gates but not for documents or scenario tests.
data.falsifier: On a throwaway project with the defaults, a point-in-time document edited to match code, an unverified claim under a reviewed stamp, or a vacuous scenario step is not caught by the new checks; or the added gates raise per-task time by more than the review budget allows.
data.mechanism: The skills encode failure modes (rewriting dated specs, a clean stamp over unverified claims, pasted review output treated as a request, stale binaries under test) that ddflow's log, gates and cross-family rule can detect mechanically if the data exists: a class per document, a reviewed sha plus deferred count, a card with falsifiers, a lens per gate. No usage data from other projects supports the size of the benefit.
