data.body:
Contract rows RC1, RC2, RC3, RC9 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "so the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify, split, evidence is logged".

WHAT: the record lifecycle, built once on the record surface, so goals, principles, rules, decisions, proposals and every later kind get it from their descriptor instead of writing it. Today api/records.py VERBS is list, show, add, edit, remove, search, revise. api/defs.py already has def_supersede and def_merge (and core/defs.py the def.superseded and def.merged events and the merged_from fold) but no surface offers them, `show` cuts the history to the newest 20 entries and keeps only digests (no before/after), a restore is only an unadvertised side effect of `revise`, and split exists for tasks only.
Add these to VERBS, generated on the CLI and as ACTIONS of the kind's one MCP tool (never a new tool; tools/list budget):
(1) `<kind> history <id> [--diff] [--limit N]`: the whole chain read from the log (not the fold's last 20): event, at, by, session, reason, digest; with --diff the field-level before and after (the def.* events carry `fields`; replay by lamport). Redacted, text fenced as data.
(2) `<kind> supersede <id> --by <id2> --reason` (wraps def_supersede; both stay, each names the other).
(3) `<kind> merge <id> [<id>...] --into <id2> --reason`: ONE log transaction: update the target (list fields tags, globs, links, categories are unioned; a scalar is kept unless --take <field>=<id> says otherwise; the text is the caller's: --text or the target's), then def.merged for each source; provenance both ways (the fold already keeps merged_from); refused when kinds differ, a source is not active, or the merge would drop a block-enforcement record into a weaker one without --allow-weaken.
(4) `<kind> split <id> --part <newid>:<field>=<value>[,..] (repeat) --reason` or `--from-file parts.toml`: ONE transaction: each part is a def.recorded with provenance.split_from = <id> (add-time duplicate check among the parts and against the rest, skipping the original), then def.retired of the original with reason and split_into = [ids]. Refuses a single part. No new event kind: split_into / split_from / restored_from are additive optional envelope fields the fold keeps in the history entry (D-compat: an older ddflow preserves what it does not read).
(5) `<kind> restore <id> [--to N|--to <lamport>] --reason`: re-records the fields of the chosen earlier version (default: the last active one) of a retired, superseded, merged or split record as def.recorded with provenance.restored_from; for a merged record the fold already drops it from the absorber's merged_from; for a split it restores the original and says the parts stay.
(6) EVIDENCE stamped on every def write (RC3): api/defs._envelope adds provenance.session (the agent's open session) and provenance.prompt (id of that session's latest session.prompt when there is one) beside `by`; additive. `show` prints them.
(7) WEAKENING FLAG (RC2, D-decision-management 2): RecordKind gains an optional `weakening(before, after) -> reason|""` hook (lower enforcement, widened override, status to retired/dropped/superseded, a guard removed). When the writer is an agent and the hook answers, the event carries weakening=<reason>; the fold exposes unacked agent changes; `<kind> ack <id>` is an OPERATOR-ONLY verb (declared field `operator_only` on RecordKind, honoured by surfaces/exemptions.py: refused on MCP with an explained exit 3) writing ONE new event kind def.acked {kind, id, digest, by}, registered with its first writer and an upcaster stamp. B-dec-manage's `decision ack` is an instance of this verb, not a second mechanism.
(8) READ-ONLY SOURCES (RC9): `readonly(record) -> reason|""` hook; every mutating verb refuses (exit 3) a record whose provenance source is an org bundle, naming source and revision and the local-override path. B-org-kinds registers the provider; with none registered nothing changes.
A kind may opt out of a verb in its descriptor WITH a reason (a proposal is never removed: reject and expire are its tombstones); the conformance test (B-rc-conformance) reads those reasons.

WHY (verified 2026-10-11): without this, five tasks each plan their own edit/retire/supersede/merge path (B199, B-rw-revision, B-coh-resolve, B-dec-manage, B-goal-model) and no task plans split or restore or a history view anywhere; evidence shown to the user is a digest, so 'who changed this rule and from what' cannot be answered after the fact; an agent can silently retire a block rule or drop a goal.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/records.py (RecordKind, _pre, _checked, _as), surfaces/records.py (the generator), api/defs.py (def_update, def_retire, def_supersede, def_merge, _envelope), core/defs.py and core/handlers/defs.py (DefRecord.history, merged_from), api/_dedupe.py, surfaces/exemptions.py, surfaces/history_verbs.py (render the new events), core/events.py (register def.acked with its first writer), core/upcasters.py.

HOW TO TEST (failing first): merge of two rules: target holds the unions, sources are status merged with successor, history on both sides names the other, one transaction (a failure injected after the first write leaves nothing half-done), replay is byte-identical; split into three: parts carry split_from, original retired with split_into, one part refused, duplicate part refused naming the other; restore returns the chosen version and history shows restored_from; history --diff shows before and after for three successive edits and is not cut at 20 entries; an agent lowering a rule from block to warn is flagged until the operator's ack, an operator edit is not flagged, ack over MCP is refused with exit 3 and the reason; a record from an org source refuses every mutating verb naming the source; old logs fold unchanged (golden); CLI and MCP bodies identical for every new verb (test_mcp_parity); tools/list budget test (raise TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET with a reason only if the added action text needs it).
SIZE: large (~800 lines + tests). Hot files api/records.py, surfaces/records.py, core/defs.py: B-goal-model, B-prop-model, B-rules-onto-record-surface, B-dec-manage, B-coh-resolve and B-rw-revision wait for this task.
ACCEPTANCE: on a throwaway repo, `rule add` -> `rule edit` -> `rule split` -> `rule merge` -> `rule remove` -> `rule restore` all work on CLI and MCP, `rule history <id> --diff` lists each step with who, when, why and session, and an agent-lowered enforcement shows as awaiting acknowledgement until the operator runs `rule ack`.
DOCS: docstring level here; the README section, the help topic `records` and the driver notes (when to merge, supersede or split) are written by B-rc-conformance (single editor of README and help.py).
data.title: Record lifecycle on the record surface for every kind: history with before/after, supersede, merge, split and restore as verbs of the one CLI group and one MCP tool, session and prompt stamped on every write, agent weakening flagged until the operator acknowledges, org-sourced records read-only

data.body:
Contract rows RC1, RC4, RC7 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "they ... can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do".

WHAT: a record kind's participation in search, recall, context packs, MCP resources, export and the change feed is DECLARED in its RecordKind descriptor and derived, so declaring a kind is the only step. This task adds the declarative fields (all with defaults) and derives the first three; the later tasks of this phase consume the others:
- search (default on): one FuncSource 'records' in services/searchcore registers every descriptor with a def_kind, yielding Hits from title + the descriptor's text fields + status/owner/phase facets; services/search.py KINDS and _DEF_KINDS stop being hard-coded lists and are built from the registry plus today's legacy entries (rule, skill, agent, schedule keep their output byte for byte: goldens first). `ddflow search --kind goal`, `--kind proposal`, `--state`, `--owner`, `--since` work for any declared kind.
- recall (the budgeted 'ask', RC7): infra/store.py RECALL_SOURCES is a fixed tuple of seven (decisions, lessons, memories, research, bugs, items, prompts): rules are NOT recallable today. Derive extra entries from descriptors: label = the kind in capitals, one 'follow it / consult it' hint line per kind (field `recall_hint`), cap of hits per kind so a large kind cannot crowd out lessons and decisions (the pack's one-per-source round robin, B-uni-context-pack); `recall --sources` accepts the new names. Existing recall output unchanged (golden).
- MCP resources: `ddflow://records/{kind}` (bounded newest-first list) and `ddflow://records/{kind}/{id}` (the record, its status, successor chain and history digest), generated for every descriptor with `resource=True` (default), replacing hand-written RESOURCES entries for new kinds; the existing ddflow://decisions, ddflow://research and others stay as they are (D-compat).
- Descriptor fields declared here (defaults inert, consumed later): `applies` (the applicability fields: globs, categories, gates, tags, always) for B-rc-context; `export` (which fields are chunk text and which metadata, a title template) for B-rc-rag-export; `feed` (binding or informational, the one-line summary template) for B-rc-changes; `recall_hint`; `resource`. Validation in RecordKind.__post_init__ (a name that is not a field is refused, like columns and filters today).
- Document the derived surface in the descriptor docstring; no per-kind search/recall/resource code is accepted in later tasks (B-goal-model's services/goals/search.py shrinks to the text-extraction function the descriptor names).

WHY (verified 2026-10-11): services/search.py lists kinds by hand, _DEF_KINDS is the frozenset {rule, skill, agent, schedule}, RECALL_SOURCES has no def kind, and RESOURCES are hand-registered: a goal, a proposal or a waiver would be invisible to `ddflow search` and `ddflow recall` until someone edits all three places, which is exactly the per-kind duplication D-unify exists to stop.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/searchcore (FuncSource, register, Hit), services/search.py (_def_docs is the seed), infra/store.py RECALL_SOURCES and api/knowledge/retrieval.py (the recall view), services/contextpack.py (Candidate), surfaces/mcp.py RESOURCES, api/records.py descriptors.

HOW TO TEST (failing first): a toy RecordKind declared only inside the test appears in `search --kind toy`, in recall under its label, in resources/list and resources/read, with no other edit; the rule, skill, agent, schedule and decision golden outputs of search and recall are byte-identical; a bad applies/export/feed field name is refused at declaration; per-kind recall cap holds with 200 toy records; resource payload is bounded and redacted; CLI and MCP parity; tools/list budget (resources are not tools).
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests). Hot files services/search.py, infra/store.py, api/records.py (after B-rc-lifecycle).
ACCEPTANCE: after B-goal-model lands, `ddflow search --kind goal "<title words>"` and `ddflow recall "<title words>"` find a goal with no goal-specific search code.
DOCS: docstrings; the help topic and README are written by B-rc-conformance.
data.title: Retrieval derived from the descriptor: any declared record kind is searchable, recallable (ask) and an MCP resource with no per-kind code; applies, export and feed declarations for the later tasks

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "Look at these skills for claude, are there ideas we could take advantage from, and extend the functionality of the ddflow tool, if such functionality or capability is missing, or impossible to implement with the current capabilities?" and, clarifying: "the idea is those skills to give us ideas for our default workflow if those ideas are worth it. How to manage skills and subagents and integrate those in our workflow is a separate development phase ... Do not add those skills to this project, just read the content and think of generic ideas that worth to be implemented in our default pipeline, but do follow the principles of this project - nothing have to be hardcoded - everything should be possible to configure, change, remove, change order, constants, variables, pipelines, workflows should be configurable, changeable, written as config (if modified default behavior) and able to be shared, managed by the user, ddflow cli or the agents, including via mcp interface".

Research R-skills-mining-gaps (CONFIRMED: what exists, what is planned, what is missing) and R-skills-mining-value (THEORETICAL: whether the ideas pay off). Skills read: e2e-scenario-testing, maintaining-documentation, mcp-cli, roborev-design-review, roborev-design-review-branch. Nothing here installs, generates or manages skills or subagents; that is P-skills and P-subagents (their authoring conventions are only noted there as input).

WHAT THIS PHASE ADDS (only what no existing task covers; everything else in the skills is already built or planned and was extended in place with a 'Skills-mining extension 2026-10-11' paragraph): (1) a persisted CLASS per document (evergreen | point_in_time | generated) that every docs check, gate and auto-fix honours, confirmed by the operator; (2) a review CURSOR per document (doc.reviewed: sha, verifier, deferred claims) so re-audits are incremental and an unverified claim never rides under a clean review; (3) a claims-versus-reality review gate whose evidence checks the VERB (the code path that enacts a claim), not the noun; (4) a terminology dictionary; (5) corpus-level docs checks (duplication, gaps, contradictions, unregistered documents); (6) scenario cards: agent-executed markdown tests with falsifiers, run as a gate and a scheduled sweep; (7) the review LENS as data per gate (today a code constant) with design, security and docs-claims lenses; (8) an optional reviewer PANEL with a synthesis record.

HOW EVERYTHING IS CONFIGURABLE: each item is data on an existing engine (document-type TOML, [docs.*] and [review.*] config sections, GateDef entries in .ddflow/gates.toml or the shipped built-ins, schedule job templates, definition records), editable by CLI and MCP, shareable through org bundles, removable or reorderable in the pipelines, and off or advisory by default so no existing project changes behaviour on upgrade. Invariants stay the floor: unavailable is never passed, cross-family review, failing-first for bugs, human gates not clearable over MCP.

B-pi-decide asks the operator first; nothing else here starts before the answers.
data.title: Default-pipeline ideas mined from five Claude skills: document class and review cursor, terminology, claims review, scenario cards, review lenses and panels, all as configuration and shipped templates

data.body:
Contract rows RC6, RC3, RC8, RC9 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "sessions are automatically informed for changes, they retrieve brief on session start".

WHAT: ONE change feed for every record kind, so a running session learns that a rule, decision, principle, goal, waiver or contested record changed WHILE IT WORKS, through the doors its harness already calls. No daemon (D-sched-no-daemon).
(1) services/changefeed.py: a pure function over the log's events from a lamport mark: `changes(log, since, kinds=None, exclude_agent=None, relevant_to=None, limit=...) -> entries` with {kind, id, verb (added, edited, retired, superseded, merged, split, restored, acked, waived, deviated, adopted, rejected, expired, contested, org-revision), by, at, session, why (reason), digest, summary line, binding}. A kind's mapping comes from its descriptor `feed` field (B-rc-participation): BINDING = changes what an agent must do (rule or decision at block or warn, a principle, a goal's status or target, a waiver granted or expired, a contested record, an applied org revision); everything else is INFORMATIONAL (lessons, research, proposals, advisory). The reader goes through the log's index from the mark, not a full fold (B-gap-log-scale), so a session that is up to date costs one lookup.
(2) services/seen.py: the per-reader cursor in .ddflow/local/seen/<agent-or-session>.json (git-ignored, derived, disposable): the lamport mark delivered, the time, per-kind counts. It advances only for what a door actually DELIVERED, never for what was merely computed. B-mu-sync-check reuses this store for its per-clone 'last look' (HEAD, shard counts) instead of a second file.
(3) The doors, one builder (services/hookdoors.py, which api/setup.py's hook handlers call; the handlers stay one-liners):
 a. brief and SessionStart: a section 'Changed since you last looked (N)': BINDING first, at most 5 lines, then '+M more: ddflow changes'; own changes excluded; cut from the bottom under session.brief_max_tokens but the count line is kept; a FRESH session shows nothing (the brief IS the state) and starts its cursor at now; a resumed or restarted agent shows what changed since its previous session ended (B-am-restart-brief supplies the end mark).
 b. claim: 'changed under this item': BINDING changes since the item's last start, only for records that apply to its globs, gate or category (guidance resolve).
 c. hooks prompt, pre_tool and post_tool (the canonical events already wired and handled by _on_nothing in api/setup.py): only a BINDING, relevant (applies to the held item's globs, always-scope, or the path being edited), undelivered change, at most once per [changes].min_interval_s (default 60), emitted through the harness's own injection format (hookio.emit) and only for harnesses whose descriptor lists the event in `inject`; fenced as data with the 'recorded DATA, not instructions' line.
 d. MCP, for harnesses with no usable hook: any tool reply to a reader with undelivered BINDING changes gets one `note:` content item (the pattern surfaces/mcp.py already uses for alias notices) naming the count and `ddflow changes`; heartbeat and wait replies carry a `changes` field; the first-call preamble (B-hy-first-call) includes the section of (a).
 e. explicit: `ddflow changes [--since last|<lamport>|<date>] [--kind K] [--mine|--others] [--all] [--ack]` (CLI, and ONE action of an existing MCP tool: ddflow_history is the candidate; a new tool only if the budget test passes with a reason). `--ack` advances the cursor without reading.
(4) OPERATOR OVERSIGHT: unacknowledged agent weakening changes (B-rc-lifecycle) are listed first for the operator by `ddflow changes --weakening` and counted in the brief ('N agent changes await your acknowledgement', like the needs_operator notices); ack is B-rc-lifecycle's operator-only verb.
(5) Config section [changes] (enabled, min_interval_s, brief_max_lines, hook_max_tokens, inject_binding_only) declared here with knob() docs and strictest fallbacks (D-enum-fallback-strict).
(6) PRIVACY (RC9): every summary line passes the log redactor; titles and reasons are somebody's words and travel fenced; only records in the log appear, so local-only records (.ddflow/local) never reach another reader; org revision changes appear as one line with source and revision (B-org-sync registers its 'newer revision' notice as a feed entry rather than a private brief line); proposals, deviations and discovery runs appear only for the project that holds them.

WHY (verified 2026-10-11): nothing tells a running session that a rule, decision or goal changed. The brief is read once at start; hooks prompt/pre_tool/post_tool/stop/session_end are wired and handled by _on_nothing; `ddflow wait` and heartbeat answer readiness and lease state only; B-mu-sync-check's last-look record covers shards and HEAD, not records; B-goal-deviation planned a private 'deviations since your last look' brief line, B-dec-waivers an expiry notice, B-org-sync a revision notice, B-sched-escalation a proposals line, B-mu-conflicts contested-record lines: five per-kind notices. A rule an agent edited in another lane stays unknown to every other running session until it restarts.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: core/events.py and the log index (infra/store.py events), api/lifecycle/brief.py (sections, budget), api/lifecycle/claim.py, api/setup.py _HOOK_HANDLERS and services/hookio.py (plan.inject, emit), surfaces/mcp.py (the alias-notice path), services/guidance/resolve.py (applies), core/provenance.py, core/redact.py, services/leases.py heartbeat, infra/localstore.

HOW TO TEST (fake clock, two readers): reader B is told once of a BINDING edit by reader A and never of its own edits; informational changes are counted not pushed; a tiny brief budget keeps the count line; a fresh session's brief is byte-identical to today (golden); a restarted agent sees what changed during its absence; the prompt hook emits additionalContext JSON for a harness that injects at that event and nothing for one that does not, throttled by min_interval_s; the MCP note appears once per change set; claim lists only changes whose records apply to the item; cursor advances only on delivery; an up-to-date reader reads no events (counter); a record title carrying 'ignore previous instructions' arrives fenced; a secret in a reason is redacted; local-only record never listed; CLI and MCP parity; weakening change by an agent is listed for the operator.
SIZE: large (~900 lines + tests). Hot files api/lifecycle/brief.py, api/setup.py, surfaces/mcp.py, config.py.
ACCEPTANCE: two live sessions on a throwaway repo: A edits a block rule; B's next prompt (or next MCP reply) carries one fenced line naming the rule, who, why; B's brief on restart lists it; `ddflow changes --all` shows it with the diff; the operator's brief shows the agent weakening awaiting acknowledgement.
DOCS: docstrings; README, help topic and driver notes (what the digest means and how to answer it) are written by B-rc-conformance.
data.title: Change feed for every record kind: per-session cursor, 'changed since you last looked' in brief, claim, prompt/pre-tool/post-tool hooks and MCP replies, agent weakening listed for the operator

data.body:
Ask the operator, record the decision, write docs/ddflow/decisions/pipeline-ideas.md. Ask one question at a time with the recommended default; record each answer verbatim (ddflow session prompt) and the decision (ddflow decision add --globs 'ddflow/services/doctypes/**,ddflow/services/review.py,ddflow/api/review.py,ddflow/services/gates/**'). Do not start any other B-pi-* task before this is answered. Evidence: R-skills-mining-gaps (CONFIRMED), R-skills-mining-value (THEORETICAL: the benefit is unmeasured; B-pi-acceptance measures it).

PRINCIPLE (operator 2026-10-11): nothing hardcoded; every behaviour is a config key, a document-type or gate definition, or a shipped template that a project can override, remove or reorder, share through org bundles, and edit over CLI and MCP; an agent's change over MCP is reported to the operator. Defaults below are all 'off or advisory': an existing project changes nothing on upgrade.

QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS
1. Document class. DEFAULT: a `contract` field on a document type (evergreen | point_in_time | generated) plus a `[docs.classes]` glob-to-contract map for documents with no type; an unclassified document is treated as point_in_time (the safe side) until the operator confirms; the confirmation is ONE group-level question (folder globs plus named exceptions), recorded as a doc.classified event with the operator's words, never decided by the agent per document. Shipped defaults: README/ARCHITECTURE/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTING evergreen; ADR, plans, specs, decisions, CHANGELOG, HISTORY, research point_in_time; region-owned exports generated. Existing [enforce].doc_exclude keeps working and is read as 'not checked'.
2. Where the review stamp lives. DEFAULT: the log (doc.reviewed event with sha, verifier, deferred count), never the file; an optional in-file stamp region is `[docs].stamp = off|region`, default off (a stamp in the file churns every clone and conflicts under P-multiuser).
3. Who may record a doc as reviewed. DEFAULT: `[docs].review_requires = cross_family` (the reviewer is not the editor and a different model family from the agent that edited), unavailable when no such reviewer ran (recorded unavailable, no review stamp); `any` and `off` selectable.
4. Auto-fix. DEFAULT: report only. `[docs.autofix].allow` is an empty list; the selectable classes are identifier, path, flag, config_default and (with the dictionary) deprecated_term; counts, bare line-number citations, absence claims, cross-reference targets, example structure, behavioural claims and claims whose ground truth is outside the repository are a FLOOR that can never be listed. Only evergreen documents; a missing counterpart is confirmed removed-versus-renamed from git history before it is called removed.
5. Terminology dictionary. DEFAULT: yes, as an opt-in definition-record kind `term` (term, definition, deprecated synonyms, scope globs, exceptions by path glob only, permanence temporary|permanent); empty on a new project; a check family `terminology` in `ddflow docs check`, warn by default, whole-word, evergreen documents only; code identifiers and UI strings are findings, never auto-fixed. Alternative: do not build it (use rules with forbidden_text).
6. Scenario cards. DEFAULT: a `scenario` document type (collection `docs/scenarios/{slug}.md`) with the sections Pre-state, Steps, Expected, Cleanup, Sharp edges and a required falsifier on every Expected line; a `scenario` gate that is NOT in the default pipeline (add it with `ddflow workflow pipeline`) and applies_when the item's globs touch the card's `covers` globs; a weekly sweep job shipped disabled. Results are scenario.ran events with one verdict per step (pass | fail | unavailable) and the observed value; unavailable is never pass. Alternative: keep scenarios as demos/ scripts only.
7. Review lenses. DEFAULT: the lens (a short intent line plus an optional prompt template) becomes data on the gate (`lens`, `lens_prompt`), replacing the two-entry constant _LENSES in ddflow/api/review.py; shipped lenses refute, intent (today's two), plus design, security and docs_claims; shipped gate `design_review` available but NOT in the default pipeline; the default pipeline is unchanged. Findings keep HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW.
8. Reviewer panel. DEFAULT: off. `[review.panel.<gate>]` members (reviewer names), min_members, verdict_rule (any_confirmed | majority | all), merge_floor (similarity for merging equal findings); every member must pass the independence rule; a panel with fewer than min_members available is partial/unavailable, never passed; the synthesis is the gate's record (one id for triage), each finding carries who found it and the agreement count.
9. MCP tool guard (from the mcp-cli skill's allow/deny). DEFAULT: do not build now; recorded as input to B-sub-sod (role-based separation of duties) where a `[mcp.guard]` allow/deny glob list per profile would sit. Say yes to file it as its own task.
10. Phase-level or task-level. DEFAULT: the claims review and the corpus checks run at the docs gate of a phase and in the docs-correctness schedule job; the scenario gate is task-level only when added.

Docs: docs/ddflow/decisions/pipeline-ideas.md.
data.title: Operator decisions for the skills-mined pipeline ideas: document class, review cursor, auto-fix, terminology, scenario cards, review lenses, panels

data.body:
Contract rows RC4, RC6, RC7 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "... can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do". WHAT: ONE relevance-matched context builder for every record kind, delivered automatically at the moments an agent starts a task, sends a prompt or is about to edit a file, and available on demand as the 'ask'. It replaces the per-kind injectors planned today (research in B-rw-context, skills in B-skills-context, decisions in B-dec-rag, goals in B-goal-inject) with providers of one engine. (1) services/applicable.py `related(repo, *, text="", paths=(), item="", kinds=None, budget, reader) -> Pack`: candidates from every kind whose descriptor declares `applies` (B-rc-participation) plus registered providers (`register_provider(name, fn)`; B-rw-context and B-skills-context register theirs here instead of building injectors). Tiers: (a) SCOPE match: always, globs, categories, gates, the item's goal chain (services/guidance/resolve.py is reused as is, so claim-time behaviour is unchanged); (b) TEXT match: the task, item title or prompt text against the context-enabled kinds through the one search engine (BM25 + trigram, semantic rerank when [rag] is configured), above [context].min_score; (c) providers. Ranking: pinned and block first, then scope specificity, then score; a per-kind cap so lessons cannot crowd out rules; near-duplicates folded by textsim; every hit cited kind:id and fenced (core/provenance); one Budget (services/contextpack.py). (2) The reader's LEDGER (the services/seen.py store of B-rc-changes): a record already shown to this session is not shown again unless its digest changed, so a long session is not re-fed the same rule on every prompt. (3) Doors, in services/hookdoors.py: UserPromptSubmit/BeforeAgent (query: the prompt plus the held item's title; budget [context].prompt_max_tokens, default 600), PreToolUse on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit (query: the path and its scope; budget 800) and claim (the existing guidance injection stays; this adds the non-guidance kinds and the goal chain's Direction line). Each only for harnesses whose descriptor lists the event in `inject`; where no hook can inject, the same pack is the answer to `recall --for` and the first-call preamble carries a one-line pointer. Nothing is injected when nothing clears the threshold; a quiet door is the normal case. (4) The ASK: `ddflow recall --for item:|path:

|text:` (CLI) and the same argument on the existing recall MCP tool (no new tool): returns the pack with the reason each hit matched (scope, goal chain, score) so an agent can judge it. `ddflow search` stays the person's lookup. (5) Config [context] (enabled, inject = scope|scope+text|off with default scope+text, min_score, prompt_max_tokens, pre_tool_max_tokens, per_kind_cap) declared here with docs and strictest fallbacks. (6) MEASURE it (the failure mode is noise): a labelled fixture of 40 real prompts/paths from this log with the records a person would want; precision and recall of the door at the default threshold are asserted and printed, and the numbers go in the task's completion evidence. WHY (verified 2026-10-11): claim-time injection exists for rules and decisions only (services/guidance/inject.py, four doors); mid-session nothing is injected for any kind; the only planned edit-time injector is research's (B-rw-context, PreToolUse on Edit/Write) and it is a private one, B-skills-context and B-dec-rag plan more, and no task injects at prompt time. Goals, proposals and waivers would each need a fifth. One engine with providers is the D-unify answer. INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{inject,resolve}.py, services/contextpack.py, services/searchcore, services/embed.py, services/hookio.py, services/hookdoors.py (B-rc-changes), services/seen.py, api/knowledge/retrieval.py (recall), core/provenance.py. HOW TO TEST: a rule scoped to src/billing/** is offered before the first Edit under that path and not again until it changes; a prompt about 'retry the webhook' surfaces the lesson and decision with those words above the threshold and nothing for 'rename this variable'; per-kind cap holds; budget never exceeded; a harness without pre_tool injection gets nothing from the hook and the same pack from `recall --for path:`; providers registered by research and skills appear; goal chain printed as Direction; injected-instruction text stays fenced; the precision/recall fixture meets its floor; CLI/MCP parity; tools/list budget. SIZE: large (~800 lines + tests). Hot files api/knowledge/retrieval.py, services/hookdoors.py, config.py (after B-rc-changes). ACCEPTANCE: on this repository, an agent about to edit ddflow/api/records.py is shown D-record-surface-contract and the rules that apply, once; `recall --for item:B-goal-model` returns the contract, the decisions and the research that govern it. DOCS: docstrings; README, help and driver notes by B-rc-conformance.
data.title: Relevance-matched automatic context for every record kind: one builder with providers, delivered at prompt, pre-edit and claim, ledger of what a session was already shown, and recall --for as the ask

data.body:
Contract row RC5 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "... search, context insert, rag export interfaces and functionalities".

WHAT: a RAG-ready export of the project's records, so an external vector store, a Claude project, a company knowledge base or another agent can ingest rules, decisions, principles, goals, lessons and research with stable ids and provenance, and keep it in step as records change. `ddflow export` today generates human documents (ROADMAP, RULES, DECISIONS, ...); `ddflow docs ask` (B-ds-rag) retrieves from DOCUMENT files; neither is a machine corpus of records.
(1) Export document kind `records` (services/export/kind_records.py, registered in services/export/registry.py; CLI `ddflow export records`, MCP the existing ddflow_export tool's `records` document; no new tool). Default target .ddflow/local/export/records.jsonl (git-ignored, derived; committing it is the operator's opt-in like any export target, D-export-selection). Options: --kind (repeatable), --status active|all, --since last|<lamport>|<date>, --with-history, --format jsonl|md-dir, --out, --check, --diff (as the other export kinds).
(2) One chunk per line, deterministic: {chunk_id "<kind>:<id>@<digest8>#<n>", doc_id "<kind>:<id>", kind, id, status, title, text (the descriptor's `export` text fields rendered as prose; long text split on sentence/heading boundaries to at most [export].records_chunk_tokens, no overlap), metadata {tags, globs, categories, enforcement, override, owner, review_by, links, goal, key_result_ids}, valid_from, valid_until, supersedes, superseded_by, merged_from, split_from, split_into, provenance {by, at, session, prompt, source, org_source, trust}, cites, fence "data"}. --with-history adds one 'revision' chunk per change (reason, who, when, before/after digest). A stable id means an unchanged record re-exports byte-identically, so an external store upserts only what changed.
(3) TOMBSTONES: tombstones.jsonl lists every doc_id retired, superseded, merged or split since --since, with the successor, so an external index deletes or redirects them (the part a plain dump forgets; uses B-rc-lifecycle's events). manifest.json: schema version, counts per kind, corpus digest, generated_at, ddflow version.
(4) Safety and privacy (RC9): the log redaction profile on every text (B-export-redact-fence); text is somebody's words, so each chunk is marked trust and fenced as data and an embedded instruction stays inert; local-only and personal records are excluded; org-sourced records are included with org_source unless [export].records_exclude_org; proposals, deviations and waivers are exported only when named in --kind. No embedding is computed or stored here (that stays the [rag] extra and external).
(5) Kinds covered: every RecordKind with an `export` declaration (B-rc-participation; default for def kinds) plus decisions, lessons and research through three small adapters until those move onto descriptors.
(6) MCP resource ddflow://records/{kind}/{id} (B-rc-participation) serves the same chunk for one record.

WHY: the operator's request names RAG export as part of the interface a record must have; the audit found none in code or tasks (searched export, rag, jsonl, chunk, llms.txt, corpus: only D-export documents and the docs-search RAG reply). Without tombstones and stable ids an external index drifts from the log.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/export/{registry,frame,write,safe}.py and api/export.py (document kinds, --check/--diff/--update, redaction), core/defs.py history, B-rc-lifecycle events, services/contextpack.py (token estimate), core/redact.py, core/provenance.py.

HOW TO TEST: golden jsonl for a fixture with an edited, a merged, a split and a retired rule plus a decision and a lesson; two exports are byte-identical; --since returns only the changed chunks and the right tombstones; a planted secret never appears; 'ignore previous instructions' in a body stays data-marked; local-only record absent; org record labelled; chunk sizes within the bound; --check detects a stale target; CLI and MCP parity; tools/list budget (ddflow_export gains no tool).
SIZE: medium (~600 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow export records --since last --out /tmp/x` on this repository yields chunks and tombstones that a 20-line script can upsert into an in-memory index; re-running prints nothing new.
DOCS: docstrings; README (how to feed an external store) and help topic by B-rc-conformance.
data.title: RAG export of records: chunks with stable ids, provenance, validity and tombstones for retired, merged and split records, as an export document kind and an MCP resource

data.body:
Contract row RC12 (D-record-surface-contract) and the documentation of rows RC1 to RC11. Operator 2026-10-11: "make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project".

WHAT: the contract becomes a test, so a future record kind cannot skip a row quietly.
(1) tests/test_record_contract.py, parametrised over api.records.KINDS and over core/defs.DEF_KINDS (a def kind with no descriptor must appear in the exemption table with its reason: doctype, schedule, trigger, skill, agent and claim have none today). Per kind it asserts, mechanically on a seeded fixture: RC1 the CLI group and exactly one MCP tool exist and a body from each verb is identical on both faces; RC2 add/edit/remove/revise/history/supersede/merge/split/restore each work or the descriptor opts out with a reason, and add refuses a near-duplicate; RC3 every write event carries by, at, reason, session and digests and replay reproduces the state; RC4 a probe record is found by `search --kind`, `recall` and `resources/read`; RC5 it appears in `export records` and a retired one produces a tombstone; RC6 a second reader is told of a binding edit through the change feed and a fresh session's brief is unchanged; RC7 `recall --for` returns it for a matching path or text; RC8 a kind with review_by lists a stale record in doctor; RC9 an org-sourced record refuses a mutating verb and a local-only one is absent from feed and export; RC10 the payload version has an upcaster entry and an old-log golden folds; RC11 a help topic or the `records` topic names the kind.
(2) tests/record_contract_exemptions.py: kind -> {row: reason}, every reason non-empty, and a ratchet file holding the total, which may only go DOWN (the P-unify guard pattern).
(3) Docs, written here as the single editor of README.md, ddflow/templates/prompts/help/records.md and ddflow/services/help.py TOPICS, and of both copies of the implement-phase driver: the README section 'The record contract' (the twelve rows in plain words, with the exemption count), the help topic `records` (lifecycle verbs, history and restore, the change digest and how to answer it, recall --for, feeding an external store from `export records`, what is operator-only), and driver notes for agents (when to merge, split or supersede; what 'changed since you last looked' means; a weakening change is flagged for the operator). Other tasks in this phase and in P-goals/P-decisions write docstring-level text only.
(4) Doctor line: `doctor` reports the number of contract exemptions and any kind whose descriptor disables a verb without a reason.

WHY: the contract is twelve rows across eight services; without a generated test the next kind (a skill, a doc type, a claim) re-opens every gap, which is how rules ended up with six hand-written MCP tools, no recall and no history.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: tests/test_record_surface.py, tests/test_mcp_parity.py, tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py, tests/test_help.py, the P-unify ratchet pattern (B-uni-guards), tests/scenarios helpers.

HOW TO TEST: the test runs green for rule (after B-rules-onto-record-surface) and for a toy kind; deleting any one derived registration makes exactly the matching row fail (mutation check per row, as B-mut-* does); the ratchet fails when an exemption is added.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + docs). Waits for every other task of this phase.
ACCEPTANCE: `pytest tests/test_record_contract.py` lists every kind and row with pass or its exemption reason; README, help and driver text updated; B-goal-acceptance and B-dec-acceptance cite it.
data.title: Record contract conformance: a generated test over every declared record kind for rows RC1-RC11, a shrinking exemption ratchet, and the README, help topic and driver text of the contract

data.body:
WHAT: every document has a persisted CLASS -- evergreen (reflects current reality; drift is a defect), point_in_time (true as of its date; drift is expected, the body is never rewritten to match code, at most a supersede banner or an as-of line) or generated (owned by a ddflow region, guarded by its hash) -- and every docs check, gate and auto-fix honours it. WHY: the maintaining-documentation skill's most expensive failure is 'bringing the docs up to date' across a dated design set and erasing the record; ddflow's only protection today is [enforce].doc_exclude, a hard-coded-default glob list that says 'not checked' and cannot say 'checked as history, edited only by banner'. R-skills-mining-gaps (CONFIRMED): no class is stored anywhere; the docs gate prompt (services/gates/defs.py 'docs') tells the agent to update what is stale with no class in sight.

INTERFACE REUSED (nothing new engine-wise): the document-type TOML (B-dt-spec) gets one field `contract = "evergreen" | "point_in_time" | "generated"`; documents with no type are classified by `[docs.classes]` (a table of contract -> glob list, e.g. point_in_time = ["docs/ddflow/decisions/**", "docs/plans/**"]); doc.classified event (kind registered via B-dt-events: path or glob, contract, confirmed_by, the operator's words as a session prompt id) folded into State.docs; the guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-inject) delivers a shipped, overridable rule to an item whose globs touch a point_in_time document; docscheck (services/docscheck.py) takes the class from one resolver. Resolution order: doc.classified (operator-confirmed) > type contract > [docs.classes] > default, and the default for an unclassified document is point_in_time (safe side) plus a doctor note 'N documents unclassified'.
CONFIG SHAPE: `[docs.classes]` contract -> globs; `[docs].point_in_time_edits = off|warn|block` (default warn: a diff that changes a point_in_time document outside its banner region or its as_of/superseded_by front matter is reported by the docs check and in the docs gate evidence; block makes the docs gate refuse a pass); `[docs].unclassified = point_in_time|evergreen` (default point_in_time). All editable with ddflow config / ddflow_configure; the shipped rule text is a template under .ddflow/rules or templates that a project overrides or removes.
BEHAVIOUR: (a) `ddflow docs check` reports drift findings (missing identifiers, stale flags, B-docs-coverage) only for evergreen documents; a point_in_time document gets one NOTE 'history: not checked, as of <date>'; a generated document is checked by its region hash, not its text. (b) `ddflow docs classify` (verbs on the one ddflow_docs tool): `--propose` lists the group-level classification (folder globs plus named exceptions, precedence: a point-in-time signal such as a dated filename or a plans/specs/decisions folder beats an evergreen name like README) for ONE operator question; `confirm` records doc.classified and is refused for an agent unless it carries the operator's words (the B-dt-interview rule). (c) onboarding (B-dt-onboard, B-docs-onboarding) asks that one question; the brief shows 'N documents unclassified' within the brief budget. (d) the claims review (B-pi-claims-review) and any auto-fix refuse a non-evergreen document.
TESTS (failing-first): a fixture with a dated design spec and a README that both drift from the code: the check reports the README only; an agent edit to the spec body is a warning (block when configured), a banner-only edit is clean; an unclassified document behaves as point_in_time and raises the doctor note; an agent confirming without the operator's words is refused (exit 3); replay rebuilds the classes; the old [enforce].doc_exclude still means 'not checked'. SIZE: medium (about 400 lines + tests). ACCEPTANCE: the above plus CLI/MCP parity and a README/help-topic paragraph.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.
data.title: Document class (evergreen, point_in_time, generated) persisted and confirmed by the operator; docs checks, the docs gate and auto-fix honour it

data.body:
WHAT: a per-document REVIEW CURSOR: doc.reviewed {doc, sha, scope full|incremental, verifier, verifier_family, claims_checked, claims_deferred, outcome passed|partial|unavailable}, folded into State.docs[path].reviewed, and a worklist built from it. WHY: the maintaining-documentation skill uses a 'last-reviewed <sha> + deferred N claims' stamp as the incremental cursor and rule 'never let an unverified claim ride under a clean stamp'. B-dt-health (planned) measures staleness from 'the document last changed', but a document can be verified without changing and can change without being verified; there is no record of WHAT was verified, by whom, or how much was left unverified (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED).

INTERFACE REUSED: the doc.* event family and State.docs fold (B-dt-events; this task registers doc.reviewed there); git range queries (services/changes, B-uni-git-queries) for 'files in depends_on globs changed since sha'; the reviewer independence check (services/gates/reviewers.family_of, agent.reviewer_family_must_differ) for the verifier; region engine (B-tpl-regions) only for the OPTIONAL in-file stamp; docs pending/status verbs (B-dt-surfaces) on the one ddflow_docs tool.
CONFIG SHAPE: `[docs].review_requires = "cross_family" | "any" | "off"` (default cross_family: the verifier is not the editor and from a different model family than the agent that edited; none available -> outcome unavailable, no cursor advance); `[docs].full_review_every_days = 0` (0 = never forced); `[docs].stamp = "off" | "region"` (default off; region writes a generated block with date, short sha and deferred count through the region engine); `[docs].deferred_blocks_clean = true` (a document with deferred > 0 is never shown as clean). A document type may override these per type ([doctype.review]).
BEHAVIOUR: `ddflow docs reviewed <doc> --sha S --claims-checked N --deferred M --verifier V` records the event (refused with exit 3 when review_requires is not met, never recorded passed on a verifier that did not run); `ddflow docs pending --stale [--json]` lists documents ranked: never reviewed; deferred > 0 (stays listed whatever the sha); a depends_on glob changed since the reviewed sha; older than full_review_every_days. An incremental pass is triage, not soundness: a claim whose ground truth is outside the repository, or the external binary, is cleared only by scope=full and counts as deferred otherwise. The brief shows one budgeted line ('3 documents due, 2 with deferred claims'); doctor notes carry the remedy. point_in_time documents are never stamped (class from B-pi-doc-class).
TESTS (failing-first): same-family verifier refused under cross_family; a document with deferred 2 stays on the worklist after a newer sha is recorded; a changed depends_on file puts a reviewed document back; unavailable verifier leaves the cursor; replay rebuilds the cursors; stamp=region idempotent. SIZE: small-medium (about 300 lines). ACCEPTANCE: the tests, parity, README/help text, and B-dt-health consuming the cursor instead of recomputing 'last changed'.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.

data.body:
WHAT: a claims-versus-reality review for documents, shipped as an optional agent gate `docs_claims` and a prompt template, plus one mechanical check. WHY: ddflow's docs check (B-docscheck-core, done) verifies the NOUN: an inline identifier or link exists in the tracked tree. The maintaining-documentation skill's central lesson is that 'X is validated / happens when Y / is done by Z' is verified only by the code path that enacts it (the verb), and that existence-only confirmation is the commonest false 'matches'. Nothing in ddflow asks for or checks a citation of the enacting code (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED), and the shipped docs gate prompt says 'check counts ... and update' while the skill's rubric hands counts, line-number citations, absence claims and behavioural claims to a human.

INTERFACE REUSED: GateDef (services/gates/defs.py): a new optional built-in `docs_claims` (agent gate, applies_to both, reviewer = different_family, requires_evidence = ["fields"], evidence_fields = ["claims", "interview", "deferred"]) -- not in the default pipeline; a project adds it with `ddflow workflow pipeline` or uses it as the doc_review gate of the doc-task pipeline (B-dt-workflow) and in the docs-correctness schedule job (B-sched-defaults). Structured evidence storage is B-gate-evidence-fields. Prompt template templates/prompts/commands/docs-claims.md (overridable through .ddflow/prompts). Class from B-pi-doc-class; cursor from B-pi-doc-reviewed; the mechanical part is a check family in docscheck.
PROMPT CONTRACT (all of it text in the template, editable): (1) read the class first and refuse non-evergreen documents (offer a banner/as-of line instead); (2) list the claims of each evergreen document by kind (identifier, path, flag, config default, route/field, count, line citation, absence, behaviour, external); (3) for each claim a verdict matches | drifted | deferred | interview and a CITATION `path:symbol` of the code that enacts the claim -- a citation that only shows the noun exists is not accepted for a verb claim ('the loader rejects X' needs the rejecting branch, 'the stream closes when terminal' needs the close on every terminal state or the one it misses); (4) a missing counterpart is confirmed removed-versus-renamed from git history (`git log -S`) before anything is called removed; (5) fixes only for classes listed in [docs.autofix].allow (default empty, report only), only when exactly one live non-test counterpart exists and the replacement leaves the sentence true; counts, line numbers, absence claims, cross-references, example structure, behavioural and external claims go to the `interview` list for the operator; (6) a second adversarial pass over the agent's own edits by the independent verifier before a doc.reviewed is recorded.
MECHANICAL PART: a docs-check family `line_citation` flags a bare `file.ext:LINE[-LINE]` citation in an evergreen document as a NOTE with the suggestion `file:symbol` (never renumbered, never auto-fixed); `[docs].flag_line_citations = true|false` (default true, severity from [docs].severity). The evidence validator rejects a claims row whose citation does not match `[gate.docs_claims].citation_pattern` (default `\S+[:#]\w+`), so 'looks right' cannot be recorded as a pass.
CONFIG SHAPE: [docs.autofix] allow = [] (floor classes cannot be listed: count, line_citation, absence, cross_reference, example_structure, behaviour, external), [gate.docs_claims] fields via ddflow config --set, [docs] flag_line_citations. Reword the default `docs` gate prompt: counts are command-determined count markers (B-docscheck-extractors) or an interview item, never hand-edited.
TESTS (failing-first): a fixture document stating 'the loader rejects an emit node that declares runner' where the symbol exists but nothing rejects it: the gate record with an existence-only citation is refused, with the rejecting branch cited it is accepted; a bare line citation is flagged and not rewritten; a point_in_time document is refused; a same-family verifier is refused; an unavailable verifier records the gate unavailable. SIZE: medium (about 350 lines + prompt template). ACCEPTANCE: tests, README/help topic, driver text for the docs step.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.

data.body:
WHAT: a terminology dictionary as an opt-in definition-record kind `term`, a `terminology` check family, relevance-matched delivery and a generated DICTIONARY document. WHY: the maintaining-documentation skill keeps normative terms (a heading is the replacement for its deprecated synonyms) with exceptions scoped by path globs, and sweeps documents, identifiers, UI strings and new commit messages for drift. ddflow has rules with forbidden text only per document section (B-dt-validate) and the id-vocabulary work (P-id-schemes) renames ddflow's OWN kinds; nothing records a project's terminology (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED: ddflow search for dictionary/terminology/glossary finds no record).

INTERFACE REUSED: definition records (core/defs.py, B-uni-def-records, done) and the RecordKind descriptor (B-uni-record-surface, done) give list/show/add/edit/remove/search/revise on CLI and one MCP verb for free, plus the add-time duplicate/contradiction check (two entries claiming the same synonym are a contradiction, an entry already defined is a duplicate); the docs group `ddflow docs term ...` and the ONE ddflow_docs MCP tool (no new tools/list entry); the guidance inject (B-uni-guidance-inject) for delivery; docscheck for the sweep; B-dt-sources `kind:terms` for the generated document type `dictionary` (target docs/DICTIONARY.md, region-owned, B-dt-library).
RECORD SHAPE: term {term, definition, deprecated[] (synonyms), scope globs (default: evergreen documents; `**/*.md`), exceptions[] {globs (path globs only, never prose), reason, permanence temporary|permanent}, status, review_by}. CONFIG SHAPE: `[docs.terms] enabled = true` (a no-op while no term exists), `severity = warn`, `code_identifiers = findings` (a rename suggestion, never auto-fixed), `ui_strings = findings`, `commit_messages = off|warn` (new messages only via the precommit service; history is never flagged), `match = whole_word`. Auto-fix is the claims review's `deprecated_term` class in [docs.autofix].allow (default off): the synonym maps to exactly one entry, whole-word, no exception covers it, evergreen document only, and the replacement leaves the sentence true.
BEHAVIOUR: `ddflow docs check` family `terminology` lists deprecated-synonym hits per evergreen document with the replacement; `ddflow docs term exception remove` refuses a permanent exception without the operator's words and a temporary one without a git-history check recorded (a scan miss is not resolution); the dictionary excludes itself from its own sweep; terms whose scope globs match an item's globs are offered at claim and in the gate prompts of a docs gate within the context budget; `ddflow docs term` shows a one-sitting-readable list (a lint warns over [docs.terms].max_entries, default 60: load-bearing terms only).
TESTS (failing-first): whole-word hit and non-hit ('config' inside 'configure'), an exception glob suppresses, a duplicate/contradicting add is refused with the answer flags, replay, parity, the generated DICTIONARY round-trips, no term means no finding and no cost. SIZE: medium (about 450 lines + a doc type TOML). ACCEPTANCE: tests plus README/help topic; the operator can add, edit, retire and merge terms by CLI and by MCP.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.

WHAT: corpus-level documentation checks -- the defects invisible to a per-document pass. WHY: the maintaining-documentation skill's corpus phase finds duplication, gaps, cross-document contradictions and a missing index; ddflow's planned checks (B-docs-*, B-dt-health) are all per document or per diff, and P-coherence checks records, not document text (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED).
INTERFACE REUSED: the docs index and chunker (B-ds-chunker, B-ds-index), searchcore similarity and the `dupes` floor logic for duplicate sections, document-type registry (B-dt-spec) for 'registered', the extractors (B-docscheck-extractors) for the same-knob-different-value contradiction, the health report (B-dt-health), the docs-correctness schedule job (B-sched-defaults), the class (B-pi-doc-class).
CHECKS (a check family `corpus` in ddflow docs check; each a config key): (1) duplicate sections across evergreen documents at similarity >= `[docs.corpus].dup_floor` (default 0.85) with the two locations; (2) documents under check_paths not covered by any document type or the index (an orphan: a FINDING to file or to register, never a mandate to write a document -- a coverage gap names a reader or is dropped); (3) a registered document whose target is missing or whose index row is absent; (4) two documents stating different values for the same extracted knob or flag default; (5) the generated index document `docs-index` (Doc | What | Class | Owns, Owns = depends_on globs) added to the shipped document-type library (B-dt-library) so the registry has a readable view.
CONFIG SHAPE: `[docs.corpus] enabled = false` (default off until a project asks; the docs-correctness job turns it on), `dup_floor`, `max_findings = 20` (a bounded report, the tail summarised), `severity = warn`.
TESTS (failing-first): a fixture with two documents that copy a section and disagree about a default: both are found, one is not when it differs below the floor; an orphan is listed; disabled by default costs nothing; budgeted output. SIZE: small-medium. ACCEPTANCE: tests, parity, help text; runs inside the weekly docs-correctness job.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.
