data.body:
Contract row RC12 (D-record-surface-contract) and the documentation of rows RC1 to RC11. Operator 2026-10-11: "make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project".

WHAT: the contract becomes a test, so a future record kind cannot skip a row quietly.
(1) tests/test_record_contract.py, parametrised over api.records.KINDS and over core/defs.DEF_KINDS (a def kind with no descriptor must appear in the exemption table with its reason: doctype, schedule, trigger, skill, agent and claim have none today). Per kind it asserts, mechanically on a seeded fixture: RC1 the CLI group and exactly one MCP tool exist and a body from each verb is identical on both faces; RC2 add/edit/remove/revise/history/supersede/merge/split/restore each work or the descriptor opts out with a reason, and add refuses a near-duplicate; RC3 every write event carries by, at, reason, session and digests and replay reproduces the state; RC4 a probe record is found by `search --kind`, `recall` and `resources/read`; RC5 it appears in `export records` and a retired one produces a tombstone; RC6 a second reader is told of a binding edit through the change feed and a fresh session's brief is unchanged; RC7 `recall --for` returns it for a matching path or text; RC8 a kind with review_by lists a stale record in doctor; RC9 an org-sourced record refuses a mutating verb and a local-only one is absent from feed and export; RC10 the payload version has an upcaster entry and an old-log golden folds; RC11 a help topic or the `records` topic names the kind.
(2) tests/record_contract_exemptions.py: kind -> {row: reason}, every reason non-empty, and a ratchet file holding the total, which may only go DOWN (the P-unify guard pattern).
(3) Docs, written here as the single editor of README.md, ddflow/templates/prompts/help/records.md and ddflow/services/help.py TOPICS, and of both copies of the implement-phase driver: the README section 'The record contract' (the twelve rows in plain words, with the exemption count), the help topic `records` (lifecycle verbs, history and restore, the change digest and how to answer it, recall --for, feeding an external store from `export records`, what is operator-only), and driver notes for agents (when to merge, split or supersede; what 'changed since you last looked' means; a weakening change is flagged for the operator). Other tasks in this phase and in P-goals/P-decisions write docstring-level text only.
(4) Doctor line: `doctor` reports the number of contract exemptions and any kind whose descriptor disables a verb without a reason.

WHY: the contract is twelve rows across eight services; without a generated test the next kind (a skill, a doc type, a claim) re-opens every gap, which is how rules ended up with six hand-written MCP tools, no recall and no history.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: tests/test_record_surface.py, tests/test_mcp_parity.py, tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py, tests/test_help.py, the P-unify ratchet pattern (B-uni-guards), tests/scenarios helpers.

HOW TO TEST: the test runs green for rule (after B-rules-onto-record-surface) and for a toy kind; deleting any one derived registration makes exactly the matching row fail (mutation check per row, as B-mut-* does); the ratchet fails when an exemption is added.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + docs). Waits for every other task of this phase.
ACCEPTANCE: `pytest tests/test_record_contract.py` lists every kind and row with pass or its exemption reason; README, help and driver text updated; B-goal-acceptance and B-dec-acceptance cite it.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the rule kind is declared today (api/records.py RULE) but its CLI is hand-written and its MCP surface is six tools, so rule enters the exemption table for RC1 (one tool) and RC4 (recall) with those reasons; B-rules-onto-record-surface and B-rc-participation remove the rows, and the ratchet makes the count go down.

Ask the operator, record the decision, write docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md. Ask them one at a time with the recommended default; record each answer verbatim (ddflow session prompt) and as a decision (ddflow decision add --globs ...). Do not start any other B-goal-* or B-prop-* task before this is answered.

QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS (evidence: R-goals-existing-map, R-goals-principles-proposals-design):
1. Is a principle a new kind or a field? DEFAULT: a field, not a kind. Add one field to the guidance record, override = none | waive | deviate (how a finding is cleared), orthogonal to enforcement (how hard a finding is). Principle = enforcement warn + override deviate; rule = block + waive; org floor = block + none; preference = advisory. Vocabulary shown to people: MUST / SHOULD / MAY (RFC 2119) next to the enforcement word. Rejected: a separate principle store (a second engine to keep in step), and enforcement alone (a warn finding needs no answer, so a soft rule fails by silence).
2. Who may deviate from a principle, and does it expire? DEFAULT: the authoring agent records a deviation, item-scoped, reason required (evidence optional), no approval, no expiry (it dies with the item), always visible in brief, completion summary and the operator's decision list. Only block rules need a person's waiver (up to 90 days, approved by digest, unchanged). A deviation from a principle on a CHECK-LESS record (judged by a reviewer) is accepted the same way.
3. Must a principle finding be answered before complete? DEFAULT: yes for SHOULD with a mechanical check or a reviewer finding that cites the id; complete refuses (exit 3) listing the unanswered ones; an answer is comply (fixed) or deviate (reason). MAY findings never refuse. Gate OUTCOME stays passed (a principle is not a blocker); the ledger carries the answer.
4. Precedence order. DEFAULT: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; nearest scope (gate, then globs, then category, then always) wins within a tier, then priority, then newest; unreconciled conflicts are a doctor note and a B-coh item, never a silent pick. Goals never override a rule or a principle. Extends D-rules-hierarchy (workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults); it does not replace it.
5. Goal record shape. DEFAULT: def-record kind goal; fields title, body, status (proposed | active | achieved | dropped), owner, target_date, parent (at most 2 levels), links (phases, tasks, decisions, research), key_results[] each {id, text, source = dag | metric | check | manual, ref, baseline, target, direction}. Progress is computed: dag = done share of the linked phases' tasks (tasks weighted equally; a removed or abandoned task leaves the count); metric = a named ddflow metric (B-gap-metrics); check = a command through the shared runner, operator-config or approved by digest only; manual = an operator attestation with a date that goes STALE after [goals].manual_stale_days (default 30) and is then reported unavailable, never green. Overall goal progress = the minimum-of-trajectory view is NOT used; show each KR and their mean, marked an estimate.
6. What does the brief show of goals? DEFAULT: at most 3 lines (active goals by priority: title, mean KR progress, weakest KR, days to target, stale flag), plus at claim the item's goal chain (task -> phase -> goal) labelled Direction, not a constraint; orphan work (completed items under no goal) counted in the roadmap and doctor, never a gate.
7. Proposal storage and triage states. DEFAULT: def-record kind proposal outside the queue (status proposed | adopted | deferred (snooze_until) | rejected | expired | superseded); adopt creates a task through services/items.add_task (dup check included) in a phase the operator names and links back; adopt/defer/reject are person-only (CLI; no MCP verb, like ddflow approve); reject REQUIRES a reason and is remembered: a new proposal whose fingerprint or similarity matches a rejected one is not filed unless it carries new evidence the operator can see. Rejected: proposal as a task state (every scheduler, board and next path would need to learn it), and proposal as a research record (no adopt/reject lifecycle).
8. Discovery cadence and budget. DEFAULT: OFF until the operator turns it on (job feature_discovery shipped disabled); then weekly by the calendar, or every 2 completed phases, whichever the operator picks; per run at most 3 new proposals; at most 7 open (proposed, undecided) at any time, and the job does not run while the cap is reached (backpressure); at most 20 000 reviewed tokens per run when B-gap-spend can measure it (UNAVAILABLE, not zero, when it cannot, and then the run cap is the turn cap); circuit breaker after 3 consecutive runs with zero adopted proposals (job pauses and says so in brief); stale undecided proposals expire after 60 days. The job files ONE research item (kind research) through the normal claim, so any lane may take it and quotas apply.
9. What may discovery read? DEFAULT: the repository, the ddflow log, its own research records, dependency advisories through the configured companions; the web ONLY if the operator enabled [discovery].web (default false); the log redaction profile is applied to every proposal body; no file contents above 40 lines are quoted. Org policy may force web off.
10. Scope. DEFAULT: goals and principles may come from an org bundle (P-org-config) as read-only team goals/principles; a project may add its own and cannot deviate from an org floor; proposals and deviations are always local to the project log; personal (local-only) goals are allowed under .ddflow/local and never reach the brief of other users.
11. Evaluation gate for turning discovery on by default. DEFAULT: never on by default; recommend turning on after B-goal-eval reports >= 3 runs with acceptance in 20-70 percent.

ACCEPTANCE: the answers are recorded as a decision with the reasons; the doc lists every question with the answer; the dependent tasks' bodies are amended if an answer differs from the default (ddflow update). Tests: none (docs only); gates: research, rules, docs.
SIZE: small. DOCS: docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): three more questions, with defaults, so the goal, principle and proposal kinds meet the record contract. 12. Who may create, activate, edit, drop or delete goals and principles? DEFAULT: the CLI and MCP offer the same verbs to a person and to an agent; an agent's add or edit of a goal lands as status proposed, and a change that WEAKENS (a goal dropped or achieved, a principle demoted from MUST to SHOULD or MAY, a rule retired, enforcement lowered, override widened) is accepted but flagged 'changed by agent' in the brief, doctor and the change feed until the operator acknowledges it (`<kind> ack`, operator-only, B-rc-lifecycle); the operator can reverse it (restore). This is D-decision-management 2 applied to every guidance and goal kind. 13. Merge and split: may two goals, two principles or two open proposals be merged, and one split? DEFAULT: yes, through the record surface (B-rc-lifecycle): merge unions links, key results and tags and keeps both ids reachable (merged_from / successor); split creates parts with provenance.split_from and retires the original with split_into; a key result keeps its id when it moves so progress history survives; deleting is retiring (a tombstone with a reason), never a purge. 14. Mid-session notification: DEFAULT: a running session is told, through the change feed (B-rc-changes), of BINDING changes only (a rule, decision or principle at block or warn, a goal's status or target, a waiver granted or expired); everything else is a count. A fresh session's brief is unchanged. Record the answers (and any difference) in docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md and amend the dependent tasks.

WHAT: the goal record. Register def kind goal in core/defs.py (DEF_KINDS) and declare a RecordKind GOAL in api/records.py so ddflow goal list|show|add|edit|remove|search|revise and ONE MCP tool ddflow_goal exist from the descriptor (D-unify 4; tools/list budget: this is one of the ~8 remaining tools, tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py). Fields: title, body, status (proposed | active | achieved | dropped), owner, target_date, parent (a goal id, depth at most 2), links (phase, task, decision, research ids), key_results (a list of tables {id, text, source = dag|metric|check|manual, ref, baseline, target, direction up|down|reach}). Validation: ids are plain keys; a link names an existing record or is reported (not refused: the phase may be filed later); source=check requires a command that is operator-configured or approved by digest (services/approval, cmdrunner); a manual KR carries the value and a date. Search source so ddflow search --kind goal and recall find goals. Authored files .ddflow/goals/<id>.toml as a generated, drift-checked view (same pattern as rules).
WHY: R-goals-existing-map: ddflow has no goal concept; the only 'Goals' is a hand-written section of the generated ROADMAP (B-rm-template), invisible to brief, claim and search. The def-record model gives history, provenance, digest, replay, duplicate check and upcasters for free, so a goal needs no parallel store (D-no-duplicates, D-unify).
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core/defs.py, api/defs.py, api/records.py RecordKind, surfaces/records.py, services/overlay.py for the file view, services/searchcore, services/approval.py and services/cmdrunner.py, core/upcasters.py (version 1 of the goal payload registered now so later fields are additive).
HOW TO TEST (failing first): add/edit/revise/retire a goal and replay the log byte-identically; invalid key-result source refused naming the field; a check KR with an unapproved command is accepted as a record but reported unapproved (never runs); the tool appears once and the parity test passes; the tools/list budget test passes; two goals with near-identical titles trigger the add-time duplicate check.
SIZE: medium (~450 lines + tests). Hot files: core/defs.py, api/records.py (shared with B-rw-claims, B-rules-onto-record-surface): the scheduler serialises them.
ACCEPTANCE: a goal with three key results (one of each source) can be added, listed, searched and shown on CLI and MCP with identical bodies; a hand-edited .ddflow/goals file is recorded by digest.
DOCS: README 'Goals', help topic goals.

DOCS NOTE: the README tool-table row comes from python -m ddflow.surfaces.tool_table in this task; the prose is written by B-goal-acceptance.

CONFIG (added by the filer): this task also declares the three config sections the phase needs, so no later task edits ddflow/config.py: [goals] (manual_stale_days = 30, review_window_items = 10, deviation_review_rate = 0.3, max_depth = 2), [proposals] (reject_floor, expire_days = 60, max_open = 7) and [discovery] (enabled = false, every_days / every_phases, max_new_per_run = 3, web = false, token_cap, turn_cap, breaker_runs = 3). Each is a knob() with doc and, for enums, the strictest fallback (D-enum-fallback-strict). Later tasks edit only their own section file.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the goal kind is declared through the contract, not around it. (1) It gets the lifecycle verbs history, supersede, merge, split, restore and the weakening/ack flag from B-rc-lifecycle by declaring its descriptor; the weakening hook answers for status to dropped or achieved and for a removed key result. Merging goals unions links and key results (a key result keeps its id so progress history survives), splitting partitions them. (2) Search, recall, MCP resources and RAG export are derived from the descriptor (B-rc-participation, B-rc-rag-export): declare `applies` (links, parent, status), `export` (title, body, key-result texts as text; links, owner, target_date, status as metadata) and `feed` (binding for status and target_date changes, informational otherwise); services/goals/search.py shrinks to the text-extraction function the descriptor names, there is no goal-specific search source or resource. (3) Add the field `review_by` (a date; owner or the operator is reminded in doctor and the brief like a decision's review_by) so a goal nobody revisits is reported. (4) An agent's add lands as status proposed and activation or dropping by an agent is flagged until acknowledged (B-goal-decide Q12). (5) An org-sourced goal is read-only locally (B-org-kinds registers the provider). (6) Acceptance gains: the goal passes tests/test_record_contract.py with no exemption.

WHAT: the SCENARIO CARD as a document type: a short markdown test an agent executes through a project's real interface (CLI, MCP, UI), with a falsifier on every expectation. WHY: the e2e-scenario-testing skill separates 'the wiring in isolation' (unit tests) from 'the wiring as assembled and rendered'. ddflow has coded scenarios (demos/scenario_*.py, tests/test_scenarios.py, B-mu-harness, B-ac-smoke) and prose test tasks (the T-* tasks of P-test-robustness: 'run through realistic scenarios end-to-end', 'run all example commands from docs'), but no durable, validated, agent-readable format with falsification conditions, and no record that a scenario ran against which commit (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED). Not wanted: tmux/CDP driving code in ddflow (ddflow has no TUI; cards for other projects carry their own recipe text), and a Playwright-style script format.

INTERFACE REUSED: the document-type engine (B-dt-spec, B-dt-validate, B-dt-library): a shipped type `scenario`, collection pattern `docs/scenarios/{slug}.md`, contract evergreen (B-pi-doc-class), `depends_on` = the card's `covers` globs; the interview/skeleton machinery (B-dt-interview) for `ddflow docs new scenario <slug>`; ddflow docs check for lint. Shipped as templates/doctypes/scenario.toml plus a skeleton; a project overrides or removes it, an org bundle carries it.
CARD SHAPE (front matter): covers: [globs the card exercises]; surface: cli|mcp|ui|other; isolation: how state is isolated (private HOME/state dir/port, read-only inputs symlinked); record: the authoritative record an ambiguous assertion is checked against (for ddflow: the event log and --json output). Sections in order: What it covers, Pre-state (fresh build from the code under test, confirmed the running instance is the new one), Steps (intent + the exact command or tool call + the label a user sees), Expected (per step, with the FALSIFICATION condition: 'if you see X instead, the step fails'), Cleanup (idempotent, touches only what the card created), Sharp edges.
VALIDATION RULES (all TOML, B-dt-validate; this task adds the one missing rule kind `each_item_matches` -- every list item of a section must match a regex -- if B-dt-validate has not): required sections and order; every Expected item matches `(?i)(fails?|falsif|instead|not )`; Expected forbids vacuous text (`looks good|works as expected|no errors`) as the whole assertion; Steps contain a code span; Cleanup non-empty; front matter requires covers and surface. Rule regexes are config ([doctype.scenario.validate]), not code.
CONFIG SHAPE: `[scenarios] dir = "docs/scenarios"`, `[doctype.scenario.validate] ...`; severity warn by default (the docs severity). Tools: `ddflow docs new scenario`, `ddflow docs check`, `ddflow docs list --type scenario` on the existing verbs.
TESTS (failing-first): a card without a falsifier on an Expected item, a vacuous assertion, and a missing Cleanup are each reported; a well-formed card validates; the skeleton validates fresh; override/remove of the type works. SIZE: small-medium. ACCEPTANCE: tests, a worked card for ddflow's own claim/complete cycle kept under docs/scenarios/ as the project's first card (project content, not shipped in the package), README/help text.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.

data.body:
WHAT: make a principle real. (1) The override field (none | waive | deviate) on the guidance record and its fold/file format/definition fields, with MUST/SHOULD/MAY shown beside the enforcement word in every door (brief, claim, gate status, review prompt) by guidance/inject.py (_line tags). (2) A deviation: ddflow decision deviate <id> --item <item> --reason "..." [--evidence ...] and its twin on the MCP decision tool; stored as a waiver record in mode deviation (B-dec-waivers); item-scoped, no approval, no expiry, reason required. (3) The completion check: ddflow complete refuses (exit 3, naming each) while a finding against a record with override=deviate is neither fixed nor deviated; a finding is a failing mechanical check result (checks.gate_verdict warnings) or a reviewer finding that cites the id (B-goal-cites). A SHOULD that has neither check nor citation is never a finding; a MAY never refuses. (4) precedence.py: the one function that orders applicable records (org floor > rule > decision > principle > preference; scope; priority) and reports an unreconciled conflict instead of picking silently; inject.rank_key calls it. (5) A deviation is shown to the operator: brief line 'deviations since your last look', decision list column, completion summary.
WHY (evidence, R-goals-existing-map): decisions already default to warn, but a warn finding requires no answer (checks.Verdict.warnings never changes the outcome), and a waiver needs a person and expires within 90 days (D-decision-management) - right for a rule, too heavy for a preference, so people will skip it and a soft rule fails by silence. RFC 2119 SHOULD is exactly 'valid reasons to ignore, carefully weighed'; Spec Kit records deviations as justified entries (Complexity Tracking); no verified tool combines reason + expiry + approver, ddflow's waiver already does for the strict case.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{record,deffields,inject,checks,waivers}.py, B-dec-model (override field lands in the decision v2 events and its upcaster; this task wires behaviour), B-dec-waivers (storage), B-dec-monitor (the decisions gate), services/completion.py (the existing refusal list), core.provenance for fencing. No new event kind unless B-dec-waivers did not carry the mode (then register it with its first writer).
HOW TO TEST (failing first): a SHOULD with a failing check: complete refuses; after deviate it passes and the summary lists the deviation; a MUST with the same check blocks the gate and deviate does NOT clear it (only waive does); deviate on a MUST refused with the reason; a MAY never refuses; precedence table test (every pair of tiers, scope tie-break, priority tie-break) and an unreconciled pair reported; fold/replay of an old log with no override field gives block->waive, warn/advisory->deviate; tool parity test; budget: pinned MUST text never trimmed (existing test unchanged).
SIZE: large (~600 lines + tests); the completion refusal and inject tags are the risk.
ACCEPTANCE: scenario in B-goal-acceptance; README section 'Principles: follow unless you say why'; help topic.
DOCS: README, help topic goals, driver notes (agent: how to deviate; when a deviation is a sign the principle is wrong).

DOCS NOTE: README and help-topic text for this task is written by B-goal-acceptance (the single README editor, so parallel tasks keep disjoint globs); this task writes the driver/prompt text it owns and a docstring-level description.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): a deviation (and a person's waiver) also applies to a pipeline requirement: the finding is 'gate X owed by record R has no outcome'. Deviating from a SHOULD requirement records the item, the gate and the reason through the same deviation record and appears on the gate row ('deviated: reason, by agent'). The precedence function is the one B-pipe-resolve calls; its tiers are not duplicated. override=none or waive on a pipeline record means the gate cannot be deviated; only waive (person, <=90 days, scoped) lifts a MUST.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the private 'deviations since your last look' brief line is replaced by the shared change feed (B-rc-changes): a deviation, a waiver, a new MUST or SHOULD and a changed enforcement or override are feed entries (binding for the ones that change what an agent must do, informational for a deviation), so a SECOND running session learns of them mid-session, not only at its next brief. Also: (1) `ddflow decision deviate --retract <deviation> --reason` withdraws a deviation recorded in error before the item completes (an unfixed finding then blocks again); a retracted deviation is kept in history and is not counted in the adherence numbers. (2) Deviation and waiver records are searchable and exportable through their descriptor (B-dec-waivers declares it), and `decision show <principle>` lists its deviations with item, reason and agent, so an agent asking 'was this ever waived or deviated from, and why' gets the answer from search and recall. (3) The principle itself is an ordinary guidance record: edit, merge, split, supersede, restore and history come from B-rc-lifecycle; demoting a MUST to a SHOULD by an agent is a weakening change (flagged for the operator).

WHAT: run scenario cards as a gate and record the result. WHY: a card that nobody can show was executed, against which commit, step by step, proves nothing; the skill demands 'report each assertion as pass/fail with the concrete observation, not looks good' and 'a card that passes because its check was vacuous is worse than none'. ddflow already has the machinery for a gate that cannot be passed vacuously (requires_evidence/evidence_fields, structured by B-gate-evidence-fields), a rule that unavailable is never passed, and path-scoped gates (B-gate-when-globs).

INTERFACE REUSED: GateDef (services/gates/defs.py): an optional built-in `scenario` gate, agent gate, applies_to task and phase, requires_evidence = ["fields"], evidence_fields = ["card", "sha", "steps"]; NOT in the default pipeline (added with `ddflow workflow pipeline task ...`, or by an org bundle); applicability from the cards: a gate-def key `applies_when_cards = true` makes it apply when the item's diff touches any card's `covers` globs (one path matcher, shared with B-gate-when-globs / B-pipe-resolve -- do not write another). Events: scenario.ran {card, sha, run_by, steps[{n, verdict pass|fail|unavailable, observation, evidence_path}], cleanup verdict, card_fixed} registered in core/events.py and folded into State.scenarios[card] (last run, last sha, last verdict). Evidence artefacts (captured pane, screenshot, on-disk record) go under the git-ignored .ddflow/local/scenarios/<run>/ with the redaction profile and a size cap, never into the log. Prompt template templates/prompts/commands/scenario-run.md (overridable): build fresh from the code under test and confirm the instance is the new one (ddflow doctor's stale-install note is the mechanical check for ddflow), isolate, drive the surface, assert against the authoritative record, capture evidence, clean up, fix the card when executing it finds the card wrong (card_fixed, recorded) and never soften a failure.
OUTCOME MAPPING (config, [scenarios].outcome): any fail -> the gate fails and the failing step is offered as a bug (found first, fixed failing-first); any unavailable step (missing binary, no network, instance could not start) -> recorded unavailable, never passed; all pass with an observation each -> passed. A pass without a per-step observation is refused by the evidence check (exit 3, lists every missing field).
SURFACES: `ddflow docs scenario list|status|record <card> --steps <json>|stdin` and the same verbs on the ONE ddflow_docs MCP tool; `status` shows each card's last sha, verdict and whether its covers globs changed since.
CONFIG SHAPE: [scenarios] dir, max_evidence_mb = 20, outcome mapping, `require_observation = true`; the gate def keys through ddflow config --set gate.scenario.<field>.
TESTS (failing-first): vacuous pass (no observation) refused; one unavailable step makes the gate unavailable; the gate applies only when covers intersects the diff and is absent otherwise (recorded N/A with the reason, never silent); a fake agent records steps and replay rebuilds State.scenarios; evidence size cap and redaction. SIZE: medium (about 500 lines + prompt). ACCEPTANCE: tests, parity, README/help topic, driver text.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.
data.title: Scenario gate and scenario.ran record: per-step verdict with observation, unavailable never passed, applies when the diff touches a card's covers globs

data.body:
WHAT: compute goal progress and the goal gap, never store it. (1) A registry of key-result evaluators (same shape as guidance/checks.py: register(kind, fn), a result is value | unavailable with a reason, an evaluator that cannot run is UNAVAILABLE and never counts as progress): dag (done share of the tasks under the linked phases/tasks, from the folded state and core.graph; removed and abandoned tasks excluded; also the number open, blocked and ready), metric (a named metric from B-gap-metrics: open bugs, review rounds per item, cycle time, gate skip rate, plus a provider hook so other services register more), check (an approved command through services/cmdrunner: exit code or a numeric last line, timeouts, unavailable on error), manual (value + attestation date; stale after [goals].manual_stale_days). (2) ddflow goal status [id] [--json]: per goal each KR with baseline, current, target, progress percent, trend since the last reading (readings are cached in .ddflow/local, derived and disposable), staleness, and an estimate flag; overall = mean of KR progress, marked an estimate. (3) The GOAL GAP signal, advisory and bounded: an active goal that has an unmet KR and no open, ready or in-flight linked task; a KR whose trajectory misses target_date by the throughput estimate (B-gap-metrics forecast; says not enough data under the minimum sample); a manual KR gone stale; linked phases all done while a KR is unmet (the plan was complete but the goal is not). The signal is a list of reasons per goal, shown by goal status, doctor and (B-goal-inject) the brief; it files nothing and blocks nothing.
WHY: Linear's initiative health is a human-written update (verified), a GitHub milestone is closed/total, Sonar is a numeric threshold on new code, a fitness function is an executable goal: the measurable ones are all counts or thresholds. ddflow already knows the DAG and the log (R-gaps-evidence: 667 items, cycle-time distribution), so progress is a projection. Unmeasurable or hand-typed progress is the known failure (goal gaming, stale green).
INTERFACE TO REUSE: core/graph.py and core/schedule.py (closure, readiness), core/progress.py aggregation, B-gap-metrics service and forecast, services/cmdrunner.py + approval.py, core/clock.py (tests inject time), services/guidance/checks.py as the pattern (do not subclass it: a KR is not a guidance check).
HOW TO TEST: fixture DAG with 3 phases of known done counts: dag KR equals hand-computed value; removing a task changes the denominator; an unavailable metric yields unavailable not 0; a check KR with a failing command is unavailable with the reason; a stale manual KR is reported stale and excluded from the mean; gap reasons each fire on a purpose-built fixture and none fires on a healthy one; fake clock; status identical on CLI and MCP.
SIZE: medium (~500 lines + tests).
ACCEPTANCE: on this repository with one real goal (for example 'P-unify accepted and pushed') ddflow goal status gives the same percent as ddflow board for the linked phase.
DOCS: README Goals section: how progress is computed and what 'unavailable' means; help topic.

DOCS NOTE: README and help-topic text for this task is written by B-goal-acceptance (the single README editor, so parallel tasks keep disjoint globs); this task writes the driver/prompt text it owns and a docstring-level description.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): goal gap reasons gain: review_by passed (B-goal-model's new field) and a goal changed by an agent and not yet acknowledged. The gap list and a goal's progress readings are feed-registered (informational), so `ddflow changes` can show 'goal X: KR2 stale' without a goal-specific path.

WHAT: put goals where the agent and the operator already look, within budget. (1) ddflow brief: a 'Goals' section of at most 3 lines (active goals by priority: title, mean KR progress marked estimate, weakest KR, days to target, stale/gap flag) inside session.brief_max_tokens, cut from the bottom like the other sections; nothing when no goal exists. (2) ddflow claim and gate status: the item's goal chain (task -> phase -> goal through links) as a 'Direction' line, explicitly labelled 'direction, not a rule: a rule or principle above wins'. (3) Orphan work: a count of items completed under no goal in doctor and the roadmap, advisory only (a project with no goals gets no noise). (4) Roadmap: a generated Goals region in ROADMAP.md fed by goal records when any exist (user prose Vision/Goals/Notes sections stay the user's, B-rm-template; this adds a ddflow region, not an edit of their text). (5) A Linear-initiative-like view: ddflow goal status already lists parents and children; the roadmap region shows the parent -> child tree.
WHY: the paper's claim that claim verifies a task links to an active goal does not exist; building it as a refusal would turn a direction into a gate and invite goal gaming (tagging every task with a goal to pass). Direction is shown, never enforced. Brief already has one injection path (guidance/inject.py) and a budget; goals are a separate short section so they cannot crowd out pinned rules.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/lifecycle/brief.py (section list and budget), api/lifecycle/claim.py (_claimed), api/gates.py, api/reporting/health.py (doctor notes), services/export/kind_roadmap.py and templates/export/roadmap.md.j2 with named regions (D-doc-regions), core.provenance fence for goal text (it is somebody's words).
HOW TO TEST: brief with a tiny budget still shows pinned rules in full and drops goals first; no goal: byte-identical brief to today (golden); claim on an item under a linked phase prints the chain; roadmap golden with and without goals; orphan count correct on a fixture; goal body with an injected instruction is fenced as data.
SIZE: medium (~400 lines + tests). Hot files brief.py, claim.py: wait for B-dec-pinned (needs).
ACCEPTANCE: a session brief on this repository shows the goal lines; a claim shows the chain; goldens updated only by the intended lines.
DOCS: README brief section; help topic goals.

DOCS NOTE: README and help-topic text for this task is written by B-goal-acceptance (the single README editor, so parallel tasks keep disjoint globs); this task writes the driver/prompt text it owns and a docstring-level description.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): goals reach a session through the two shared doors rather than a goal-only path: (1) the brief 'Goals' section stays (at most 3 lines, dropped first under a tiny budget) and sits beside the shared 'Changed since you last looked' section (B-rc-changes); a goal's status or target_date change is a BINDING feed entry, so a session already running is told without waiting for its next brief. (2) The claim 'Direction' line and any text-matched goal come from B-rc-context's builder: the goal chain through links is a SCOPE-tier candidate (so claim, the pre-edit door and `recall --for item:<id>` all print the same chain), a goal whose title or key results match the prompt is a TEXT-tier candidate, always labelled 'direction, not a rule'. No goal-only injector, search source or resource is written here. Test additions: a second live session is told of a goal's status change within one prompt; the chain printed by claim equals the one from `recall --for item:`.

WHAT: the proposal record and its triage. Def kind proposal (core/defs.py) and a RecordKind PROPOSAL (api/records.py) so ddflow proposal list|show|add|edit|search and ONE MCP tool ddflow_proposal exist from the descriptor, plus the triage verbs as ops: adopt, defer, reject, snooze. Fields: title, body (problem, evidence, acceptance, globs, size in S/M/L, estimated tokens), goal (a goal id; may be empty only for proposals tagged maintenance), evidence (research ids/claim ids, metric readings, advisory ids, file:line), principles_checked (ids + comply|deviate|n/a), fingerprint (normalised title + globs digest), source (job id + run key or agent), status (proposed | adopted | deferred | rejected | expired | superseded), decided_by, decision_reason, snooze_until, adopted_as (a task id). Rules: (1) a proposal is NOT a queue item: next, claim, board and status never see it (they read items); (2) adopt <id> --phase P creates a task through services/items.add_task (the one way a task is created, add-time duplicate check included), copies globs and body, links both ways, and records adopted_as; the operator may edit the body first; (3) adopt, defer, reject are PERSON-ONLY: the CLI verbs exist, the MCP tool offers add/edit/list/show/search only and the exemption is a field in surfaces/exemptions.py with that reason (same precedent as ddflow approve); an agent may add a proposal; (4) reject requires --reason; a rejected proposal stays in the log and is checked at every add: a new proposal whose fingerprint matches or whose similarity (services/similar) is at least [proposals].reject_floor to a rejected or deferred-not-due one is refused with the old id and reason, unless the new one cites evidence the old did not (the evidence list is diffed); (5) defer needs snooze_until; the proposal reappears in the list on that date; (6) undecided proposals expire after [proposals].expire_days (default 60) to status expired (kept); (7) an MCP resource ddflow://proposals (open proposals, newest first, bounded) next to ddflow://research, which stays the research log; (8) every proposal body goes through the log redaction profile and is fenced as data wherever shown.
WHY: R-goals-existing-map: nothing like it exists (ddflow://research renders findings with verdicts, not proposals; the paper's ddflow_feature_propose / ddflow_proposal_triage / task adopt do not exist). Jules suggested tasks, Dependabot, Renovate and Linear Triage all keep suggestions OUT of the work queue until a person accepts, offer decline-with-reason, snooze and duplicate, and remember ignores; idea spam is the failure they all cap. B-research-items files tasks directly from a verdict, which is right for the operator's own research and wrong for unattended discovery.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/records.py + surfaces/records.py (one tool per kind; check tools/list budget test), core/defs.py + upcasters, services/items.add_task, services/similar.py and api/_dedupe.py (closed-match semantics of B-coh-readd-closed, reversed here: a rejected match is NOT re-added), services/approval.py not needed, surfaces/exemptions.py, surfaces/mcp.py RESOURCES.
HOW TO TEST (failing first): adopt creates exactly one task and links it, a second adopt refused; next/board unchanged by 50 open proposals; reject without reason refused; re-proposing a rejected idea is refused naming the rejection; the same idea with new evidence is filed and linked as supersedes; snooze hides until the fake-clock date; expiry; MCP tool has no adopt verb (parity exemption test); replay identical.
SIZE: medium-large (~600 lines + tests). Shares core/defs.py and api/records.py with B-goal-model (serialised by needs).
ACCEPTANCE: scenario in B-goal-acceptance.
DOCS: README 'Proposals', help topic goals.

DOCS NOTE: the README tool-table row comes from python -m ddflow.surfaces.tool_table in this task; the prose is written by B-goal-acceptance.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the proposal kind meets the contract. (1) Descriptor verbs: list, show, add, edit, search, history, merge (two OPEN proposals about the same idea: the merged one keeps both evidence lists and records merged_from, and the rejected-ideas memory sees both fingerprints) and split (one proposal that bundles two ideas); remove is NOT offered (reject and expire are the tombstones; the descriptor opt-out carries that reason, read by the conformance test); restore is allowed only for expired proposals. adopt, defer, reject, snooze stay person-only declared fields. (2) Search, recall and the ddflow://proposals resource are derived from the descriptor (B-rc-participation), so `ddflow search --kind proposal` and recall find open AND decided proposals (a decided one is exactly what an agent about to re-propose needs); proposals are exported only when named in `export records --kind proposal` (local to the project, RC9). (3) The feed (B-rc-changes) carries 'proposal adopted / rejected / deferred' as informational entries addressed to the proposing agent's session, so a lane learns the fate of its proposal; 'N proposals await a decision' stays a brief line (B-sched-escalation). (4) review_by is not needed (expiry covers staleness).

Acceptance for P-goals, end to end on a throwaway repository with a fake clock and a stub researcher (no network, no real model):
1. A MUST rule with a mechanical check (a forbidden import) blocks the decisions gate; deviate is refused; only an approved waiver clears it for at most 90 days and it resurfaces on the day after expiry.
2. A SHOULD principle with a check: a diff that violates it makes complete refuse listing it; ddflow decision deviate --item ... --reason ... lets the item complete; the completion summary and the brief show the deviation; a MAY never refuses.
3. A reviewer finding citing [id] is stored with cites; a cited id that was not sent is flagged.
4. Five deviations by two agents in ten items make the principle due for review (ddflow decision review); reaffirm moves review_by, change files a superseding PROPOSED decision for the operator; nothing changes by itself.
5. A goal with three key results (dag, metric, manual): progress equals the hand-computed value; the manual KR goes stale on the fake clock and drops out of the mean; the goal gap lists 'no open work toward an unmet KR'; the brief shows the goal in at most 3 lines and drops it first under a tiny budget while a pinned MUST stays whole; the claim of a task under the linked phase prints the goal chain as direction.
6. Discovery (enabled for the test): the due job files one research item; the stub files 5 candidates; 3 become proposals, 2 are dropped (one equal to a rejected proposal, one violating a MUST); the cap of open proposals stops the next run and the brief says why; adopt creates one task, reject records its reason, and re-proposing the rejected idea is refused naming the rejection; three runs with no adoption pause the job. next/board never listed a proposal.
7. An org bundle carrying a floor principle (override none) cannot be deviated from by the project; project-level goals/principles layer on top; proposals and deviations stay local.
8. CLI and MCP bodies are identical for goal, proposal, deviate and report; the tools/list budget test passes; README, help topic goals and the implement-phase driver (both copies) updated.
Files: tests/scenarios/test_goals.py plus the doc files. SIZE: medium. This task finds integration gaps: any gap it finds is filed as a bug, not patched here.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): 9. CONTRACT CONFORMANCE (scripted, throwaway repo, fake clock, two agents A and B with sessions, plus the operator): (a) A adds a goal, a principle (a SHOULD rule with override=deviate) and a rule, on CLI and MCP with identical bodies; B's brief at start lists the active goal and the pinned rule. (b) A edits each (clearing a field), B's NEXT prompt (or next MCP reply) carries one fenced line naming the changed rule and principle, who, why (B-rc-changes); B's own later edit is not echoed back to B. (c) A splits the rule into two and merges two goals; `history --diff` of each shows who, when, why, session and before/after; the originals are tombstoned with split_into / merged_from; a restore of the merged goal brings it back. (d) A, an agent, lowers a rule from block to warn: it is accepted and flagged 'changed by agent' in the operator's brief until `rule ack` (refused on MCP with exit 3); the operator reverses it with restore. (e) `search --kind goal`, `search --kind rule`, `recall` and `recall --for path:<glob of the rule>` find the records (the rule is offered once before the first edit under its glob and not again), a rejected proposal is found by search. (f) `export records` contains the goal, the principle and the rule with provenance, a tombstone for the split original and the merged goal, and a second export with --since last contains only what changed. (g) delete = `remove` with a reason and the record is still in `history` and in the export tombstones. (h) tests/test_record_contract.py passes for goal, rule, decision and proposal with the exemption count unchanged or lower. File: tests/scenarios/test_goals_contract.py (and the existing test_goals.py items 1-8 unchanged). A gap found is filed as a bug, not patched here.

WHAT: a scheduled sweep that runs the scenario cards that are due and keeps them honest. WHY: cards rot (the skill: 'executing the card tests the card'); without a due rule they run once and drift. ddflow's schedule layer (P-schedule: schedule.defined events, due evaluation, run keys) and the cadence passes (integration_tests) already express 'run X every N tasks/days'; no job runs end-to-end scenarios (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED).
INTERFACE REUSED: a shipped schedule job template templates/schedules/scenario_sweep.toml (disabled by default, report-only; B-sched-defaults guarantees that a template file is enough to add a job) with a jinja prompt templates/prompts/commands/scenario-sweep.md; B-sched-due for due evaluation; the `integration_tests` cadence pass text in the driver (B-docs-periodic-passes) gains 'run the due cards' as a documented step; the bug tool for a failed step; doctor notes.
DUE RULE (config, [scenarios.sweep]): a card is due when never run, or its covers globs changed since the last scenario.ran sha, or the last run is older than `max_age_days` (default 30), or the last verdict was fail or unavailable (retry). `ddflow docs scenario status --due [--json]` is the one list the job and the brief read. A failed step files a bug (found-before-fixed, failing-first regression test, a unit test where the live path is gated), an unavailable step is listed in doctor ('card X unavailable since D: <reason>') and never counted as passing; a card fixed during a run is a doc.checked record.
SURFACES: no new tool; `docs scenario status --due`, the brief line ('2 scenario cards due'), the doctor note, and the job's prompt. The T-* tasks of P-test-robustness (T-integration-workflows, T-documentation-accuracy) are expected to be expressed as cards once this exists (pointer added to them).
TESTS (failing-first): each due condition with a fake clock; a failed step files exactly one bug and re-running does not file a second (dedupe); unavailable is never green; disabled-by-default job costs nothing. SIZE: small. ACCEPTANCE: tests, README/help text, the schedule template overridable by file and removable.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.
data.title: Scenario sweep: due rule (never run, covered code changed, age, last failed or unavailable), a shipped disabled schedule job, bugs for failures

data.body:
Re-filed by the 2026-10-10 reorganisation audit: part of B-uni-record-surface (done) was never delivered. api/records.py declares the RULE RecordKind but nothing generates the real `ddflow rule` group from it (api/records.py says it is wired to nothing until a family moves onto it; its named wire-in site, B-rules-cli, was removed on 2026-10-10 as 'already delivered', which covered the commands but not this). The original B-uni-record-surface asked that rules (and the knowledge kinds) move onto it and onto def-records, removing about 500 lines; the def-record half is done (B-uni-rules-import).

WHAT: wire api.records.RULE into the real CLI and tool table: `ddflow rule add|edit|list|show|remove|search|sync` and the rules MCP tool are generated from the descriptor, keeping the group word, every flag and every output byte (goldens, tests/test_rules_cli.py, tests/test_rules_surface.py, the tools/list budget). Delete the parallel code: RuleDedupAnswer and _cross_kind in api/rules.py, the hand-written handlers in surfaces/declared/rules.py, rules_manifest where the def view supersedes it. Then either declare lessons, bugs, items and research as RecordKinds, or record a decision that they stay hand-written, naming the duplicated blocks (api/decisions.py:90 vs api/items.py:507; api/knowledge/bugs.py:68 vs research.py:76); decisions are B-dec-manage's, research B-rw-query's, lessons and bugs B199's, so only items and viewers have no owner. Also add the two small things the original rule CLI body asked for and the registry pilot lacks: `rule list --state` (if rules have a state) and an incremental `rule tag add|remove` (today `rule edit --tags` replaces the whole list).
ACCEPTANCE: ddflow/ shrinks by the measured amount (about 500 lines was the estimate), all rule tests unchanged, one MCP tool for rules, the three duplicated definitions gone.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: api/records.py RULE declares only title, content, tags, scope, priority and globs, so ddflow rule add cannot set enforcement, override, status, owner, review_by, checks, links, categories or gates, although services/guidance/deffields.py stores them and the file format reads them (verified: ddflow rule add --help). When rules move onto the generated surface, add those fields to the descriptor (enforcement, override, status, owner, review_by, categories, gates, links as flags; checks as a file or TOML table argument) so a strict rule (MUST: block) and an unstrict one (SHOULD/MAY) can be created from the CLI and MCP, with the same dedupe and the same limits. Acceptance gains: ddflow rule add --enforcement block --override waive produces a rule that resolve/inject ranks as pinned when always-scope.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): also take the contract rows for rules. (1) Rules gain the lifecycle verbs from B-rc-lifecycle (history, supersede, merge, split, restore, ack) by declaration; the six hand-written MCP tools (ddflow_rule_add, _edit, _list, _remove, _search, _show) plus _sync collapse to ONE tool (the tools/list bytes shrink; the sync stays an action) and the rule row of the conformance exemption table (RC1, RC4) is deleted by this task. (2) Rules join `ddflow recall` (RECALL_SOURCES has no rule today) and the resources through the descriptor (B-rc-participation); `applies` = scope, globs, tags, categories, gates. (3) An agent's rule add with enforcement block, or any edit that lowers enforcement or widens override, is flagged until acknowledged (weakening hook); rule remove by an agent likewise. (4) A rule's `review_by` is settable (flag) and listed stale in doctor. (5) Rules are exported by `export records` and by the existing RULES document; hand edits of the generated .ddflow/rules/*.toml still import by digest and appear as a feed entry.

Built on the record surface (B-uni-record-surface) so CLI and MCP bodies are identical. It covers B199's decision part, coordinated with B199 rather than duplicated. Filters: category, status, owner, glob, stale, enforcement, with-checks. Authored files are .ddflow/decisions/<id>.toml, read through the overlay loader and imported by digest the way rules are (D-unify 7), so a team can keep decisions in review-friendly files. A hand edit becomes an event, and an older ddflow preserves unknown fields (D-compat). The add-time duplicate and contradiction check covers decisions (B-coh-contradiction). An agent's add is status proposed; acceptance is a person's act (B-uni-approval), per D-decision-management.

D-decision-management (2): an agent MAY accept a decision; the acceptance is flagged 'accepted by agent' (brief, doctor, decision list) until the operator acknowledges (ddflow decision ack <id>) and the operator can reverse it (back to proposed or rejected). Waivers stay person-only.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): edit, remove/retire, supersede, restore and history are NOT built here as decision-specific code: they are the lifecycle verbs of B-rc-lifecycle declared on the decision descriptor (today `ddflow decision` has only add, list, show, search, applicable, supersede: no edit, no remove, no history). `decision ack` is B-rc-lifecycle's generic operator-only ack verb with the decision-specific wording ('accepted by agent'); decision merge and split come with it. This task owns what is decision-specific: categories, accept/reject/deprecate transitions, the authored .ddflow/decisions/*.toml files, the /decide prompt, filters. Decisions also carry the feed (`feed`: binding for accepted decisions at block or warn) and the export/applies declarations.

A search source for decisions on the shared engine (B-uni-search-core), with category, status and enforcement facets. ContextPack ranks the applicable decisions first, then the related ones. MCP resource ddflow://decisions/{id}. Embeddings cover decisions when the [rag] extra is present (B-semantic-recall).

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): no decision-specific search source, resource, injector or export is written here: the decision descriptor declares search, `applies`, `export` and the resource (B-rc-participation), `ddflow://decisions/{id}` is kept as an alias of `ddflow://records/decision/{id}`, relevance-matched injection at prompt, pre-edit and claim comes from B-rc-context (decisions are scope-tier candidates, so the existing claim behaviour is unchanged), and the RAG export is B-rc-rag-export. What stays here: the category, status and enforcement facets in search/recall filters and the semantic recall coverage of decisions. Acceptance gains: a decision found by `search --kind decision --category X`, offered once before the first edit under its glob, and present in `export records`.

A waiver is a record linked to the decision and check, with scope globs, a reason, an expiry (maximum from D-decision-management) and approval through B-uni-approval. A waived finding passes the gate with 'waived' visible in gate status, brief and the completion summary. An expired waiver makes the finding live again and notifies in brief and doctor. `ddflow decision waive|waivers|unwaive` on CLI and MCP. A proposal to change the decision instead is a proposed superseding decision for the operator, never automatic.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the waiver record carries a mode, approved (as above: person, scope globs, expiry at most 90 days) or deviation (recorded by the authoring agent for a record whose override is deviate: item-scoped, reason required, evidence optional, no approval, no expiry). One storage and one display path, so brief, gate status and the completion summary list both. A deviation can NOT clear a finding on a record with override waive or none (refused with the reason). The CLI verb for a deviation (ddflow decision deviate) and the completion refusal are B-goal-deviation; this task only makes the record able to hold the mode.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): waivers and deviations are record kinds under the contract: store them as a definition kind with a RecordKind descriptor (not an ad-hoc table) so that history, search, recall, export, the feed and the conformance test come from the descriptor. Operator-only: granting an approved waiver (declared field); an agent's deviation is its own mode. A waiver nearing expiry (7 days, [decisions].waiver_warn_days) and an expired one are BINDING feed entries (B-rc-changes) addressed to the approver and to sessions holding items under its scope, in addition to the brief and doctor notices above. `unwaive` is the generic remove (tombstone with reason); a waiver cannot be merged or split (descriptor opt-out with that reason).

WHAT: the review LENS becomes data on the gate, with shipped design, security and docs_claims lenses and an optional `design_review` gate. WHY: the roborev-design-review skills show review TYPE as a first-class choice (design versus bug versus security) on the same diff or branch. In ddflow the lens is code: api/review.py:1299 `_LENSES` holds two strings (rubber_duck, critic) used only for a combined review's intent, a gate without an entry is never combined, and services/review.py renders ONE system prompt (templates/prompts/review_system.md, 'refute it') for every gate a reviewer serves, overridable per reviewer (system_prompt_path, extra_rules) but not per gate. A project that wants a design review or a security review must hand-write a reviewer per lens. This is also a hard-coded default that cannot be configured (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED).

INTERFACE REUSED: GateDef (services/gates/defs.py) gets two fields: `lens` (one intent line) and `lens_prompt` (a prompt-template name resolved by the same PR.resolve that resolves review_system, so .ddflow/prompts overrides it and an org bundle ships it); the combined review (B-gate-econ-review-combined) composes the lens lines of the gates asked from GateDef instead of _LENSES; services/review.py picks `lens_prompt` of the gate being reviewed, falling back to review_system, then the reviewer's own system_prompt_path (a per-reviewer override still wins, as today); extra_rules unchanged. Shipped lens templates under templates/prompts/review_lens/: refute.md and intent.md (byte-identical to today's behaviour, pinned by a test), design.md (module boundaries and interfaces, a parallel implementation of an operation that already exists, migration and compatibility of stored data and config, naming against the terminology dictionary when B-pi-terms is on, test strategy), security.md, docs_claims.md (the verb-not-noun lens for a documentation diff). Optional built-in gate `design_review` (reviewer = different_family, applies_to task and phase, requires_evidence = ["report"], `applies_when` empty by default so a project sets the interface globs) -- NOT in the default pipeline; B-architecture-pass and B-security-pass use their lenses instead of private prompts.
CONFIG SHAPE: `ddflow config --set gate.design_review.lens_prompt design`, `gate.<id>.lens "<line>"`, `[review].lens_dir` (extra template directory), gates.toml entries; all editable by CLI and MCP (ddflow_configure) and carried by org bundles. The default pipeline and every recorded outcome are unchanged.
PRESENTATION: a review result prints the verdict first, then findings grouped HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW with file:line (pin what ddflow review prints today before changing anything); the follow-up offered is the gate's triage/fix on the one record id (the panel task keeps one id).
BRANCH/COMMIT SCOPE is already data: ddflow review --branch/--base/--commit exists; the lens applies to any of them.
TESTS (failing-first): default behaviour byte-identical for rubber_duck/critic and the combined intent text; a gate with lens_prompt=design sends the design template (fake reviewer records the system prompt); a project override file wins; an unknown lens_prompt is a config error naming the key; _LENSES is gone. SIZE: medium (about 300 lines + 5 templates; hot files api/review.py and services/review.py: claim only when ready to edit and after B-review-parallel-gates). ACCEPTANCE: tests, README/config --explain, driver note on when to add a design_review gate.

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.

data.body:
`ddflow decision status` lists, per category: live decisions, those with checks, compliance (pass/fail/unavailable/waived), stale ones (review_by passed), triggered revisits and open waivers. Doctor and brief carry budgeted reminders. A periodic 'decision review' job files one task per due decision. `decision review <id> --reaffirm|--change` records the outcome. Contradicting research is routed to the operator through B-rw-vs-decision.

Operator 2026-10-06 (rules/decisions unification): build this on the shared guidance engine (B-uni-guidance-core/-inject/-enforce); no rule- or decision-specific matcher, injection or enforcement path.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: the revisit triggers named above gain repeated-deviation (a record with override=deviate whose deviation rate over its last N applicable items, or deviations by 2 different agents, passes a configured rate). The trigger is registered by B-goal-report through guidance/review.register_trigger; the review record and its outcomes (reaffirm, change, plus promote to MUST or demote to MAY) are this task's. The per-category compliance report adds deviation and unanswered counts. Never automatic.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the review facility is generic over kinds that go stale: guidance/review.register_trigger and the review record accept any kind whose descriptor declares review_by (goals gain it in B-goal-model, rules via B-rules-onto-record-surface), so doctor and the brief list stale goals and rules by the same code that lists stale decisions; reaffirm / change outcomes are recorded with the generic lifecycle verbs (a 'change' is an edit or supersede with a reason). Review is done by a person or an agent: both CLI and MCP offer `decision review`, and an agent's 'change' outcome that weakens is flagged for the operator.

WHAT: an optional reviewer PANEL per gate: several independent reviewers examine the same diff, their findings are merged into one record with agreement counts, and one verdict is synthesised. WHY: the roborev skills fan a review out to a named panel and treat the synthesis job as the parent: verdict, findings and the fix offer attach to the parent, never to an individual reviewer ('3 reviewers: bug P, security F'). ddflow has parallel gates (B-review-parallel-gates: two DIFFERENT gates concurrently, each its own record) and a planned pool (B-reviewer-pool: ONE reviewer answers each chunk, spill/failover); neither has several reviewers reviewing the SAME chunk and a merged result, and 'found by 3 of 3 independent reviewers' is a confidence signal the triage flow (ddflow review triage) cannot see today (R-skills-mining-gaps, CONFIRMED).
INTERFACE REUSED: ReviewerDispatch (B-uni-kind-pipeline.4: pool -> route -> context pack) gets a `panel` stage beside `pool`; the chunk runner and hedge/race logic in services/review.py; heavy slots from services/slots.py (B-af-slots) and [reviewer].max_concurrency; the independence rule per member (reviewer_family_must_differ, family_of); finding_digest and the similarity from searchcore to merge equal findings; the existing gate record, triage and round counter (a panel review is ONE round of its gate); B-pi-review-lens for a lens per member.
CONFIG SHAPE (all data, off by default): `[review.panel.<gate>] members = ["reviewer-a", "reviewer-b", "reviewer-c"]`, `min_members = 2`, `verdict_rule = "any_confirmed" | "majority" | "all"` (default any_confirmed: any HIGH or MEDIUM finding not refuted fails the gate, as today), `merge_floor = 0.8`, `lens = { reviewer-a = "refute", reviewer-b = "security" }`, `family_distinct = true` (prefer distinct families, B-reviewer-pool's knob). Editable by CLI/MCP, removable, carried by org bundles.
BEHAVIOUR: each member must pass the independence rule against the author or is skipped with the reason; a member that is unavailable is listed, never hidden; fewer than min_members available -> the gate is recorded partial/unavailable, never passed; findings equal by digest or similarity >= merge_floor become one finding carrying `found_by` and `agreement`; the record's header reads like `3 reviewers: refute P, security F, design P`; `ddflow review triage` and any fix flow address the ONE record id; the evidence names which member said what (provenance, fenced as data).
TESTS (failing-first): three fake reviewers, one finding found by two: merged with agreement 2; one member unavailable with min_members 3 -> partial; a same-family member skipped with the reason; verdict_rule majority versus any_confirmed; concurrency cap respected; panel config absent -> identical to today. SIZE: medium (about 450 lines; hot files services/review.py and api/review.py: after B-pi-review-lens and B-reviewer-pool). ACCEPTANCE: tests, parity, README/config --explain, driver note on cost (a panel multiplies reviewer calls; the review budget [review].max_rounds is unchanged).

RECORD-SURFACE CONTRACT (project-wide; this task meets it for what it adds): CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) and on the existing verb tool, never a new tools/list entry; list/show/add/edit/remove (merge and split where the kind has duplicates or parts), search, relevance-matched context insert into brief/claim/gate prompts within the context-pack budget, RAG export through the docs search interface, every change logged as an event with who/when/why, sessions told of changes (brief at start, a notice for changes since), an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. Standing rules: unavailable is never passed; a reviewer of another model family; a bug found on the way is filed first and fixed failing-first. Everything in this task is configuration or a shipped template that a project overrides, removes or reorders, and an org bundle can carry; nothing is a code constant.
