data.body:
New relations contradicts X / supersedes X / coordinates X on the add, new event kinds record.contradicted and record.resolved registered with a first writer. The decider: operator for decisions, rules and instructions (the add is parked in a needs_operator list shown in the brief); the agent for tasks, bugs and lessons, who must record why. Outcomes: keep old (new refused with reason), keep new (old superseded), extend (merged text), coordinate (both stay, linked with a note of how they differ), delete (old marked removed; the events stay). Unresolved contradictions show in brief and doctor.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the outcomes keep old / keep new (supersede) / extend (merge) / delete (retire) call the lifecycle verbs of B-rc-lifecycle (supersede, merge, remove with reason) instead of new resolution code; this task adds only the relations contradicts / supersedes / coordinates, the needs_operator list and the decider rules. The resolution is therefore in `<kind> history` and in the change feed like any other change.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces B-rw-revise's own events: uses the def-record revise/supersede/retire/merge paths (B-uni-def-records, B-uni-record-surface), with a mandatory reason, who/model family, and the source or probe that justifies the change. Revise = same claim, rev+1; supersede = the world or source changed (valid_until + superseded_by, Graphiti-style invalidate-not-delete); merge records same_as. On revise/supersede/retire: list every anchor pinned to the old revision (they become 'outdated'), open one re-verification task per anchor group or block items touching them; the reviewer clears the pin with `ddflow research pin <claim> --code <anchor>` (Doorstop suspect-link clearing). A claim that becomes REFUTED (by probe, failing vector or a verifier) files a bug per anchored code site naming the claim; the refuting vector is the natural regression test. Evidence of every correction stays in the log.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: also covers the requirements of B-rw-revise (superseded in design by this task): `research show` prints the revision history (revisions, valid_until, superseded_by, the reason and who); the silent same-id overwrite stays a bug (fix-B14d796e03b), not a feature.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): revise, supersede, retire and merge for claims are the generic verbs of B-rc-lifecycle declared on the claim descriptor (history with before/after replaces 'show prints the revision history'); this task keeps what is claim-specific: the revision bump, validity windows, anchor suspect-marking, refuted-claim bug filing.

D-research-system (operator 2026-10-08), research R-research-system. Replaces the design of B-rw-inject and B-rw-query's retrieval (they must not build their own injector, search or embedder). Claims are a SearchSource in the one engine (statement, mechanism, structured fields, quoted passage, tags indexed), fused BM25 + trigram (+ embeddings when the [rag] extra is present), and a ContextPack builder with per-context budgets: brief ~2k tokens (claims first, record collapsed), claim time (top neighbours for dedupe), review ~3k (anchored claims + vectors), edit time ~1.5k. Edit time: the PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write (through the one hook table, B-uni-hooks; harnesses without such a hook fall back to the claim/brief injection and the MCP tool) injects the claims anchored to the file being edited, with their grade, vectors and a one-line citation; exact anchored claims are always included, fuzzy hits only fill the remaining budget; claims about third-party tools carry staleness labels. MCP: tool `ddflow_research_for(path|symbol|text)` and resource `ddflow://claim/<id>`. Each pack fenced as data with provenance. Fixes B204's gap in this area: a task whose globs have anchored claims cannot complete without the pack having been offered (recorded).

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): research is a PROVIDER of the one relevance builder B-rc-context (services/applicable.register_provider), not a private injector: the edit-time door (PreToolUse on Edit/Write), the prompt door and the claim door are B-rc-context's, with the same ledger (a claim already shown is not shown again unless its revision changed). Do not write a research-only pre-tool handler or the `ddflow_research_for` tool: the ask is `recall --for path:|symbol:|text:` (symbol: is added to its argument syntax by this task). Exact anchored claims stay always-included inside the pack.

Acceptance for the phase, on a throwaway project (ddflow init, no companions, no network, fake reviewers) and then on this repository read-only. (1) DEFAULTS CHANGE NOTHING: with no new config, gate status, brief, workflow output and the default pipelines are byte-identical to the previous release (golden test); an existing project upgrading gets no new gate, job or finding. (2) Each idea enabled by config only: a dated spec protected by its class (an agent edit to the body is reported), an unclassified document treated as history with the doctor note; a doc.reviewed cursor puts a changed document back on the worklist and keeps a deferred one; a deprecated synonym found in an evergreen document and not in a point_in_time one; the claims gate refusing an existence-only citation; a corpus duplicate and an orphan; a scenario card with a vacuous step refused, an unavailable step never passed, a due card listed by the sweep; a design lens gate sending the design template; a three-reviewer panel merging a finding with agreement 2. (3) CONFIGURABILITY: every behaviour above changed, disabled, reordered and removed through ddflow config / ddflow_configure and the workflow commands (no code edit), shipped templates overridden by files under .ddflow, an org bundle carrying the settings to a second throwaway project; an agent's change over MCP reported to the operator. (4) Every new verb has CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test) on the existing ddflow_docs and review tools, with tools/list inside the byte budget. (5) Replay rebuilds classes, cursors, terms and scenario runs from the log. (6) Update R-skills-mining-value with the measured outcome (was the benefit real: number of point-in-time rewrites caught, unverified claims surfaced, vacuous scenario steps refused, duplicate or contradicting findings); a record that cannot be measured stays THEORETICAL. (7) README, help topics, driver text and per-agent delta notes describe the new switches and their defaults.
data.title: Acceptance for the skills-mined pipeline ideas: defaults change nothing, each idea on by config alone, shareable, replayable, measured

data.body:
Use skills where they matter. Research R0e6ddb15a3. Unify only the 'what applies' VIEW: one bounded block that ranks rules, decisions and skills together by glob match and BM25, shared by brief, claim and the gate and reviewer prompts (views/markdown.py _brief_skills is the seed); rules and skills stay separate record types and ddflow never copies a skill's content into the log. Per-task assignment task add --skills (listed first), glob scoping from a skill's paths/metadata, recall/RAG over skills, pointers only, token-budgeted. Claude's paths/when_to_use are Claude-only: a spec-valid skill must work without them. Blocked on D-skills-open-questions-4 item 3.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the shared 'what applies' block is B-rc-context's builder (services/applicable.py); skills register as a PROVIDER (glob-scoped relevance from a skill's paths or metadata) instead of a skills-only block, and the reviewer-prompt block calls the same builder. Per-task assignment `task add --skills` stays here.

Each kind registers with the overlay loader once (B-uni-overlay); this task proves each one resolves from an org bundle, is overridable by the project unless required by policy, reports provenance, and that executable parts stay inert until approved. Skills from an org bundle reuse the skills install/lock path (B-skills-install) rather than a second installer. Org-required companions appear in the brief's companion line with the source named.

Operator question 2026-10-07 (can corporate rules define companion tools, MCP servers, subagents and their use, rules, policies, architectural decisions, command prompts, workflow configuration?): two kinds were missing from the list and are now in scope: (1) architectural decisions and decision packs (owned by B-dec-presets; pinned 'always' decisions from B-dec-pinned, evidence requirements from B-dec-evidence, and policy-document sources from B-dec-policy-sources arrive through the same bundle; a decision the company enforces cannot be superseded locally); (2) subagent routing and separation of duties (B-sub-route, B-sub-sod) as org-set defaults, with 'allow' lists for which agents may satisfy which gates. The company's MCP servers are companions: each entry's launch line, install command and hooks are executable content, inert until a person approves its digest, then registered into each agent's config by the one mcpconfig.register writer.

SCOPE CARVE-OUT (operator 2026-10-10, following the order review): this task does NOT cover (a) skills from an org bundle (they reuse the skills install/lock path of B-skills-install) and (b) subagent roles, routing and separation-of-duties defaults with the 'allow' lists (B-sub-route, B-sub-sod). Both depend on tasks that run later (P-skills, P-subagents, rounds ~22-23) and would have pushed all of waves 3 and 4 back. They are moved to B-org-kinds-skills-subagents in P-subagents, which runs after those tasks. Every other kind in the list above is wired here as described.

EXTENDED 2026-10-11 by P-goals: principles (decisions or rules with override=deviate), the override field itself, and goals are syncable kinds: an org bundle may carry team principles and team goals (read-only in the project, labelled with the source and revision in brief and doctor; a project adds its own on top). Proposals, deviations and discovery runs are never synced (local project log); the [discovery] knobs may be pinned or capped by policy (for example web = false). Personal goals under .ddflow/local never reach another user's brief.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): register the read-only provider of B-rc-lifecycle: every mutating record verb on a record whose source is an org bundle refuses (exit 3) naming the source and revision and the project-override path (the project layers its own record on top, which is a new local record, not an edit of the org one). A newly applied org revision is ONE feed entry (B-rc-changes) with source, revision and the count of changed records, binding when any of them is a rule, decision, principle or goal.

Detection runs in the background worker's budget (B-uni-local-worker) and the schedule/trigger engine (B-uni-triggers) -- no private timer. `org diff` resolves the config with the candidate revision in a temp layer stack and prints changed knobs, added/removed/changed assets, new executable content needing approval and new policy violations the project would hit. `org update` creates a task whose deliverable is the org.lock bump plus any project fixes, gated like any change; with integration=pr it opens a PR. Signed enforced policy with auto_apply=enforced applies immediately and records org.policy.applied. Offline or fetch failure: keep last known good, note it, never treat 'could not fetch' as 'no policy'.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the 'newer revision appears in the brief with a diff summary' line is registered as an entry of the shared change feed (B-rc-changes) rather than a private brief section, so a running session sees it through the same doors; `org diff` stays the detailed view.

PRIORITY: MUST. WHAT: `ddflow sync-check` (also a doctor section, run automatically after a pull by an optional post-merge/post-checkout hook and by `ddflow brief` when HEAD changed since the last look): read-only, compares what the pulled log and tree now say with this clone's last look (a small .ddflow/local/last-seen record: per-shard event count and last id, HEAD) and reports, each with the exact next command: contested claims/ids/records (B191 and fix-B230e852e10), two live claims by one name from different clones, an event whose ts is more than [log].skew_tolerance_s from now (B5a6651cd8e: names the author, says leases of that clone are unreliable), a shard that SHRANK or vanished since last seen (Ba24a8d32ee: 'N events lost; find them with git reflog / origin', never auto-repair), ddflow.seen stamps newer than this version and the team minimum (B-mu-version-policy), instruction files with two managed blocks or an older stamp than the log (B63635ddc6a), generated views or config.toml with conflict markers (B6b8d1f7a0f), managed git hooks missing (Bec9a971c5d), clone behind its remote (git fetch status; 'brief shows stale knowledge' of scenario 10), removed items with live leases (B71dedb76d2). Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 could not run. Extends B-gap-log-backup (reuse its lamport/content notes; do not duplicate) and B189's unpushed lines.
EVIDENCE: scenarios s1, s2*, s4, s5, s6c/6d, s6i, s7, s10, s11 in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-delian-src-ddflow--claude-worktrees-bridge-cse-015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK/e0567917-2370-56c0-a094-caf440a8b983/scratchpad/mu. INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/reporting/health.py check registry, services/eventcommit.py, ddflow.seen/capabilities events and the skew guard, fsio.Managed header reader, ticks for the 'last look' cadence, command registry (declared command, CLI and MCP from one declaration). HOW TO TEST: every harness scenario ends with sync-check and asserts the finding and the remedy text. SIZE: medium-large (~700 lines). ACCEPTANCE: no scenario in R-multiuser-experiments leaves a clone 'Healthy' when it is wrong.

NOTE 2026-10-11 (bug fixes ahead of this task): bug Ba24a8d32ee fixed by fix-Ba24a8d32ee (per-shard high-water mark in .ddflow/local, doctor PROBLEM when a shard shrinks, `doctor --accept-lost-events`); remaining scope: the sync-check section, the shared 'last look' record with HEAD/remote staleness, a helper that re-imports lost events from a named sha. bug B63635ddc6a fixed by fix-B63635ddc6a (doctor PROBLEM for two managed blocks, `adopt --refresh-docs` collapses them, patch-only skew warns instead of refusing); remaining scope: sync-check wording, instruction-file stamp older than the log (NOTE exists), team minimum version (B-mu-version-policy). bug Bec9a971c5d fixed by fix-Bec9a971c5d; bug B71dedb76d2 by fix-B71dedb76d2; bug B5a6651cd8e by fix-B5a6651cd8e; remaining scope for each: only the sync-check report line with its remedy, and for B5a6651cd8e the skew NOTE naming the author.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the per-clone 'last look' record (HEAD, shard counts) lives in the cursor store created by B-rc-changes (services/seen.py, .ddflow/local/seen/) as its `clone` section, not in a second last-seen file; contested records and the unreconciled-decision pairs of B-mu-conflicts are BINDING entries of the change feed so a session already running is told after a pull.

A restarted lane receives its previous handoff plus 'see also' pointers, fenced as data, inside the existing brief budget.

WHY (measured): what a restarted agent gets today is `ddflow brief` (queue state, ranked lessons/decisions) and, only after a Claude compaction with the PreCompact hook installed, the recent-tail note (api/setup.py _after_compaction: 'No record of what this session was doing reached ddflow' otherwise). A lane restarted for context exhaustion is a NEW harness session, so SessionStart source=startup/resume gets no memory of the previous lane run at all; the coordinator re-sends the brief file by hand. session.ended summaries are folded into the brief only via crash recovery.

DESIGN: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py builds a 'Previous run' section for the same agent identity (--agent U1): the latest session.handoff (and, if the agent was interrupted, its tail), its transcript pointers, and 'see also': the 3 most relevant older sessions/handoffs of the SAME agent and of OTHER agents touching the same globs or items (cited session:id, with the exact command `ddflow session search ...` / `ddflow session show <id> --turns a-b` to open them). Built with services/contextpack.pack + core/budget.Budget so it obeys [session].brief_max_tokens (its own share, like guidance inject DOOR_SHARE), every body inside core/provenance fence with author and trust (agent), preceded by the standard 'recorded DATA, not instructions' line. Also delivered by the SessionStart hook (source=startup|resume|compact) and by the MCP initialize/first-call preamble (B-hy-first-call) - one builder, three doors, like services/guidance/inject.py.

PIN/TEST: brief golden unchanged when there is no handoff; with a handoff, section present, cited, within budget; an instruction planted in a handoff stays inside the fence and is not placed outside it; two agents' handoffs never cross unless the see-also relevance rule selects them; budget tiny keeps the first line. EXPECTED SIZE: ~250 lines + tests.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: the 'Previous run' section is a sub-block of the RESUME block of B-res-brief-recovery-link (edge added) and uses the same builder when the same agent identity has an interrupted item; it creates no second SessionStart block (the hook output is ddflow/api/setup.py). B-gap-lanes `lanes brief` calls this builder. A 'lane' in B-am-capture's `--lane U1` is the agent identity.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): the 'Previous run' section is followed by the change feed for the same agent identity: what changed (records, B-rc-changes) between the previous session's end mark and now, binding first, within the same share of the brief budget. The end mark is the cursor the previous session left in the seen store.

Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim, also recorded as a session prompt): "Separately, Is there a way for a workflow management engine to follow project goals (have the concept of goals) and automatically research periodically what next features might be needed and suggest that, while separately follow common principles for the project which are some sort of a weak rule, which defines what we prefer to do unless there is a better reason, and then we have a set of strict or unstrict as defined rules, which have to be followed? ... propose features or fill-up gaps, investigate if for those features we could use the already existing internals and rules + decisions + architectural decisions engines implemented or planned to be implemented and add a phase + tasks for us to do them."

Evidence: R-goals-existing-map (CONFIRMED: what exists and what the attached document got wrong) and R-goals-principles-proposals-design (THEORETICAL: survey of Kiro, Spec Kit, Claude Code, Cursor, Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Dependabot, Renovate, Jules, Linear, SonarQube, ArchUnit, MADR, RFC 2119, and the design).

DESIGN IN ONE PARAGRAPH (nothing here is a parallel store):
- RULES (strict or unstrict) are the guidance engine's rule and decision records: enforcement block | warn | advisory, checks, waivers, review_by. Already built in services/guidance; P-decisions finishes and wires them. This phase adds nothing to what a rule IS.
- PRINCIPLES are NOT a new kind. A principle is a guidance record (a decision or a rule) whose OVERRIDE MODE is deviate: follow it unless you record a reason. A rule is override=waive (a person approves, scoped, at most 90 days, D-decision-management) or none (an org floor). RFC 2119 vocabulary: MUST = block + waive|none, SHOULD = warn + deviate, MAY = advisory. A finding against a SHOULD must be answered (comply or deviate with a reason) before the item completes; repeated deviations flag the principle for review. That feedback loop is what keeps a soft rule from silently vanishing or silently becoming hard.
- GOALS are a new definition-record kind (def.* events, record surface, search, history, upcasters come free): a title, an owner, a status, linked phases/tasks/decisions, and key results with a measurable source (dag progress, a ddflow metric, an approved check command, or a dated manual attestation that goes stale). Progress is computed, never typed. A goal never overrides a rule; it steers what the brief shows, what discovery proposes and what the roadmap displays.
- PROPOSALS (periodic feature discovery) are a second new def-record kind that lives OUTSIDE the queue until a person adopts it, so next/claim never see an unreviewed idea. A shipped, opt-in schedule job files ONE research item per run whose output is at most K proposals, each citing a goal, evidence, a principle check, a size estimate and a dedupe result against the board AND against rejected proposals. Adopt/defer/reject (with reason) are person-only. Caps, backpressure, a circuit breaker and a rejected-ideas memory prevent idea spam.
- PRECEDENCE: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; the nearest scope wins within a tier; goals never constrain.

Order: decide -> {deviation, cites, goal model} -> {progress, proposal model} -> {inject, discover} -> report -> acceptance -> eval. Held behind the P-gaps core, the docs wave and P-decisions (D-old-work-behind-core-docs): it builds on the decision engine tasks B-dec-model, B-dec-waivers, B-dec-monitor, B-dec-review, on B-research-items and the schedule tasks, and on B-gap-metrics.

Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Do this too, again for this project and ddflow in general by default, and - A second cross-family reviewer endpoint: a small gain, about 30% in busy periods only. It would need to be from a different model family to keep the independence rule.' Measured (research R-task-time, slow2): one reviewer endpoint served 214 calls/day; average concurrency 1.5, peak 9; minutes per 5000-char chunk 2.0 at 1-2 concurrent calls vs 3.0-3.3 at 6-8, so saturation costs ~30-50% only in busy periods; [reviewer].max_concurrency = 10 and hedge = 3 are already set. Build GENERAL support for a pool of reviewers per gate (ddflow already lists several [[reviewer]] entries with gates=...; check how they are chosen today in services/review.py and config.py before designing): (1) SPILL: when the preferred reviewer for a gate is at its max_concurrency, or its recent latency exceeds [review].spill_after_s, the next chunk goes to the next independent reviewer of that gate; (2) FAILOVER: an unreachable/erroring reviewer falls to the next one (recorded in the evidence which reviewer answered each chunk; a gate is never recorded passed on a reviewer that did not run); (3) INDEPENDENCE stays enforced for EVERY pool member: each member must pass the author-vs-reviewer family check (reviewer_family_must_differ, family_for, router-set rule in config.py) — a member that would not be independent of the author is skipped with the reason, never used; (4) DIVERSITY knob [review].prefer_distinct_families (default true): among independent members prefer one whose family differs from the other pool members' families so a second endpoint of a DIFFERENT family adds a second opinion rather than a second copy of the same model; [review].require_distinct_families (default false) refuses a pool whose members share a family when the operator wants strict diversity; (5) `ddflow reviewers list` shows the pool per gate with family, load and last latency; `ddflow doctor` notes a gate with a single reviewer under sustained saturation and says how to add a second (`ddflow reviewers add ... --local`); (6) `ddflow reviewers detect` proposes additional endpoints it finds (reachable, different family) and writes them to the git-ignored local layer by default (D-nobody's-own-services: endpoints, hosts and model names of a private deployment are NEVER committed; refer to a service by role in task bodies, research and commit messages). All configurable via config, CLI and MCP (ddflow_configure, reviewers add/detect on the local layer): spill_after_s (default 120; 0 = never spill), prefer_distinct_families, require_distinct_families, a per-reviewer weight/priority. Shipped defaults for every project; with a single reviewer everything behaves exactly as today. FOR THIS PROJECT: the code cannot supply the endpoint; after the task merges, the operator (or `ddflow reviewers detect --write` on this machine, which writes .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml) adds the second endpoint; the task must NOT commit any address or private model name. Acceptance (failing-first, fake reviewers, no network): with two independent fakes and the first at max_concurrency the second gets the next chunk; an erroring first fails over and the evidence names the answering reviewer per chunk; a pool member of the author's family is skipped with the reason; prefer_distinct_families orders a different-family member first; require_distinct_families refuses a same-family pool with exit 3 and the remedy; a single-reviewer project is byte-for-byte unchanged; knobs settable via config --local and ddflow_configure; tools/list byte budget green; README + config --explain + shipped driver docs (D-readme-current); the generality acceptance below.

GENERALITY (operator: general feature of ddflow): shipped defaults in the package; works on upgrade and on fresh `ddflow init` with no config change; tests in a throwaway project (no companions, no network); no reference to this repository's hosts/models/agent names anywhere in code, messages or shipped docs; docs ship in ddflow/templates; works for every agent integration.

(relayed by the lead via the question tool, genuine operator answers 2026-10-11)
1. Placement of P-record-contract: "After the P-gaps core, before docs wave".
2. Agents may weaken records, but weakening is flagged until the operator acknowledges (default flag).
3. Mid-session injection default: scope plus text match with a high threshold, a measured precision floor and a ledger of already-shown.

data.alternatives: Per-kind lifecycle, notification and export tasks (rejected: five or more copies, the pattern D-unify exists to stop); a daemon pushing notifications (rejected: D-sched-no-daemon, ddflow answers at the doors a harness already calls).
data.consequences: Shared mechanisms are built once (P-record-contract) and goals, proposals, rules and decisions consume them; per-kind search sources, resources, injectors and lifecycle code are not written. More verbs live inside the one tool per kind, so the tools/list budget is not spent per verb.
data.context: Operator request 2026-10-11 after P-goals was filed. Existing basis: D-unify 4 (one record surface), D-no-duplicates, D-compat, D-lean-and-trusted, D-decision-management, D-viewer-lists-consolidated. Audit found no mid-session change notification, no merge/split/history verbs on the record surface, no RAG export, and search/recall/resource registration hard-coded per kind.
data.decision:
The record-surface contract (operator request 2026-10-11, verbatim in the session log: every goal, principle and rule follows the project's principles: MCP and CLI interfaces; add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert and RAG export; the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify and split; evidence is logged; sessions are informed of changes automatically, get the brief at start, and can search, ask or automatically receive context related to what they do). Every record kind (rule, decision, principle = a guidance record with override=deviate, goal, proposal, waiver and deviation, and every later kind) meets these rows; a kind that cannot meet one lists an exemption with its reason in the conformance test, and exemptions only shrink.
RC1 One declaration, two faces: one RecordKind descriptor (api/records.py) generates the CLI group and ONE MCP tool per kind (verbs are actions, never a tool per verb; tools/list budget test), bodies identical (parity test). Operator-only verbs are declared fields (surfaces/exemptions.py): refused on MCP with an explained exit 3.
RC2 Verbs: list, show, add (add-time duplicate and contradiction check, D-no-duplicates), edit (field level, clearing allowed), remove (= retire with a reason: a tombstone, never a silent hard delete), revise (whole replace), search, and the lifecycle verbs history, supersede, merge (many into one), split (one into several), restore. Every mutating verb needs a reason. Merge, split and supersede link both records with provenance. An agent's weakening change (lower enforcement, retire, drop, accept) is flagged for the operator until acknowledged (D-decision-management 2).
RC3 Evidence: every change is a log event on the def.* envelope with who, when, reason, session, source prompt (via the session) and before/after digest; show and history [--diff] display it; replay reproduces it; text is redacted (D-unify 6) and shown fenced as data.
RC4 Retrieval derived from the descriptor, no per-kind code: ddflow search --kind, the kind's own search, ddflow recall (the budgeted ask), context-pack candidates cited by kind:id.
RC5 RAG export: chunks with stable ids, status, validity, provenance, redaction, trust fence and tombstones for retired, merged and split ids; ddflow export records; MCP resource ddflow://records/{kind}/{id}.
RC6 Sessions are informed: at start the brief (bounded, fenced, pinned never trimmed) and the SessionStart/first-call door; at claim the guidance and direction that apply to the item's files, gate and category; mid-session the change feed ('changed since you last looked', with the agent's own changes excluded) delivered through the prompt, pre-tool and post-tool hooks where the harness honours injection, otherwise as a notice on MCP replies, heartbeat and wait; relevance-matched context (scope match first, then text match to the task, thresholded, once per session unless the record changed).
RC7 Ask: ddflow recall (and recall --for item|path|text) for agents, ddflow search for people; both over the one engine.
RC8 Review: kinds that can go stale carry review_by or a staleness rule, surfaced in doctor and brief; revisit triggers and repeated-deviation triggers register with the one review facility; acts that need a person are declared operator-only.
RC9 Scope and privacy: org-sourced records are read-only locally, labelled with source and revision, and the project layers on top; proposals, deviations, waivers and discovery runs are local to the project log; local-only records never reach another user's brief, feed or export; every displayed text is redacted and fenced.
RC10 Format: new payload fields are additive and the upcaster is registered with the kind's first writer (D-compat); an older ddflow preserves what it does not understand.
RC11 Docs: a help topic per kind (or the shared 'records' topic), the README tool-table row generated, driver notes for agent-facing behaviour.
RC12 Conformance: one generated test over every declared kind asserts RC1 to RC11 (task B-rc-conformance).
Built by phase P-record-contract (B-rc-lifecycle, B-rc-changes, B-rc-participation, B-rc-context, B-rc-rag-export, B-rc-conformance) in the core wave after the P-unify checkpoint, with the P-goals, P-decisions, rules and other tasks extended to use it rather than build per-kind versions. Defaults chosen without the operator, to confirm: split = child def.recorded events with provenance.split_from plus a def.retired of the original carrying split_into (no new event kind); the mid-session feed delivers only BINDING changes (rule, decision, principle, goal status, waiver expiry, contested) and counts the rest; remove stays a tombstone and there is no hard purge except the redaction purge.

Operator answers 2026-10-11 (genuine, via the question tool; recorded with ddflow session prompt, relayed by the lead):
1. Placement: P-record-contract runs AFTER the P-gaps core (B-gap-log-scale, B-gap-lanes, B-gap-plan-lint: phase-level needs, as the other held phases) and BEFORE the docs wave's round 8 phases: P-docs-generic, P-roadmap and P-docs-search each need P-record-contract (so docs-wave documents are written against the finished record surface). P-doc-templates and every P-gaps task are NOT delayed (P-doc-templates stays ready in round 4, P-gaps in round 1): making P-doc-templates wait would have delayed it, so only the round 8 phases wait. Everything behind the docs wave moves one round later (sim_order: 0 cycles, 0 stuck).
2. Weakening: an agent may weaken a record (lower enforcement, widen override, retire, drop, accept), but a weakening is accepted and FLAGGED 'changed by agent' in the brief, doctor and the change feed until the operator acknowledges it (`<kind> ack`, operator-only; B-rc-lifecycle). Default confirmed.
3. Mid-session injection (RC6): scope match plus text match with a HIGH threshold (nothing injected when nothing clears it), a measured precision floor asserted on a labelled fixture (B-rc-context), and a ledger of what the session was already shown (not shown again unless the record changed). Default confirmed.
4. The operator ACKNOWLEDGES this decision as an operator decision. RAG export (RC5) default target is .ddflow/local/export/records.jsonl (git-ignored, derived); committing exports is opt-in.
Defaults listed above as 'to confirm' (split as child def.recorded plus def.retired; BINDING-only mid-session feed; remove is a tombstone, no purge) stand as defaults.

data.body:
Ask the operator, record the decision, write docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md. Ask them one at a time with the recommended default; record each answer verbatim (ddflow session prompt) and as a decision (ddflow decision add --globs ...). Do not start any other B-goal-* or B-prop-* task before this is answered.

QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS (evidence: R-goals-existing-map, R-goals-principles-proposals-design):
1. Is a principle a new kind or a field? DEFAULT: a field, not a kind. Add one field to the guidance record, override = none | waive | deviate (how a finding is cleared), orthogonal to enforcement (how hard a finding is). Principle = enforcement warn + override deviate; rule = block + waive; org floor = block + none; preference = advisory. Vocabulary shown to people: MUST / SHOULD / MAY (RFC 2119) next to the enforcement word. Rejected: a separate principle store (a second engine to keep in step), and enforcement alone (a warn finding needs no answer, so a soft rule fails by silence).
2. Who may deviate from a principle, and does it expire? DEFAULT: the authoring agent records a deviation, item-scoped, reason required (evidence optional), no approval, no expiry (it dies with the item), always visible in brief, completion summary and the operator's decision list. Only block rules need a person's waiver (up to 90 days, approved by digest, unchanged). A deviation from a principle on a CHECK-LESS record (judged by a reviewer) is accepted the same way.
3. Must a principle finding be answered before complete? DEFAULT: yes for SHOULD with a mechanical check or a reviewer finding that cites the id; complete refuses (exit 3) listing the unanswered ones; an answer is comply (fixed) or deviate (reason). MAY findings never refuse. Gate OUTCOME stays passed (a principle is not a blocker); the ledger carries the answer.
4. Precedence order. DEFAULT: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; nearest scope (gate, then globs, then category, then always) wins within a tier, then priority, then newest; unreconciled conflicts are a doctor note and a B-coh item, never a silent pick. Goals never override a rule or a principle. Extends D-rules-hierarchy (workflow enforcement > project rules > agent defaults); it does not replace it.
5. Goal record shape. DEFAULT: def-record kind goal; fields title, body, status (proposed | active | achieved | dropped), owner, target_date, parent (at most 2 levels), links (phases, tasks, decisions, research), key_results[] each {id, text, source = dag | metric | check | manual, ref, baseline, target, direction}. Progress is computed: dag = done share of the linked phases' tasks (tasks weighted equally; a removed or abandoned task leaves the count); metric = a named ddflow metric (B-gap-metrics); check = a command through the shared runner, operator-config or approved by digest only; manual = an operator attestation with a date that goes STALE after [goals].manual_stale_days (default 30) and is then reported unavailable, never green. Overall goal progress = the minimum-of-trajectory view is NOT used; show each KR and their mean, marked an estimate.
6. What does the brief show of goals? DEFAULT: at most 3 lines (active goals by priority: title, mean KR progress, weakest KR, days to target, stale flag), plus at claim the item's goal chain (task -> phase -> goal) labelled Direction, not a constraint; orphan work (completed items under no goal) counted in the roadmap and doctor, never a gate.
7. Proposal storage and triage states. DEFAULT: def-record kind proposal outside the queue (status proposed | adopted | deferred (snooze_until) | rejected | expired | superseded); adopt creates a task through services/items.add_task (dup check included) in a phase the operator names and links back; adopt/defer/reject are person-only (CLI; no MCP verb, like ddflow approve); reject REQUIRES a reason and is remembered: a new proposal whose fingerprint or similarity matches a rejected one is not filed unless it carries new evidence the operator can see. Rejected: proposal as a task state (every scheduler, board and next path would need to learn it), and proposal as a research record (no adopt/reject lifecycle).
8. Discovery cadence and budget. DEFAULT: OFF until the operator turns it on (job feature_discovery shipped disabled); then weekly by the calendar, or every 2 completed phases, whichever the operator picks; per run at most 3 new proposals; at most 7 open (proposed, undecided) at any time, and the job does not run while the cap is reached (backpressure); at most 20 000 reviewed tokens per run when B-gap-spend can measure it (UNAVAILABLE, not zero, when it cannot, and then the run cap is the turn cap); circuit breaker after 3 consecutive runs with zero adopted proposals (job pauses and says so in brief); stale undecided proposals expire after 60 days. The job files ONE research item (kind research) through the normal claim, so any lane may take it and quotas apply.
9. What may discovery read? DEFAULT: the repository, the ddflow log, its own research records, dependency advisories through the configured companions; the web ONLY if the operator enabled [discovery].web (default false); the log redaction profile is applied to every proposal body; no file contents above 40 lines are quoted. Org policy may force web off.
10. Scope. DEFAULT: goals and principles may come from an org bundle (P-org-config) as read-only team goals/principles; a project may add its own and cannot deviate from an org floor; proposals and deviations are always local to the project log; personal (local-only) goals are allowed under .ddflow/local and never reach the brief of other users.
11. Evaluation gate for turning discovery on by default. DEFAULT: never on by default; recommend turning on after B-goal-eval reports >= 3 runs with acceptance in 20-70 percent.

ACCEPTANCE: the answers are recorded as a decision with the reasons; the doc lists every question with the answer; the dependent tasks' bodies are amended if an answer differs from the default (ddflow update). Tests: none (docs only); gates: research, rules, docs.
SIZE: small. DOCS: docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md.

Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request, D-record-surface-contract, phase P-record-contract): three more questions, with defaults, so the goal, principle and proposal kinds meet the record contract. 12. Who may create, activate, edit, drop or delete goals and principles? DEFAULT: the CLI and MCP offer the same verbs to a person and to an agent; an agent's add or edit of a goal lands as status proposed, and a change that WEAKENS (a goal dropped or achieved, a principle demoted from MUST to SHOULD or MAY, a rule retired, enforcement lowered, override widened) is accepted but flagged 'changed by agent' in the brief, doctor and the change feed until the operator acknowledges it (`<kind> ack`, operator-only, B-rc-lifecycle); the operator can reverse it (restore). This is D-decision-management 2 applied to every guidance and goal kind. 13. Merge and split: may two goals, two principles or two open proposals be merged, and one split? DEFAULT: yes, through the record surface (B-rc-lifecycle): merge unions links, key results and tags and keeps both ids reachable (merged_from / successor); split creates parts with provenance.split_from and retires the original with split_into; a key result keeps its id when it moves so progress history survives; deleting is retiring (a tombstone with a reason), never a purge. 14. Mid-session notification: DEFAULT: a running session is told, through the change feed (B-rc-changes), of BINDING changes only (a rule, decision or principle at block or warn, a goal's status or target, a waiver granted or expired); everything else is a count. A fresh session's brief is unchanged. Record the answers (and any difference) in docs/ddflow/decisions/goals-principles.md and amend the dependent tasks.

OPERATOR ANSWERED 2026-10-11 (D-record-surface-contract-r2, session prompt): Q12 ANSWERED: the default stands. Agents may create and weaken goals and principles, and a weakening is flagged 'changed by agent' until the operator acknowledges it (`<kind> ack`, operator-only). Q13 and Q14 are covered by the contract's defaults (merge and split through the record surface with a tombstone and no purge; the mid-session feed delivers BINDING changes only and counts the rest) and stand as defaults until the operator says otherwise. Mid-session context injection (B-rc-context) is scope plus text match with a high threshold, a measured precision floor and a ledger of what was already shown. RAG export default target is .ddflow/local/export (git-ignored; committing exports is opt-in). Q1 to Q11 are still to ask.

Contract rows RC4, RC6, RC7 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "... can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do". WHAT: ONE relevance-matched context builder for every record kind, delivered automatically at the moments an agent starts a task, sends a prompt or is about to edit a file, and available on demand as the 'ask'. It replaces the per-kind injectors planned today (research in B-rw-context, skills in B-skills-context, decisions in B-dec-rag, goals in B-goal-inject) with providers of one engine. (1) services/applicable.py `related(repo, *, text="", paths=(), item="", kinds=None, budget, reader) -> Pack`: candidates from every kind whose descriptor declares `applies` (B-rc-participation) plus registered providers (`register_provider(name, fn)`; B-rw-context and B-skills-context register theirs here instead of building injectors). Tiers: (a) SCOPE match: always, globs, categories, gates, the item's goal chain (services/guidance/resolve.py is reused as is, so claim-time behaviour is unchanged); (b) TEXT match: the task, item title or prompt text against the context-enabled kinds through the one search engine (BM25 + trigram, semantic rerank when [rag] is configured), above [context].min_score; (c) providers. Ranking: pinned and block first, then scope specificity, then score; a per-kind cap so lessons cannot crowd out rules; near-duplicates folded by textsim; every hit cited kind:id and fenced (core/provenance); one Budget (services/contextpack.py). (2) The reader's LEDGER (the services/seen.py store of B-rc-changes): a record already shown to this session is not shown again unless its digest changed, so a long session is not re-fed the same rule on every prompt. (3) Doors, in services/hookdoors.py: UserPromptSubmit/BeforeAgent (query: the prompt plus the held item's title; budget [context].prompt_max_tokens, default 600), PreToolUse on Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit (query: the path and its scope; budget 800) and claim (the existing guidance injection stays; this adds the non-guidance kinds and the goal chain's Direction line). Each only for harnesses whose descriptor lists the event in `inject`; where no hook can inject, the same pack is the answer to `recall --for` and the first-call preamble carries a one-line pointer. Nothing is injected when nothing clears the threshold; a quiet door is the normal case. (4) The ASK: `ddflow recall --for item:|path:

|text:` (CLI) and the same argument on the existing recall MCP tool (no new tool): returns the pack with the reason each hit matched (scope, goal chain, score) so an agent can judge it. `ddflow search` stays the person's lookup. (5) Config [context] (enabled, inject = scope|scope+text|off with default scope+text, min_score, prompt_max_tokens, pre_tool_max_tokens, per_kind_cap) declared here with docs and strictest fallbacks. (6) MEASURE it (the failure mode is noise): a labelled fixture of 40 real prompts/paths from this log with the records a person would want; precision and recall of the door at the default threshold are asserted and printed, and the numbers go in the task's completion evidence. WHY (verified 2026-10-11): claim-time injection exists for rules and decisions only (services/guidance/inject.py, four doors); mid-session nothing is injected for any kind; the only planned edit-time injector is research's (B-rw-context, PreToolUse on Edit/Write) and it is a private one, B-skills-context and B-dec-rag plan more, and no task injects at prompt time. Goals, proposals and waivers would each need a fifth. One engine with providers is the D-unify answer. INTERFACE TO REUSE: services/guidance/{inject,resolve}.py, services/contextpack.py, services/searchcore, services/embed.py, services/hookio.py, services/hookdoors.py (B-rc-changes), services/seen.py, api/knowledge/retrieval.py (recall), core/provenance.py. HOW TO TEST: a rule scoped to src/billing/** is offered before the first Edit under that path and not again until it changes; a prompt about 'retry the webhook' surfaces the lesson and decision with those words above the threshold and nothing for 'rename this variable'; per-kind cap holds; budget never exceeded; a harness without pre_tool injection gets nothing from the hook and the same pack from `recall --for path:`; providers registered by research and skills appear; goal chain printed as Direction; injected-instruction text stays fenced; the precision/recall fixture meets its floor; CLI/MCP parity; tools/list budget. SIZE: large (~800 lines + tests). Hot files api/knowledge/retrieval.py, services/hookdoors.py, config.py (after B-rc-changes). ACCEPTANCE: on this repository, an agent about to edit ddflow/api/records.py is shown D-record-surface-contract and the rules that apply, once; `recall --for item:B-goal-model` returns the contract, the decisions and the research that govern it. DOCS: docstrings; README, help and driver notes by B-rc-conformance. OPERATOR ANSWER 2026-10-11 (D-record-surface-contract-r2): the default [context].inject = scope+text is confirmed with a HIGH min_score default (precision over recall: a quiet door is the normal case), a precision FLOOR that the labelled fixture must meet and print (fail the task, not the door, if it cannot), and the ledger of what a session was already shown (a record is not re-shown unless its digest changed).

data.body:
PRIORITY: MUST (first; everything else waits for it). WHAT: ask the operator the multi-user design choices, with recommended defaults, and record them as decisions in docs/ddflow/decisions/multiuser.md (one decision per question, --globs on the code it governs). Write the options, my recommendation and the evidence for each, then WAIT for the operator.
QUESTIONS AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS:
1 Claim arbitration across clones. Options: (a) optimistic: allow, detect at merge (today, B191); (b) [flow].claims=remote, a CAS ref refs/ddflow/claims/<id> (B192, built, tested: second claim exits 3, offline remote refuses); (c) a dedicated claims branch; (d) 'git push as the lock'. DEFAULT: (a) for solo or one-machine; (b) is the recommended team default and ddflow doctor/onboard offers it when a second author appears in the log; (c)(d) rejected: they need a push per claim and a branch ddflow cannot repair. Note forks (PR flow) cannot push refs to upstream: claims stay optimistic there.
2 Same-id policy. DEFAULT: every record kind follows B191: a second DIFFERENT definition under one id is CONTESTED and settled by `ddflow resolve`, never merged field-by-field; an identical re-add is not a contest; ids minted by ddflow are content/clone-derived (D-id-schemes-final) so human-chosen ids are the only source.
3 Id minting. DEFAULT: human-chosen ids stay allowed; `task add` without an id mints hash ids; teams may choose [ids] templates with a user or clone token (P-id-schemes).
4 Version skew between users. Options: refuse writes of the older clone (today), tolerate read-only, warn. DEFAULT: keep refuse-write/allow-read for FORMAT_LEVEL or event-kind differences, but make a PATCH difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL a warning (no refusal) from the first release that ships this task, and record a team minimum version in the log.
5 Shared config / policy source of truth. DEFAULT: committed .ddflow/config.toml is team policy; .ddflow/local is per user and may only tighten or set machine facts (paths, endpoints, worker counts); org bundles (P-org-config) sit below the project; gate pass evidence records which layer supplied the command.
6 Commit vs local. DEFAULT: committed: events, config, gates, rules, docs/ddflow managed drivers; generated views (QUEUE.md, LESSONS*.md) NOT committed by default in a team project (git-ignored, `ddflow render` on demand, CI renders), or committed with a merge=ours style strategy chosen in B-mu-generated-files; local: clone-id, index, runs, hooks.
7 Privacy of host names and paths in the shared log. DEFAULT: derived agent ids use a user-chosen handle instead of the host name once a project has more than one author; evidence tails pass the redactor; absolute paths never enter events (already true).
8 Lease semantics across machines. DEFAULT: a lease is evidence of intent, not a lock: expiry for another clone's lease is judged from heartbeat events seen locally; release/gate writes on a live lease of another agent need --force with a reason; no stealing (D-reclaim report).
9 Branching flows supported and tested. DEFAULT: trunk-based and PR-with-merge-commit, rebase-merge and squash-merge are tested in the harness (squash/rebase/merge of shards already PASS); gitflow and release lines with `port` are tested after B-mu-harness; long-lived branches work with `ddflow sync-check` run after every pull.
10 What is SKIPPED on purpose: a central lock or claim server, a daemon, vector clocks or a CRDT library, per-user signing keys inside the log (later, with B-org-trust), automatic resolution of contests, Perforce-style exclusive checkout of source files.
11 Roll-out order. DEFAULT: B-mu-harness, B-mu-identity, B-mu-conflicts, B-mu-sync-check, B-mu-generated-files, B-mu-lease-guards, B-mu-version-policy, then the GREAT tasks.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: decisions API (decision add --globs), B-gap-decide pattern. HOW TO TEST: the decision file exists, every question answered or explicitly deferred, tests/test_decisions_live.py-style check passes. SIZE: small. ACCEPTANCE: each downstream task cites its decision id.

NOTE 2026-10-11 (bug fixes ahead of this task): the 11 DEGRADED multi-user bug fixes (fix-<bug id>) were built on proposed decision D-mu-bugfix-defaults, not on your answers; revisit it first: 1 claims optimistic + contested surfaced, 8 lease guard scoped to another CLONE, receipt-time expiry, 4 patch skew warns, 5 local command labelled not refused, 6 only conflict handling not the tracked-vs-ignored choice.

ANSWERED 2026-10-11 (operator, relayed by the lead; decision D-mu-bugfix-defaults-r2, which supersedes D-mu-bugfix-defaults): question 1 (claim arbitration): optimistic, contest surfaced, merge/complete refused, nothing auto-resolved, accepted as built. Question 4 (version skew): a patch-only difference with the same FORMAT_LEVEL and no capability gap warns instead of refusing; other gaps still refuse. Question 5 (shared config): a local-only gate command pass is labelled now (command_layer/command_digest), refusal only as a later opt-in. Question 6 (commit vs local): generated views stay TRACKED in git and are regenerated on conflict (this overrides the not-committed default). Question 8 (lease semantics): receipt-time expiry, up to one TTL late, never the claimant's wall clock; the lease guard is per clone (release and gate run/record/skip on another clone's live lease need --force with a reason). Also decided: missing git hooks and machine-absolute launch paths are doctor NOTES (PROBLEM only under [enforce] block). NOT explicitly answered, still the recommended defaults and not contradicted: saw/UNRECONCILED for overlapping decisions, the event-loss high-water mark, and question 10 (no server, no daemon). Questions 2, 3, 7, 9 and 11 remain open. This task stays open.

data.claim: No for the index: on 3,129 real records (and 11,380 doc/code chunks) SQLite FTS5 is 10-60x faster per query, 10x cheaper to cold-start (19 ms vs 220 ms in-process, 13.5 MB vs 66 MB RSS), has phrase/prefix/trigram that DuckDB FTS lacks, and its index updates incrementally. DuckDB wins only on scan analytics over raw jsonl at 500k+ events (1.3 s vs 6.9 s at 1.13M events) and on vector scan at 30k+ vectors; neither is a bottleneck at ddflow's 56k events / 3k records.
data.falsifier: DuckDB lexical query p50 under SQLite's, or cold start under 50 ms, on the same corpus.
data.mechanism: Same texts (3,129 records from the real index.db: lessons, decisions, research, bugs, prompts, items, memories; 11,380 chunks of repo docs/code) loaded into SQLite FTS5 (porter+unicode61, plus trigram) and DuckDB 1.5.6 FTS (porter, english stopwords). DuckDB FTS needs INSTALL fts from the network (not in the wheel), the index is a static snapshot (not updated on insert), and it has no phrase/prefix/trigram. Per-query medians over 20 reps x 15 lexical queries (+5 phrase, 5 prefix, 5 substring, 4 regex).

Ranking overlap@5 over 15 real ddflow queries, DuckDB BM25 vs SQLite FTS5 BM25: 0.83 (records) / 0.84 (docs), top-1 identical 12/15; vs ddflow's fused ranking 0.81 / 0.77 (differences: stopword list, OR semantics, BM25 variant). Analytics over the real jsonl (56,551 events, 38.7 MB; events/agent/day + gate failure rate + item.started->completed median in one pass): python json.loads+Counter 0.40 s vs duckdb read_json x3 scans 0.27 s (0.21 at 4 threads), 0.07 s on a loaded table; synthetic 10x (565k events, 389 MB): 3.6 s vs 0.88 s; 20x (1.13M events, 779 MB): 6.9 s vs 1.3 s, duckdb RSS 3.0 GB at 20x. data.question: Does DuckDB beat SQLite FTS5 for ddflow's search/recall index, cold start, memory and analytics on the real data (2026-10-11)?

data.claim: DuckDB 1.5.6: the Python wheel statically links core_functions, icu, json, parquet only; fts and vss are NOT bundled and need INSTALL from the extension repository (network; fts 11.6 MB, vss 32.9 MB downloaded; works with a pre-seeded extension_directory offline). FTS index does not update automatically when the table changes; BM25 only; docs mention no phrase/prefix/trigram. Storage: newer reads older since v0.10, older reading newer is best-effort, migration is EXPORT/IMPORT DATABASE (so a derived index would need rebuild-on-version-change; harmless for a derived cache). Concurrency: one read-write process, or many read-only processes; no multi-process writers (Quack remote protocol beta). HNSW persistence needs an experimental flag because WAL recovery is not implemented for custom indexes. Licence MIT. Wheels: linux x86_64 21.6 MB, aarch64 19.5, macOS arm64 15.5, win amd64 13.2; installed _duckdb .so 58 MB.
data.falsifier: fts present as STATICALLY_LINKED in duckdb_extensions() of a stock wheel.
data.mechanism: Read duckdb.org docs pages (full_text_search, internals/storage, connect/concurrency, vss) via fetch and summarised by a small model: wording quoted below is the fetch tool's quotation, not read by eye on the page; wheel facts measured: duckdb_extensions() in the installed 1.5.6 wheel, LOAD fts offline failed with 'Extension fts not found', INSTALL fts then LOAD succeeded in 0.45 s, PyPI JSON for wheel sizes, dist-info METADATA for licence.

data.probe_output: extension_name/installed/mode: core_functions,icu,json,parquet STATICALLY_LINKED; fts, vss, httpfs, sqlite_scanner NOT_INSTALLED. LOAD fts -> IO Error: Extension fts.duckdb_extension not found. INSTALL fts+LOAD OK 0.45 s (11.6 MB), vss 0.62 s (32.9 MB). Page quotes: 'The FTS index will not update automatically when the input table changes.'; 'any DuckDB version released after [v0.10] can read files created by previous versions'; forward compatibility 'best effort basis'; 'multiple processes can read from the database, but no processes can write' in read-only mode; HNSW 'WAL recovery is not yet properly implemented for custom indexes'.

data.claim: Wall time is CPU-bound Python in the log read + fold, repeated several times per command, plus an eager import of the whole CLI; git subprocesses (0-23 per command) and I/O are not material. Extends R-perf-100k and the read-snapshot record Rb9e3498a92.

data.claim: Not now. The measured cost is algorithmic and avoidable inside Python (asdict deep copies, 3-6 folds per command, full-log reads for a Lamport max and a dedupe check, eager import of the whole CLI): fixing them is small, keeps 7,258+ tests and the event format, and is worth ~2.5-6x on the hot commands before any native code. A native fold/parse core (PyO3) pays only when the log passes ~500k events (fold+read ~27 s CPU, 1.3 GB RSS in Python), which at 4.1k events/day is ~4-5 months out and which snapshots/coalescing (B-gap-log-scale) push out by a factor of 5-10. A full rewrite is not justified: the hot core is ~13.5k of 110.7k source lines (12%); 36% of the lines are services/ that are I/O and policy.
data.falsifier: A profile where the fold's cost remains dominated by interpreter overhead after asdict and repeated folds are removed at 56k events, or an event log above 500k events within the next quarter.
data.mechanism: wc -l of ddflow/ (110,731 lines, 393 files; core 8,807, core/handlers 1,945, infra 7,793 (log.py 1,802, store.py 983), services 40,913, api 12,696, surfaces 4,987, config_sections 2,635); tests 129,183 lines / 611 files / 7,258 test functions. Compiled-parse proxies measured: orjson/msgspec 2.7-2.9x over json.loads (0.36 -> 0.12-0.13 s per 56k events); DuckDB read_json (multithreaded C++) ~0.25 s for the 779 MB / 1.13M-event log per pass vs 6.9 s Python; Python interpreter start 15-40 ms and import of the CLI 0.25-0.55 s are the non-algorithmic floor a native single binary would remove for hooks (a Rust/Go binary starts in ~1-5 ms: THEORETICAL, not measured here). Effort and risk figures are estimates (THEORETICAL).
data.probe: Arithmetic from R-perf-profile-2026-10-11 and R-perf-duckdb-measured; estimates: cheap Python fixes 1-2 weeks of lane time; PyO3 fold core ~4-6 weeks (handlers 1,945 + model 401 + records + upcasters, JSON-equal State output proven by replay-equivalence over this log) plus wheels per platform (maturin, 6-8 targets) and a pure-Python fallback that must stay bit-identical; Rust/Go hook binary ~3-4 weeks and a second implementation of the redactor, Lamport allocation, shard format, flock protocol and upgrade stamps; full rewrite 6-12 months and every one of the 22 harness descriptors, the 112 MCP tools, upcasters and 7k+ tests reimplemented.
data.probe_output: Thresholds that would justify native code (proposed, to be configured as budgets): (a) hook p50 (SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / heartbeat) over 300 ms idle after the Python fixes -> a Rust or Go fast path for the hook subset only (append + Lamport high-water + redaction); (b) fold+read of the shared log over 3 s idle after snapshots/checkpoints at the expected size -> PyO3 core; (c) steady-state RSS of a resident MCP server over 1 GB -> same; (d) more than 1M events in an active log. None is met today after the cheap fixes are applied; (a) and (b) are met TODAY without them (hook prompt 1.27 s, status 3-5 s under load; idle likely half).
data.question: Is a rewrite of ddflow (whole, or a native hot core) in Rust or Go worth it, and what would justify it (2026-10-11)?

data.body:
WHAT: keep the event log and the CLI fast as it grows. (1) Measure first (research record): per-kind bytes and counts, time of fold / index rebuild / status / next at 1x, 4x, 16x this log, where the 5.4 s of `ddflow status` goes (parse, fold, index, render). (2) Coalesce lease renewals: lease.renewed is 24,413 of 53,163 events (46%); log one only when the expiry would otherwise move by more than [lease].renew_log_min_s (or keep per-machine heartbeats in .ddflow/local via infra.LocalStore and fold only the last committed renewal), without changing what an observer on another clone computes as expiry. (3) Evidence out of line: gate.failed/passed carry 52% of bytes; store large evidence/tails as content-addressed blobs under .ddflow/blobs/ referenced by hash (event id stays a content address; doctor verifies the blob; tamper-evidence unchanged). (4) A checkpoint: a verified folded-state snapshot at a lamport mark so a read replays only the tail (B-log-snapshot-knobs already exists for the read snapshot; reuse it, do not add a second). (5) Shard rotation/archive is OUT of scope unless the measurement shows it is needed.
WHY: R-gaps-evidence: 35 MB and 53k events in 13 active days (~2.7 MB per active day, ~1 GB per year at this intensity); status 5.4 s, next 2.2 s with six lanes polling. T-performance-scale only measures, and is scheduled after all feature work; the operator feels this today. Temporal's lesson (R-gaps-survey): history replay is only viable with bounded history per execution, i.e. checkpoints.
INTERFACE TO REUSE: infra.EventLog and its read snapshot, infra.LocalStore (D-unify), the upcaster/version mechanism (D-upgrade-event-kinds) for any new event shape or blob reference, doctor for the new notes, config_sections/log.py for knobs. Any change to what is written needs an upcaster and the skew guard (D-upgrade-skew-guard); old logs must still fold identically.
HOW TO TEST: replay-equivalence: fold of the old log == fold of the coalesced/blob log for status, next, board, lease expiry, on this repository's real log copied into a tmp dir; a size/time ratchet test on a generated 10x log (cap runtime, no sleeps); blob tamper detected by doctor; two-clone merge test with coalesced renewals; failing-first for each.
SIZE: large (3-5 days of lane time, ~600-900 lines plus tests). Hot files: ddflow/infra/log.py, ddflow/services/leases.py -- expect to wait for B-hy-commit-events.
ACCEPTANCE: measured before/after table in a research record; lease.renewed share under 10% of events on the generated workload; `ddflow status` under 2 s on this log; byte-identical fold output on this log; old ddflow refuses or reads the new log per the skew guard; README/ARCHITECTURE updated.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: (4) correction: the existing read snapshot (infra/log.py) stores PARSED events, not folded state, and B-log-snapshot-knobs only promotes its knobs. Extend that one snapshot file with a verified folded-State record at a lamport mark so a read replays only the tail; do not add a second mechanism. (2) caution: core/handlers/leases.py (`_late_renewal`, the pairwise lease-window logic) uses the last renewal to widen a lease window, so keeping heartbeats only in .ddflow/local is allowed ONLY if the expiry another clone computes is unchanged within grace_s; prove it with a two-clone test. The globs above gained the model, the lease handler, events, claim/heartbeat api, the [lease] section, doctor and the docs for that reason.

Performance-research extension 2026-10-11 (R-perf-profile-2026-10-11, CONFIRMED; R-perf-rewrite-2026-10-11): the 5.4 s of `ddflow status` is not mostly parsing. Measured on a clone of this repo (56.5k events), cProfile: (1) `core/records._claim` calls `dataclasses.asdict(lease)` three times per lease.renewed during the fold (234k calls = 6.4 s of a 15 s profiled status; prototype in a scratch copy replacing it with a flat dict copy: status -24% cpu, fold alone 0.68 -> 0.28 s). Do this FIRST in this task: build the claim-window dict without asdict (the Lease is flat apart from two lists), pinned by a replay-equivalence test that the folded State and lease windows are byte-identical on the real log. (2) One command folds the log 3x (api/_base._load, services/leases.scan -> _fold, reporting/overview.status), the SessionStart hook 6x, MCP initialize 5x: fold once per command from one read and pass the State down (prototype ratio 0.62 of baseline on status); a per-process memo keyed by the log digest is acceptable only if the State is not mutated by callers (localize mutates: copy or make it pure). (3) infra/log._highest_lamport loads the parsed snapshot of ALL 240 shards (marshal.loads, ~0.4 s at 56k events) before every append, so every write command, hook and heartbeat pays a full-log read: keep a per-clone high-water Lamport sidecar in .ddflow/local verified against the shard sizes/tails (read only the last line of each shard on a cache miss), never trusting it past a shard whose size changed. (4) The existing read snapshot gave 1.5x at 56k events and no gain at >=113k events in the scratch harness (symlinked events dir; verify before relying on it) - the folded-State checkpoint above is the real fix, with the scaling curve as the budget: ~45 us CPU and ~2.3 KB RSS per event, 565k events = 28 s / 1.3 GB, 1.13M = 44 s / 2.6 GB, linear. Acceptance additions: a measured before/after table of `status`, `next`, `brief`, `heartbeat`, `hooks prompt` and `hooks session-start` on this log and on the generated 10x log (script in the research record's scratchpad path, to be moved into B-perf-bench), `status` under 2 s idle, an append in a fresh process under 100 ms at 56k events, fold count per command asserted by a test (status folds once). Globs added for (1)-(3): ddflow/core/records.py, ddflow/api/_base.py, ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py, tests/test_fold_once.py, tests/test_lamport_highwater.py.

Also check what are the performance bottlenecks of the current ddflow tool, is there any value of rewritting it in a faster programming language, like rust or go?" Evidence: R-perf-duckdb-measured, R-perf-duckdb-facts, R-perf-profile-2026-10-11 (CONFIRMED), R-perf-rewrite-2026-10-11 (THEORETICAL); earlier: D-no-duckdb (binding), R-perf-100k, Rb9e3498a92, R-gaps-evidence. The log-read/fold/Lamport fixes live in B-gap-log-scale (extended 2026-10-11, P-gaps core wave); this phase holds what is NOT there: the operator decisions, the benchmark harness with budgets, the import-time and hook fast paths, MCP start-up and resident cache. data.title: Performance: measured budgets, hook latency, import time and the log read path (no rewrite, no second database unless thresholds are crossed)

data.body:
ASK THE OPERATOR; nothing else in P-perf starts before this is answered. Evidence: R-perf-duckdb-measured, R-perf-duckdb-facts, R-perf-profile-2026-10-11, R-perf-rewrite-2026-10-11. Record the answers as decisions (ddflow decision add --globs ...) and file docs/ddflow/decisions/performance.md.
1. DuckDB. Default: keep D-no-duckdb as is (SQLite FTS5 stays the only index, vectors for B-semantic-recall/B-ds-semantic in the same SQLite). Measured: FTS5 is 10-60x faster per query, 10x cheaper to start (19 ms vs 222 ms, 13.5 MB vs 66 MB RSS), has phrase/prefix/trigram DuckDB FTS lacks, updates incrementally; DuckDB FTS is a static snapshot installed from the network (not in the wheel), the file format needs EXPORT/IMPORT across versions, one writer process. Alternative (not recommended now): an optional ddflow[analytics] extra behind a config-selected analytics backend (read_json over the shards; 5x faster than Python at 1.13M events, 1.3 s vs 6.9 s) - revisit only if the active log passes 500k events AFTER B-gap-log-scale; it would need its own task (interface, offline extension handling, version rebuild).
2. Rewrite. Default: no rewrite, no native module now. Thresholds proposed (stored as [perf] budgets, B-perf-bench): hook p50 over 300 ms idle after the Python fixes -> Rust/Go fast path for the hook subset only; fold+read over 3 s idle at the expected size after checkpoints -> PyO3 core; resident MCP RSS over 1 GB or an active log over 1M events -> same. Accept, change numbers, or drop.
3. Budgets (defaults, idle machine, this repository's log): ddflow --version 150 ms; hooks prompt 300 ms; hooks session-start 1.5 s; heartbeat 300 ms; status/next/brief 2 s; MCP initialize 1 s; fresh-process append 100 ms. All configurable.
4. Resident state. Default: the MCP server keeps the folded State cached by log digest (no new daemon; D-sched-no-daemon stands). Alternative: a long-lived command daemon for the CLI (rejected by default: a process to supervise per clone).
5. Order. Default: the cheap fixes ride in B-gap-log-scale (P-gaps core wave, already extended); the rest of this phase follows it.
Size: small (one question round). Acceptance: answers recorded as decisions; tasks below adjusted or dropped to match; docs/ddflow/decisions/performance.md filed.
data.title: Operator decisions: DuckDB, rewrite thresholds, hook budgets, resident state (recommended defaults in the body)

data.body: WHAT: `ddflow perf [--commands ...] [--log-scale 1|4|16] [--runs N] [--json]` and MCP tool ddflow_perf (identical bodies, parity test): runs the hot commands (version, brief, next, status, gate status, claim/heartbeat on a scratch item, hooks prompt, hooks session-start, search, recall, doctor) as fresh processes in a scratch clone of the project (never the live store), records wall AND cpu time (cpu is robust against a loaded machine), median/min/max, git subprocess count (a shim on PATH), peak RSS, and the fold count; compares each to the budget in [perf] config and exits 1 over budget, 2 when it could not run, with the load average printed beside every number and the run flagged noisy above a configured load per core. Also the import-time table (-X importtime top modules). WHY: R-perf-profile-2026-10-11: every number we have was measured by hand in a scratch directory under load 30-300 on 192 cores; without a ratchet the 0.19 s import (R-perf-100k) became 0.5 s unnoticed and status grew to 5.4 s. INTERFACE TO REUSE: the generated 1x/4x/16x log fixtures of B-gap-log-scale and T-performance-scale (do not write a second generator: the scratch generator used for the research renames subjects and ids and shifts Lamport, ~30 lines), infra.LocalStore for results under .ddflow/local, the cadence service (ddflow cadence) for a periodic run, config_sections/ for knobs: [perf] budgets per command (ms), runs, noisy_load_per_core, log_scale, enabled_in_ci. NOTHING hardcoded: budgets, thresholds for the native-core triggers of B-perf-decide (fold seconds, RSS, event count) and the commands list are config; doctor prints a NOTE when a stored result exceeds a budget or a trigger threshold. TESTS: budgets parse and are honoured (a fake slow command exceeds, exit 1); load-noise flag; CLI/MCP parity; scratch clone leaves the live store untouched (hash of .ddflow before/after); a failing-first test per knob (dead-knob ratchet). SIZE: medium (~500 lines plus tests). ACCEPTANCE: a table for this repository in a research record, a cadence entry that fails when a budget is exceeded by more than the configured margin, README/ARCHITECTURE documented.
data.title: ddflow perf: a benchmark harness on CLI and MCP with budgets in config, a generated-log fixture and a cadence check

data.body: WHAT: `ddflow --version`, `--help` and every hook subcommand currently import the whole CLI: cpu 0.53 s for `import ddflow.surfaces.cli` (-X importtime: ddflow.api 0.56 of 0.62 s total, ddflow.api.knowledge 0.18, ddflow.api.ci 0.18, ddflow.config 0.07, jinja2 0.04, services.export 0.06, upgrade_apply 0.07) against 0.04 s for bare Python, measured under load (about half idle). Make command dispatch lazy: the registry maps a command name to a module path and imports that module only when invoked (argparse parser construction from declared data stays cheap, or the parser for one command is built on demand); keep jinja2/tomlkit lazy until first use; hooks import only infra.log, the redactor and the session service. WHY: R-perf-profile-2026-10-11; it is the floor of every agent action that runs a ddflow process (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, git hooks, every CLI call). D-compat: no behaviour change; the existing hoisting work (R9ce3581787: 36 deferred imports hoisted) pushed the other way - cycles stay broken through the registry, not function-local imports, and the earlier tests that forbid function-local imports must keep passing. INTERFACE TO REUSE: surfaces/registry.py and declared/ tables, the single parser source of CLI+MCP parity (mcp.py must still list all 112 tools from the same table). TESTS: failing-first import-budget test: `python -X importtime -c 'import ddflow.surfaces.cli'` imports no module under ddflow.api/ddflow.services except those the command needs (assert by module set, not by milliseconds, so it is load-proof) plus a measured-budget check through B-perf-bench; full CLI/MCP parity and help-text goldens unchanged. SIZE: medium (~300 lines, touches hot files: expect to wait for B-hot-files). ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow --version` cpu under 4x bare Python startup on the same machine; before/after table in a research record; no golden changed.
data.title: Import time: load a command's modules only when it runs (--version and hooks without importing the whole api), pinned by an import-time budget test

data.body: WHAT: R-perf-profile-2026-10-11 measured (cpu, loaded machine, 56.5k events): hooks prompt 1.27 s, hooks session-start 6.0 s with 10 git calls. Prompt hook: capture_prompt's double-fire check calls read_all() over all 240 shards (0.68 s profiled) to look at the last few seconds of ONE session - read only the tail of the session's own shard (and the harness' dedupe key), never the whole log; the append then uses the Lamport high-water of B-gap-log-scale. SessionStart: 6 folds (19 of 29 profiled seconds), an inline index rebuild (store.ensure 5.5 s) and the worktree drift scan (enforce.drift 4.8 s) run before the brief is printed - fold once; print the brief from the cached State; move the index rebuild and drift scan behind the brief (deferred, background-safe, or only when stale by the existing fingerprint), keeping the safety checks that must precede the first tool call. Hooks stay 'always exit 0'; a hook over its budget logs a NOTE instead of failing. WHY: this is the number every agent session pays on every prompt; the 3 s DOUBLE_FIRE window bug B72b9ab33fc was caused by this very startup cost. INTERFACE TO REUSE: infra.EventLog shard tail reader, B-gap-log-scale high-water and fold-once, services/sessions.capture_prompt, [perf] budgets (B-perf-bench) for hook_ms, config knob [perf].hook_deferred_work (default on). TESTS: failing-first: prompt hook reads at most the own shard (assert bytes read / shards opened via the log's read counters on a 240-shard fixture), session-start folds once (fold counter), the double-fire dedupe still holds with a slow second process (reuse test_a_copy_slow_to_start_is_still_the_same_firing), brief output identical; budget test through B-perf-bench. SIZE: medium (~400 lines). ACCEPTANCE: hooks prompt under 300 ms and session-start under 1.5 s idle on this log, before/after table in a research record; CLI/MCP parity unaffected; docs updated.
data.title: Hooks: UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart do bounded work (own-shard dedupe, one fold, no index rebuild or drift scan inline)

data.body: WHAT: R-perf-profile-2026-10-11: spawn to initialize reply took 9.1 s (5 folds; surf_mcp.fill_queue for the instructions text is 12 of 25 profiled seconds, plus upgrade_plan.build 9 s); every later tool call re-folds (ddflow_status 4.2 then 3.4 s, brief 3.6, next 1.4, recall 1.9, show 0.8, resident RSS 255 MB), so a long-lived server gains nothing from being long-lived; tools/list is 112 tools = 100,012 bytes (~25k tokens) in every session. (1) Initialize returns static instructions at once and fills the queue/upgrade summary lazily on the first ddflow_brief/ddflow_next (the client waits on initialize before showing the agent anything). (2) Cache the folded State and the read snapshot in the server keyed by the log digest (cheap stat of shard sizes/mtimes), invalidated on any append by this process or a changed shard: a call on an unchanged log is index lookups only; fold-once from B-gap-log-scale is the prerequisite. (3) Tool list: measure bytes per tool, shorten descriptions that repeat the CLI help, keep every tool (parity) - or deferred tool schemas if the client supports them; the operator decides how far (B-lean-and-trusted already trimmed once: reuse its measurements). Nothing hardcoded: [mcp].state_cache (bool, default true), [mcp].lazy_instructions (bool, default true), [perf] budgets. TESTS: failing-first: initialize returns without touching the log (fold counter 0, read counter 0); two status calls on an unchanged log fold once; an append from another process is seen by the next call (cache invalidation, two-process test); a cached State is never mutated by a caller (compare against fresh fold on the real log); tools/list byte budget ratchet. SIZE: medium (~400 lines). ACCEPTANCE: initialize under 1 s and a repeated ddflow_status under 0.3 s on this log, idle; table in a research record; docs.
data.title: MCP server: answer initialize without a status fold, keep the folded State resident by log digest, and shrink the 100 KB tool list

WHAT: residuals of fix-B71dedb76d2 (merge 2a1b7e67).
