data.body:
WHAT: an identity/host leak early warning that runs locally and in CI parity: a cheap check, not the full runner emulation (which produced 26 false failures). One of: a pytest option (e.g. --ci-identity) that fixes getpass.getuser(), socket.gethostname() and PATH stubs for a configured subset of the pinned-transcript tests; or a lint script (scripts/ci/identity-leak-check.py, wired as a pre-commit/pre-push hook) that flags pinned fixtures and goldens containing the developer's user name or host. Prefer the lint if the option cannot be made false-positive-free; either way the subset, the extra forbidden strings and an on/off switch are configurable (a [ci] knob or a file listing), default on, and the failure message names the file, line and the value found.
WHY: pinned transcripts that embed the author's user or host pass locally and fail on every other machine and in CI; the failure is found late, by the runner.
TEST (failing first): a fixture containing the current user name is flagged; a clean tree passes; the knob switches it off; the subset selection is honoured.
SIZE: small to medium (~150 lines). ACCEPTANCE: the check runs in the pre-push stage in under 5 s, no false positive on the current tree, documented in README.
data.title: Identity and host leak early warning for pinned fixtures: a cheap CI-parity check

data.body:
WHAT: bug B-loop-transcript-slow. tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py::test_the_loop_cli_transcript_is_unchanged takes about 110 s alone and was given @pytest.mark.timeout(1800) as a workaround. Find why (suspect: many subprocess CLI invocations, each paying the 0.5 s import cost, plus per-call folds of a growing log) and cut it under about 30 s without losing what it pins (the byte-for-byte transcript): batch or in-process dispatch for the steps that do not need a fresh process, keep one real-process pass for the cases that do. Also look at the timing seams of tests/test_local_ticks.py and tests/test_review_rechunk.py, which failed once under load (sleep/clock/poll assumptions: inject the clock or wait on a condition, not a fixed delay).
WHY: a 110 s test dominates the parallel unit_tests gate and forces a 1800 s per-test timeout that hides real hangs; flaky timing tests train agents to rerun and ignore failures.
TEST: the transcript golden is unchanged (diff is empty); the test's runtime is asserted by measurement in the research note (before/after), the per-test 1800 s timeout mark is removed; the two flaky tests pass 50 times in a row under `-n 48` load.
SIZE: medium (~150 lines of test code). ACCEPTANCE: under 30 s alone, golden byte-identical, no timeout mark above the default, timing seams fixed or documented.
data.title: Slow test: cut test_the_loop_cli_transcript_is_unchanged under 30 s and fix the timing seams of test_local_ticks and test_review_rechunk

Today the gate command is a free string (`uv run pytest ...` in .ddflow/config.toml [gate.unit_tests]; [ci].command empty = pre-commit pre-push stage). Check how the gate command is run (services/gates/runner.py, defs.py, services/ci.py) and whether `uv run --python X` can be a config knob: e.g. [gate.unit_tests].python = "3.11" (or a list for a matrix, each recorded as its own outcome) and [ci].python, expanded into the command via the same uv selection; absent version = unavailable recorded honestly, never passed (a missing interpreter is `unavailable`).
WHY: bugs found only on CI's other Python (B-proc-stdin-resume on 3.12.3, the 3.11 floor) are not caught by the local gate on the developer's default interpreter.
TEST (failing first): the knob adds `--python <v>` to a uv command and is refused/ignored with a clear note for a non-uv command; a missing interpreter records unavailable; config golden and knob doc updated.
SIZE: small to medium (~120 lines). ACCEPTANCE: gate config selects the interpreter, this repository's own config can turn on 3.11, documented in README and config golden.

Wire it in doctor next to `notes.extend(UP.doctor_notes(st))` in ddflow/api/reporting/health.py: `notes.extend(US.doctor_notes(repo, st))`, with a test that a TIMEOUT marker makes `ddflow doctor` print the note and that it disappears once the project is at the running version. Update the README sentence that says "ddflow doctor follows". ALSO in ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py: pass the folded state, US.take_for_brief(repo, st) in _upgrade_notices (today the marker path re-folds the log once per brief while a timeout note is pending; roborev finding on the parent fix). Add ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py to this task's globs.

Follow-up of fix-Ba24a8d32ee (merged b4aed93b): the lost-event detection (services/shardmarks.py) and the CLI-only ddflow doctor --accept-lost-events are not in the README or the recovery help topic. Document: what the shard high-water mark is (.ddflow/local/shard-marks, per branch and shard: count, last event id, size; raised never lowered), the PROBLEM text, the reflog/git log --all/git show hints, accept as an operator-only CLI action (not an MCP tool), and the known limit (an interior event removed then regrown to the old count before any ddflow command looks cannot be told from growth; belongs to P-multiuser sync-check). Docs gate evidence with the README claim check.
data.title: Document ddflow doctor --accept-lost-events and the shard high-water mark (README, recovery help topic)

data.body: Operator 2026-10-12: look into gate flapping after the pause. ddflow loops reports 13 gate_flapping findings, mostly critic and rubber_duck (fix-Ba24a8d32ee: 11 verdict changes each; fix-Bfc9daca269: 8 on critic). Find out whether it is reviewer nondeterminism, round-budget semantics (a gate that reports findings stays failed until the budget is spent, then passes on refutation), chunked re-review repeating findings already fixed, or a ddflow bug. Evidence: ddflow loops and the gate events of those items. Output: a research record with a verdict and, if warranted, a fix task (failing-first). Reuse the existing review triage and gate evidence; nothing hardcoded.
data.title: Research: why critic/rubber_duck gates flap (11 verdict changes on fix-Ba24a8d32ee, 8 on fix-Bfc9daca269)
